en: From prehistory to Terina.

Small church of fifteenth-century origins with a single nave, with rustic façade, sailing bell tower and a tiny rosette; during the plague of 1630 the Dominicans used it as a lazzaretto and from the windows of the facade the food was passed to the plagued ones. The main work is the Crucifixion on the background wall, attributed to the school of Liberale da Verona and rediscovered at the beginning of the nineteenth century; on the left wall a fresco with Saints Peter, Mary Magdalene, Antonio Abate, Quirico and Giovanni Battista, and under the roof a fragment with lamb and palm perhaps coming from the Lombard church of Santa Giustina.

About 10 km from the center, the village was a centre of the partisan struggle: the shrine is in Martyrs Square of Liberty. In summer it is a destination for hiking and free flight, in winter skiing with the Rucas facilities up to 1,800 m to Costa Ciapè.
The heart of Pratola's devotion.
The Romanesque on the floor.
The public palace of a small autonomous lordship.
A landscape of rocks carved by water.
Walk through the walls and the prior palace.
A fortress of the historic city.

On a limestone spur on the high valley of the Trigno, it probably stands on ancient Sannitique positions; the village is closed by a belt of about 750 meters with houses incorporated. Originally it was made up of distinct fortified bodies, a small church, a cylindrical tower, a fortress and a wall; in the seventeenth century the d'Alessandro added drawbridge, courtyard and warehouses and transformed it into a noble residence. There they had a famous horse farm (in 1711 Giuseppe d'Alessandro published the treatise "Pietra di Paragone dei Cavalieri") and, between 1780 and 1795, a factory of majolica and competing porcelain of Capodimonte, remembered by the Museum of Ceramics in the former tavern of the manor. On the first floor the chapel with marbles, stuccoes, a canvas of a student of Solimena and the relics of St. Alexander brought in 1787; hosted Theodor Mommsen during the visit to the excavations of Pietrabbondante.
€5 whole; €15 for all Florentine dinners (7 days)
Church of the 10th century in the southwestern part of the Colfiorito plateau, towards Visso.
Urban art in the ruins.
A natural area of about 7,000 hectares between Grosseto and Livorno, with wild boars, roe deer, deer and istrices, and the alum quarries linked to Elisa Bonaparte.

Country at the foot of the Apuans between Massa and Versilia, dominated by the Aghinolfi Castle, the cornerstone of the Gothic Line in 1945; downstream Villa Schiff Giorgini with the documentation center on the war, the churches of San Vito and Modesto and of Sant'Eustachio, Mount Pasquilio dear to Ungaretti and Montale, the oasis of Lake Porta and the sea of Cinquale.
Calatia and the Appia in a Carafa hunting mess.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 0 of the 3 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
The battlefield of the nations.
Roman galleries dug by Emperor Claudio from 41 A.D. to regulate the waters of Lake Fucino and protect the houses from the floods; you can visit them with guided tours.
Interactive route on the history of Padula and Vallo di Diano from prehistory to the nineteenth century. Included in the integrated ticket "Certosa" and "Padula"
Nature and panorama in the city.
A hike to a panoramic summit.
Facades carved thanks to the illustrious bathers of the past.

Parish church started in 1524 on a church with three naves with circular pillars, linked to the Cusani: in 1541 Giovanni Giacomo Cusani built the chapel of the Archangel Raffaele, today baptismal with a red marble bathtub, and in 1577 St. Charles blessed its bells. Marbles, paintings, altars and choirs are of Six, Seven and Nineteenth Century; at the main altar there is a wooden cross carved and gilded with a wooden group of Maddalena, Madonna and San Giovanni, in the chapels an eighteenth-century altarpiece of the martyrdom of San Sebastiano and the wooden statue of the Madonna del Rosario with the paintings of the Mysteries, as well as two confessionals of the seventeenth century. Without architectural barriers.
Quiet bay not far from the town, with fine ochre sand.
He collects works of painting, textile art and goldsmithery related to the cathedral.
A stop in the middle.
access to the ruins forbidden for security, visit only from outside
The palace of the merchant Francesco di Marco Datini, among the stages recommended in the center.
An open-air museum of the time between stone houses.

The only museum of this kind in Italy, founded in 1989 in a territory that produces scales since 1860: over 9,000 objects between scales, swing and stade, with posters, catalogues and vintage photos, from the Middle Ages to today. The route includes the Labyrinth of phenomena (we weigh with the gravity of the Moon and Jupiter), the Gallery of Crafts, the Canal of History and the Gallery of the Swings and the great staders for Parmigiano Reggiano, barrels and salt. Saturday, Sunday and holidays 10-12.30 and 15.30-19 (15-18.30 with sunshine); weekdays by reservation.

Remains of the Roman city of Suasa, abandoned in the 6th century A.D., excavated by the University of Bologna with the Superintendence: base road, commercial forum, two necropolis, houses and the amphitheatre (end of the 1st century BC, discovered in 1990), where performances are held in summer. The heart of the park is the Domus dei Coiedii, from the 1st century A.D., at the most splendid in the 2nd century: under a modern roof, with raised walkways, mythological, floral and geometric mosaics and a floor with more than fifteen types of marble form the most important unitary complex of the Marches. Opening hours: 24/4-30/6 and 1/9-8/12 Saturday, Sunday and holidays 15:30-19:30; July-August Tuesday-Saturday 16-20, Sunday 10:30-12:30 and 16-20.
From the sea to a waterfall in the woods.

Fortress built from 1360 on the hill Sant'Elia for Cardinal Egidio Albornoz on a project by Gattapone, seat of the papal governors and prison until 1982; since 2007 it houses in fifteen halls the National Museum of the Duchy, with materials from the fourth to the fifteenth century.
The palaces of the village.
A rarity of the Middle Ages.
Snow at Turin's reach, even for families.

In front of the library of the Convent of Santa Maria della Pietà, in Vatolla, at 430 meters above sea level, there is a monumental olive tree recorded by the Campania Region: about 400 years, 295 cm of circumference and 5 meters of height. The popular tradition is that Giambattista Vico sat there in a stone seat to read Aristotle and other Greek and Latin authors.
Walk suspended at 36 meters on the Lima.
A Renaissance cloister to cross.
Chamois, ibex, and bee-jacks on the Marines.
To watch at night, when the arches light up some blue, yellow and fuchsia neons by the artist Marco Lodola.

Bridge covered in wood on the Brenta at the point where the river narrows, symbol of the city and national monument since 2019; in the Great War the troops headed for the plateau of the Seven Municipalities crossed it.
Stone houses and rascard in wood of traditional architecture.
Neoclassical marble theater from the 19th century, behind Piazza Alberica next to the monument to Garibaldi by Carlo Nicoli.
Naturalistic path with garden of the five senses, orchard of ancient varieties and didactic path in the woods.

Built in the 17th century on the ruins of the medieval fortress: in the courtyard a well dated 1632, year of completion; two stone staircases go up to a loggia with arches and the rooms preserve monumental chimneys.

Documented at least from the 12th century, it passed from the lords of Velturno to the counts of Tyrol and then to the Wolkensteins, who held it for over six centuries: among them the poet and traveller Oswald (1377-1445). The large halls of representation added between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries give it the present form: Gothic hall with three spans, loggia with frescoes of coats of arms, painted chapel and the New Hall of the Knights (1618 circa) with wooden ceiling inlaid coffered; decisive restorations of the Südtiroler Burgeninstitut at the end of the twentieth century. The Museum of Castles exhibits about eighty scale models. Guided tour only (German or Italian, 40-50 minutes plus 15 minutes for the exhibition), from Holy Thursday to October 31, closed on Monday; Invalid Museumcard.
The largest cerro in Italy.

The cathedral, inside the castle, houses the sacred inch of the saint in a silver reliquary, shown during the holidays; next to the cloister, part of the first Benedictine monastery built in Sicily at the behest of Ruggero II.
A country still in 1901.

Borgo dell'alta Val di Sole at about 1,000 meters, at the confluence of Noce and Vermigliana, with the hamlets of Cusiano and Fucine: the Castello San Michele with its 25-metre mast, the church of San Vigilio from 1180, Stuva Nova and, from the end of November to the Epiphany, the Borgo dei Mille Presepi.

Church mentioned already in the thirteenth century, turned star and net at the beginning of the sixteenth century, parish since 1515; the Romanesque bell tower probably dates back to about 1300 and the baptismal font dates back to 1033. The main altar of 1850 frames a altarpiece by Orazio Giovanelli from 1630 with the martyrdom of San Vigilio. It is a pilgrimage destination for the painting of the Sorrowful which, according to tradition, \"piense" from 1733 to 1738.

In Palazzo Mastromarchi, inaugurated on May 1, 1985 and dedicated to the Castrovillarese painter Andrea Alfano, born from a donation of the former members of the association "Sestium" and works donated by artists from all over Italy. There are 236 paintings and drawings and 23 20th century sculptures, with names such as Guttuso, Turcato, Treccani, Fazzini and Emilio Greco.

Considered the first parish church of the valley, of the VI-VII centuries and rebuilt in the XII: it has no facade because it replaces the rock wall on the Oglio, and you enter from the side, by a portal carved with animal and vegetable motifs and the statues of a lion and a lamb. Three naves with apses protruding on the overhang, Lombard crypt with Roman materials of reuse and frescoes of the Tre-Quattrocento.

Confraternal church of 1613 dedicated to Saints Gregorio and Vito, linked to a rich confraternity that prayed for the dead: the Baroque interior has a golden altar that reproduces the mountain of Purgatory and the church offers views of the surrounding landscape.

Borgo della Vallelonga, the ancient Transaqua Valley, between woods and mountains on the border with the National Park of Abruzzo, Lazio and Molise, at altitudes between 850 and over 1600 meters. It preserves the historic center with walls, doors, tower and square, the Archaeological Civic Museum in Palazzo Botticelli and the Museum of peasant civilization and work.
Alleys and walls of the medieval village above the village.
The village on the beach.
Three great sweaters in a 16th century forge.
Probably the oldest church in the city (XI century), rebuilt in the eighteenth century by Girolamo Frigimelica with unfinished facade and works of Palma il Giovane and Garofalo.
Water and sea in the plain.
The ancient capital, with the Portaccia of the castle on the Arno.
A church turned into a theatre.

In the villa built at the end of the nineteenth century by Ricciotti Garibaldi, the last son of Giuseppe and Anita, he tells of a border territory between the Papal State and the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies: at the entrance the plastici of the convent of San Giorgio, the castle and the villa; on the lower floor are found from prehistory (fossil of Elephas antiquus italicus) to the imperial age, with the dagger of a fair warrior from the necropolis of Casal Rotondo; on the upper floor tools and crafts of the peasant and pastoral tradition, the local festivals and relics of the Garibaldi family. Accessible to the disabled.

Natural reserve oriented at the foot of Capo Tindari, of about 400 hectares of Mediterranean maquis, with three brackish lakes, the cliff, the wide beach of Marinello and, behind the head, the caves of Mongiove with natural arches, faraglioni and the cave of Donna Villa.

Castle of the Bishops of Ivrea, born from a walls of the IX-X century around the church of St. Peter, with the mast of the XI century, the round towers of 1390 and the spiral staircase of 1509-1512; in 1363 Bishop Pietro de la Chambre was held prisoner. In 1885 Alfredo d'Andrade bought it for 7,000 lire and restored it in medieval style, creating between 1912 and 1915 the Salone di Re Arduino; since 1991 it is part of the Giodice family and hosts hotels, restaurants and conference center. Private: internal visits should be requested from the property (tel. 0125 672111).
the MiC card (updated to December 2020) reports "Closed" every day at the times

On four floors of an ancient building tells the story of the village and of the weaving: Lorsica was among the main centers of the Genoese manufacture, whose fabrics in the sixteenth-sixth century were known in the world as "Velours de Gênes" . It exhibits frames, tools for spinning, canning and dyeing and antique fabrics (damasks, lamps, linen macramè, an embroidered planet of the parish). According to the Metropolitan City opens Saturday and Sunday 16-18 from April to October and 15-17 from November to March, and by reservation on other days (tel. 0185 95019).
Natural hot water at the foot of the mountains.

The middle course of Savovato, between the territories of Rogliano, Altilia, Parenti, Scigliano, Belsito, Carpanzano and Marzi, known for the waterfall of Cannavina, about 15 meters high. Within 20-30 km there are four historical bridges: of the Roman Ischia (16th century, in Balzata), of Tavolaria (16th century, about 200 m downstream of the confluence of the Cannavina), of the Fratte (late medieval reconstruction of a perhaps Roman structure) and of Sant'Angelo, called The place is reported several times in the FAI census "The Places of the Heart."

The highest peak (884 m) of the reliefs between Giardini Naxos, Taormina and Castelmola, reached by a bare and panoramic path; from the summit you can see Castelmola, the Greek theatre of Taormina, Isola Bella and Etna. It is one of the most frequented ramps by paragliders.
Ancient streets and squares with vintage buildings, decorated portals, porticoes and capitals, of Roman origins as evidenced by the votive cippo of the first century A.D. preserved in Santo Stefano.
Medieval tower in the center of Cene, of Gallic origin according to the tourist portal, with Roman stands.
The village in panoramic position among the chestnut groves, on the road of the Muraglione Pass towards Romagna.
It preserves the funeral monument of the Filangieri family, the work of Domenico Gagini (1481).
In the Bishop's Palace next to the cathedral, he collects paintings of the Venetian and Neapolitan schools.

The city of the arcades at the confluence of five valleys: the Straight Carruggio, the cathedral of Our Lady of the Garden, Palazzo Rocca with the civic gallery and the archaeological museum of the necropolis of the Iron Age.
Aquarius born in August 2010, offers a path deep in the sea between fish and sea creatures. The MiC tab indicates opening from Tuesday to Friday 10-13 and Saturday 16-19.
A quarry lake became a city park.

An eighteenth-century church with a single nave with three altars, the largest inlaid marble, built next to an older bell tower (a stone at the base has the date 1607) that dominates the village; on the left of the entrance there is a stone fountain of 1701 coming from the sacristy. It was damaged by the earthquake of November 23, 1980, and reopened to worship on December 20, 1997; it traditionally houses a relic of the saint.
The rectangular temple of Portuno and the round temple of Hercules Winner, both of the second century BC, in Piazza Bocca della Verità.
One of the great fortresses of the eighteenth century in Europe.
A typical example of railway architecture.
The only surviving door of the ancient wall surrounding Barletta.

Ring of about 10-12 km, almost all flat (2-3 hours walk), partly suitable for strollers and bikes. On the west bank are the so-called Napoleonic fortresses, actually fortifications from the eighteenth-nineteenth-century Austria, of which ruins, walls and trenches remain, and the Roman Bridge with a waterfall that falls directly into the lake.

Lusérn, at 1,333 meters on the plateau between Folgaria, Lavarone and Passo Vezzena, is the last island where the Cimbrian language, ancient Bavarian dialect, is still spoken fluently: the Haus von Prükk museum house, the documentation center and, on Cima Campo, the fort of the Great War.

Wanted by Cardinal Alessandro Farnese and designed by Antonio da Sangallo the Younger at the beginning of the sixteenth century, with frescoes from the sixteenth century and hexagonal floor. The patron saint is celebrated on September 1st with procession and the traditional cookies of Sant'Egidio.
The green lung of the Tarvisian millennial.
The most spectacular city of the dead in prehistoric Sicily.
The Brescia popular and night.
Visitable only on occasion of extraordinary openings (calendar on the site of the Regional Museums Directorate)

Medieval village on a ridge of tuff between the valleys of Chiarano and Mola, gathered around the Fortress Colonna with the Sala Pinta frescoed by Federico Zuccari; the territory is part of the Regional Natural Park of Veio, with Etruscan-capenati necropolis.
Palladio and Veronese together, in the most famous Venetian villa of Treviso.
Novara in the Risorgimento.
The Magi parade with portraits of the Medici.
Walk through terraced vineyards.
Birdwatching between flamingos and herons a few steps from the sea.

Established in 1992 in the former Palazzo Bono in 1605, it tells with photographs and tools the peasant life and the ancient trades of the fields: reconstructions of kitchen, bedroom and classroom of the late nineteenth century, a small watermill, the 1:40 scale model of Cascina Colombera and documents from the sixteenth to the twentieth century; from the museum you can see the Monte Rosa.
Outdoor art in the middle of the green.

It rises on the remains of a fifth century basilica, with Romanesque façade of the thirteenth century; during the nineteenth-century restorations a large pavement mosaic emerged of about 900 square meters of the middle of the sixth century.
The eighteenth-century organ with the saint at the top.
The square of the plane tree overlooking the Comino Valley.
Medieval doors and the memory of the knives.
Roman Asculum.
A short walk through glimpses and small town stories.
The hamlet of travelers.
Among the oldest churches in the country, Baroque, with stuccoes, allegorical statues, tortile columns and a majolica floor of the factories of Burgio.
The chalk ridge seen from the ruins of the castle of Tossignano, part of the UNESCO site on karst.
temporarily closed for renovation and renovation; reopening indicated for April 15, 2025, to be verified
The history of Italian espresso.
The relics of Saint Dominic.
Brigands' forest with a view of the Circeo.
Real hills above the Riviera.
The original props of the films.

The ancient church of San Vincenzo was rebuilt between 1655 and 1683 and its bell tower would be part of the keep of an ancient castle. Next to it, two eighteenth-century palaces with frescoed rooms: Palazzo Fedrigotti, today the town hall, and Palazzo Vannetti.

In the Biogenetic Reserve of Fallistro, established in 1987 and part of the world network of UNESCO Biosphere Reserves, over sixty larch pines and mountain maples up to 45 meters and about 350 years old, planted in the seventeenth century by the Barons Mollo, owners of the nearby hunting casino (the purchase of land is documented by an act of 1631). Between the seven and nineteenth century the estate had mill, spinning mill and chapels; since 2016 trees and Casino Mollo are entrusted to FAI.
entrance by reservation for organized groups and school groups, with extraordinary openings during the year (tel. 039 6659488)
The Romanesque mosaic of the 12th century.
The war told live.
To be checked: openings with Pro Loco on reservation
An amphitheatre among the olive trees.

On a hill just outside the village, reached by a characteristic staircase; the legend wants it erected in the fifteenth century after the Virgin expelled the evil spirits that tormented the shepherds. It preserves frescoes and since 1479 it is the destination of a solemn procession every year.
The Punic fortress on the high ground.

San Michele is the reference area of Trento Doc, with the highest concentration of producers in Trentino, between international and autochthonous varieties; in Faedo Müller Thurgau grows higher and Chardonnay, aromatic Traminer, Lagrein and Schiava lower. The tourist consortium refers to the list of wineries that can be visited; Italia.it also remembers the distillates of the hilly area of Faedo.
The fresco survived 1693.
Basin of glacial origin above the village, reachable by car, with a small play area on the shore.

The work designed by the Lodigian artist Giuliano Mauri, stands on a sheltered hill along the ascent to Pizzo Arera: over 20 metres high, it has a gothic five-nave plant with 42 beech columns, supported by about 1,800 spruce poles, 600 chestnut branches and 6,000 metres of hazel branches taken from the nearby woods and tied with ropes, pins and nails. In time the beech trees will grow until they no longer need scaffolding, destined to deteriorate.
An oratory of the 200s.
Canyon dug by man in five centuries of mine.
Medieval church, probably the oldest in the territory, which preserves some original frescoes; one, of the fifteenth century, is now at the Bishop's Museum of Foligno.
Natural pool of transparent waters between granite walls, in the Mello Valley: easy path of about an hour and a half with 150 meters of altitude difference, from spring to autumn.
The oldest Jewish community in Europe.
Along the ancient mule tracks.
The pavement of the hole under the steps of the center.
openings only on established days with mandatory booking (calendar 2025); villa under restoration
For a fee: rates on the spa website

About 164 hectares south of the centre: it is the largest wetland on the western shore of Lake Maggiore, Special Conservation Zone of the Natura 2000 network; the north part is oasis of protection since 1988. Canneti, yellow water lilies, black alder forests and rare ferns; over 300 species of birds recorded and a colony of cormorants on the Partegora Island. About 4 km of trails and a birdwatching shed, dogs on a leash.
Pay on one of the cleanest rivers in Europe.

It was built around 1813 from a rustic building used as a barn and inaugurated in 1852 with I Capuleti and Montecchi di Bellini: up to 400 seats, 47 stages on three orders and a curtain painted by hand with the Fiera di Luzzara in the presence of the Gonzaga princes.
Two and a half kilometers of walls.
The entrance to the Roman forum.
The Roman city under the village.

The birthplace of St. Louis Gonzaga, the world's patron saint of youth, and a place where Henry Dunant created the Red Cross after the battle of Solferino in 1859: the heart is Piazza Dallo, with the Basilica of St. Louis, the Aloisian Museum, the International Museum of the Red Cross and the Bondoni Pastorio Museum.

The village of the Upper Seriana Valley with a history of over 3,000 years: in Castello the archaeological park and Antiquarium Parra Oppidum degli Orobi tells the town mentioned by Plinio; in the historical center the parish church of San Pietro with a altarpiece of Giovan Battista Moroni, on Mount Cüsen the sanctuary of the Holy Trinity and, above the village, the paths towards Monte Alino and Mount Vaccaro.

Jump of about 32 meters formed by the stream Noaschetta, right above the center of the village. A signposted and easy path starts from the parish church and in about 15 minutes passes behind the waterfall, under a cave, from where you can observe the jump from a privileged position. Accessible all year round.

Città dei Castelli Romani, the ancient Velitrae Volsca, with the Gothic Torre del Trivio in Piazza Cairoli, the Cathedral of San Clemente with the Diocesan Museum and the Town Hall that houses the Civic Museums with the famous sarcophagus of the labors of Hercules.

Built in the first decades of the first century AD and discovered in 1976 thanks to aerial photos: 107 meters by 84, for 12,000-14,000 spectators according to estimates, with the arena later lowered and a forum for notables; in part it is still under the modern houses and today it hosts shows and recreational activities.
Canoeing and trails on the large lake of Barigadu.
The key to reading Signia.

In Piazza Garibaldi, a few steps from the lake, there are several large plane trees, three of which with trunks of more than 4 meters circumference. They are the last survivors of Luino's historic row of plane trees, largely destroyed in recent decades for plant protection reasons.
A walled village that tells its centuries in the stones.
The waterfall on the side of Sardagna above the city, visible even from Piazza del Duomo and reachable by going up towards the hamlet.

Under the Caves of Catullo, overlooking the Fortress of Manerba: large slabs of polished white rock that descend into clear water. Partly free and partly with rental beds, free showers; you can reach it from a gate just before the entrance to the caves with a dirt road and steep descent among the olive trees. Dogs on leash, forbidden camping and fires.
The plan of the city engraved in slate.
The walled village was born from the ruins of Semifonte, razed to the ground by the Florentines in 1202, with the Hospital of the Pilgrims of the fourteenth century.
The hamlets of Bozzana, Bordiana, San Giacomo and Samoclevo have grown around ancient chapels, which preserve structures and altars from Gothic to Baroque.
Roman gate rebuilt around the middle of the 1st century A.D. along the Augustian walls of 33-32 B.C., decorated with pilasters and vegetable motifs.
Of very ancient origins: the excavations have found walls of at least three previous churches, visible under the transparent floor.

The Franciscan monastery was founded in 1610 and completed with the church of the Holy Trinity around 1632-33; between 1702 and 1706 the Milanese Giuseppe Quallio, with Corbellini, Mutoni and Reti, built the basilica of the Virgin of the Martyrs with octagonal dome, painted by Pietro Antonio and Gregorio Are. Below is the underground sanctuary dedicated to Saint Efisio and Saint Gregory the Great, with polychrome stucco statues; next to the oratory of St. Michael (1758-59), with dome decorated by Gregory the Are, and the cumbessias of the pilgrims. Free entrance.
Medieval village enclosed by ancient walls and crossed by narrow alleys, founded around the year 1000 by Farfen monks. The southern entrance is marked by the medieval tower.
The Gothic masterpiece of Piceno on the cliff.

City of the Sassi, dug into the rock on the side of Gravina and UNESCO heritage with the Park of the rock churches: the Sasso Barisano and the Sasso Caveoso around the Civita and the Cathedral, the frescoed rock churches, the Palombaro Lungo under Piazza Vittorio Veneto and, beyond the gravina, the Materan Murgia.

Around the castle there are medieval houses, including the so-called "Casa del Boia" (House of the Boya). In front of the castle the parish church of San Nicolò, documented since 1576; next door, near the ancient public oven, Santa Maria, quoted in 1514. Outside the village the oratory of San Rocco (documents of 1600), San Vito, perhaps the first church of the place (VI century), today the cemetery chapel, and San Defendente, between the end of the sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries, on the road to Belforte.
€12, reduced €8

The territory has 27 noble villas, built mainly from the nineteenth century, some of rich merchants. The Sughere Trail passes from the village of Crocetta next to Villa Minutoli Tergimi, built on the remains of a Longobard period tower, then touches Villa Baldini, with an Italian garden, where Paulina Bonaparte lived for a short time, and Villa Hernandez; with Mount Aquilata on the left, a road in pebbles leads to the church of San Frediano and the village of Compignano.

Radura surrounded by birch trees on the watershed between Po and Varaita, about an hour's walk on paths suitable for mountain biking, with a green stone stone cippo of Monviso located in 1992 by the Martiniana Alps; not far from a viewpoint on the Monviso massif.
The civic heart of Bologna since the thirteenth century: San Petronio, Palazzo d'Accursio, Palazzo del Podestà and, next to it, the Neptune of Giambologna.
The great swamp of the Mincio among reeds, water lilies and lotus flowers.
Built in 1496 for Sebastiano Ferrero when he became lord of the manor.

Baroque church built in 1602; the main point of interest is the high altar, completed in 1725. The bell tower dates back to 1828-32, the baptismal font of 1699 and the holy waterworks of 1513; the nineteenth-century organ is of the Collino brothers. He preserves paintings by Lorenzo Delleani, Barbavara, Marietti and Morgari. He put on Saturdays and preaching at 5:30 p.m., Sundays and holidays at 10:30 p.m.
Monumental complex arose after the apparition of the Virgin of 1536, with an artistic heritage documented in the archives; next to the museum of the sanctuary.
Sienese art in a former convent.
The cathedral that guards the Shroud, the cloth in which according to tradition the body of Jesus was wrapped; the dome of the chapel is the work of Guarini.

The village of mint is named after Cardinal Guglielmo Massaja, a missionary in Ethiopia; it houses the parish church of Saints Peter and George attributed to Benedict Alfieri, the remains of the church with double apse of San Martino di Castelvero and, in the town hall, a didactic workshop dedicated to Monferrato and Cardinal.
The fortress basilica seen from the top of the walls.
The seaside square designed by Enrico Salvais in 1925, with a chessboard of 8,700 m2 of over 34,000 black and white tiles, 4,000 balustrade columns and the gazebo for the rebuilt orchestra.
The palace overlooking Piazza Vecchia, under whose porticos you pass to reach Piazza Duomo.
An ancient icebox became a place of exhibitions.
The fortified entrance door of the village.
The history of the Comino Valley in five rooms.
The city's art gallery.
Iron, nativity scenes and great photography in a convent.
The tick hidden under the village.
Let's Marche signals historic center, monuments and museums only partially open
The mosaics of the villa that perhaps gave the name to the city.
The Alpine station at the foot of the glaciers.
The stone that tells the birth of the fortress.

The Segat, in the former sawmill of Meida, tells woodcutters, segantini and carpenters and the main tree species, with the collection \Bepo and Jan Cherlo Â of a family of carpenters of Moena for four generations. The Malghier, in the Mèlga cheese factory in Fassa, is dedicated to butter and cheese, with the production rooms visible and the dealer.

Gerrei's country known for the archaeological park of Pranu Muteddu, the Sardinian stonehenge with about sixty menhirs among the corkshops; on the plateau above the village the monotorre nuraghe of Goni looks at Lake Mulargia.
The monastery of Saint Benedict.
Upland meadows and starry skies.
Small village on a rocky spur about 800 meters on the slopes of San Vicino; close, what remains of the Benedictine abbey of Valfucina of the 11th century.
Built in 1108 and modified in 1656; the first plant remains the three apses.

Comune Padovano sul Bacchiglione at the foot of the Euganean Hills, with the Castle of San Martino della Vaneza, whose tower dates back to the 11th century and which houses the river museum, and the Oratory of the Holy Cross, a small church of Lombard origin already documented in 874.
The masterpiece of the Ligurian Renaissance fortification.
The village turns on foot uphill.
An almost unknown baroque palace.

Municipality of the Bergamo plain whose parish church of San Nicolò preserves paintings of Palma il Giovane, Sante Peranda and Francesco Cavagna and a wooden choir of Giuseppe Caniana; the territory is part of the Agricultural Park of Rio Morla and the Rogge.

Natural lake at about 845 meters born about 4,000 years ago from a great landslide that cleared the valley: over 3 km2 and more than 120 meters deep, between the Brenta Dolomites and the massif Gazza-Paganella; on the bottom was found an ancient forest. On the north shore the beach with meadows and fine gravel beaches, boat rental, pedal boats, canoes and SUP; in summer you swim. From the north arm an easy path of about 20 minutes leads to the pond of Bior.
The park offers hiking trails and includes the promontory of the villa of Tiberio; the cliffs of Punta Cetarola, which close the bay south, are protected by a Blue Oasis of the WWF.

In the Old Rion, with a triangular plan with a single surviving polygonal tower, probably of Norman origin; in the Swabian age was Domus Imperialis and in 1263 hosted Elena of Epirus and the court of Manfredi. Conquered by the Angioins in 1268, it passed among many feudal families until 1808, when the State sold it to the Marquis Gaetano Gallerano. Restored by privates, today it houses a restaurant; from the square with colonnade you can see the woods of Straface and the Dolcedorme Serra.

Archaeological collection in the church of Santa Maria Assunta, started in 1958 by Father Michele Jacobelli and acquired by the Municipality in 1978: fossils, blocks of the walls of the pre-Roman city of Cominium and former Roman anatomical vote (III-I century BC) from the votive crest of Pescarola; also exhibits musical instruments, agricultural tools and popular costumes from various parts of the world.

On the Fortress, castle of the Tre-Quattrocento restored in Gothic style and revisited in the nineteenth century, with a juvarrian staircase and a large park. There lived the Countess of Castiglione, who married Count Francesco Verasis Asinari of Costigliole very young; today hosts ICIF, Italian cooking school for foreigners, and the Consortium Barbera d'Asti and Vini del Monferrato. Visitable in some periods, closed from November to March.

Cittadina dell'alto Chienti shaped by Cardinal Evangelista Pallotta, with the Pallotta castle (restored after the earthquake 2016), the town hall with the Paradise Room by Simone De Magistris, the Collegiate Church of San Martino, the castles of Vestignano and Cross and the lake of Pievefavera.

Woods, charcoals and panoramas in the Apennines of Ponzone.

A village about 650 meters on the slopes of Mount Sellaro, about twenty kilometers from the Ionian, built near the Greek settlement of Arponion and dominated by the remains of a medieval castle; the church of St. Peter holds valuable paintings. It is the City of Bread and Slow Food garrison, with a feast dedicated to bakery.
Built on a source that, according to the source, once served a mosque for the ablutions prescribed by the Koran.

The neoclassical theatre on Piazza del Popolo, indicated as a remarkable example of neoclassical art, is named after Victoria Colonna, founder of the city.

The town of the Gargano National Park between the lakes of Lesina and Varano, with the historic center of Terravecchia gathered around the castle and the historical ethnographic museum in Palazzo Fioritto; in the territory the Dolina Pozzatina, the largest karst phenomenon of Puglia, the Grotto dell'Angelo on Mount of Helium and the sixteenth-century Torre Mileto on the coast.

Built in 1486 by the Augustinians after the apparition of the Virgin (1476, according to tradition) to a silent shepherd who regained his voice, preserves late-fourth-century ogival arches, baroque enlargements and a neoclassical façade of 1897. On the high altar the wooden statue of Our Lady, covered for centuries by a plate of copper painted sliding; inside a wooden Crucifix of about 1600, a canvas of Augustine Ratti of 1750, a confessional of the seventeenth century and the fresco of the miracle of G. Quinzio. In the former convent, the restored cloister and the refectory with the Last sixteenth-century dinner frescoed in front of St. Augustine.
A medieval abbey re-emerged in the valley of the Trigno.
Open only from 20 June to 30 September, Saturday and Sunday 15:30-18:30 (Ecomuseo del Casentino)

Built in 1490 thanks to a donation by Countess Paola Gonzaga, wife of Count Leonardo di Gorizia; the first-baroque high altar (about 1600) is adorned with a late-Gothic relief with the Adoration of the Magi by Michael Parth (about 1520). Open from early April to early October, 8-19.

15 km of route between green hills, with a series of walkways that cross several times the Progno d'Illasi between the right and the left bank; connect Cogollo di Tregnago (starting in Marani) with the historic village of Cimbro di Giazza and ends in the forest of Giazza, running gently at the foot of the mountains.
A Savoy residence.

Hill country overlooking the lower valley of the Agri and surrounded by clay gullies of the Regional Reserve, the largest of the Basilicata; in the center the Mother Church of Santa Maria d'Episcopio, the Clock Gate and the Terravecchia district.

In the convent founded in 1441 by Blessed Margherita di Savoia, the baroque church with an elliptical plan by Bernardo Vittone and the Archaeological Civic Museum and Natural Sciences . Federico Eusebio is held in 21 rooms; in the courtyard there is the White Truffle Fair.
A trip to the cosmos next to the observatory.
The fortified village in Val Taro, capital for almost four centuries of the small state of the Landi, with stone roads, palaces and tower houses.

Born in the Archduke's Park in 1873 by Archduke Albert of Austria, it is a botanical garden with more than 200 species of trees and shrubs from all over the world, from monumental conifers to Mediterranean plants, favored by the mild climate of Garda; managed by the Trento Natural Science Museum, it has a flat path with information panels.

On the site of a first monastic complex of the 5th century a Romanesque church arose in the 11th century; the cloister, behind the church of San Michele, and the bell tower dates back to the 12th century, with the cloister of Lanfranco da Ligurno. The colonnade has capitals of different styles; national monument since 1911, today houses modern art exhibitions.
The ancient Via Valeriana, from Piazza Cavour, among the noble residences; Palazzo Sertoli hides a ballroom frescoed by Giovan Antonio Torricelli.

The village overlooks the gulf with small ports always animated and a port among the largest on the island for number of fishing boats; the Church of Maria Santissima del Lume was built on the initiative of a group of fishermen.

Municipality of Karst isontino that houses the military shrine of Redipuglia, inaugurated in 1938 on the slopes of Mount Six Busi with the remains of over one hundred thousand Italian soldiers of the Great War, the Shrine museum and the Austro-Hungarian cemetery with 14,550 fallen.
Built between 1641 and 1647 around a Majesty who remembered a miracle.

Municipality of Monti Sicani with the Teatro Andromeda, work of the sculptor-pastor Lorenzo Reina, the eighteenth-century Hermitage of Santa Rosalia next to the cave of the saint, starting point of the Itinerarium Rosaliae, and part of the reserve of Monte Cammarata.
Recent reconstructions reported by Visit Cuneese.

Medieval church with three aisles at the cemetery, with frescoes on the inner walls and under the vault; next door stands the building of the bishop's summer residence.

The castle was built around the ninth century on the hill Sant'Angelo by the lords of Sonnino; it remains the high cylindrical tower of four floors that dominates the maze of alleys.

Opened in 1998 in the building that since 1907 hosted the first large knife factory in Maniago, documents the processing of steel in the factories of the area and its technological evolution, rebuilding the working environments and exhibiting past and present productions. It also houses the wood and iron section of the Provincial Museum of Rural Life Diogene Penzi. Free with FVGcard.

Church dedicated to the patron Saint Foca, a soldier born in Antioch and converted to Christianity, celebrated on 5 March and the second Sunday of August; according to the Municipality stands on the site of the castle of Pendina.

The semicircular port was rebuilt on a Roman plant designed by Antonio Winspeare and Francesco Carpi: works since 1772, operating in April 1779 with the ignition of the lantern on the pier. The neoclassical church of the SS. Trinity, with circular plan with dome, was built since 1775 in three years. At the end of the harbour basin there is a mitreum with zodiacal decorations of the III-IV century AD.
Frescoes and a nice organ in the village of San Rocco.
Two ethnographic museums: Casa Satta reconstructs environments as they were at the beginning of the twentieth century, Casa Mereu shows the furnishings of a noble residence.

Arbus fraction about 10 km from the village, in the valley of Is Animas that descends towards Piscinas, now a ruined village and desert. The silver, lead and zinc mines were active from 1855 to 1968, with the greatest development under British society Pertusola and Lord Thomas Brassey; seven villages with 900 rooms housed up to 2,500 people. The granite direction of the castle remains, called \"castle" (1870, Neo-Medieval style), the church of Santa Barbara (1916) and the villas Wright and Ginestra.

Country on the slopes of Monte Amiata: the Baroque church of the Opera with the paintings of the Nasini, the sixteenth-century Palazzo Nerucci with civic museum and art collection, the Piazza degli Verdi with the loggia, the Palio of 8 September in Piazza Garibaldi and, in Montenero d'Orcia, the museum of vine and wine.
Typical stone building with a square view by the stonemasons, where to deepen the machining of cheese of the Magredi.

The Sunesi church of the Devil is mentioned as a parish head already in the 11th century and mentioned in a bull of Innocent II of 1132; the surviving masonry, in pebbles and bricks with spine strokes of fish and hanging arches on the south side, is attributed to the first half of the 11th century. In 1843 the facade and choir were demolished and the orientation changed. In the choir there is the tomb with the relics of San Genesio; above the tomb of the Della Porta, an ancient fresco with Madonna enthroned, San Genesio and the Archangel Michael, while the vault of the nave is frescoed in the eighteenth century. Roman finds were found in the area, today at the Broletto di Novara.
Wooden auditorium designed by Renzo Piano in front of the Spanish Fort, created after the earthquake for concerts, conferences and shows.

Statue of the Madonna degli Alpini 4.20 meters high, laid on May 19, 1971 at 911 meters on the mountain overlooking the village (the card calls it both Pizzo Guazza and Corno Falò); on the first Sunday of September the alpine celebrates Mass. On the same summit on May 1st, the "Mas" was replanted, the fir tree brought to the town on April 25th, which on the evening of June 1st became the opening bonfire of the Feast of the Apparition.
Mantua art of the twentieth century inside a tower of Gonzaga.

One of the largest squares in Europe, the foyer of the Arena with the "listòn," the long sidewalk of bars and restaurants, the gardens, the seventeenth-century Palace of the Gran Guardia and Palazzo Barbieri.
The National Museum on the History of Jews in Italy, in the former prison of Via Piangipane.

It is annexed to the Capuchin monastery (1617-1619), has on the high altar the Queen of the Angels of Salerno (1630), a Blessed Bernard from Corleone by Vincenzo Manno, a Via Crucis of 14 wooden tablets of the eighteenth century and a sundial on the facade.
It exhibits the excavations of the Rock, including the treasure of Scarlino.

Special Conservation Area of 570 hectares with arid prairies and over 35 species of wild orchids; the ridge walk from the village offers wide views of Prenestini and the limestone walls at 1218 meters are a historic site of climbing in Lazio.

Archaeological area of the ancient Roman post station of Baccano along the via Cassia, one of the rare tasks identified with certainty and widely explored; in the same place the remains of the Granai Chigi.
A medieval water forge as it was.

The 121-metre-high brick dome of Alessandro Antonelli, among the most daring brick buildings in the world, climbs with a guided tour up to 100 meters, and up to the Hall of the Compasso also in a wheelchair.
The reborn cathedral after the earthquake.

The castle, part of Ariano County, rises on the remains of a Sannite fortification in polygonal walls; it lived there the Queen Margaret of Durazzo with her children, including the future King Ladislao, who in 1381 renewed the statutes of the country.

The political and religious heart of the city, with the Cathedral of San Zeno, the Baptistery, the Palace of Bishops, the Town Hall, the Palace of Pretorio and the Tower of Catilina; in July it hosts Pistoia Blues.

Built towards the end of the fifteenth century by Bonifacio or Rodolfo d'Avise: three-storey building with square tower, the first on the left entering the village.
An open-air family stop.

Parish Museum inaugurated in 1979 above the sacristy of Santa Maria di Piazza, in the ancient oratory of Our Lady of Mercy in 1420, with furnishings, statues and objects of the churches and confraternities of Mogliano. The altarpiece of Lorenzo Lotto with Our Lady in glory and Saints John the Baptist, Antonio da Padova, Maria Maddalena and Giuseppe (oil on canvas, 330 x 215 cm), commissioned in 1547 by Mayor Jacomo Boninfante for 130 gold shields and delivered in 1548 by the pupil During Nobili.

About 8 hectares in the plain at the foot of Mount Cairo, one of the largest Roman areas of southern Lazio, largely still to be dug. Volscian settlement of the V-IV century B.C., quoted by Livio in 211 B.C. for the passage of Hannibal, became a colony under the Second Triumvirate and declined with the Longobards in the sixth century; there was born Juvenal. You can see Porta Capuana, the best preserved monument, the remains of the theatre and the Capitolium and the Vecciane Thermal Baths, with an inscription of about 9 meters in the frigidarium; the amphitheatre was largely destroyed in 1960-61 by the works of the Autostrada del Sole.

Ancient bishopric of Trento who, with the castles of Corno and Noarna, watched the streets towards the lake of Cei; conquered by the Castelbarco in the middle of the thirteenth century, in 1456 passed to the counts Lodron, who transformed it into a noble residence. Today it belongs to the Miorandi family; in August it hosts Castelfolk.

In the old town, in a tower with terrace on the Sagittarius Valley and on the lake of San Domenico: objects of peasant art, models of a mill and a gulchiera built by the miller Domenico Grossi and wool fabrics of the traditional male dress of Villalago and Scanno; slides of landscapes and daily life are projected. According to the MiC is open from Monday to Saturday, 15.30-18.30.

The birthplace of Pope Pius V (Antonio Ghislieri, 1504-1572), the only Piedmontese pontiff, who built the Dominican complex of Santa Croce in 1566 with works by Giorgio Vasari and today the seat of a museum; in the center remain his birthplace and the parish of Saints Peter and Pantaleone.
The eight mills.
A small mystery of Raphael in a private house.
The castle on the bay.
The sixteenth-century villa bought in 1906 by Enrico Caruso, with the park of the Tribolo and the museum with its room and its caricatures.
Borgo dell'interra di Bordighera, Orange Flag, with the historic center accessible only on foot or with the Bee, the Baroque church of San Lorenzo and the Loggia dell'Aria.

Church of the Capuchin complex dedicated to San Michele Arcangelo, consecrated on 15 October 1662 by the bishop of Albenga; facade with a large semicircular window, reached by a cobbled climb. The interior with a single nave with two side chapels contrasts the white walls with the dark wood of altars and coverings; it preserves the statue of the Immaculate on the altar and a French Via Crucis in sepiolite.

Medieval village in the hills on the slopes of Mount Amiata, closed by the walls, land of oil PDO: the church of San Bartolomeo with the Sienese polyptych, the Oratory of San Rocco with the frescoes of Girolamo di Domenico, the sanctuary of Our Lady of Charity, the Museum of Oil with the olive tree in the Cisternone and, two kilometers away, the Garden of Daniel Spoerri.
Along the southern side of the Roman walls, the best preserved Roman tower.

Ancient parish church which became collegiate in 1317 and rebuilt in baroque forms in 1668, with a single nave with a coffered ceiling: it preserves a Last Supper by the Flemish Denijs Calvaert (1611) and the relic of Santa Spina, in a silver reliquary since 1635, exposed on Angel Monday and the penultimate Sunday of August, when Carlo Fortebracci's donation is recalled.
The secret cell discovered in 1947.

Mediterranean maquis garden with over a thousand species of Mediterranean and exotic plants, some at risk of extinction, and view over the entire gulf. On the plateau called "Chianu d'a Batteria" there are four artillery stations.

Parish until 1676, in Lombard Romanesque style with a single nave, with traces of the building of the Mille at the base of the bell tower; until 1810 the Orsaresi buried there. Inside stuccoes and frescoes of the eighteenth century recently restored. It rises in the castle's shelter.
Built in 1054, it dominates the old town and preserves towers and crenellated walls of its defensive past.
The Messinese Renaissance in a village.
Walking in the Roman city of Giovenale.

Walls born in the 12th century and redesigned in 1574-1593 by Baldassarre Lanci for Francesco I de' Medici: an almost perfect hexagon of about 3 km with five bastions and a citadel, today a green walk with the Old and Corsican gates.
Covered market of the fifties with local products such as sardenaira, pesto and oil.

The beaches of the sea of Rome with historic establishments, rationalist architecture and liberty, skate park and the Fishermen's Borghetto with the procession of the Stella Maris and the festival of the telline.

The square occupies the site of the Support, the basin with octagonal plan built in 1432 by Niccolò III d'Este on the Naviglio, with saracinesche that maintained constant water level: according to VisitModena the first in Italy, taken from Leonardo in Milan about fifty years later; it was underground after the detour of the channel at the beginning of the twentieth century. The mill remains, of nineteenth-century appearance but of more ancient origins: with sixteen millstones it was the largest in the region, it also operated a millstone, a shiner for rice, a public sawmill and then the dynamo that illuminated the country; closed in the twenties.

Rocca probably Longobard, destroyed by the Franks in 590 and rebuilt, took its name from the Scaligeri who held it from 1277 to 1387; then passed to Visconti, Venice and Austria and was declared National Monument on August 22, 1902. The pentagonal mast is 31 meters high (70 meters on the lake) and the viewpoint is 24 meters on the water; it houses the Museum of Natural History of Baldo and Garda (multimedia route), the Hall of Galee on the navigation and transport of Venetian ships by land in the fifteenth century, and the Goethe Hall in the former Austrian powder keg, with bust of the poet in the garden. In summer the lawn of the Lacaòr serves as an outdoor theatre.
Following the saint of Lemon.

Founded in 1960 and since 1999 in the Palazzo Sticchi-Ruberti, noble residence of the early twentieth century that with the Municipal Library forms the cultural complex L'Alca; it is the only museum of the Mezzogiorno dedicated to the reconstruction of the prehistory of Salento, with sections of geology and paleontology, paleolithic and prehistoric art, Neolithic and age of metals, ethnography with African art objects. Touring hours: Mon-Fri 9-13 and 16-18:30, Sat-dom 16-18:30.
The loggia on the vineyards.
The city of silk.
The childhood of the "Swan of Catania."

Birthplace of the painter, behind the Duomo, identified thanks to documents of 1516-1578 and restored with the patronage of Camillo Vazzoler: during the works ceramic fragments of the recent Bronze Age (XIV-XIII century B.C.) and an inscription of 1492 emerged. It houses reproductions of the works of Cima, a small archaeological museum and the Cima Foundation; in front of the entrance a bronze statue of the painter inaugurated in 2024. Open Saturday and Sunday afternoon.

Church of Romanesque-Gothic origin on a rocky hill above the stream, linked to the monks of San Teofredo di Le Puy and then to the priory of Bersezio; remain a Gothic portal, a Romanesque apsidiola and a sailing bell tower incorporated in the tower, while the date April 2, 1680 on the apse indicates the probable reconstruction, on the model of Santa Maria a Cuneo by Giovenale Boetto.

A show of Sardinian flavors.
Nature and views of the Lucane Dolomites.
A castle-calendar with the lives of the nobles intact.

An irregular double-plan castle with a polygonal main façade reached by a large stone ramp; the cobbled courtyard leads to a three-arched loggia with Ghibelline blackbirds on the noble floor. Some scholars date to the year 1000 the western tower with a polygonal sloping base; the family De Sterlich-Aliprandi, present from the XV-XVI century, owned it until the mid-Twentieth century, when the building had already lost its military function. With the houses-walls, it delimits a ring space around the hill; the restoration was completed in 1993 and many rooms conserve vaults, arches and stone pillars.
The first suspended bridge in Italian iron, on the Appia.

Church of the Arbëreshë community where the Greek-Byzantine rite is celebrated, especially on 5 and 6 January and on Easter holidays; it preserves an iconostasis and frescoes of the vault in false mosaic.

Built on the medieval fortifications guarding the Panaro: the current structure is from 1402, designed by Bartolino da Novara, enlarged in 1425-30 with Giovanni da Siena; extensive eagles, courtyard with triple loggia on Gothic pillars and frescoes of the fifteenth century. With the 2012 earthquake the tower collapsed and the castle was badly damaged.
12th century bastion at the southern end of the ancient fortifications, overlooking the Sibillini Mountains, Mount Conero and the Adriatic; at Christmas there is the living Nativity scene.
Stairs to the castle.
In restoration since 2011: for now only the Courtyard of Honor is used
The great fortress built by Emperor Frederick II as a fortified residence for its garrisons.

Established in 1985 as an exhibition of traditional terracotta, it has been enriched with donations and purchases of majolica and documents the country's long ceramic tradition with collections from prehistory to contemporary age; since 2010 it hosts the entire collection of terracotta whistles donated by the Milanese collector Mario Briosi. It shares the premises with the Municipal Library, which has a section of studies on ceramics. Hours indicated by MiC: Monday-Saturday 8:30-13:30 and 15:00-20:00, Sunday closed.
It tells the story of the feudal and rural aristocracy of the ancient curatory of Parte Montis through works of art, weapons, customs, documents and ancient books.
From the 18th century, an example of Piedmontese baroque.

The city of Sforza in the Ticino Park: Ducal Square wanted by Ludovico il Moro and closed by the Duomo façade, the Sforzesco Castle with the Tower of Bramante and museums ranging from the ancient Lomellina to the shoes.

Renaissance urban plant with medieval walls and four doors, stone portals of the Seven-nineteenth century, Palazzo Pandiscia (formerly Cappucci house, residence of San Gerardo), a Renaissance loggia and a Roman arch. Via Tagliata is the oldest street in the country: here in 212 BC the Roman proconsul Gneo Fulvio Centumalo was camped. In Piazza De Sanctis the bust of Francesco De Sanctis.

The lake, formed by the rivers Tirso, Taloro and Tino and used to produce electricity, is dominated by the hill of S'Urbale; around the village springs and woods can be walked, inhabited by deer, deer, mouflons and foxes, under the granite slopes of Sa Marghine.
The ruins-symbol of Ribera, overlooking the Verdura valley.
Walk among oleanders, orange trees and roses, with views of the island of Garda and, in winter, on the snow-covered Monte Baldo.
A monastery-refuge in the woods.
A 17th century convent with period furnishings.

A walk of 62.7 km in three stages between Paola and Paterno Calabro, crossed several times by the saint between the two convents; the last stop from San Fili climbs to the beech forest of Bosco Luta, crosses the coastal ridge and descends on Paola. Upon arrival the pilgrims receive the Witnessium.
Damaged by the 2012 earthquake, in restoration: visitable only from the outside
The museum in a 15th-century convent dedicated to the founder, Abbot Luigi Bailo, with art collections and a gallery added in 1938.

private residence, visible only from outside

In the former seventeenth-century convent of the Capuchins, next to the church of San Francesco, it tells the geology of Sardinia and Marmilla, from the formation of the Mediterranean to the evolution of Monte Arci, an ancient volcano today regional park. It exhibits thousands of minerals and about 1,800 fossils, including fossil fish, colored diaspris, hydrothermal minerals such as quartz, limedonia, fluorite and large crystals of calcite, dioramas on the activity of the volcano and a room with fluorescent minerals. The collections are born from the cataloguing work of Vincenzo Incani.

Town of the high But valley towards the Passo di Monte Croce Carnico: the Torre Moscarda of the thirteenth century with museum and botanical garden, in Timau the museum and the Ossario temple of the Great War and, in summer, the lake Avostanis above Malga Pramosio.

The church of San Giacomo, rebuilt in the sixteenth century, houses with the sacristy and the House of the Regency a small museum of sacred art: paintings of Moncalvo and his daughter Orsola Caccia, goldsmiths and antique fabrics and the work "I Canonici di Lu" by Pietro Francesco Guala.
The large market square and the collegiate church of 1257 with the Majesty of the Master of Figline, the Saint Joseph of Andrea della Robbia and the Martyrdom of Saint Lorenzo del Cigoli.
The frescoes outside the door.
On the summit of the same name, over 1,000 meters, it houses an effigy of the Madonna considered miraculous, carved by Domenico Gagini in 1471.
The colorful village suspended on the lake.

The village preserves the typical architecture with stone houses, narrow and ups and downs and wooden gates, and the structures of the small medieval centers: walls of surroundings, urban doors, a tower, the square and the main church.

Opened in 1991 to preserve the tradition of straw hat, in the former palace of Piazza Roma, documents all the phases of processing, from the collection to the sale to the pressing that gives the final shape, with photographs, panels and original machinery. The section "Marche," so much of hat "details" has hats reinterpreted by regional excellences in glass, ceramics and wood.
Ascent normally paid (indicated €5 full / €3 reduced from secondary source). Now suspend.

Designed in 1723 by 23-year-old Francesco Maria Preti on the model of the Redeemer of Palladio, open to cult unfinished in 1746, with facade of 1892-93 by Pio Finazzi. In the Costanzo chapel, on the right of the presbytery, the Pala di Giorgione, sacred conversation commissioned by the leader Tuzio Costanzo after the death of his son Matthew (1499). In the Duomo works by Ponchini, Palma il Giovane, Paolo Piazza and Beccaruzzi; in the sacristy seven fragments of frescoes by Veronese from the demolished Villa Soranzo of Treville and paintings by Jacopo Bassano. Open mon-sab morning and afternoon (15-17.45), Sunday only afternoon; sacristy on request.
The villa of the Sartorio.
The frescoed crypt of the thirteenth century.
The ancient village with narrow streets between the old stone houses.
The historical beach of the Gradesi.
The symbolic tower of the village.
Country of Val Cenischia at the foot of Moncenisio, seat of the Benedictine abbey founded in 726, lighthouse of the Carolingian culture along the Via Francigena.

The most beautiful row of cypress trees in Lombardy, in the area of the cemetery on the southern shore of the gulf, is defined: the 133 largest specimens, close to the lake, exceed the 25 meters of height and some trunks over 4 meters of circumference.

The house where Pavese was born on 9 September 1908 was the summer residence of the parents; sold in 1916 after the death of his father, it does not preserve original furnishings and is private property. Behind it is the hill of Gaminella, opposite that of Salto, and from the house you can see Moncucco, the hill of poetry "I mari del Sud" . It is only seen from the outside, alone or with the guided tour of the Foundation.
The Piazza delle Catene, of the Two-Three hundred, with the cathedral, the nineteenth-century Town Hall and the monument to Leopold II of Lorraine called Canapone, signed by Luigi Magi in 1846.
Under the cathedral, the Christian origins.
The theater season in Vicenza.
The Antrodoco mistrà.

Large artificial lake created from the fifties of the twentieth century with a dam on the river Ambiesta, used for hydropower: bathing is not allowed, but you take bike walks and excursions on the paths along the banks and trout fishing. From Tolmezzo take the provincial road 1 towards Sella Chianzutan; for the best panoramic point you leave the provincial road at Chiaicis via Ambiesta, and a road bridge crosses the lake. Nearby, the abandoned village of Pusea can be reached only on foot or by bike.

Pineta publishes near the center, overlooking the northern promenade, acquired by the Municipality in the late 1970s: benches, a dry tub designed by the painter Luigi Celommi, play area and free fitness area. It bears the name of Sigismondo Savini, whose villa rises in front.

In the ancient church of Guardia, then atelier of the painter, sculptor and poet Cyril Grott, born in the village: collection-exhibition of his paintings and sculptures, with the public section on the ground floor.

Built in the fifteenth century on a rocky spur overlooking the main square, it is an example of extensive military architecture with trapezoidal walls and truncated corner towers; on top there is a hanging garden with conifers. The earthquake of 1920 left little of its original structure; inside you can see the base of the bell tower of the Romanesque church of San Sisto and stretches of medieval walls emerged from the excavations, and at the feet there is the stone fountain called \"pilon" .
A forest in town.

The fourteenth-century church of the historic centre, already mentioned in the 13th century in the Ratio Decimarum; it contains two frescoes from the fourteenth century of the Orvieto school, a saint's waterworks from 1680 and, in the sacristy, a fifteenth-century cross.

In the western sacred area of the Gaggera, it was one of the first places of worship of the colony, with a first sacellus of the end of the VII century BC and monumental propylenes of the middle of the V; next, the shrines of Zeus Meilichios and Ecate and the sacellus of Hera Matronale. Thousands of votive statues have been found here.

Founded in 1142 by Blessed Bishop Hartmann, it is still an active monastery of Augustinian Canons; in 1742 it was the largest in Tyrol and in the Middle Ages it hosted a school of copyists and choral chanting. The church of the Assumption, Romanesque, was transformed into baroque forms; to see the frescoed Gothic cloister, the courtyard well with the wonders of the world, the roundabout Castel dell'Angelo (a former hospice and defence), the rococo library, the gallery with medieval paintings by Michael and Friedrich Pacher and Marx Reichlich, the wall of the Turks, the mill and the cellar, where the abbey still produces its wines (Sylvaner, Müller-Thurgau, Kerner). Free tours from Monday to Saturday 10-17, closed Sunday and Catholic holidays.

A single nave church in the homonymous hamlet, with paintings and decorations by Musso (1912) revived by prof. Cold in 1977, side porch, large churchyard and bell tower of 20.50 m built by the foreman Eugenio Torchio.
Indicated €8 whole, €2 reduced (Ministry, 2024); in MyFE Card

Founded at the beginning of the 2000s by Simone Quetti, a former pupil of the Pavoni printing school in Brescia, he tells the evolution of printing with machines still working that can be tried: presses of the nineteenth century, a linotype, flat-cylinder machines and a plate "Heidelberg"; with the guide you learn the traditional typographical techniques. Guaranteed opening by reservation (tel. 346 8315120, museodellastampa.artogne@gmail.com).
The first cathedral in the rock.

On the north-western coast of Caprera, golden sand and fine, the seabed gradually descends with natural pools among the rocks, suitable for families; Garibaldi moored the boats there and the pier is still visible.
Romanesque church of the 12th century, about 2 km from the village on the hilly ridge to the right of the river Versa.
Third Sunday of the month.

To the north of Vaste, the excavations brought to light a early Christian basilica built on a martyrion of the fifth century, surrounded by a vast necropolis with tombs of various eras; near is the crypt of Saints Stefani.
Inside the Biodiversity Park, outdoor works by Dennis Oppenheim, Tony Cragg, Jan Fabre, Mimmo Paladino, Antony Gormley, Wim Dlavoye, Marc Quinn and Stephan Balkenhol.
The balcony surrounding the houses of the center: from via Nardelli the view of the Itria Valley, with trulli (the housedde) and masserie, is particularly suggestive at sunset.

Angular tower of the medieval wall curtain, to the right of the turret gate: it was used as a prison and then incorporated as a staircase in the old school building; today it is isolated next to the school building.
The tower of the coat of arms of Lamezia.
Automes to operate with your own hands in a 9th century castle.

Opened on November 21, 1998 in the engine room of the nineteenth-century hydrovora of Amolara, on the outskirts of Adria, in the area of one of the richest Etruscan necropolis beyond Po: it tells the management of the waters in Polesine from prehistory to today and preserves the two centrifugal pumps that pushed towards the sea the excess waters of the Lower Old Country. The name comes from an ancient incision at the entrance. Next to it, the Hostel Amolara organizes excursions by bike and on foot.

The center is known for the arched houses and the typical Carnic houses of the patriarchal period; in front of Palazzo Unfer stands Palazzo Beorchia-Nigris, called Casa Grande, noble residence of the seventeenth century today seat of the town hall.
The nineteenth-century clock on the main square.
The church of the village and the feast of the Assumption of August.

The seventeenth-century fountain in Peperino, symbol of the victory of Lepanto; the "miracle" of the fountain that gives wine occurred the first time on October 4, 1925 and is repeated with the Festival of Grapes in early October, with the historical procession reminiscent of the return of Marcantonio Colonna da Lepanto.
In the workshops of the Citadel, the masters of the mache build figures over twenty meters high; the museum tells more than a century of Carnival with models, historical posters and installations.
Monumental fountain with the goddess Ceres, designed by Giuseppe Barone.
The country's sweet water.
The small medieval walled village of Vertine and the parish church of Spaltenna with a fifteenth-century crucifix, along the tour of Gaiole castles.
With its 2,587 meters it is the highest peak among those surrounding the Resia Valley.
€3, reduced €1,5
From wheat to pasta.
A rock contended by the captains of Ventura.
View of the Bidente valley.

An eighteenth-century shrine, then renovated, on the outskirts of the village on a rocky spike overlooking the valley of the river Molinu, a destination of pilgrimages. The festival, the most important of Thiesi, is held in the first days of September with mass, panegyric, costume procession, folk groups and knights of the Meilogu.
Rock with prehistoric engravings at 1600 m altitude, on the path to Colle Dondogna and Valle d'Aosta.
The noble palaces of the Iron Trade era.
Patti's typical sweet-salate.
Common: access to Cala Feola and natural pools regulated by seasonal reopening orders (ORD. 80, 83, 87, 109/2025)
We're going to her in the beech tree.
One of the five places managed by the Istituto Villa Adriana and Villa d'Este.
The Etruscan origins of Follonica iron.

In the park of Villa Landolina, in a building of Franco Minissi (1967-86): about 9,000 m2 and over 18,000 finds from prehistory to early Christian, including Venus Anadiomene and the sarcophagus of Adelphia.
A Maratta in a village church.

Bishop's castle of the 13th century on a hill above the city, once a summer residence of the bishops princes, then renovated and with walls renovated in wood, glass and steel; the main entrance is the south gate, once with drawbridge. Reinhold Messner has set you up MMM Ripa, an interactive museum on mountain peoples of Asia, Africa, South America and Europe (Sherpa, Inca, Tibetans, Mongols), with their cultures, religions and tourism, including objects, documentaries and meetings.
Church of the Immaculate Conception, called the New Church, founded in 1742.

Ecomuseum spread over the history and traditions of the Grana Valley linked to the cheese Castelmagno, based in San Pietro: the museum has an interactive set up on the processing and history of cheese, and in the country figures of straw in ancient clothes, the  "babaciu" , tell the mountain life between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. The route also includes mills, sawmills and hydroelectric power plants and the Extramuseum, a family ring of 4 km with ten totems (magic folder €10). Open Saturday and Sunday or by reservation.

Valico at 2472 meters reachable by car in summer; the hospice still welcomes the pilgrims of the Via Francigena and in front of a museum tells the history of the hill from ancient cults to the hospitality of today.

Cited in 1507, it probably dates back to a pre-Romanesque room of the twelfth century; gothized and enlarged around 1500, it has altars, pulpit and confessionals of the early nineteenth century in rural Baroque style. Of the original decoration remain the Coronation of Mary and the legend of St. Nicholas; on the ascent, a Way of the Cross with four newsstands and wooden figures of about 1700. It's on a panoramic hill outside the country.
A 15th century Franciscan complex with cloister and frescoes.
About forty mural paintings with scenes of rural life, nature, animals and characters of fairy tales, which make the capital the hamlet of bread and murals.

Municipality of the Brescian shore of Garda born in 1928 from the fusion of Toscolano and Maderno, between the Valley of the Cartiere, the Romanesque Basilica of Sant'Andrea, the Roman villa of the Nonii Arrii and the botanical garden Ghirardi, inside the Regional Park of Alto Garda Bresciano.
Eighteen pianos from the eighteenth century to the early twentieth century; the visit ends with a short live concert in costume.
The balcony on the Faraglioni.
In front of the city lies the wreck of the oil tanker Haven, one of the most famous diving points of Liguria; the site is challenging and must be faced with a local diving center.
Romanesque capitals in serene stone, one different from the other.

17th century church with Gothic portal; inside monolithic columns in local sandstone, marble altar, a large painting with San Bernardino da Siena and a plaque dedicated to Cardinal Taliani. From the church a path leads to a panoramic point and descends to Pineta Taliani.

16th century castle on the sea that contains the oldest Roman fortress and medieval village, on the site of Pyrgi, Etruscan port of Caere founded between the end VII and beginning VI century BC. The oldest part is the Saracen Tower (XI century); in the village the Chapel-Baptistery of the fifteenth century has frescoes attributed to the school of Antoniazzo Romano. It houses the Museum of the Sea, the Antiquarium of Pyrgi, the Museum of the Territory and the Castle Museum, and is open all year round.

Ancient parish church mentioned as early as 702, the current building was begun at the end of the XII century and completed in the façade at the beginning of the fourteenth century, and documents the passage from the Romanesque to the Gothic: façade in stone with pale and dark bands and brick with frieze of interwoven arches, crochet capitals, triumphal arch with acute sixth. The cappuccinos settled there in 1623; the restoration of 1971-1996 brought back to light truss and semicircular apse. Inside is a statue of the Redeemer Christ of the 13th century and a fragment of the Annunciation of the Boxilius brothers (about 1484).
The castle, 324 metres away, belonged to the city of Fano, which preserves high escarpment walls; in mid-July it hosts the historical reenactment of Trebbiatura.
The city of Malatesta: the Malatesta Library, the first civic library of Europe and UNESCO World Memory, the Fortress on Garampo Hill and Piazza del Popolo with the Masini Fountain.

The centre of Lessinia Verona, between the districts of Cimbrian origins and high pastures: the ethnographic museum "Lessinia": man and the environment "Tells alpine pastures, cheesemaking and ice production, with two open-air sections, the Coletto of 1729 and the Giassàra of Gritz; from the surroundings start trails towards the alpine pastures of Bocca di Selva and Mount Tomb.

Collection of tools, furnishings and objects of the peasant life belonged to Giovanni Filippini, expert in the agricultural traditions of the low Brescia, today owned by the Municipality; among the pieces stands out a nineteenth century sieve to separate the seeds. The museum is dedicated to Giovanni Bonsignori, priest, educator and agronomist. Visits by reservation.
The Trentino bubbles in their place of origin.
A youthful canvas of the Nuvolone in a Romanesque church became baroque.
Walk through churches and confetti.
About ten kilometers of fine golden sand; the stretch towards Muravera ends at the beach of Ginestre - Scoglio di Peppino, on the border between the two municipalities.
A walk to a piece of history of Italian skiing.
For those who love opera.
The square with the statue of the philosopher Bernardino Telesio, the Teatro Rendano and the Palazzo del Governo, next to the historic garden of the Villa Vecchia.
The symbol of Eagle and Forgiveness.
The collegiate with the Cavalier d'Arpino.
The square at the foot of the Bishop's Palace and the Madruzzian Tower erected to guard the city, the heart of Christmas markets and cultural fairs and events.
The finds of Lagaria.
16th century frescoes in a Palladian school villa.

On the hill of Civitella, in the shadow of a chestnut grove, the excavations have returned terrace walls, tiles, vases, an arched door and foundations of the fourth century BC, remains of a fortified center that controlled the valleys towards the sea of Velia. On the south side there is a well preserved door with narrow corridor and stone hinges of the wooden door; the central plateau, excavated only in part, has a paved space and a building perhaps of worship, as suggested by a votive deposit.
To see from Piazza di Porta Ravegnana even without climbing.
Frattesina, the great store of the Bronze Age.

Set up in the former elementary school of the village of Trinco, at the foot of the Kolovrat, it collects objects and tools of rural life from the end of the nineteenth century to the middle of the twentieth century: an anthropological and ethnographic journey on life in the Natisone Valleys, a Slovenian linguistic and cultural area of Friuli. It also preserves relics and photographs of the Great War. Visits only by appointment (Pro Loco Nediške Doline).

Hamlet at 72 meters, town mentioned already in the IX century, with the church of Santa Maria Assunta and the castle transformed in the eighteenth century into a noble residence; in the courtyard of the castle there is the small oratory of San Rocco and in Piazza Pignini the eighteenth-century civic tower of the clock.

Canal dug by the Visconti (Bernabò Visconti second in-Lombardy) during their domination, after 1348: it left from the Churches, passed through Lonato and returned after about 15 km; in the nineteenth century it was partly covered, especially in the center of Carpenedolo. It follows a cycle route between Montichiari and Carpenedolo.
15th-century fortress with square plan with cylindrical towers and large moat, also used as prison.

Example of spontaneous architecture of white houses, paved alleys to chianche, arches, hidden courtyards, balconies, stone masks and external ladders, in the four districts Bère Vecchie, Scheledd, u Pantène and L'Isule. The village was destroyed by the Goths and rebuilt around the abbey of the Basilian monks.
The medieval arch.
A complex nuraghe on the plateau.
Everything turns in an hour.
Roman mosaics under a country church.
The most photographed portrait of the lake.
Under the hill.

The parish was documented in 1438, dedicated to Saints Philip and James since 1518; the current three-nave church was built in the early nineteenth century and preserves paintings from the nearby former oratory of San Lorenzo, already home to the Confraternity of San Rocco and San Martino, which on the counterface has a Latin plaque of 1576.
The villa of Masonic friezes.
Lake 1911 and forest with the park visitor center, 5 km from the village.

Sanctuary of the patroness built between the XII and XIII century, at the end of a large square in the center of the village; the pronao was added for defensive purpose by Charles of Anjou. Once entirely frescoed, it preserves three pictorial phases (a Byzantine face of Our Lady, fragments of Basilian origin, profiles of monks and a Dormitio Virginis) and paintings by Gian Domenico Catalano. Under the floor, collapsed in the 1960s, a cemetery hypogeum with ten cells re-emerged. The patronal celebration of August 15 culminates in a great pyrotechnic race.
Church and monastery date back to 1453 and survived the earthquake of 1693; in the church a statue of a Gagini.

Locality at 1450 meters at the foot of the Corno Piccolo, the main ski resort of the Teramano: a quadriposto and a two-seater chairlift go up to 2000 meters to the Arapietra, with about 20 km of downhill slopes and a cross-country trail; in summer base for excursions on the Gran Sasso.
A panoramic ridge on the main plateaus of Abruzzo.
A walk among the wooden giants.
