A fortified nucleus (castrum) built around the Mille, it assumed in the last quarter of the fifteenth century the current quadrilateral plant with angular towers in Visconti-forzesco style; from 1412 the fief was of the Beccaria, and on January 30, 1573 the Marquis Agostino Litta bought it to transform it into a country villa. In 1680 the tower of the drawbridge became the entrance gate, where you can still see the seats of the locks; in the early eighteenth century the Long Channel was started, or Loggia delle Dame, which ends in the Mirabella tower with a view. Donato al Comune dai Robecchi, heirs of Litta, today houses a school, municipal services and the archaeological museum.
The green amphitheatre of Villa Borghese that every year hosts the CSIO, one of the best horse races in the world.

Born in the seventies from the collection of the masonous Andrea Tubino, technical Italsider, and named after him in 1993, he has over 4,000 pieces on several floors of the former Augustinian convent of Piazza Castello, built on a slope with two floors towards the square and four towards the valley: ethnographic and archaeological collections, figures of the nativity scene and mechanized crib, lamps, minerals and fossils, the chapel of the convent and the reconstruction of a blacksmith's forge. It tells of the period in which the valley lived of iron processing and hosts an international photographic exhibition with works by Gianni Berengo Gardin, Fulvio Roiter, Franco Fontana and others. Tel. 010 926210, 347 1496802.
Erected to celebrate the victory over the Salassi in 25 BC, almost 12 meters high, at one fornice, at the beginning of Via Sant'Anselmo.

It is located in the former FS station and in vintage freight wagons, with the Quasimodiano Museum, the Train-Museum and the Garden-Museum-A. Quasimodo: he holds documents, relics, writings, audiovisual materials and the Milanese study of the poet, Nobel Prize in literature in 1959.
In the hamlet of Serra, the ecomuseum collects the ethnographic material of Val Casotto: work tools and objects of everyday life of the past.
The relics and the saint's cell.
The sulphurous waters that make Caramanico a spa destination from the sixteenth century.
A sanctuary built on a Roman villa.
Reservation required according to the MiC card
Punic walls and baronial palace at a glance.
The fortress to defend Florence since the year Mille, the most historic property of Frescobaldi, today winery.
The palace of the dukes with the garden on the cliff.
The palace of the Dukes of Atri.

The territory is marked by calanchi excavated by erosion in millennia, surrounded by vineyards including those of Dogliani DOCG. From the locality of San Giuseppe starts stage 2 of the Tanaro Path, an easy route that from the landscape of the calanchi crosses hills and ancient villages up to Castellino Tanaro.
Thermal water in the village, also for families.
MiC card (updated 2021) indicates closed every day, times to check with the Municipality
The church was born on an ancient gate of the village.

Borgo dei Monti Lepini from the historic centre, mostly medieval, home to Pope Leo XIII (Gioacchino Pecci), which enriched it with restorations, churches and fountains by Michele Tripisciano; to see the Palazzo Pecci, the Palazzo Aldobrandini with the civic tower and the convents of Sant'Agostino and San Pietro.
Sunny village at 1489 meters in the middle of the Matterhorn valley, with the villages of Petit-Monde and the view from the Colle di San Pantaleone.

Mulino built in 1747 by Don Antonio Milano and restored in 2014, among the last examples of readable water grinding using the traditional method to ...ritrécine.It offers laboratories, sensory experiences and guided tours within the museum.
The underground theatre of Herculaneum.

Built on a cliff near the center at the beginning of the 17th century, it has a majolica ceiling painted between 1615 and 1617, made of 780 votive bricks with profiles, coats of arms, astronomical symbols, animals and flowers; In 1963, Carlo Levi called it the Sistine Chapel of Italian majolica.
On a hill with grassy square about 300 meters from the village, overlooking the Sangro Valley and Barrea Lake.
Country between villages, forests and the highest vineyards in Europe from the point of view of Mont Blanc, with one of the oldest towers in the region.
The Roman and Neapolitan baroque saved from the earthquake.

Country of the Val Canale at the foot of the Julian Alps, in the Middle Ages called Bamberghetto: the seventeenth-century Venetian Palace with the Ethnographic Museum, the Napoleonic ruins of the Fort Hensel, the Museum of the Tarvisio Forest at the Bagni di Lusnizza and, in Valbruna, the paths of the Val Saisera between resonance firs and trenches of the Great War.
Tasting the Colli Lanuvini in the fortress.

Fortress with a symmetrical rectangular structure with two high towers at the ends, stone and brick with ceilings and wooden roofs; an internal inscription recalls the restoration of the brothers Iacopo and Sebastiano di Montegnacco in 1480. Consolidated after the earthquake, today it is home with exhibition function: check the possibility of visiting.

The wetlands of the ancient salt pans, established in 2000 (54.5 hectares) and managed by LIPU, at the slopes of Mount Climati along the coast, in the middle of the industrial pole. There were 216 species of birds, about 40% of the Italian ones, including the major stern (symbol of the reserve), the courier of Leschenault and the firecracker fulvo; the sultan chicken, extinct in Sicily in the fifties, reintroduced by LIPU and INFS, has nested there spontaneously. Open every day; guided tours for groups and schools by reservation.

It rises in the Cascina Sant'Ambrogio, of origins dating back to the fourth century, which Sant'Ambrogio bought as a summer residence and left to the Church of Milan with the usufruct to his sister Marcellina, who lived in monastic form. From 1098 to 1613 the church customized the relics of the Magi Kings; inside two side frescoes depict Marcellina, Sant'Ambrogio and Satiro and the saints Sebastiano and Pope Fabiano.
Venue of the Albisola Museum, with works by artists of the twentieth century including Lucio Fontana, Wifredo Lam, Agenore Fabbri and Emanuele Luzzati.

The large square dominates: built from 1610 by order of San Carlo Borromeo on a project originally designed by Pellegrino Pellegrini, it has the façade designed in 1780 by Giuseppe Piermarini, who also designed the square and its trees, covered in travertine with statues in 1951. Inside stuccoes, paintings and frescoes in the vault and sides of Leoni, the Rusca and Levati, called in 1780 thanks to Giuseppe Maggiolini.

Country built ex novo around the SAICI plant, whose works began in 1937 and ended in less than a year; inaugurated in 1940 under the name of Torviscosa and celebrated by Filippo Tommaso Marinetti with a long poem. The square is dominated by a high tower and the long brick building of the CID.

In the upper part of the city, built from the year 1000 in Romanesque style on the foundations of a Roman temple of the first century BC; next to the Palazzo del Vescovado of fourteenth century origin.
The neoclassical of Calderari and the paintings of the Maganza.
The works of the woodcarvers in the village church.

Ring of about 5 km, without difficulty and suitable for every season, just over two hours: it starts from Villa Mantua Benavides in Valle San Giorgio, rises between arable land, meadows and vineyards touching the sources of the Pissarotto del Tòrmene and the Fontanelle up to the saddle between the Rusta and Gemola mountains, and returns on CAI path. Along the road emerge the basaltic tuffs of the first volcanic phase of the Hills and the 'basalto a risetti of Mount Gemola , with cavities full of calcite, natrolite and analcime.
The imperial village with its mint on Lake Maggiore.

Trapanese City at the foot of Monte Bonifato: in Piazza della Repubblica the fourteenth-century Castle of the Counts of Modica, with the regional Enoteca and the Museum of Popular Traditions; along Corso VI April the Baroque Mother Church with the frescoes of Guglielmo Borremans and the works of the Gagini, the Museum of Sacred Art and the Church of Saints Paul and Bartholomew; at the top of Bonifato the Reserve of the Bosco d'Alcamo.
It preserves the votive material of St. Anastasia and other nuragic sites in the area, including an altar shaped like nuraghes and objects in bronze and terracotta.

Of Lombard-Norman origin, it is mentioned for the first time in a document of 976 and belonged to Sanseverino, Orsini and Pignatelli before the purchase by the Lancellotti in 1632. Fired by French troops in 1799, it was rebuilt in the late nineteenth century by Prince Filippo Lancellotti in an eclectic style: the crenellated walls contain two courtyards with fountains, apartments, representative rooms, stables, chapel and a tower with loggia overlooking the Vallo di Lauro.

Ancient thermal baths known since ancient times, with hot, alkaline and radioactive water. From the locality Bregolana a network of trails and old mule tracks crosses the Wood of the Bagni, recommended in spring and autumn, with the sources to be visited all year round and a sensory path realized by ERSAF with the Union blind and visually impaired of Lombardy.
The walls of the center transformed into an open-air tunnel.
Castello dei Pico, Palazzo Comunale and Oratorio della Madonna della Porta are closed for restorations after the 2012 earthquake: they can only be seen from the outside
For those who love opera and symphonic music.
Among the sites of the heritage of Aosta reported by the regional portal.
A valley-museum of open-air geology.
A little-known Garibaldi episode.
A part of the journey between Bologna and Prato.
The Angevin village on the cliff.

Virtual Archaeological Museum inaugurated in October 1995 by Regione Lazio e Comune: with photographs, casts, plastics and virtual reality stations reconstructs roads, public and private buildings and daily life of Norba, a Roman city of the Republican age, and exhibits finds from excavations. MiC timetable: Tuesday-Saturday 9-18.

Of the demolished church of Santa Maria in Castro remains the left aisle, now the porch of the square, with a fresco of the Madonna with the Child of Vincenzo Pagani; from the village, entirely surrounded by walls, the look comes to the Conero and the Gran Sasso.
The large monastic complex on the hill of Galluzzo with the cycle of Passion frescoed by Pontormo, which can be visited with guided tours of about an hour.

On the eastern side of the Vesuvius, which takes its name from the third fire, the lava flow of 1631: the MATT exhibits the frescoes and the ori of the Roman villas of Cava Ranieri buried in 79 AD, the house-museum of Salvatore Emblema preserves the works of the artist and the pine forest of Piana Tonda is crossed by an accessible path of the Park.
The residence of the Dukes Ceva Grimaldi.
The only trace of the medieval castle.
The Blue Flag Sea of Fondi.
The Gothic on the square of the Three Churches.
Homage to the composer from Catania.
The sculptures between the houses.
Quadrilobed nuraghe in white square stone, surrounded by numerous bases of huts.

Villa probably from the early sixteenth century, originally with family chapel and a large park, transformed several times over the centuries. The ground floor was restored and reopened in 2001, the first floor in 2007; today civil weddings are celebrated.

The seaside and tourist resort has long been known on the Ionian coast, divided between Montauro and Stalettì: it takes its name from a large rock near the shore, 13 meters high, from which dives are made. Clear waters and cliffs are the frame of the beach; italia.it indicates it as an indispensable stop of the Calabrian summer.

On the hill above the village, it preserves the fortifications of the fourteenth century; the oldest part was almost destroyed by the earthquake of 1117 and remains the Tonda Tower with horseshoe. Originally had three drawbridges, today one. Towers and masts rise from the end of March to the end of October; the panoramic terrace looks at the morainic hills and in summer the courtyard hosts shows and outdoor cinemas.

On the shores of the lake, on the remains of a Roman villa of the first century AD: built by the Benedictines in the sixth century, it preserves the wooden statue of the Madonna with Child of the thirteenth century, celebrated on Monday after Pentecost; the bell tower also served as a watchtower.

Ancient feudal capital of the Da Palù and among the most significant villages of the Reggian hill: the Court of Dalla Palude has a seventeenth-century court and happened there, on 17 November 1944, the massacre of the partisans remembered as Martyrs of Legoreccio; next to the sixteenth-century tower house of the Rabotti and the fifteenth-century House of the Terzi, called "La Dogana" in memory of the border between Duchy of Modena and Parma State.
At 1,300 meters, near the church of Santa Maria della Neve, the 'domos de nie', 17th century wells used as snow.
Contemporary art in a former distillery.

On Mount della Rocca the ruins of the castle of the Frangipane, medieval fortress last bulwark of defence for centuries, that protected the Tolfetani also from the Napoleonic army; next, the sanctuary of the Fortress, built to protect the small church from above, with a panoramic churchyard on the village and hills.
It preserves paintings of the fourteenth century and frescoed lunettes above the main portals; inside a small cloister and the monumental tomb of a captain.
Half a kilometer of medieval arcades.

Renaissance residence built by Federico da Montefeltro since 1464, with a project attributed to Francesco di Giorgio Martini: elevated courtyard, lymphaeum of Ludovico Carducci, chapel of Cardinal Giuliano and Sala del Trono (Duke's Theatre); in the eastern loggia Duke Guidobaldo died in 1508. It houses the Civic Museum founded in 1901 by scholar Augusto Vernarecci, with exhibits of prehistory, picena culture and especially of the Roman Forum Sempronii, and the Pinacoteca civica.
An eighteenth-century building of 17 rooms that documents the life and culture of Rosazza and Valle Cervo, with the precision instruments of the technical school.

Cited in the documents from 1288 but probably before the Mille, it has a massive tower with the entrance to the base: it is the only example in Lombardy of clocher-porche, the bell tower that acts as an entrance porch. Inside there are frescoes from the XV-XVI century.
The largest canyon in Friuli.
Archaeology of the territory from Neolithic to modern age in three rooms, with finds of Serra Orrios, Nuraghe Mannu, Tiscali and caves of Bue Marino and Ispinigoli.
The frescoes re-emerged after centuries.

It rises in the highest part of the village, on the ancient fortification of the village, inside the walls. Attested as early as the 14th century, it owes its current appearance to an important restoration of the 16th century: two-side roof, bell tower with square base next to the facade and portal in Renaissance stone with flat architrave, surmounted by a bezel decorated with rosettes and the ray monogram of San Bernardino da Siena. In 2025 the project to repair earthquake damage 2016 was approved.
The seventeenth-century obelisk and the Bellerofonte fountain, among the monuments of the city centre.
The sculptures in bronze, wood and ceramics donated to the Municipality by the artist born here in 1918.

Set up in 1980 with the renovation of the parish house next to the Holy Trinity, it preserves furnishings, furnishings, hand-embroidered sacred vestments, cups and monstrators of the seventeenth century. According to the site of the Municipality is open every day from 10 am to 6 pm (the 2019 catalogue indicated it was open on request: best to call the parish, 0364 91223).

The village of the majolica at the foot of the Gran Sasso: the church of San Donato with the majolica ceiling that Carlo Levi called the Sistine of the majolica, the houses of the potters and the Museum of ceramics.
Waterfall in a narrow gorge excavated by the Magnone stream, fed by Lake Tenno, with walkways and panoramic points; near there is a botanical garden.
The panorama of the country and the plain.

A well-known place for over 500 years and famous worldwide for the number and conservation of the fossils of the tertiary era, especially fish and plants, in five layers superimposed of fine limestone; it is a mountain above Bolca crossed by tunnels, which with the Monte Postale forms a paleontological park. Visit the inner gallery and search the land for small fossils.

A few meters from the cathedral, underground complex probably Roman: two rooms dug in the sandstone with walls in stone and pillars up to five meters high, part of the water system linked to the aqueduct that fed the baths of Vibinum.
Millstones and old crafts in Vermenagna Valley.
The other face of the Isonzo front.

The historic Palazzo Canestrari houses the museum, which preserves artistic artifacts from the churches of the territory, in particular works by De Magistris. It is part of the Sistine Museums of Piceno.
The cliff of the prayer of Saint Rita.

Erected in 1330 by the abbot Nicola da Ferrazzano on a chapel of 1277, from 1332 she was a cathedral for the bishops of Volturara; renewed, was consecrated on July 8, 1703 by Cardinal Vincenzo Maria Orsini, then Pope Benedict XIII. It has a Latin cross plan with three naves, dome with yellow and green majolica, bell tower of about 35 meters symbol of the village, late dogotic rosette with the Carafa coat of arms and two portals of the fifteenth century from the abbey of Mazzocca; the bronze door of Valeria Sicily (2009) has 24 tiles on the patron saints. It preserves the reliquary bust of St. Bartholomew of the Neapolitan goldsmith Filippo Del Giudice (1767), the main altar in polychrome marble of the early eighteenth century, a stone tabernacle of 1541 and, in the treasury, silver and a mitria of the seventeenth century.

The Rota is a natural islet of peat, roots and marsh herbs that wind and currents move on the lake, already described by Pliny the Elder in Naturalis Historia. It is observed from the watchhouse at the end of the Nature Path   •Puzzillo •Puzzillo: 0.6 km flat (30 minutes), almost all on a wooden footbridge in the reed, which can also be walked by strollers; departure signposted in Sorgentina, via Lago Fibreno, with parking in via San Venditto near the old mill.
The wooden Annunciation of the Pisan school and the canvas of the Allori.

The Kuerc (the cover) is a loggia symbol of Bormio, was born in wood in 1387, burned in 1855 and was rebuilt: here justice was administered and popular councils were gathered; noteworthy are the dragon-shaped showers. The fourteenth-century Torre delle Ore, with coats of arms, sundial and painted clock, housed the Bajona bell that called the population to assemblies, parties and emergencies. On the square there is also the Cortivo, an ancient office of archives, council and warehouses, with signs of the Milanese period.
Two Roman bridges on Flaminia.
The castle found.
The heart of mining Sardinia.

Large circular lime kilns placed on the slope, partly underground and open at the top, used until the 1950s: of the 30 recorded there remain 17, some restored for documentary purposes. The easiest to see are those of Fraìna Alta, La Guarda and Pattachin, the latter visible from the valley floor road.
An outdoor museum of chapels and funeral monuments.
The shrine of the patron goddess of Lanuvium.
The museum occupies the entire western side of Piazza San Benedetto, in the heart of the historic centre.
A work by Hans Clemer.
ridge roads between Emilia and Liguria.

Beni in the place called "Casinae Scanasane" are mentioned already around the year 1000; restored in the fifteenth century, when the village became a fortified farmhouse, at the beginning of the sixteenth century passed to the Trivulzio, which transformed it from a fortress into a country house, of which the cylindrical towers remain. In 1836 he passed to the Visconti di Modrone. It preserves graffiti decorations and Gothic arched windows; a part has been renovated under the protection of the Fine Arts.
€8, reduced €6 (path 1, prices 2024)

Villa of the fifteenth century, now a municipal cultural centre and seat of the Museum of Arms, with a large park, baroque salons, mozzoni lunettes and, in the private chapel on the ground floor, a bas-relief of the Nativity.
The oldest church in the valley, of Romanesque layout, erected by the Benedictines around the Thousand; it preserves frescoes with evident Byzantine influences.
In the ancient Rione Castello, it is one of the architectural symbols of the village.
Alfonso Simonetti's paintings.
Italo-Albanian identity in a live museum.
The composer's house.
Anthola woods with deer and blooms.
Hot thermal water with views of the Garda.

Fishing village on the sea, with crystal clear waters; the beach of Lampare has been awarded for several years by the Blue Flag. The bottom is pebbles (recommended rubber shoes) and a large rock shaped by erosion is the guardian of the bay; from the promontory you can see the 38th Parallel Pyramid of the Fiumara d'arte. Free parking along the road.
Calette under the cliff of the Conero.

Funeral monuments from the last republican phase to the first century of the empire; in the oldest tombs of the territory amphorae and vases testify the influence of the Greek colonies of the coast from the eighth century BC.

Valcuvia municipality a few kilometers from Lake Maggiore, with the sixteenth-century Villa Della Porta Bozzolo del FAI and its terrace garden, and on the hills the village of Arcumeggia, the painted village, transformed since 1956 into an open-air fresco gallery.
The rebuilt Romanesque Cathedral.
A park to discover.
The terraced sanctuary that goes up with the country.

It was cited as a new ecclesia sancti Gregori, built in 1237, born as a small chapel and became a parish in 1632, transformed in the eighteenth century and for the last time in 1932. It has four chapels on the side with barrel vaults and paintings from the 16th to the 18th century: a Pietà, perhaps from the Richino, the altarpiece with the Madonna and Child dated 1569, a painting by Pietro Marone, frescoes detached from the ancient church of San Velgio and paintings by Giuseppe Remida; in sacristy angels reggigandelabro baroque.
A late-gothic table in town hall.
the Province indicates castle and towers in bad state and records the Clavesana castle card under Vasia: check access and localization
The gorge excavated by the stream Fersina at the gates of the city, accessible on walkways with guided tour.
Remains of a 15th century castle on a cliff overlooking the valley of Ofanto; there is little left. The first fortress was born after the Saracen attacks of the IX-X century (Castrum Petrae Paganae).

Inaugurated in 1868 on a project by Virginio Vespignani, who transformed the old Vico Squarano into a boulevard portico on the model of the Parisian passages; since 1901 the square is named after Verdi.
A low and jagged coastline with hidden coves and wide stretches of sand; in the hinterland ancient farmhouses between olive groves and almond groves.

Former Venosta Palace, a residence of the Cinque-Seicento in front of the parish church of San Martino; in the eighteenth century it had the present entrance with the loggia above and preserves a porch courtyard with stone doors surmounted by stuccoes.
Medieval frescoes in the countryside.
The baroque at the gates of the ancient center.
Bathrooms and lake tour on foot or by bike.
A polyptych from the early fifteenth century in a mountain village.
A 16th-century church in the center.
Then a tasting of Chianti Rufina.

Forging the Catalan style dated 1675 by an inscription on stone ('IHS Glaudo Calvi 1675) with a large forge for copper and a small for iron and coal, sweaters and mantic moved by the Soana water; it remained active until 1952 and was restored by the Park. It is the core of the Ecomuseum of Copper: it shows the phases of pre-industrial processing, it has a didactic workshop with documentaries on the use of copper in peasant life and an exhibition on the magnin, the now streetwalkers of the valley, some of which then worked on the bodies of the Turin automotive industry. Information hours (Tel. 011 8606233).
A fortified village of the 12th century on the hills of Subasio.
A Roman sanctuary on the water, between caves and river.
The Treasure of Anagni's popes.

The brown of Segni is celebrated at the end of October with the Festival of Brown and the Copeta procession; on the table the fregnaquanti, very thin egg pasta with meat sauce, the appal of cooked fava beans crushed with garlic, oil and chilli, and the black truffle of Lepini.
The historic elegant cafe of Via Fillungo, meeting place of Giacomo Puccini.
Learn wine by walking through the vineyards.
The fine sandy beach can be reached on foot along Via Byron, with boats and colourful houses mirroring in the clear sea.
The castle of the leader with the chapel of the swallows.

Born in the mid-nineteenth century as a private residence of the noblewoman Lady Florence Trevelyan, it is an English garden on several levels with botanical garden and the ...Victorian Follies , bizarre constructions between romantic and Gothic taste with strong oriental influences; views of the bay of Naxos and Mount Etna.

Sanctuary of the Madonna della Consolazione, patron saint of the city, in the upper part of Reggio: it houses the icon painted by Nicolò Andrea Capriolo in 1547-1548. The current building, designed by Anna Anastasi Sbarracani, was completed in 1961 and in 1971 elevated to a minor basilica.
Lakes born from ancient gravel quarries filled with groundwater, used for recreational and sporting activities; the wetlands around host more than a hundred species of birds.
For the fans of the Caliph.
The beaches of Vindice, Acquatraversa, Santo Janni and Gianola; VisitLatium signals one of the ten beaches Flag Green of Lazio in Formia.
The panorama of Gangi rooftops.
Walk on three historic streets in a gorge.
In the crypt the marble sarcophagus with the relics of St Romualdo, founder of the Camaldolese.
Another Camaldolese testimony of the village.
The paintings of Maffei and Ricchi on the castle hill.

Birthplace of Achille Ratti, Pope Pius XI, Desio revolves around the square of the Council with the basilica of the Santi Siro and Materno and the eighteenth-century Villa Cusani Tittoni Traversi del Piermarini, \"Villa of Delight" with its park and the Scalvini Museum; complete the visit the birthplace of the pontiff, today museum, and the mineralogical museum Â"La Miniera" Â"La MineÂ" .

Ancient industrial location at the foot of the north side of Vizzini, among hills of figs of India: the name comes from ...conceria , the activity that took place there thanks to the summacco and the springs. The village was renovated in the twentieth century and abandoned in the 1960s. It preserves the forms of the late 18th and 19th centuries and was set by Cavalleria rusticana by Franco Zeffirelli (1982) and La Lupa by Gabriele Lavia (1996).
closed to cult for damage of the earthquake of 1962 (Common)

It rises on the temple of the Emiliano Forum and climbs up a stairway; the mosaic of the portico has a marine theme, perhaps a voyage of crusaders by sea, and inside mosaics with knights, battles and fantastic animals; the bell tower is lightened by numerous arches.

Marche village in bricks enclosed by a 15th-century wall among the best preserved of the Marche, with the tower of the Sperone attributed to Francesco di Giorgio Martini, the staircase of the Piaggia with the Polenta Well, the Goldoni Theatre, the Civic collection of art "Claudio Ridolfi" and the places of Santa Maria Goretti, born here in 1890.
Medieval fortified village where the whole country works on wine and oil, with cellars in deconsecrated churches connected by an underground "wine pipeline."

Cities of painted facades and chocolate in the south of the province of Alexandria, long under the control of Genoese, with the decorated palaces of the historic center, the Salt Fountain and the Museum of the Championships dedicated to Costante Girardengo and Fausto Coppi.
Roman structures linked to the Via Flaminia, still present in the territory.

Erbarium and botanical garden with about 1,300 species of cataloged plants; it also exhibits ancient tools for wood processing, the four phases of the transformation of small logs into coal and a classification of many species of mushrooms.
Made in the Palazzo dei Conti Guidi, with Gothic portal and two works of the fifteenth century: a Madonna from Donatello's workshop and a Redeemer from Andrea Ferrucci's workshop.
The 11th century, rebuilt in the 15th and enlarged in the late 19th century, with a Romanesque bell tower among the oldest in the region.
Small church of the eighteenth century that houses an ancient wooden cross; it is reached on foot from the village along a path of moderate slope.

Champions of the marble of Frabosa, the Verzino chosen in the seventeenth century for many Turinese churches and Guarino Guarini for the dome of the Chapel of the Shroud, exposed with original tools along the route to the multipurpose hall and the hall of the Town Hall, with the installation \"Marmi to touch" by Daniele Aletti. In Via di Bossea 2 the workshop-museum of sharp irons, restored in 2017, tells of the Frabousan knives documented since 1790 (free visit on request).
In the theatre the Hall of the Thirty and the rebuilt dressing room of Beniamino Gigli; the museum preserves the costumes of the tenor.
The raw sea of the Bari.

Sanctuary in the countryside, about 2.5 km north of the center, built by the feudal lord G.B. Barbò with the contribution of the population to remember a miracle: the deaf-domed daughter regained the word while offering flowers of field to a painted Madonna, image still very venerated by the Soresinesi.
An enchanted corner of the village.
The small hill symbol of the thermal baths, with the column of Jappelli.

Built in 1759 on the remains of a votive newsstand, it houses a painting on tuff considered miraculous with a former gold vote, a fresco of the 15th century Madonna and Child and a wooden statue of St. Rocco of the 15th century.
The oldest church in the valley, in the smallest village of Liguria.
The key to reading the country's solar dials.
The portrait artist of Milan of the late nineteenth century.

The parish church in which, according to the municipality, Gioacchino da Fiore was baptized: three naves with basilica plant and presbytery with dome after 1753; damaged by the earthquake of 1905 and restored in 1906. It houses the ceiling painted in 1787 by Cristoforo Santanna, the altarpiece of Our Lady of Heaven with Saints James and John the Baptist of Theodorus of Henry the Flemish, a wooden crucifix of the fifteenth century and a glass blown in the middle of the sixteenth century. Open every day 7-21.
Crafts of wood and peasant life in over 2,700 objects.
A very lively neighborhood.
€5 (only museum); €10 with the park; 18-25 years €2; free under 18
The vote against the plague.

Along the Via Flaminia, home to one of the oldest confraternities in the city, dates back to the 14th century; portal of 1537 and sixteenth-century fresco on the façade. Inside the polychrome terracotta group of the Madonna della Misericordia, the "Strage degli Innocenti" and the "Visitation" by Claudio Ridolfi and fragments of fourteenth-century frescoes (Crucifixion, Martyrdom of St. Apollonia, Commentary on the dead Christ).
Garden that collects numerous plant species of the Apennines and includes a pond.
The village barracks.
Baroque art and view of the valley.

Inaugurated in 2003 in a former industrial warehouse of the early 20th century in the center, on over 3,000 m2, it is indicated as the largest museum of cycling in Europe. A long central track tells the story of the bicycle, from the prototype attributed to Leonardo and from the draisina to the prototypes in titanium, with about forty bicycles; on the sides the history of the components and the Giro d'Italia, two rooms with vintage films, a virtual reality room with computerized bikes and the Sala dei Campionissimi with relics of Fausto Coppi and Costante Girardengo, born in Novi. It also houses the permanent exhibition "Tesori Sacri" from the civic collection, ten paintings from the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Hours from October to April: Friday 15-19, Saturday, Sunday and holidays 10-13 and 15-19; from May to September: Friday 16-20, Saturday, Sunday and holidays 10-13 and 16-20; closed 25 December and 1 January.

Plate mentioned in a document of the fifteenth century, of veal cooked slowly with a set of spices, celebrated every year by the Palio of the stew among the local cooks called "stofatari" (stofatari), other typical product is tarese, traditional salami recognized by Slow Food.
A sanctuary on the way to transhumance.
Galleries, cisterns and tunnels dug into the tuff, up to 40 meters below the road: a journey of 2,400 years from the Greek era to today, recovered by volunteers.
A hermitage rebuilt stone on stone in the middle of the beech trees.
Contemporary art inside a medieval castle.

Palace of medieval origin, today hidden by the rococo decorations of the windows, already seat of the university; it is accessed from the Arch of the Gate. The ground floor served as a storeroom of food and oil and the back from prison, of which remains a grate in via Tanese, the ancient Via Giudea. The tower, which had a sundial, houses a rare public clock with cables of the nineteenth century, surmounted by a statue of San Vito, patron, and a sailing bell tower.

Dedicated to transhumance along the tratturous royal route from Abruzzo to Puglia, it traces the history of the island in Irpinia with a wide cultural and anthropological heritage, in a modern building that plays with light and water effects on the surrounding landscape. Totally accessible.
The miners' village.
The 11th century building where the abbots administered justice on the abbey's territories, once connected to the complex by a loggia.
The park along the Serchio river in the Piana di Lucca, signposted by Visit Tuscany.
Gladiators in the rock.

The castle dates back to about 1460, with a quadrangular plan around a large courtyard, with a cylindrical tower, a square tower and a tower where you can still see the entrance with drawbridge; transformed between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, passed to the Savoys in 1867 with the wedding of Maria Vittoria From the Well of the Cisterna and Amedeo of Savoy, who built the royal apartments there, and was sold to private individuals after the Second World War. The village, which had more than 500 inhabitants at the beginning of the 20th century, is now almost depopulated and in precarious state, but offers views of the rice fields with the Alps in the background.
Ten enlarged reproductions of his works exhibited in the country, next to the landscapes that inspired them.
The fourteenth-century sign of the fortified village.
Peak of 1,768 m reachable by ski lift from Camigliatello, starting point of different cross-country ski trails, among larch woods and white firs.
The intact medieval castle above Flaminia.
A ruin inhabited by the sight, with tavern under the walls.
Cottages and pastures at the foot of the Monzoni.
The work of the sculptor Onofrio La Leggia, recalls the miners' craft depicting them pushing wagons loaded with sulfur ore.

Built between 1431 and 1502 in Gothic-Renaissance forms, with a white marble portal attributed to Sansovino or his school; it preserves works by Giovanni Buonconsiglio, two counter-façade frescoes attributed to Giorgione and on the main altar the great Transfiguration of Paolo Veronese (1555-56).
Guided tours for a fee: fare with reservation
The mother church of Cortina with the bell tower symbol of the valley.
The parish church of San Bartolomeo preserves, in a silver reliquary of the eighteenth century, the relics of the three Magi Kings, kept from 1098 to 1613 in the small church of Sant'Ambrogio.

The most important archaeological area of the municipality: almost fifty late-Etruscan burials arranged on terraces overlooking the village, with an ancient ritual quarry road that connected the sources of Bacchus and the stream to the upper part, where probably stood a natural sanctuary.
The Roman Parma under the feet of passers-by.
The riverwalk.
Ancient forest equipped with picnic areas and benches, crossed by a naturalistic path with panels on flora and fauna.
Civic art next to the Duomo.

The Romanesque-Gothic basilica was built on the remains of a temple dedicated to Venus and a early Christian basilica, which dominates the city and the port from the hill of Guasco in a spectacular way.

It gives its name to the agricultural village of Buccinasco Castello, in the countryside of the South Milan Agricultural Park just outside the West Tangenziale. It is a single block with a square plan on two floors, brick exposed with the front entrance plastered; on the opposite side a portico of five spans on the ground floor and a loggia of ten spans on the first floor. There are traces of walls of the fourteenth century and the loggia is of the sixteenth century; it is among the oldest buildings of the municipality and appears in the municipal coat of arms.
A Romanesque parish church of Lombard origin.

Cittadina della Riviera del Brenta, river port since the 15th century thanks to its basin, with its monumental squero; in the hamlet of Sambruson the eighteenth-century Villa Badoer-Fattretto with the Museo del Villano, the Roman antiquarium Lino Vanuzzo and Villa Venier Velluti.

Forest plateau between Urbino, Isola del Piano and Fossombrone, up to 648 meters, with about 1500 hectares of wood at high stem born largely from the reforestations started in 1915 with black pines and continued until the 1950s, so much to form a living catalog of conifers; there live deer, wild boars, foxes, badgers and raptors. Sixteen marked trails of non-high difficulty and a mountain bike circuit.

XV century church built on the ruins of a medieval castle, in the center of the ancient village, reached by a monumental staircase of the eighteenth century with a view from the churchyard. In the sacristy tears of late-four hundred frescoes, a fifteenth-century table with the Baptism of Jesus and a Pietà by Vincenzo Angelo Orelli; the baptistery, made from the ancient chapel of San Rocco on a project by Vito Sonzogni, is decorated with mosaics and sculptures by Claudio and Attilio Nani.

You enter from the Alfonsina Gate, with the Duchess and Ippolita towers, built in the Aragonese defenses after the Turkish devastation of 1480; inside, stone paved alleys that descend to the sea, granite bomb balls and the walk on the bastions.
From the Sibillini to the sea at a glance.
The prehistoric steles.

The libraries founded in 1897 in the Benedictine Monastery, combining the bookstores of Benedictine fathers and other collections: over 270,000 volumes, illuminated codes, manuscripts, parchments and incunabula.

Bormio 2000, the heart of the ski area, can be reached by cable car; another cable car climbs to the panoramic Cima Bianca (3.012 m), from which the legendary Stelvio track leads to the village (1.225 m). Bormio is also a base for excursions in the Ortles-Cevedale group.

Borgo della piania Brescia of Roman origins, known for the Horse Fair at the end of April-early May; in the center the Piazza della Libertà redesigned by Mario Botta with the bell tower, the Baroque Cathedral, the nineteenth-century buildings of Rodolfo Vantini and the church of Santa Maria dei Campi with frescoes by Vincenzo Civerchio.
Walking along Via Torre you can reach the Torre del Gran Priore, dating back to the 12th century, from which you can get lost in the alleys of the historic center.
The three surviving galleries in the French style of the center; the Galleria San Federico is located where there was a hospital.
The most important Moroni in his hometown.

In a house-tower of the thirteenth century in the center of Bazzano, opened in 2003 by the cultural group Il Camino: interactive routes on the processing of hemp and on the culture of wine, to see, touch and listen, with activities for schools. Recognized Museum of Quality by the Region.
Altomedieval church several times renovated, with Romanesque bell tower.
The giant stove symbol of the city.
To be checked on the Marconi Foundation website
The flamingos just a stone's throw from the city.

The most populous city of Abruzzo, on the sea at the mouth of the Pescara river: the promenade and the Bridge of the Sea, the Dannunzian Pinewood, the birthplace of Gabriele d'Annunzio in Pescara Vecchia and a network of museums from ethnography to ceramics of Castelli.
A rare peasant architecture in Italy.

It is located in the attic of the Institute including and studying, documenting and enhancing popular games and toys: over 250 contemporary works of art on the theme of the game and a hundred ethnographic toys, especially from Basilicata and Puglia, with exhibition curated by Donato Allegretti.

The stream that descends from Schiara al Piave: gorge and gorge of the Ardo, the Pont de la Mortis and Bus del Buson, an ancient gorge suspended among the most important geomorphological emergencies of Veneto.
The Romanesque bell tower over the river.
A view that has drawn Sardinia.
The Gothic Cistercian of Fossanova in a mountain village.
The frescoes of the blessings.

The caves of the Carrubella, Santa Rosalia, La Portella and Pizzo Miletta districts and the necropolis of Ciachea district testify to the oldest human presence in the territory; the findings of the necropolis are preserved at the Archaeological Museum of Palermo.

Rebuilt in the fifteenth century on the ruins of a medieval building, it was enlarged around 1667 demolishing bell tower and facade to lengthen the three naves, designed by the foreman Stefano De Stefanis of Graglia, and restored in the nineteenth century. Inside the altar in polychrome marble by Francesco Olgiati (1776), late-sixth century altars by Giuseppe Giudice and Francesco Colombera di Viggiù, stuccos and columns painted with fake marble; outside friezes by Paolo Giovanni Crida.
Wild Crinals of the Prato Apennines.
Satire and comic book in the dance hall of the Sixties.
The capital of Valsesia, the city of Gaudenzio Ferrari, dominated by the Sacred Mount of 1491, the oldest in northern Italy and UNESCO.
Four speakers in one village.
Hidden waterfall at the bottom of a canyon excavated by the Massangla stream near Tiarno di Sotto: an easy walk of about 20 minutes from the old mill, in the woods among several waterfalls.
The house Cogoleto ties to Colombo.

Natural inlet on the Gulf of Salerno, in zone B of the Marine Protected Area, reached by Torca (via Nula) in about 1 hour of descent and 1 hour and a half challenging ascent, in the sun and without water. In the seaside village there are Roman cisterns, the viceroyal tower against the Saracens and the remains of the abbey of San Pietro (beginning of the year 1000), with votive chapel, stems of columns and marble bases.
The new village of Gonzaga.

In the village of Guggal, at 1,180 meters above sea level inside the Monte Corno Natural Park, the house where Prince Bishop Zwerger was born is today a museum with objects and documents about his life; you can visit only with guide.
The ancient nucleus, called "Il Guasto" is part of the Historical Villages of the Marche Region; Italia.it signals the presence of noble palaces and under its streets run the caves.
An octagonal temple on the river, where the Tiber was worshipped.
A short distance from the village, suitable for picnics and walks; from here you walk to the alpine farmsteads of Stavel.
Count Cesare Mattei's nineteenth-century eclectic castle, father of electromeopathy, between Moorish and medieval styles; in 2026 he reopened the Arab wing, closed for thirty years.
The medieval fountain of the city.
From the Roman port of Vada to the castle.
A fortified mill of the fourteenth century.
An art break from the beach.

In Vigna di Valle, on the lake between Bracciano and Anguillara, in the buildings that until 1945 housed the Experimental Centre for Flyers: aircraft and engines that tell Italian aviation in four pavilions, from pioneers and dirigibles (Troster) to the polar flights of Nobile and the Schneider Cup (Velo), to the Second World War (Badoni) to the contemporary jets (Skema). Recommended visit over three hours.
The parish church, in Baroque style, dates back to the 17th century. It has only one nave with seven side chapels and a large presbytery.
The village on the peninsula of Lake Orta, Orange Flag and among the most beautiful villages in Italy, with the island of San Giulio and the Sacro Monte Franciscan UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The harpsichord of "Tu" comes down from the stars.
Remains of the first century A.D. Roman villa that occupied the north side up to Punta Eolo; according to tradition the daughter of the Emperor Augustus was exiled there.

Nuraghe, village of a dozen huts and three tombs of giants of the Middle and Recent Bronze Age (XVI-XIII century B.C.); next to the first tomb six conical betiles, three with female forms, called "perdas marmuradas."

A split in the rock frames a small wedge beach, joined above by a bridge between the two walls; the fishing village with the monazzens, ancient tool stores, has been restored. It was set of the film L'Amore by Roberto Rossellini with Anna Magnani, and on the first Sundays of July it hosts dives from cliffs from almost 30 meters.

A hilly village with a medieval structure gathered around Piazza Matteotti, with the Collegiate Church of Santo Stefano, the Pincio viewpoint open from the Sibillini to the Adriatic and the eighteenth century Villa Buonaaccorsi with its Italian garden; on the sea the hamlet of Porto Potenza Picena, with the seaside village and the Blue Flag promenade.
The patron saint of the city.
Cathedral of the sixteenth century overlooking Piazza Grande.
Low and crystalline water in front of Tavolara.
The spring under the altar, in the middle of the rice fields.
The main street.
The fountain shaped like a boat by Pietro Bernini at the foot of the Trinity of the Mountains.
On April 25, the wild asparagus festival offers exhibitions, food stands and walks among wild plants.
The red of the cinnabar inside the mountain.

Prescce is the country with the largest number of cave-trappeti, mills carved in stone: 23 are inserted in the underground network of the country and still store presses and millstones. They open on Piazza del Popolo, where until the beginning of the twentieth century the life of the oil mills took place, so much so that we talk about a village hidden under the square. The Touring indicates opening on request and free entrance.
Kiefer's towers.
Dervio is the starting point for walks and excursions, including the Trail of the Wanderer, certified by the Italian Touring Club.

Historical village, ancient fishing village on the shore of the lake with small squares and a marina; the Promobellagio distributes free of charge a self-guided itinerary of the hamlets (San Giovanni, Pescallo, Civenna).

It dates back to the tenth century: a round arch, flanked in the following centuries by a smaller opening, gave access to an Arab fort with walls and tower, which continued to defend this part of the city under Byzantines and Normans.
The sacred cliff of the Isarco Valley.
To be verified: cumulative ticket with TAMO and Domus Stone Mats
The Duke in the sacristy.

Built between 1201 and 1202 after Verona had made the village a Free Village (1185), it was set on fire by the army of Ezzelino da Romano in 1232 and rebuilt in 1243, when the Podestà Enrico III da Egna built the main tower; it was part of Serraglio Scaligero along the Tione. With Venice (1405) it lost importance and was used as garrison and customs; the City bought mast and prisons in 1882 and in 1890 the tower was restored and equipped with clock. After the collapse of a corner tower the restorations of 1926-1935 created the public gardens; the great restoration of 2023 opened the interior halls and a new walkway with installations on medieval civil and military life. Opening hours April-October: Tuesday-Friday 10-13 and 14.30-17.30, Saturday 10-13 and 16-19, Sunday 10-12 and 15-19 (in August only Friday-Sunday); November-March: Thursday 10-13, Friday-Sunday 10-13 and 14.30-17.30.

A few meters from Piazza Risorgimento, pays tribute to Giovanni Paolo Feminis, born here and emigrated to Cologne, inventor of the formula of the Cologne Water, and to Giovanni Maria Farina who spread it.
Walk in the forum of Roman Carnia.
Excavation area open only during summer campaigns

Public garden for families inaugurated in 2010 next to the abbey of Santa Maria at the foot of Chienti: 10,000 m2 of lawn with games, benches and tables, connected by a bike path to the smallest park in Europe.
In the hamlet of Limonetto, at the base of the Colle di Tenda on the border with France.
Mosaics and stele of the early Christians.
The fresco of Niccolò dell'Abate.
The monument of Niccolò Orsini and the altarpiece of Antonio del Massaro

The upper part of the village, called "u' Castieddu" gathers the medieval tower and the mother church of Santa Maria Assunta, of the second half of the twelfth century; the lower part, outside the ancient walls, overlooks the valley. From the square of the tower you can see Monte Cervati, the highest peak in Campania, the river Bussento and the Sanctuary of Novi Velia. In the village also the churches of San Michele and San Rocco, the chapels of San Giovanni Battista and of Sant'Anna and the Palazzo Marchesale; the houses preserve gardens, common ovens and "stieri" , once stables and today dispensed.
The panoramic terrace is permanently closed after restoration.
Fortified village born in the IX century, when the inhabitants moved to the height to escape the invasions; it preserves the medieval aspect with views of great suggestion along the river Lete.

Rectangular piazza portico, always the heart of the city, with the Doge's Palace, the Palazzo del Cavalleggero and the parish church of the Assunta (1578-82) with its brick façade, with eighteenth-century decorations, the Chapel of Bibiena and a Crucifix donated by San Carlo Borromeo.
€10 guided tour

The capital of Valsugana is the only village in Trentino, developed on both sides of the Brenta, with a historical centre of Venetian origin along Corso Ausugum, the Venetian Bridge, Castel Telvana that dominates the village, the permanent exhibition of the Great War and, in Val di Sella, the open-air museum of Arte Sella.
A trip to the iron tunnels that made the history of Elba.

Traditionally, the first church in the village, with a Greek plan until about the eighteenth century and then a Latin cross; the Greek cult is documented until 1570. Legend has it that on the outer left wall a stone is walled up brought by the Templars from Palestine.
The sketches for the Verona Arena by the author of the frescoes of the Duomo.
A thousand years of fortifications on a spur of the coffin.

In the Romanesque crypt of the church of Santo Stefano, in Precetto: about twenty natural mummies discovered in 1805 after a Napoleonic edict on the exhumations, the oldest of about four centuries ago, the most recent of the nineteenth century; the conservation is due to the microorganisms of the soil and constant ventilation. The church, built over an older building, has three aisles, Baroque apse, the Martyrdom of Santo Stefano by Giuseppe Rosi (1759) and a crib frescoed by Pierino Cesarei (1595). Info: tel. 0744 780708.

Since 1997 in the former headquarters of the Consortium for Fisheries and Aquaculture of Trasimeno, in San Feliciano: four rooms named at the moments of the day of the fisherman tell the geological origin of the lake, the fishing from prehistory to today and the fish fauna, with the cast of the "Venus del Trasimeno" , Etruscan-Roman net weights, a rare collection of water birds, aquariums with local species and a multimedia room shaped like a boat. Hours: July-August Mar-dom 10-13 and 16-19.30 (sat-dom also 21.30-23.30); April-June and September-Jo-dom 10-13 and 15-18; October-December and March-Sat-dom 10-13 and 15-18; January-February by reservation. Info: tel. 075 8479261.
The silk story that gave the country its name.
€5 unique ticket of the museum route
The oldest church in the memory of the city.

Central square dedicated to a hero of the First World War born in Citerna, with a sixteenth-century well and the Civic Tower, which preserves a rare mechanical clock of the sixteenth century with wooden gears; the terrace looks on the basin of the Tiber towards the Apennines. The center, built between the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries, has two doors: Roman gate to the south and Porta Fiorentina to the north.
Archpriest's church of the village that, with San Domenico and the Civic Museum, houses works by Mattia Preti, born in Taverna.

Built around 1500 to the west of the village by Ferdinando Pappacota, whose king Frederick of Aragon had granted the fief in 1496: it was a fortress with three towers, blackbirds, cannons and underground passages. Sold around 1700 to Andrea Doria Panfili, then passed to the Onorato family; remain the blackbirds of the south tower, wounds and an ancient well.

About 280 hectares of wooded plateau along the rocky ridge of Malvarone Cinghio (722 m), between calanchi, chestnut groves and clearings, with the valley of the Lerna stream between rocky walls and karst forms. More than 80 species of birds, foxes, badgers, roe deer and wild boars; at the Oratory of Sassomassiccio there is a small pond in a sinkhole, purchased by WWF Modena in 1994.

Great palace inside the walls wanted by Count Fabio Landriani, with severe arched portal with rustic frames. It hosts the municipal collection of contemporary, figurative and abstract graphics, often artist's proofs (Adriano Calavalle, Mario Bellagamba, Walter Piacesi, Dino Ciacci, Sandro Tombari, Mario Borghi), a work by Anselmo Bucci, a tablet by Emilio Antonioni and the bicycles of the craftsmen and street vendors from the twenties to the fifties, equipped with barbers, crockery, carpenter, shoemaker, freighter, for bread, milk and fried fish. In summer there is the Market of the Feudatario of handicrafts and antiques.
A rare museum in Italy on boaters' lives.
Ancient Romanesque church near the Fortress, along the Ru Nero, where in the twelfth century the bodies of the two saints were transferred.
Street art in Pistoia.
The villa where Tasso wrote the song to the Metauro.
The staircase on Piazza del Popolo.

It tells how the inhabitants of the valley have adapted in the millennia to difficult conditions: finds of the site of the Ganglegg from the Neolithic to the Roman age, finds along the Via Claudia Augusta, the history of the roges (the Waale of the Malser Haide are from 2023 immaterial heritage UNESCO), the ... children of Swabia emigrant to work from the seventeenth century, the street vendors ...Karrner and the stallion Avelignes Folie, born in 1874, parent of the race. Changing exhibitions and film screenings; 5 minutes walk from the station.
Panoramic village overlooking the Strait of Messina, indicated for sunset on the Strait.
closed to the public for restoration works, guided tours only by reservation (tourist site of the Municipality)

Born from the donations of Annibale degli Abbati Olivieri Giordani (1708-1789), on the ground floor of the seventeenth-century Palazzo Almerici: furnishings of the necropolis of Novilara with the famous figurative stele, a bilingual Etruscan-Latin inscription and Roman finds.
A unique water show: check the opening times of the waters.

Medieval village on a plateau of tuff on the valley of the Tiber, between two streams, home of two popes and linked to Orsini, Colonna, Borgia and the Rovere; to see the neoclassical cathedral of Pietro Camporese, the basilica of the patron San Famiano and the castle Altemps, where he walked d'Annunzio.
Museum of Science and Planetary with a large dome, entitled to the astronomer Cosentino of the sixteenth century Giovan Battista Amico.
The epigraph of the letter from heaven.
Visitable only ground floor and park, degraded upper floors (FAI); visit by telephone reservation (Tourism Turin)
The symbol of Modica.
Green and Roman walls in the center.

In the former 14th-century church and convent, the cycle of the Stories of St. Francis painted by Benozzo Gozzoli in 1452, the chapel of St. Jerome, the art gallery, a Roman statue of Hercules and the ancient cellars.
The Byzantine church of the village.

In the South Milan Agricultural Park, Noviglio hosts the Kartell Museum, in the factory designed in the sixties by Anna Castelli Ferrieri and Ignazio Gardella, and historic farmsteads such as the Castellazzo, fortified complex before the fifteenth century with traces of a Visconti coat of arms, and Tavernasco.
A bathroom in the Mingardo.
Living in the Renaissance.
Villa with a large park frequented by painters macchiaioli, D'Annunzio and Sem Benelli, who in the tower of the park wrote La cena delle scoffe.
A Pietro da Cortona in Valmarecchia.
The treasures of the church of Sant'Osvaldo.
Palaces of the sixteenth century and the Jewish and Waldensian districts.

Irpino village dominated by the Castle of Guevara, with the sixteenth-century Grand Gate, the Mother Church, the ancient Via dei Finestroni and the viewpoint of the Tombola; in the woods the sulphuric source of the Refieto and the tratturo of transhumance.

Village of hills south of Parma on the Via Francigena, with prehistoric traces in the territory: in Varano Marchesi the Palace of Pallavicino, the ruins of the castle and the Museum of history and peasant civilization, in Sant'Andrea Bagni the thermal baths with eight different mineral waters.
Minerals, fossils and fauna of the mining territory.

Two-storey building, with six round arches on the ground floor, windows on the upper floor and the high clock tower next to it; on the façade the frescoed coats of arms of the families who ruled the city, a walled Gothic loggia and a fresco of the Madonna and Child between the Saints Sigismondo and Christopher.
Corinaldo's painter and the prince's helmet.
The queen's romantic garden.
Ring path of about 7 km between pastures and beech woods, easy and suitable for families, proposed for mountain biking.
The village-castle overlooking the Valnerina.
About €5 whole / €3 reduced (date to recheck). Free with BW Card
The most elegant lawn.
The great forest of the Colli Albani half an hour from Rome.

Cities at the gates of the Valle d'Itria, famous for the Caves of Castellana, karst system of more than 3 km discovered by Franco Anelli in 1938, with the White Grotto and the Speleological Museum dedicated to the discoverer.
The Alcantara River among the lava rocks.
normally not accessible; open with guided tours for the Spring FAI Days (21-22 March 2026)

It is located in Loreto because Our Lady of Loreto, proclaimed in 1920 as the patron saint of aviation, protects aviators. It exhibits a unique collection in Italy of dozens of uniforms complete with the Regia Aeronautica, largely original and in some unique cases, and hundreds of pieces from the birth of the Regia Aeronautica to today.
The churches of the lower city.

The ancient parish church of San Cassiano stood outside the walls and existed in 1329; in 1583 the Municipality bought the land next to the shelter for a new church, finished in 1628 and dedicated to the Annunciation. In 1817 the parish passed from the diocese of Ivrea to that of Turin.
The sculpted facade and the statue of the patron.

Sacred art of the valley inside a medieval tower.
It houses an altarpiece by the painter Cesare Peruzzi.
The decorated loggia of the village and the palace that today houses the municipal offices.

The city's living room, once an urban stretch of the road to the Passo del Settimo: palaces with portals, coats of arms and balconies of families like the Salis, Palazzo Pestalozzi-Salis of the sixteenth century where Ludovico Castelvetro died, the Piazza Ploncher with the stone of the gogna and sixteenth-century frescoed houses; traces of the walls remain.
Tratto della via consola carved for 221 meters in the living rock, which culminates in an arched passage 4 meters high; in the Middle Ages the arch was the door of the village.

It was identified with the castle, a fortified residence built overhanging the coast in a defensive position and present in the Torino cadastre of 1759-1760; it is believed that the Marquis Luigi Malaspina has redone it at the end of the eighteenth century giving it its current appearance. The Marquis, who spent the autumn holiday in it, accommodating poets and Lombards, provided it with an English garden with waterfall, temple, pond and a cenotaph dedicated to the poet Sannazzaro, and a private theater. It is private property: it can be seen from the outside.
Church of ancient origin founded by the Farfensian monks and much remodelled over the centuries; it preserves a crucifix considered miraculous, celebrated in August with the feast of the Crucifix.
From Cala Nave, walking on the cliffs, you reach the lighthouse with a view of the ancient port and the Roman fish ponds dug into the volcanic tuff, visible also in snorkeling.
A 19th century theatre intact for one night at the opera.
Next to the stairway of San Giovanni, dedicated to the local textile tradition.
The seaside village of ...Sapore di sale.

The Renaissance Oratory of San Sebastiano (XVI century), with the bell tower rebuilt after the earthquake of 1887, was the provisional seat of the Glass Museum until 2004. The oratory of San Rocco, erected in 1590 and originally dedicated to Saint Filiberto abbot, protector of glassmakers, was retitled after the plague of 1628-1631 and restored in 2008: it preserves the statues of the two saints, and the seventeenth-century one of San Rocco comes out in procession on 16 August.
Fossil fauna until about two million years ago, including a Pliocene cetacean found in Allerona.
Magna Grecia before and after Sibari.

On the second floor of the Tower of Tubre (door of the church), since 2011 a permanent exhibition on the life and works of Paul Flora, graphic designer and illustrator born in Glorenza who for about 25 years designed cartoons for "Die Zeit"; he lived mainly in Innsbruck, but Glorenza remained his point of reference.
The Klimt stolen and found.
The historical garden with two loggias: the Loggia Valmarana, perhaps designed by a pupil of Palladio, and the loggia built by Baldassarre Longhena in 1649.
The medieval symbol of the village.
Perhaps of Byzantine origin, with Baroque interior, recently restored.

Museum of furniture and culture in Valligiana: documentation centre on the furnishings and culture of the valleys, with objects and furniture that show how the valley populations conceived their home. It also hosts temporary themed exhibitions. Opening hours on request (tel. 0121 800716).
MiC card reports every day closed, opening to be checked
You can see at a glance the idea of an ideal city.

Daunia, Roman and early Christian city on the Ofanto: Hellenistic hypogeas and their furnishings in the National Archaeological Museum, the park of San Leucio with the temple of Minerva and the basilica, and the mausoleum of Boemondo next to the cathedral of San Sabino.
The castle of the poet Isabella Morra.

The house that Giorgio Vasari, born in Arezzo in 1511, bought and frescoed between 1542 and 1548: a rare example of the late Renaissance artist's house, with about fifty paintings of the Florentine Gallerie.
Kalsa Museum site which is part of the Regional Interdisciplinary Gallery of Sicily together with Palazzo Abatellis and Palazzo Mirto.
The Baroque altar with the ancon of Pietro Ramus.
The metro cathedral in the heart of Bari Vecchia, a splendid example of Romanesque Apulian, not far from the castle.
Jerusalem in miniature in Pusteria.
The hospital founded according to tradition in 1277 and active until 2013, with the glazed terracotta frieze of the Works of Mercy of Santi Buglioni and the history of Pistoiese health care.
Neoclassical theater on Piazza del Popolo, with a theatrical season.
Franciscan Gothic on the Black.
Ruins and views of the valley.

In the woods of oaks, maples and chestnut trees near the village, the Franciscan monastery founded according to tradition in 1223, when St. Francis was still alive, with fourteenth-century cloister with arches; from 1423 it bears the name of Blessed Giansante Biancorsini, who lived there since 1362, whose body rests in a golden urn of the eighteenth century. During World War II, some 300 people, including many Jews, found refuge there.
The village that inspired the painters.
The religious reference of the village.
Two works of Bramantino in a hamlet church.

In the parish, he exhibited the Treasure of Santa Maria Maddalena, a former vote of the faithful with Gallura jewels from the 16th to the 18th century, statues, paintings, tapestries and vestments, and the altar furnishing donated by Admiral Nelson: three neoclassical silvers made in 1804 in Barcelona, with autograph letters. Open all year round from Monday to Friday 10-13.30; afternoons and weekends by reservation.

Complex nuraghe on a hill above the marina of Sarrala and Foxi Manna: central tower at tholos of the beginning of the Middle Bronze (XV century BC) with three secondary towers added up to the 11th century BC, in granite boulders. The inner chamber has about 4,5 m of diameter and 8 m of height, with two niches to ogiva; on the slope remains of a village not excavated. You get there by leaving the car and continuing on foot on a path.
The ruins of the first Norman monastery.
Completely renovated in 1804, it preserves the Romanesque crypt and some sculptures on the façade that were part of the original rose window.
The island is understood only by the sea.
Parish church of the second half of the sixteenth century, on the way to the Formazza Valley, with stuccoes and Baroque decorations of the eighteenth century.
Perfect with the kids.
The oldest tower in the village, surviving the monastery.
Fortified village with the abbey of Santa Maria Assunta of 1092 and crypt of the tenth century, in the regional park.
The Sculptor of the Bagnanti.

Church of the ancient monastery, mentioned already in 1027, before 1180 and 1223, dates engraved on the ambo and on the altar; declared national monument in 1902. You can visit with the same service as the oratory of San Pellegrino.
Keys to read the valley.
Overlooking a small irregular square, the current building dates back to 1759; the bell tower is obtained from a medieval tower of the walls and inside there is a medieval sarcophagus.
Nature and movement.
The history of Castel Goffredo between water, Gonzaga and weaving.
Towers against pirates.
The sacred art of the Council.

Mountain centre in the heart of the Regional Park of the Serre, born around the Certosa founded by Bruno di Colonia, the first Carthusian monastery in Italy. The old town, rebuilt after the earthquake of 1783, has carved granite portals and late Baroque churches, among fir woods and beech trees crossed by the Frassati Path to the sanctuary of Santa Maria del Bosco.
The mountain blacksmith's workshop, intact.
The artists' villa.

The 11th century Abbey, documented since 1037; preserves a Madonna with Child by Ruggero da Todi (1295). The original portal was sold in the 1930s and today it is at the Metropolitan Museum in New York; the on-site one is a 1967 copy.
The trulli still inhabited, away from the crowd.

Built in Norman times by Count Riccardo in 1134 and rebuilt by the Aragonese, who gave him Catalan traits. In the fifteenth century it passed to the feudalist Giovanni Antonio Petrucci; confiscated, it was donated to Consalvo de Cordova and then passed to the Capua, the Grillo and the marquisa of Clarafuente, wife of the prince of Angri. Today the ruins remain, with an imposing tower, decorations wanted by the sovereigns of Naples and frames in tuff.
On the tower a bas-relief dated 1504 with the rampant lion, symbol of Frederick II.
An industrial history along the river.
It houses a 17th-century canvas by Vincenzo Manenti; VisitLazio indicates it as a stop not to be missed.
The shrine of the miraculous canvas of San Domenico.
The Abruzzo peasant world and a medieval mill.
A photo of the UNESCO heritage vineyards.

Country on the western side of Monte Arci, on the largest Sardinian deposit of obsidian, exploited by the 6th millennium BC: the Obsidian Museum, the only monothematic museum in Europe dedicated to this rock, the paths between the ancient workshops of Sennixeddu, the obsidian sculptures in the squares and jewelry shops.
Under the church of Santa Prisca all'Aventino, the sanctuary of Mitra discovered in 1934 and destroyed around 400 A.D.; visits by reservation, currently suspended for valorization works.
The fifteenth-century Casa dei Nani, the oldest in Orta, Palazzo Gemelli with frescoed facades with mythological subjects and the eighteenth-century Palazzo De Fortis Penotti (Ubertini).

Renaissance village of the Abruzzo Apennines, with the Collegiate Church of Santa Maria del Colle with five aisles, sixteenth-century palaces, the Museum of lace in Palazzo Fanzago and the beech wood of Sant'Antonio in the Majella Park.
The viewpoint overlooking the Cinque Terre.
The ancient plebanic church, religious heart of the territory for over a thousand years.

In the Regional Natural Park of Veio (about 15,000 hectares on the territory of the ancient Etruscan city, crossed by the Via Francigena), the Valle del Sorbo is a Site of Community Interest between Campagnano and Formello with small waterfalls, streams, oaks and meadows; there stands the Mola, water mill built by the Orsini in the fourteenth century and active until 1950.
The triumphal gate of the baroque city.
Gallura granite in every way.

Gothic tower of about 50 meters built in 1353 by the Masters Comacini at the crossroads of three streets: born as a bell tower of the church of Santa Maria del Trivio, it was separated in 1622; damaged by the bombings of the Second World War, was rebuilt.

The medieval nucleus is built on a pre-existing fortified structure; the houses have stone portals built between the seventeenth and nineteenth centuries by local stonemasons. In Piazza Tommaso Campanella the monument to the philosopher, who stayed in the Dominican monastery; between the noble residences Palazzo Pancaro (16th century) and Palazzo Giacobini, an ancient hospital called "home of pilgrims" (1584).
From July 28, 2021 the porticos are World Heritage: 12 sections chosen from 62 km of the city. The Pavaglione, next to San Petronio, is the most central stretch.
Prehistoric Saharan Selci in Lomellina.
Red rocks and coves.
An open-air street art museum in Irpinia.
A solitary church carved into the rock and decorated with frescoes, a precious treasure chest nestled among the rocks, reachable with a short detour from the abbey of San Vincenzo al Volturno.
A kiss downtown.

It is located in the former church of San Rocco, a renovated seventeenth-century building, and tells the trade of the anchovies of the Maira Valley with testimonies from Dronero, Celle di Macra, Macra and Paglieres. Three sections: the anchovies (clothes, instruments, posters), fishing and the transport of fish (a lampara, chests and the typical cart), trade of anchovies (documents and municipal registers of the nineteenth century); closes a video with interviews with anchovies and ex anchovies. It is part of the Ecomuseum Alta Valle Maira; according to the Municipality is open on Sundays from 23 June to 1 September (10-12, 14-18), otherwise on request (tel. +39 0171 999190).
The old prisons of the farmhouse.
A theater of stage paintings in the square.
You only enter with the guide on weekends.

The Roman city of Altinum extended for about a square kilometre, with hole, basilica, theatre, amphitheatre and spa; after the invasions of the seventh century the inhabitants took refuge in the islands of the lagoon, especially in Torcello. Today in Altino you can visit two open-air archaeological areas, one just a few steps from the museum; the ticket is that of the Archaeological Park (museum and area).

Born at the end of the 12th century as a boundary stronghold between the judges of Cagliari and Arborea, it was fortified in 1355 by the will of Peter IV of Aragon and in 1409 it was conquered by the Spaniards after a decisive clash; it has a square plan of 26 m on the side, walls 12 m high and four crenellated angular towers. In the twentieth century General Nino Villasanta restored it and transformed it into a home museum: today it houses the study of the general with the correspondence with D'Annunzio, the Gondi halls, the Salone delle Milizie with the Tricolore della Vittoria and the Bulletin della Vittoria signed by Diaz, it rises on the world wars and the countryside of Africa, the feudal district and a collection of waxes between the sixteenth and nineteenth century, indicated as the largest in Europe. It is not certain that Eleonora d'Arborea stayed there.
Porta Casale e Porta Licinia, probably fourteenth century, and Porta Sant'Egidio, built between the late eighteenth and mid nineteenth century next to Porta Sant'Antonio, today Porta Nuova.
The Merano of Russian holidaymakers.
Flat pedaling.
The gifts of Sixtus V and two tables by Vittore Crivelli.

An agricultural and holiday country of the high Varaita Valley, at the confluence of the valleys of Chianale and Bellino, which takes its name from Castrum Delphini built in 1330 by the last Dolphin Umberto II; it is the gate of the Bosco dell'Alevé, the largest Decemberta of the Alps, with its center visit, the ethnographic museum and the open-air museum of the "Santi del popolo" (Saints of the People).
Giant course, Italia.it
The truest Rome.

The square is surrounded by the public buildings of the Venetian era: the Dogana of the XIV century, the Monte di Pietà founded in the sixteenth century with a rare moeca  "Leon" above the door (now seat of the IAT office), the municipal loggia of the XVI century, remaking of the Gothic foundation, and the Town Hall with inscriptions and sixteenth-century coats of arms of the Podestà; near there is the small Piazza Beccaro with frescoed facades.

Romanesque church of the second half of the 12th century, dated also thanks to a seal of Barisone II, Judge of Torres, found inside in 1831; a single nave with apse, in limestones with basalt inserts with bichrome effect, sailing bell tower and hanging arches. Partly demolished at the beginning of the 19th century, it was restored in 1982 with the reconstruction of the southern side and the wooden roof.

From the avant-garde of the twentieth century to the Middle Ages, with archaeological section, futurist works, ceramic deco, furniture and paintings by Manlio Trucco, Albisole's pharmacy vases and in the garden La Battle of Agenore Fabbri of 1948.

In front of the small church of the Madonna di Galloro in the hamlet of Sant'Angelo, an oak over 21 meters high with circumference of 6.8 meters and estimated age over 600 years, considered the largest tree in Italy of its species.
The tower of poetry.
The Palace of the Gardens in the Doge's Garden Estense, home of exhibitions of the Fondazione Modena Arti Visive.
The cathedral of the city, among the churches indicated on the visit of Sulmona.
Along the Noncello, meadows, groves and humid areas suitable for birdwatching.
The Baroque altar in wood and mother of pearl and the lions of 1264.

The Baroque cathedral, the main church of the city; in the bishop's palace next to the diocesan museum with sacred works of art and Neolithic finds from the Pule, and the library of the seminary in a frescoed hall at the end of the nineteenth century, with over 40,000 volumes and the Red Book of town history (1323-1507).
The Mysteries of the Flemish Rosary.
A lake in the Nebrodi beech forests.
Next to the fortress, with a wooden crucifix made by a young Michelangelo.
A symbolic peak of World War I, for experienced hikers.

Stone houses on the hill of the Fortress with plant around the Mille; in via Frangipani the Palazzaccio, ancient Palazzo dei Priori with the clock tower, and the Baronial Palace where lived Pietro and Ludovico Frangipane in the fifteenth century; the church of Sant'Egidio has the apse in the ancient walls. At the foot of the village Piazza Vecchia (Piazza Matteotti), from which the village grew after the discovery of the alum, and the Panetti palaces (courtyard with octagonal cistern), Buttaoni (loggia on three levels) and Celli.

About 3 km from the village stood a fortified village, abandoned between the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries for unknown causes (perhaps war or plague); its church became a shrine, long officiated by a hermit and also used as a cemetery, and in the mid fifteenth century begged Blessed George of Biandrate. The pilgrimage, linked to the feast of Our Lady on July 2nd, then joined the pilgrimage of Pasquetta. Free entry during functions.
Church mentioned for the first time in 1135 and built in several phases.
It occupies the south half of Piazza Sant'Oronzo: of Augustan age, excavated from 1900 by Cosimo De Giorgi for about a third, national monument since 1906; the rest is still under the square.
The tower with the olive tree on top.
Among the largest travertine caves in Italy, with a waterfall.
Tarquinia Cathedral.

Water mill of 1750 in the center of the village, still moved by the Riu Mannu that flows under the building and able to grind wholemeal flour. The halls, ordered by master Bruno Murtas, exhibit tools of the peasant house, of the shepherds and of the crafts (brands for the cattle, wooden, cork and iron measures, tools for cheese, weaving and bread, furnishings, accessories and toys) and two vehicles of the late nineteenth century, an ox-cart and a carriage. Tuesday-Sunday, with seasonal hours (July-August 10-13 and 15-19); wheelchair accessible entry.
Extensive delights owned by the Municipality, with three hectares of park, along the Ring of the Borgia by bike.

In the historic House of the Pretura, tools and objects of use of the Upper Brembana Valley with rebuilt living environments, to understand how farmers and artisans have adapted their instruments over the centuries; tickets to the Pro Loco.

Umbrian village on the Tiber Valley, linked to the leader Bartolomeo d'Alviano and dominated by the castle Doria Pamphili, now town hall and seat of three museums; at the foot of the artificial lake born in 1963 with the dam on the Tiber, today WWF oasis of about 900 hectares loved by birdwatchers.
Portals carved in slate in the alleys.

Parish church built at the end of the eighteenth century on a 14th century church; it was once the cathedral of the village. It preserves the medieval retablo of Saint Anne, attributed to the Master of Sanluri.
The river that disappears in the mountain.
The 18th century parish church on the site of the castle.
Built by the Sforza on the Strona stream at the turn of the fifteenth century, it has a sharp sixth arch and a low one, with the central stack resting on a rock in the stream.
15th century bridge with sharp arches on the Scrivia stream.
