Tenth century complex with Romanesque church, medieval cloister of the XI-XIII and two bell towers, a Norman and a Baroque maiolic; for centuries home of mitrated abbesses, it houses the museum with the artifacts of the city from prehistory to late antiquity.

H-shaped villa in the forms of the mid-nineteenth century, with sections of an eighteenth-century farmhouse, wrought iron balconies, rooms with decorated wooden ceilings, marble fireplaces and precious furniture, in a vast park with centuries-old oaks and chestnut trees. The lawyer and politician Achille Marazza left it to the Municipality; it houses the Achille Marazza Foundation, whose library preserves books, prints, parchments, incunabula, five hundred and ancient medals, with a section of local history from Piedmont-Lombardy from the sixteenth century to today.

Designed by Francesco Gallo, master of the Monregal Baroque, it has a floor in local quartzite ('Bargiolina'), portal and niche in Piedmontese Baroque (the statue of the Baptist was placed there in 1911); Romanesque bell tower and baptismal font remain of the oldest building.

Castle built in the 12th century, seat of the Counts of Mede and then of the Sangiuliani. In the center of the village are still sections of the walls of the XIV-XV century, an elegant loggia of the following period and a crenellated tower; today it houses the Masinari library and the civic museums.
A home lived, not a cold museum.

Porcelain dolls, automata and ancient mechanical toys, exhibited in the eighteenth century Villa Cutò (Aragona Cutò), recognizable for the elegant five-arched loggia. Times indicated by the source: Tuesday-Friday 9-13 and 15.30-18.30, Saturday and Sunday 9-13, Monday closed.

On the hill of the church of Santa Valburga documents the human presence in the area from the stone to the iron age, with the replica of a sacrificial altar; the surrounding site preserves one of the largest collections of human remains of the region, from the 6th century BC. Next to the F'Hochhaus, a fifteenth-century log house moved and rebuilt, where coins, dice, forks and a 15th-century deck of playing cards have emerged, perhaps the oldest cards from .Watten in South Tyrol; outside traditional crops. Open from mid-May to late October.

Ring path suitable for all that starts from the church of Casale, on the slopes of Monte Pranzà, and crosses the chestnut grove with picnic areas and benches; Casale is known for the via delle Castagne and the panorama of the valley up to Pizzo Arera.
The light of the valley.
Eight centuries of sacred architecture in a few steps.

Built between 1813 and 1830 on the circular tower Mirabella of the walls of Rocha Magna, it measures about 92 meters including the statue of San Fedele of 7 meters; it is indicated as the highest bell tower of the circular base of Europe. Rebuilt after a fire of 1893, it has the current statue since 1896; on the wall is carved the lion of St Mark, sign of Venetian rule since 1428. The ascent, with internal and external stairs, offers views of the old town and the Oglio.

The village descends with steep streets to the lake; in the center the church of San Giovanni Battista, indicated as the oldest of Varenna. Along the lake promenade, between the old town and the boat, a poem by David Maria Turoldo dedicated to Varenna; the Hotel Royal Victoria recalls the unknown stay of Queen Victoria in 1838, and Villa Mapelli was the residence of Luisa Campioni Venini, dedicated to Piccolo mondo antico di Fogazzaro. An itinerary of about 1 km on the ground floor, from Villa Monastero to the lakefront, takes about an hour.
The fortress extended in the center, today seat of the municipality, with the hanging garden and the tombstones of memory.
Polia's sculptor came home.
Contemporary art house and headquarters of the Lecchese Alpine Observatory with interactive stations.

One of the last stretches of unbuilt coast of the Gulf of Gaeta, between the Aurunci Mountains and the sea, with hills up to 123 meters of Monte di Scauri, broom and cyst spot, Aleppo pines on the cliffs and a cork grove; the butterfly Charaxes jasius flies there. Along the promontory, the remains of the villa of Mamurra, a formian knight and engineer of Caesar, with cisterns and caves are covered for hundreds of metres; part of the coast is a protected marine area.
The medieval bridge of legend.

Rebuilt in 1732 with the stones of the demolished castle, designed by Ticino Giovanni Maria Borsotto; inside a Via Crucis of the Mantua Lanfranco and a table with the Madonna delle Grazie with figures in relief.
Built in 1619, they preserve an altarpiece of 1618 by Gherardo delle Notti and a group of the Nativity of 1633.
The symbol of Trevico, still linked to the rites of the country.
€4, reduced €2; cumulative with the museum €6, reduced €2
Founded in 1977 by naturalist Pietro Parenzan, since 1993 in the premises of the sixteenth century former abbey of Santa Margherita.

Documented from the 12th century, rebuilt in 1280 with the union of the Cistercian monastery of Casanova and modified in the mid-500s by the abbot Giovanni Battista Umbriani of Capua (apse octagona, portico, raised bell tower); single nave with transversal arches of Cistercian type and golden altar with polychrome statues of the 17th century. The walls are covered by cycles of fifteenth-century frescoes; in contrast to the Judgment of the late 1920s of the fifteenth century, with the "bridge of the hair" that souls cross to enter Paradise, is among the most important paintings of Abruzzo.
Benedictine shrine on a cliff just off the city, among the most photographed places in Tropea.
The highest water jump in the Grigne.

Ancient Borgo Franco founded by Bologna on the Via Emilia and home of the legend of the tortellino: the portico center with the archaeological museum Simonini and the churches of Santa Maria Assunta and San Giacomo, the romantic park of Villa Sorra, the towers of the castle of Piumazzo and the collection of vintage cars Righini at the castle of Panzano.

In the public gardens, with the busts of Vito Domenico Palumbo, De Santi and Gabrieli, there is a funeral stele in marble of the fourth century BC donated by Athens in 1960: it depicts Thanatos accompanying a young woman and bears the inscription in griko "Zeni esù en ise ettu" 'sti Kalimera" .

Church of the Confraternity of the Trinity built at the beginning of the seventeenth century, dedicated first to San Lorenzo and then also to the Exaltation of the Cross and San Felice: simple exterior, interior with rich Baroque decoration. In the nearby hamlet of Piatonia, the church of the Immaculate, erected around 1610 by the homonymous confraternity, has an airy interior with many vintage paintings and a remarkable high altar. Free entry during functions.
The medieval palace.

The University's historical collections: the Museum of Paleontology, born in 1776 at the behest of Duke Francesco III d'Este as part of the Museum of Natural History; the Museum of Zoology and Comparative Anatomy with about 3,500 naturalized vertebrates; the Museum of Human Anatomy with the anatomical theatre wanted according to the dictates of Antonio Scarpa and the first Italian anthropological collection; the Laboratory of mathematical machines with its geometric instruments.

Small village on Lake Orta, known for the tradition of turning the wood told in the museum made in an ancient tournament; to see the parish church with the Romanesque bell tower, the lake promenade and the hilly hamlets of Crabbia and Pratolungo.

A medieval wall of elliptical shape with original moat and towers of the gates up to 30 meters high; the walkway of the round, 15 meters high and almost two kilometers long, has been secured by a recent restoration and is entirely accessible. Along the tour you will find the Captain's House and the Tower of Malta, with views of Euganean Hills, Berici Mountains, Pedemontana and Monte Grappa. Hours: April-September 9-18, March and October 9-17, November-February 9-16; closed on 25 December.
Thirty-five hectares on the Capuchin and Cardeto hills, with maquis and views of the city, the Old Lighthouse, the Bastione San Paolo, the Castelfidardo Powderhouse and the Jewish Cemetery.

Established in 1996 on the south-western slopes of Amiata, it protects about 1,000 hectares on a series of peaks, the highest Poggio della Vecchia (1,086 m) and Civitella (1,107 m). Woods of ash, beech and oak, with the "Bosco della Fonte" (Bosco della Fonte) of great naturalistic interest and monumental chestnut trees near Selvena; there live buzzards, allocches, common owls, foxes, singers, wild boars and roe deer.
The cathedral of the historic center, near the Mensa Ponderaria.
The old town is spread between the Lombard castle and the church of San Francesco; in the alleys there are trattorias of traditional cuisine.
The abbey on the hill of Covignano, with the frescoes of Benedetto Coda and the Adoration of the Magi painted by Giorgio Vasari, who here in 1547 had his Lives copied.

City of Lomellina along the Via Francigena, traditionally linked to the battle of 773 between the Franks of Charlemagne and the Longobards of King Desiderio; the city symbol is the basilica of San Lorenzo with the Gothic façade and the paintings of Cerano, Lanino and Procaccini, while at the gates of the city stands the abbey of Sant'Albino. It is known for the Salame d'Oca di Mortara IGP and the Palio of late September.
The shrine of the water of the Nuragians.
The MiC card indicates the museum closed every day: check the opening with the Municipality (tel. 0827 32009).

Neoclassical palace of the first half of the nineteenth century, with two columns on high lava stone bases on the sides of the entrance. In the novel Mastro Don Gesualdo there is the wedding banquet of Gesualdo and Bianca Trao; the name La Gurna was chosen by Verga and is not that of the owners.
The submerged rock formation between Ostia and Torvajanica covered with marine organisms, marine protected area.
A Madonna from the Pinturicchio shop.

In the former Carmelite convent of Santa Maria de Senioribus, opened in 1990 and re-arranged in 2011, documents the palafittic villages of the Bronze Age of Garda and the Moorish amphitheatre: homes, agriculture, ceramics, metals, ornaments. The most famous piece is the Lavagnone plough, found in 1978, oak with beech yoke, of about 2000 BC, with a dedicated room. Free on the first Sunday of the month and with the Museums Lombardy Subscription.
Secular oaks and views of Mount Etna.
The history of the castle majolica.

Mandrolisai and Brabaxianna country known for its artisan weaving, with red trachyte houses and murals with carpets: the MURATS textile art museum, the churches of San Sebastiano and San Basilio, the sanctuary of Santa Maria di Abbasassa and, among woods and gorges, the Byzantine Castle of Medusa.
Remains of a castle on the Sciliar massif, in a high and panoramic position; recommended visit period from April to November.

Museum of narration and not collections, multimedia and interactive, dedicated to the cultural landscape from the Julian Alps to the sea and to the history and currentity of the area in which they historically live the Slovenian provinces of Udine, Gorizia and Trieste, with interactive paths and multimedia frescoes; it is also center of documentation, archive and research. Admission fee according to the Touring; open daily, 10-13 and 14-16, with times that can change.
€6 whole; €4 reduced; free up to 12 years

The heart of the village is Piazza del Popolo, a lively square dominated by the great Fontana del Nettuno, called in the village  \u gigantiÂ, and surrounded by buildings and palaces including the Palazzo del Trono.
It dominates from the promontory of Marturano the ancient inhabited; destroyed by the earthquake of 1783, it was rebuilt in the nineteenth century on the ruins in a more solid form.
A masterpiece of the Romanesque Lombard.
View of the woods of the valley.

The sixteenth-century church of the Santa Maria district with portal of 1493; the cycle of main frescoes is by Vincenzo Tamagni and Giovanni da Spoleto (1516) and the left apse houses glazed terracottas of the sixteenth century. Around, Renaissance noble palaces.
The Baroque heart of the Lodron village.
APT Val di Sole: Wednesday 10-12 and Thursday 16-18; Trentino Grande Guerra indicates opening 2026 by reservation (tel. OJ L 347, 20.12.2013, p. 671.
The most beautiful castle in Radda territory.

Established in 1984 and part of the Archaeological Park of Gela, on two floors in Piazza Garibaldi tells the territory from prehistory to the Hellenistic age with the findings of the excavations 1977-1984: Neolithic ceramics and the bronze age, archaic indigenous ceramics of Greek forms often decorated with birds with fantails, two stele with Greek inscriptions by Balate, the accessories of the necropolis of Valle Oscura (VI century BC) and the Hellenistic one of Castellazzo with ceramic siceliotic red figures. Accessible with elevator.
A hidden cloister.

Eight hectares with about 1,300 plant species, a pond and streams among the ruins of the medieval town of Ninfa: castle, walls, churches and a restored town hall. Ninfa, bought by the Caetans in 1298, was destroyed under Barbarossa and again in 1382 and then abandoned; since 1921 Gelasio, Roffredo Caetani and Marguerite Chapin transformed it into a romantic garden, to which Lelia Caetani gave the present form. Regional natural monument since 2000, is managed by the Caetani Foundation; you can visit with guided tours from March to November according to annual calendar, with mandatory booking on gardendininfa.eu (save 10% for FAI subscribers).
Adventure park in an ancient oak wood, with picnic areas and five routes of increasing difficulty more baby and junior paths for families.
For the retablo of Sanluri Master.

Documented in 1084 and Parish since 1195, in the thirteenth century it was one of the most important of Parmense; it decayed after 1470 and in 1787 lost facade and first three spans. Rebuilt in the 13th century above a church of the 11th, it has three naves of seven spans and three apses, whose lower band is in Roman bricks of recovery; the restorations of 1967-72 brought to light the thirteenth-century structures. It rises isolated between fields and channels.
A baroque jewel of Vittone in the open countryside.
The Crucifixion of the pupil's workshop.
Fresh in the summer, in the woods of Amiata.
One of the great cathedrals of Marche.
The king's holiday castle.

Water jump between high rock walls, reachable in about an hour from the parking lot on the highway towards Rovereto through the forest of the Gon, or in a quarter of an hour walk from Guardia; in winter it is illuminated and becomes a monument of light and ice.
A rare early medieval architecture among olive trees.

It collects tools, customs and customs of the agricultural works of the territory, with captions and cards edited by Villarte and written in dialect to protect the local speech. Open from April to October on the first and third Sundays of the month, 14-17.
The municipal observatory and the museum dedicated to the astronomer born in Perinaldo.
12th century church with frescoes including a representation of the Divine Comedy with Dante and Virgilio.

Completed in the eighteenth century in place of the little church of Santa Maria del Bosco, cited in the mid-500s; a recent restoration brought to light eighteenth-century temperas and frescoes in the presbytery.

On the eastern hill rise the E temple, dedicated to Hera, of the middle of the fifth century BC and largely reassembled in the 1950s and 1960s; the F temple of the middle of the sixth century BC, perhaps dedicated to Dionysus; and the G temple, begun around 530 BC and never ended up destroying the city, among the greatest in the Greek world. The park, which the Region presents as the largest in Europe with 270 hectares, includes acropolis, necropolis and three hills.

The center revolves around St. John's Square, with the ancient Community Palace (the salon is visited only by permission), the medieval Provana del Sabbione Palace, the Borgovecchio Street and historical squares such as Carlo Alberto Square, Savoia Square and Liberation Square, called Piazza dell'Angelo. Among the houses stands the House of the Grand Bastardo Renato of Savoia, with terracotta ornaments and painting and sculptural decorations. The noble palaces cannot be visited inside.
Parish church of fifteenth century origin, renovated in 1731.
A medieval castle that contains an entire city.

In the Torrione, a sixteenth-century tower of sighting and defense against Turkish incursions about 12,67 metres high, built after the restoration of the castle of Barletta by the military architect Evangelista Menga (1540 approximately): over 150 paintings, sculptures and drawings by modern artists, including the Pastorello di Francesco Galante, painter of the Neapolitan school of the late nineteenth century, and reproductions of works by Raffaello, Masaccio and Guido Reni.
The Damini and the golden organ.
A walled village with views of the Valdinievole.
The cradle of culture in Italy.
Walking from square to square in Montefeltro.
Complex built for the Humble and passed to the Barnabites, today predominantly baroque.

The mountain (about 825 meters) rises from Piazza Carmine with a staircase of 183 steps in four ramps, between stations of the Via Crucis, the prison called Filippo D'Angiò and the bell ringed by pilgrims; on top the sanctuary built by Giovanni Chiaramonte in 1370 on the structures of the castle, with a Madonna enthroned between the Saints Damiano and Cosma by Filippo Tancredi and two reliquary urns (1498, with the bones of San Paolino; 1649, by Francesco Rivelo, with those of Sant'Onofrio), and the former convent of the Filippini Fathers. From the summit you can see 25 villages, the sea of Agrigento, the Madonie and Etna; climb about 30 minutes, visit about an hour.
The rampant horse comes from here.
Museum inside the sanctuary of the Madonna della Stella: it contains a bas-relief by Nicolò Speciale by Francesco Laurana and a triptych attributed to Antonello da Messina.
The baroque living room of Ortigia.
The ribbon village and its parish.

Medieval and Renaissance buildings alternate with small houses; the upper part goes back to the Norman foundation and the streets towards the castle are of medieval plant. Among the noble palaces with portals and carved balconies stands out Palazzo Bartimmo, with eighteenth-century portal and loggia with three arches; at the top of the village, behind the castle, the clock tower. There are also some remains of the fortress of 984, erected by the feudal Roberto del Torpo.

Liberty-style houses arranged in semicircle along the steep streets of the center; the parish church of San Sebastiano houses a Baroque wooden altar and the Rosary church is from the seventeenth century. From the main square you can see the valley and Mount Acuto.
The fortress from which the village was born, today home of the culture of the village.
It belongs to the lords of Quart, bought in the second half of the fourteenth century by Jean-Michel Piquart.

Palace between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries preserved in the original form: two floors on an entire block, portal in decentralized stone, double staircase from the garden and on the gate the coat of arms of the Jordan with two rampant lions, a palm tree and the inscription "Onofrius Giordanus 1613" . The rooms with frescoed ceilings and neoclassical motifs were the scene of historical events when Montefusco was the capital of the Principality Ultra; today it hosts events and exhibitions (and in part the barracks of the Carabinieri). Visit by reservation.
A sky painted with saints.
A theater inside the buildings.

Venue of the Town Hall in front of the Cathedral, built between 1742 and 1761 on a project by Vincenzo Sinatra, with portico of Ionic columns on three sides; inside the Hall of Mirrors, oval with stuccoes in Louis XV style; the upper floor was added in 1951.
A 14th century parish church overlooking the calanchi.

Temple of Hellenistic age dated to the third century BC, in a cult area frequented at least from the sixth century BC: almost square cell, access to steps flanked by two fountains fed by lead pipes, floors and painted walls. Votive deposits suggest a dedication to the goddess Mephyte; it was destroyed during the Second Punic War (about 217-215 BC). It is the only testimony of a Sannitic sacred building found in Irpinia.

A few minutes from the hamlet of Villanova Strisaili, the shores of the lake are frequented by hikers and mountain bikers and its waters as canoeists; in the surroundings the gorge of Pirincanes and the waterfalls of Rio 'e Forru, which are admired by a natural balcony.
The promenades with the noble palaces overlooking the river, to be seen at sunset; in June the Luminara of San Ranieri illuminates them with thousands of lights.
The theatre in the hall of the dukes.
The church overlooking the Dora.
The Theatre of Tergeste.
The Romanesque ruins of the village.

City of Murgia overlooking the deep ravine of the ravine: the bridge of the aqueduct that joins the two banks, the archaeological park of Botromagno, the Romanesque cathedral, the rock church of San Michele delle Grotte and the seventeenth-century palace of the Fondazione Pomarici Santomasi.
In San Bruno the municipality has set up a park with windmills: a historical-environmental path that continues the offer of the Museum of peasant civilization.
The Longobard roots of Cremona.

Neoclassical residence with influences of the late Sicilian Baroque, built at the end of the eighteenth century on a project by Giuseppe Venanzio Marvuglia for Ferdinando di Borbone, who chose the Ficuzza as a hunting reserve and summer holiday. The interiors have undergone plundering and transformations and remains only the chapel of the original style; today it houses thematic paths and a multimedia room on the nature of the reserve.
A medieval castle still readable.
€7 (reduced €5; free with FVGcard)
Panorama of the Aeolian Sea between rustic portals.

Impressive 16th century building that dominates the eastern side of the promontory of Terra Murata; in 1529 the village became a fief of the family of Avalos and between 1830 and 1988 the palace hosted a prison.
A Camaldolese hermitage over Fano.

The baptismal church of the city, begun in 1312 next to the disappearance Porta Sant'Andrea, in front of the Palazzo d'Arnolfo: classic façade with pediment and three arched porch on Tuscan columns decorated with rounds of Robbiana school, inside with a single nave with wooden cover.
A frescoed imperial villa a few steps from the center, far from the crowds of Pompeii.
In the territory of Casarza, there are pillows, geological formations that testify to ancient underwater volcanic eruptions.
The heroes and the fountain of youth.

In the upper part of the village remain the access tower, the walls and the watchtower in stone and brick; inside the walls the church of San Sebastiano wanted by Ferrante Gonzaga. The Fortress was demolished in 1600 and part of the castle destroyed by the French in the war of Spanish succession.
Built by the Caetani in the 14th century next to the Torre dei Templari, today it is the seat of the Town Hall; the courtyard is accessed by an arch on the right side of the square.
A monumental tree in the beech tree.
The story of Marshal Badoglio in his home country.
The Tuscan Province is in summer bloom.
A slow walk on the shore of the lake.

The municipality of the National Park of Vesuvius, known for its copper craftsmanship, St. Anastasia preserves the Sanctuary of Our Lady of the Arch, built between 1593 and 1610 around the miraculous image of 1450 and destination every Monday in Albis of the pilgrimage of the Fujenti.
Ancient fortified seaside village with pastel-coloured houses along the beach, with a Saracen style of influence.
The sundial of the astronomer Themistocle Zone.
The wealth of the merchant city.
The civic museum of natural history of Bra.
The pre-Roman walls in blocks without mortar.
The Vatican school apse mosaic.
An important example of the fifteenth century Piedmontese architecture, home to cultural events and exhibitions.
Walk inside the memory of the destroyed city.
The Mother of the Killed.
Church perhaps of the thirteenth century, enlarged in the fifteenth with Latin cross plan and late-Gothic decorations; in mid-January the fires of San Sebastiano anticipate the carnival.
A small historical theater in the province.

The capital of the Roman Camonica Valley after the conquest of 16 BC, preserves the archaeological park of the theatre and amphitheatre and, in the historic center, the National Archaeological Museum with the statue of Minerva from the shrine of Breno.
Middle Ages and Roman baths together.
The machines of essence.

On the outskirts of the village, a granite monolith almost three meters high decorated with concentric circles, curved sticks and 23 cups, symbols related to fertility and the death-rebirth cycle; Italy.it dates it to 3000 BC and is perhaps coeval of the necropolis of Istevene.
The gateway to the Park trails.

The main square is closed by Palazzo Campanelli, Palazzo Comunale and Palazzo Montani; along the walls runs Via Limbo, with arches and medieval vaults. Porta da Monte, west entrance, still bears the coat of arms of Ascoli, from which the village depended until 1292; from the Belvedere Don Giuseppe Caselli the panorama spans the Marche and Abruzzo Apennines.
Ruins with views of the Sciliar.
Church built in 1572, just outside Porta Rastrella in the southern part of the village, where according to tradition a pilgrim saw a star stopping for three days on an image of the Madonna.

Village of the Moorish hills linked to the battle of June 24, 1859, which inspired Henry Dunant the foundation of the Red Cross: on the hill the Rocca Spia d'Italia, the Risorgimento Museum, the Ossario Chapel and the Red Cross Memorial.
The oldest Romanesque church in the Bormida Valley.
Museum set up at the Istituto tecnico industriale "Montani."
The eighteenth-century paintings of Giacinto Diana.
The frescoed Byzantine baptistery.

Romanesque church built in 1126 by Chiebizo, Wariento and Annone, as a façade inscription recalls; born with three naves, in the fifteenth century it was reduced to a single nave and enriched with the stone portal and the rose window. Inside there are frescoes, altars, a saint's waterworks of 1412 and an ancient wooden image of Our Lady; on the third Sunday of Lent there is the secular Festival of Bastia. Open on Monday afternoon for the 17:00 Mass and for events.

14th-century church with Romanesque-Gothic façade and 14th-century stone rosette, wooden choir in walnut from the 15th century and a single Baroque nave; part of the former convent houses the town hall.
The lost origins of the country.
The only original door left of the walls of the 12th century, in Lanciano Vecchia; traces of the walls remain in Civitanova and Lanciano Vecchia.
The largest of the four coastal lakes of the Circeo National Park, connected to the sea by two canals; the largest brackish lake in the province.
At the exit of Borgo Stretto.
Small 18th-century church with a majolica terracotta floor with a fine marble portal, probably coming from a more important church and destroyed.
The port fish market, one of the most important in Italy.
Contemporary art in a 17th century palace.
The great blue lake under the Brenta Dolomites.
A nuragic village of 200 huts overlooking the sea.
White sand and services for everyone.
Church of thirteenth century origin with facade, trifora and bell tower in tuff.
Medieval trade intact.
Waterfalls and a Roman bridge in the woods.
Nature a stone's throw from the center.

Tratto dell'Alta via dei Monti Picentini: 11.5 km from the Piana del Dragone (687 m) in Campolaspierto (1307 m), with 1120 m climb and 520 m descent, EE difficulty, about 6 hours. It passes through the source of Acqua delle Logge (1250 m), the Porta di Annibale, the summit of Monte Termino (1806 m), Colle Lungo and the Rifugio degli Uccelli, between chestnut woods and beech woods.

On the hill of San Pietro, obtained from the temple of Apollo of the third century BC, converted to worship in the sixth century and expanded in the twelfth with three aisles, apse and crypt. It preserves an ambo and an iconostasis cosmates of the 13th century with inlays in porphyry and numerous graffiti; damaged by the earthquake of 1915, it was restored in 1955-57. Visit by reservation required (340 6255973).
Read the hour on a sundial as big as a square.
The open-air set by Don Camillo and Peppone.
The city between two rivers.

Palaces noble of the village, many built in the eighteenth-nineteenth century after the earthquake of 1694 that destroyed much of the village; one of the Laviano palaces was designed by Piacentini. In the village there are also neoclassical portals.
The defenses against the corsairs, with a view to the rooftops.
The castle where Dante took refuge in exile: you enter from the Lion Gate, in the courtyard a scenic staircase leads to the large frescoed hall; from the bell tower overlooking the whole valley.
Civic, archaeological and sacred art museum in a 14th-century palace, with wooden sculptures by Francesco di Valdambrino and a large mosaic of the 4th century A.D.
The cave of the patron hermit, among the Fortresses.
It contains paintings and frescoes, a 17th century wooden crucifix and a wooden choir.

Ancient Canossian court of the Bassa Reggiana, then fortified outpost of the Municipality of Reggio and from 1432 of Gonzaga: the fortress with the mast of 1242, Martiri Square with the eighteenth-century theater Giovanni Rinaldi, the art collection of Antonio Ruggero Giorgi in town hall and the valleys reclaimed towards Novellara.
In the footsteps of the young Father Pio.
The Romanesque on the square of Maderno.

In the ancient warehouses of salt at Linguella, next to the Martello Tower, finds of Elba and the Tuscan islands from the end of the 8th century BC to the 5th century AD; a few steps away the remains of the Roman villa of Linguella.

Along the course the palaces Giampietro (with medieval courtyard), Colamico, Sozj, Ursini and Coppa Zuccari; further on the Baronial Palace, the oldest noble residence of the village. Alleys, churches and views of the sea and mountains.
Museum-interactive printing laboratory in the hamlet of Mine, with presses, lead and wood characters and lithographic stones used in laboratories for all ages.
Memorial park near the Garibaldi Museum, with the ara-hosary of the fallen Garibaldi. Every 3 November in the square is celebrated the anniversary of the battle.

Parish of the diocese of Alba, mentioned for the first time in 1635 and described in the visits of 1644 and 1730; it was rebuilt in 1662 and partially rebuilt in 1956. In the seventies of the twentieth century the presbytery had a structural intervention and in 2015-2016 the cover was restored.

Also known as San Pietro al Camposanto, it is the oldest church in the territory, probably before the thousand: born as parish of the village of Fenestrella, it then became a cemetery church. Rectangular hall with semicircular apse, façade with stone and brick bands and frame with woven hanging arches; the side walls were raised in bricks around 1690.

The eighteenth-century villa, formerly the residence of the Duke of Atri, on a hill above Piazza Santa Restituta in front of Monte di Vico; in 1952 the publisher and producer Angelo Rizzoli, who collected rare plants from the five continents, from the domestic pines symbol of Ischia to jacaranda, ginkgo and eucalyptus. The garden is visited with the museum; in the villa the Museo Angelo Rizzoli exhibits more than 500 photographs of the years when Ischia became the destination of politicians, divines and journalists.
An intact Orvieto castle in its walls.
The shrine of lovers.
€27 in low season, €32 in high season; €38-42 with the Ferrari Museum in Maranello

In the historic centre remain the walls of the ancient castle of the Counts of the Castle, lords of Agrate in the 11th century, partly destroyed in the 15th century; the intact coat of arms remains. At the bottom of Vicolo Castello you can see the three-level tower-door with a portal in sharp arched brick. It is private property, visible only from the outside.
Seat of the Captains of the Mountain until the sixteenth century.
Basilica that preserves frescoes, pulpit and baptismal font of the eighteenth century; the statue of the saint is carried in procession on the patronal feast of mid-September.
The heart of the UNESCO Rolli site.
The town square between neoclassical and style porticos.
The doors of the oldest Calcidian colony in Sicily.
Romanesque-Gothic church with carved reliefs, a reed organ of 1758 and the retablo of Our Lady of Itria.
The building cut in two by a gallery.
The oldest party in the village.
The history of Diano in stone and sacred art.
In the cumulative Diocese (5 monuments)
Bernardo Buontalenti's loggia next to the clock tower, one of the most famous views of Pisa on the Arno.
It hosts 25 local citrus species, with the citrus case.
The park of the villa.
Valtellina peasant life and vestments donated by Richelieu.
The symbol of Taormina, between pebble beach and garden.
Modern art of the South.
Antiquarium at the Hermitage Park centre, with workshops, which exhibits the main findings of the Gothic settlement (V-VI century) excavated on the mountain.
A Romanesque bezel in the heart of the village.
A bell tower of 86 meters that dominates the whole Wine Road.
The balcony of Taormina, magical at sunset.
Public area of over 40,000 square meters on the right bank of the Enza, frequented mainly in summer.
Tuscan Mezzadria and a doctor between science and Freemasonry.
The walls that resisted Taranto and Archidamo.
private property ruin (MiC)
The tombstone of the gift of Valentine's Day.
A cycle of 17th century frescoes in a restored country church.

The promenade runs around the water mirror where recreational boats and a fleet of fishing boats live together, keeping alive the marine tradition: the arrival of boats loaded with fish in the middle of the afternoon is a must-see sight, and the shrimps of Santa Margherita are a local specialty. Around the boutique, bar for the aperitif and beaches of the area Ghiaia, the most beautiful near the center.
Giovanni Battista Giovenale's 1901 villa, baroque with Liberty contaminations, home of the museum for decorative arts.

Village of the upper Sagittarius Valley, between Valle Peligna and Marsica, fortified in the 12th century and known as the town of snakes for the Serpari Rite: every May 1st the statue of San Domenico Abate parades for the village covered with live snakes. To see the historic center with the district of San Nicola and its medieval tower, the Sanctuary of San Domenico, the church of Santa Maria delle Grazie and the museum-center studies dedicated to popular traditions.

Città dell'Università della Calabria along the Crati, with the medieval historic centre on the hill called "Borgo dei Musei": the Norman castle of 1095, the churches of Santa Maria Maggiore and the Rosary and art museums from the sixteenth century to the contemporary.
Fortified village at 701 meters, with stone houses, whose castle was destroyed by the Bolognese in 1271; in the nearby nucleus of the Fontanini there are late medieval houses.
A baroque church born of one vote.
The cathedral dedicated to St. Procolo martyr, built over an ancient Temple of Augustus on the Earth Rion.
A walled village remained intact.

Locality at the entrance of the Riviera di Ponente, about 20 km from Genoa, at the foot of Mount Beigua: a historic center overlooking the sea, long beaches, the park of Villa Negrotto Cambiaso with peacocks, the Sanctuary of the Child of Prague on the hill and the cycling track to the sea up to Varazze.
Arch of rock near the mouth of Mingardo, on the border with Camerota, which is a passage towards a tongue of fine golden sand on the Tyrrhenian Sea; from the beach you can see the Rabbit's Scoglio.
The Franciscan frescoes.

Country of granite on the plateau of Mount Acuto, about 750 m between pastures and corks, with about 60 domus de janas and 32 nuraghi: the necropolis of Ludurru at the gates of the village, the nuraghe Loelle along the road to Bitti and the sculptures of the Wood Symposium and the Granite scattered along the streets.
An easy view of the lake and Salaria.
€3 whole, €2 reduced, €1 children
The work of the intelvese masters in the church of their country.
The most spectacular spring in Sardinia.
The city's most elegant streets.
A large monastery among the olive trees.

Home gallery set up as a permanent exhibition by Carlo Battista Castellini, carpenter of Bornato who collects nativity scenes since childhood: over a thousand pieces from more than 130 countries. The group Nativity scenes of the World was born in December 1998; during the Christmas period the collection is opened as an event, during the year it is visited on request telephone (030 725385, 348 7800332). Entry not accessible in wheelchair.
In the fourteenth-century church of St. Nicholas, mosaics from antiquity to contemporary, with the sections Mosaics between Hell and Paradise and the Genius of Waters.

A common place between the hills of Versilia and the lake of Massaciuccoli, stop of migratory birds protected by the LIPU Oasis; on the shores of the lake the archaeological area of Massaciuccoli Romana with the villa of Venulei, on the hills the Romanesque parish church of San Pantaleone in Elici, the village of Gualdo and 27 noble villas, including Villa Baldini linked to Paolina Bonaparte.

The Baroque town of Val di Noto, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2002: Ragusa Ibla with the Cathedral of San Giorgio di Rosario Gagliardi, the Ibleo Garden and dozens of churches; the cathedral of San Giovanni and the archaeological museum; the Castle of Donnafugata in the countryside.
The oldest hamlet of Verezzi, which seems to be dug into the rock, with caves on the side of the hill inhabited already in the Paleolithic and the main religious buildings.
A stop in the streets of the center.

Ancient Roman post station on the Popilia street, made famous by the novel of Carlo Levi        .Cristo stopped in Eboli , the historic center develops between the Longobard castle and the church of San Francesco, in whose former convent is located the National Archaeological Museum of the Middle Sele Valley.
A fishing village with its Romanesque oratory.
The history of the straw hats of Signa, produced on an industrial scale from the eighteenth century to the fifties.
A fifteenth-century altar in a small oratory.
The Longobard castle on the highest hill, from which the village was born.
A Renaissance jewel signed by Raffaello's father.
Two squares from the paved worked in the area of the ancient castle of the Marquises of Clavesana (XI century), of which traces remain, between caruggi and houses united by archivolti.

It dates back to about 1100 and is perhaps the oldest church in the country, with stone walls with fishbone and semicircular apse. In the apse frescoes between the late fifteenth and early sixteenth century: Christ in almond with the symbols of the Evangelists and, below, prophets, apostles and a Madonna del latte.

Flegrea Island of the Gulf of Naples, reachable by ferry from Naples or Pozzuoli in about an hour, with the colorful houses of Marina Corricella, the fortified village of Terra Murata with Palazzo d'Avalos and the abbey of San Michele Arcangelo, and the islet of Vivara connected by a bridge.
On Mount Fumaiolo, on the border with Tuscany, the Tiber and Savio are born, starting point of excursions in the woods.
A village with over one hundred works of art outdoors.

Masse, 400 meters away, is reached on foot from Siviano along an ancient road in white pebbles; there is the church of San Rocco, of the XV century and restored in the XVII. Not far away, a large red sandstone boulder marks, according to tradition, the meeting place of witches.
It's seen from miles on the plain.
Renaissance frescoes and the buried St. Christopher.
From the main tower, Gran Sasso and Maiella.
The three-faced crucifix.

The village is the birthplace of Francesco Crispi, founded in 1635 by inhabitants of Caltabellotta and crossed by the rivers Verdura, Magazzolo and Platani; above the valley of the Verdura there are the ruins of the Castle of Poggiodiana, whose tower is in the municipal coat of arms, near the Wolf Gorges, while the village of Seccagrande overlooks the sea.

Two emerald green lakes, large and small, in the thick woods of Monticolo near San Michele, in a protected landscape area of 100 hectares frequented by hikers, knights and bathers; from the large lake stands among the reeds the "Seeschlössl" . A signposted path runs around both lakes starting from the parking lot.
For enthusiasts it is a destination alone.
The great church of rebirth after lava.

In the "Piana delle centeno farme" it preserves traces of a village of the Bronze Age (about 1200 BC, with a decorated fibula, a torques and Baltic amber beads), a nucleus of Etruscan houses around 500 BC with Etruscan and Greek vinarium amphorae, and two Roman farms: Black Fossa A, of the II century BC, with a calcatorium for wine, and Black Fossa B, dedicated to weaving, cheese and wine. The site has dedicated tours.
Art and spirituality at the foot of the castle.
A altarpiece attributed to Andrea del Sarto in a hamlet church.
A medieval village closed between two towers.

It was built in the seventeenth century, when the village was founded under Spanish rule, with houses in the agricultural tradition of the Middle Campidano and ancient portals; in the historical center is the archaeological museum.
Mountain and nature protected.

Opened in April 1999 in the former church of Our Lady of Mercy, already hospital: rooms with interactive machines, panels, rocks and fossils on tectonic plates, earthquakes, volcanoes, internal structure of the Earth up to the nucleus and geology of Umbria; on the upper floor didactic workshops. The MiC indicates it as the first interactive museum of Earth sciences in Italy.
The Modena Baroque in an ancient college.
For visits and openings please contact the IAT Office in Siena, Il Campo 1, tel. +39 0577 292222
The world's largest archive of fabric moulds.
The remains of the Roman theatre of the city.
Giotto's mosaic and the oldest Nativity.

Next to the cathedral it houses silver (statue of the seventeenth century, candlesticks of the fifteenth century, a tabernacle of the seventeenth century, a pastoral of the sixteenth century), golden bronzes, vestments, avori from the twelfth to the eighteenth century and parchment miniate, among which three liturgical rolls Exultet of the twelfth and thirteenth century wrapped on a wooden rod called umbilicus; according to Italia.it there are only 32 specimens in the world.
A civic museum in the historic center.

8,1 km (2 hours and 45, 340 m ascent, medium difficulty with steep sections) from Pontida cemetery to Sanctuary St. John XXIII, recommended from spring to autumn. In the territory of Sotto il Monte touches the Abbey of Sant'Egidio, the Torre San Giovanni, a panoramic point on Sotto il Monte and Brianza, the Via degli Alpini, a restored historical staircase that descends to Ca' Maitino, and the pope's birthplace.
To be checked (with the crossing authorized by the Park)
The square of the bars in the center, meeting for the aperitif and evening.

Built in the 17th century on a previous religious building, it consists of two churches side by side and very similar, with two entrances and two naves of four spans. In the left aisle the paintings of the Last Supper and of the Virgin with saints, on the right the altar of the Suffragio with the altarpiece of the Madonna with Child; on the back wall the statue of the saint carried in procession. For the patronal feast (20 May) the bonfire of San Bernardino is lit at the bridge next to the church.
times and methods of visit not indicated by the source; contact pa-fleg@cultura.gov.it

Ecomuseum dedicated to wood: a section for children with toys, cradles and shoe soles, a path on street vendors, sculptures of the symposium, an exhibition on the ancient trade of the coalmaker and an audio path with sensory headphones on the voice of the trees, with Mauro Corona.
Baroque altars and the Flight of the Angel.

First mentioned in 1286 and probably built around 1200 on the foundations of a prehistoric castle, it was the seat of the lords of Rottenburg; some frescoes remain. From the ruins you can see Lake Caldaro, the Wine Road and the Adige valley; you can climb up from the parking lot of Kreithof in about an hour and a quarter.

The parish church dominates the centre of the village, in the square where the narrow streets of the village converge: the origins are medieval, but the current building largely derives from the reconstruction between the end of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries; inside works of sacred art of the seventeenth century.
The "Manhattan of the Middle Ages" of the more than seventy medieval towers remain 13-14, in the historic UNESCO heritage center since 1990, on the Via Francigena.
The first municipality of the Rhêmes Valley, houses scattered at 1218 meters, among the most agricultural in the Aosta Valley, with the rye granaries.
In the house that belonged to the son of Ludovico Ariosto, the finds from the Neolithic to the Roman age of the territory of Bondeno, the oldest settlement of Ferrara.
Greek remains and Jesuit memories in the heart of the country.
€18 whole; €12 from 18 to 25 years; free under 18

Collection of historical weapons, from white to firearms, from defence and hunting, chronologically ordered from the fifteenth century, with the history of families and local armoring tradition; a didactic section shows with videos and technical models and manufacturing processes. Free up to 13 years old and for residents of the municipalities of the Trompia Valley Museum System. Sunday only guided tours for groups of at least 25 people, booking 15 days before.
The Holy Stairway of the Ciociaria.
Church of the XIII century near the main square: above the main altar the altarpiece of the Assunta del Perugino (1513) and the gonfalone painted by Benedetto Bonfigli in 1472.
The altarpiece of Caesar Peruzzi.
It tells of the emigration of 700,000 Marches.
The walls of Augusta Praetoria.

Partly historic garden with gazebo, in the historic center overlooking Largo Arturo Anelli, cool in summer thanks to a vegetation partly centuries old; there is an open bar kiosk except in winter. From via Milano 23 or via Monza 12, from the gate at the end of the library parking lot.
The fifteenth-century symbol of the village.
The open square on the sea.

The centre preserves narrow medieval streets and, from above, views of Mount Etna, the Ionian Sea with the Gulf of Augusta and the Nebrodi woods. The square dedicated to Count Ruggero is the heart of the city that in 1060 the Norman chose as its headquarters, the first capital of Sicily; next to the square the Palazzo Pretura houses the museum dedicated to Robert Capa.
The convent and the pope of Fivizzano.

Founded in 1222 and largely rebuilt after the earthquake of 1732: single nave church with eighteenth-century portal, pulpit, choir and organ, cloister and small square with the spire of San Raffaele of 1777; in the convent are the town hall and museums.
The oldest church in the village, founded in 1047, contains frescoes and a wooden portal carved by local craftsmen and dated 1697.
With the most imposing Baroque altar in the valley; the parish museum preserves a very rare Madonna-Squeak.

Dedicated to the period between the Napoleonic age and the twentieth century and wanted by the military rowing Giuseppe Beccari: relics, documents, medals and Italian and foreign uniforms, hundreds of firearms and whites, a library of military history with thousands of volumes and an archive of letters and diaries of fighters and postcards. It is located in the former Caserma di Cavalleria (1857-1864), barrier-free; times indicated by the City: Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday 15-17.30, groups by reservation.
Built on the site of the church of San Salvatore and consecrated in 1654, overlooking the main square.
A medieval village swallowed up by the woods.

Inaugurated in 2002 on the ground floor of the seventeenth-century Villa Adele (Villa Pamphilj), in nine rooms it tells the ancient Antium from its origins to the imperial age: protohistoric funerary furnishings of the IX-VIII century BC, votive deposits of the Republican age, underwater finds, mosaics and frescoes of the Imperial Villa and a cycle of plaster paintings of the second half of the II century A.D.; on loan from the National Roman Museum the Nero's music niche with Ebbro Hercules. Closed on Mondays; reservation not required.
The meeting place of the city, with the church of San Domenico and the former Jesuit college, today town hall.
Sweats and forges of the oldest ironworks in Tuscany.
Mills and ironworks along the stream.

Area of 26,500 m2 with the center of the Roman city of Industria, implanted in Augusta age at the Celtic-Ligurian settlement of Bodincomagus and river port on the Po remembered by Pliny the Elder. You can see the large semicircular sanctuary of Isis and Serapide with monumental hedra and two small temples, the podium of a temple with staircase and part of the blocks with houses, taverns and shops; many bronzes produced here are at the Museum of Antiquity in Turin. The northern margin is marked by the remains of the medieval parish church of San Giovanni di Lustria, cited in a diploma of Otto III of 997. Visits through the Athena Cultural Association.
The peasant life of Val di Sole, room by room.

Museum inaugurated in 2010 by the Municipality and the Sassu Foundation in the country where the painter (Milano 1912-Pollença 2000) spent part of his childhood: 120 graphic works from 1929-1995 donated by the heirs, among aqueforts, aquatinte, pricks and lithographs, with the folders of the Orlando Furioso (1974), of the Fallen Horses (1973), the engravings on the Apocalypse and the five lithographs Homage to Sardinia with verses by Sebastiano Satta. In the nucleus also the two mural cycles of the sixties,          the Angevin Moti , on the antifeudal motions of the late eighteenth century of which Thiesi was the center promoter, and   ... The Life and Nature.

On the central square, dedicated to the patron saint: built in the early seventeenth century in Baroque style by the noble Vincenzo Rossi, with wooden decorations, stuccoes and polychrome marbles reappeared with recent restorations.
To understand the peasant life and the Grika culture of Salento.
To understand the "ideal city."

Route that connects the fifteenth-century churches around the village (Santi Anna e Giacomo, Santa Caterina, Sant'Antonio abate, Santa Lucia), along an ancient path, with views of the surrounding landscape. Part of the municipal territory is part of the Natural Park of the Julian Prealps.
The feudal palace on the main square.
Goethe to Rome.
A walk through springs and a lost grand hotel.

Formed from the hamlets of Cerano, Veglio and Giuslino on the slopes of the conical mountain San Zeno, Cerano d'Intelvi houses the only museum dedicated to stucco and intelvese scagliola, the church of San Tomaso from the Romanesque bell tower and, at the top of the mountain, the hermitage of San Zeno.
Make the complete tour of the walls at 15 meters high.

In the oratory of the Battenti of the Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta: paintings and sacred furnishings from the sixteenth to the eighteenth century, with works by Girolamo Siciolante, Francesco da Castello, Matteo Rosselli, Giovanni Domenico Fiorentini and Odoardo Vicinelli.

The centrepiece of the urban system was already in the early Middle Ages, stratified by the 14th century Gothic to the nineteenth-century renovation, with the Town Hall, the Basilica of San Benedetto, the cathedral and Castellina.
The botanical garden just inside the walls, included in the cumulative ticket with the two towers.
Arabic and Jewish alleys in golden stone.
Sardinia Tourism describes it as the most beautiful beach on the coast of Arzachena; it is among the coves near Cannigione.
The sea of Orosei Gulf.

Renaissance Palace of the XVI-XVII centuries in front of the Fortress, perhaps on a project by Jacopo Barozzi called the Vignola. Celebrate the spiral staircase with oval plan, self-supporting, 106 steps, attributed to Barozzi and built by Bartolomeo Tristano.

Lagoon behind the Cinta, from which the cord of dunes separates it. There live folks, friars, red herons and royal Germans, and during migrations there are pink flamingos: it is a place suitable for birdwatching.

A hilly village among olive groves, in the golden triangle of oil with Pianella and Loreto Aprutino; outside the village the Romanesque church of Santa Maria del Lago preserves the polychrome ambo of Nicodemo da Guardiagrele of 1159.
The medieval source with the fresco of the Tree of Fecundity, saved from a veil of limestone: a tree from which dozens of phallics contended by women hang.

The Baroque parish was designed by Bartolomeo Ricca di Savigliano and built between 1779 and 1783 on the site of an ancient covered market, with bricks cooked in a furnace opened specifically outside the village. The church of San Sebastiano, built from the first fifteenth century, is now home to the Town Hall; next to it stands the bell tower of the fifteenth century.
The weaving of the drap, rustic wool fabric worked on the ancient wooden frames by the cooperative Les Tisserands.
The symbol of Novara.
Nature and Sannite walls above Campobasso.

Built between 1733 and 1743 on a project by Luigi Vanvitelli at the behest of Clement XII as a lazzaretto, cargo depot and port defense, it rises on an artificial island connected to the mainland by three bridges; today it houses the Homer Museum, exhibitions, concerts and a summer cinema.
Ancient Rome outside the center.
The promenade is decorated with over 1,600 ceramic tiles from Castelli, with the Paris-Constantini and Gasbarrini villas and the Kursaal of 1913.

Church of the seventeenth century in the hamlet Villa, main testimony of the past of a village that in the Middle Ages was the cornerstone of the Huguenots and in the sixteenth century knew the condemnations of the Inquisition and the Sabauda repression of Calvinist doctrines.
The Romanesque of 1175.
Guided tour of the gallery €3, reduced €1; fossil research laboratory €5

Along the river Fosso-Acquafredda ruins of ancient mills, many of the Caligiuri family; the best preserved is the 'mulino di Caligiuri' or 'dei Greci', from the district inhabited in the fifteenth century by Albanian population. Numerous water jumps, including a waterfall the highest detected, between pines and ferns; safe paths and picnic area, with enhancement works started in 2026.
The old fishing port at the end of the promenade, starting point for Posillipo.
The Valadier and the crucifix of Saint Francis.
Ceramics, glass and artist glazes and the clarity of Viviani in a restored villa.
The walls surround the oldest nucleus of the city, between elegant palaces and Renaissance churches.

On the top of the hill the theatre of the battle between the troops of Garibaldi and the Bourbon army, reachable along the provincial road: an obelisk 30 meters high, in neoclassical style with Greek elements, guards the bones of the fallen of the battle of Calatafimi of 5 May 1860. There is a ticket combined with the Archaeological Park of Segesta.

Frescoes of 1425 by Erasmus da Brunico with stories of St. Nicholas, rediscovered in the restoration of 1996-97, and keys of vault painted in the early sixteenth century with saints, portraits of nobles and a monk making a smile; copies of the original statues are on display on the altar.
In the former church and convent of Santa Chiara along via Duomo, it collects the testimonies of the Sannitica and Roman Venafro.

Medieval church in Romanesque style restored in 1838. Above the main altar there is a Holy Trinity of the Camaiorese Francesco Pellegrinetti and under the apse a Madonna with Child in wood carved by Andrea Pisano.

Opened on 21 June 2009 and managed by the Fondazione Paese di Don Camillo and Peppone, it tells the story of the peasant life of the 1950s and the flood of 1951, with the reconstruction of a set and an exhibition on film making.
The cathedral overlooking Piazza Grande.
The castle of the municipality.
The craftsmanship of Ladin iron.
A mining tunnel overlooking the sea.
The traces of the Maratea Superiore.
First Sunday of the month and previous Saturday
The city under the bombs.
On the plateau of Pranu: a nuraghe with mastium and quadrilobed bastion and the village that surrounds it.
The forest is home to the Zelkova sicula, endemic tree dating back to the Tertiary.
The classic excursions of the Marsicano side of the Park.

Country at the meeting between Val Chisone and Val Germanasca, which grew around the textile industry since the nineteenth century: the Ecomuseum tells the story of spinning, silk mill and cotton mill with the route        'From wire to wire, while the anti-aircraft shelters, the exhibition on the Resistance and the remains of the seventeenth-century fort at the Park of Peace remind the story.

The Benedictine abbey of San Michele della Chiusa on Mount Pirchiriano, 962 meters, a monument symbol of Piedmont since 1994: the Scalone dei Morti goes up to the Zodiac Gate, with frames carved with zodiac signs and constellations.
The Della Robbia glazed terracotta.
Who were the authors of the engravings?
A sixteenth-century villa became a town hall.
The chestnut village.
Summer ice at 500 meters.
One of the most beautiful museum houses in Europe.
Paths between Austro-Hungarian fortifications and the remains of the First World War; the Road of Peace passes next to trenches, tunnels and fortifications of the Great War.
The residence of the Orsini, today City Hall.
On foot or by bike to Varazze.
A collection of ancient and modern dolls with costumes, which traces the history of the toy.
A fortress between medieval legend and English excavations.

Bell tower with cusp of 1577, 16th century frescoes with stories of the Old and New Testament by Giulio Urbanis, pupil of Pomponio Amalteo, and in the apse a wooden altar painted and gilded by Antonio Tirone of 1522.
The tour of a castle in Vallesina.
From the spur to 603 meters the view spans the valley of the Tenna, the Sibillini Mountains and the hills.
The ancient piazza delle Erbe, a market place, with the Palazzo dei Tribunali Antichi and the Torre dei Guttuari.
Medieval details around the square.
Palms, sand and bikes along the sea.
One of the most authentic beaches in the Maremma.
Of the great fortress designed by Francesco di Giorgio Martini for Duke Federico da Montefeltro there is only the 33 meters deep cistern.
The sixteenth-century frescoes of Thanner in a hamlet church.
The hermitage among the forests of Casentino, where nature, silence and sacred architecture merge.
Tombs painted five thousand years ago.
Ancient Etruscan Lucumonia and Roman city, home to Vasari, Petrarch and Guido Monaco, with the cycle of the Legend of the True Cross by Piero della Francesca and Piazza Grande de "Life is beautiful."

The Civic Tower on Piazza Vecchia, from which you can enjoy a panoramic view; every evening at 22 pm plays the rite of the hundred chimes. Next to it, the Palazzo del Podestà houses the 16th century Museum of the Museum of Stories.
Reni, Bruegel and Van Wittel in a small Umbrian village.
Picnic area surrounded by greenery on the banks of a pretty pond.

Municipal park overlooking the Mincio, dedicated to the Comm. Giancarlo Gauli, with the ethnographic museum, hostel, bar and restaurant; a small landing place allows you to board boats and canoes, with canoes, water bikes and boats. Free pedestrian access, parking on the river.

Built in the first half of the sixteenth century, on the occasion of the pestilence of 1527-28, in honor of the patron saint of the plague patients: it is the oldest monument in Offanengo. An example of Lombard architecture of the period, it preserves frescoes in the apse area, after 1566.
Fresh in summer, less than an hour from Florence.

Built in 1644 by the Compagnia del Sacramento and the Ducci family; two lateral stone altars conserve 17th century paintings: on the left the Death of Saint Joseph, on the right the Madonna del Rosario with the Saints Domenico, Nicola, Francesco, Caterina da Siena, Caterina d'Alessandria and Maria Maddalena.
The partisan war told in the valley.
Well-preserved village from which starts the Ru Marseiller, route between Verrayes, Saint-Denis and Chambave that also passes from the castle.

One of the three coastal towers erected in 1473 against the Saracen raiders: 14 meters high, rises on a cliff; from the shore emerge the remains of a pier used between the 5th century BC and the III AD.

Designed by the entrepreneur Tino Sana and opened since 1987, it occupies 3,500 m2 on three floors: rebuilt shops (chair, inlayer, sculptor, luthier, cage, turning machine), the path from tree to wheel with ploughs, barrels, wagons and boats, a village street with taverns and crafts, a puppet theatre, a collection of bicycles with section on Felice Gimondi, historical motorcycles and a wooden plane of the First World War. Open Mon-Fri 9-12, Saturday 15-18, Sunday 9.30-12 and 15-18; closed in August and on holidays.
Park built at the end of the nineteenth century in romantic garden style, with about 750 plants; it is used for different events.
The village on the cliff overlooking the Amiata.

Church of the XII-XIII centuries attributed to the master Sarolo of Muro Lucano, cited in a bull of Innocent III and entrusted in 1444 to the chapter of the cathedral; rebuilt from 1624 by bishop Pier Luigi Carafa, whose coat of arms overlooks the portal in terracotta. At the main altar a mural painting of Byzantine taste with the Madonna and Child; it is among the main Marian places of the region, a destination of pilgrimages especially in May.
The great sculptor of the Cardinals, at his house.
An imposing church that preserves a rib of the saint, the one above the heart, and the great Mosaic of the Centenary.
A medieval castle in the hamlet.

The western part of the municipality is part of the park, which extends from the high Valsesia to Campello Monti, its easternmost point and gateway; Valstrona is the only municipality in the park outside the province of Vercelli. Chamois, ibex, roe deer and royal eagle; many paths, with information from the municipality and from the visitor centers in Valsesia.
The historic heart of the town on the sea.
Among the most scenic historical bridges of the Apennines.
A medieval castle off the trails.
Church and Franciscan monastery at the foot of the castle.
The memory of the high valley charcoali.
Walk or cycle up the valley to the cimbrian village.

The hexagonal tower of the High Country, the castle's castle was granted in 1146 to the Gualtieri brothers by the bishop of Fermo; restored by Giuseppe Sacconi in 1901, it has the pendulum clock of 1902 and is the symbol of the city.
The tomb of San Gaspare Del Bufalo.
The history and archaeology of Corato and Alta Murgia.
The ancient defenses of the city on the sea.
Breaking into the sandstone rock rich in fossils of Pliocene, destination of tourists and paleontologists; the route to reach it is among the most characteristic of the area.
Aldobrandesco building restored by the Orsini between the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, home to the Museum of Palazzo Orsini and the Civic Archaeological Museum.
Excursions to the Small Dolomites.

Bridge of the Via Flaminia of about 27 BC, near Narni Scalo sul Nera: of the four original arches remains standing the first, the largest; collapsed in part around the Mille, in the medieval documents was called "Ponte Rotto" .

Twelve carriages of the Valperga di Masino family, mostly nineteenth-century: coupé, vis-à-vis, gala carriage and a wheelchair for children, with accessories and fabrics of coating, works by the Turinese builders Goggia, Cesare Sala and Giuseppe Panigoni. Opens on selected dates.
The textile tradition of Brunico.
For a jewel of the first Renaissance I strive in the fields.
The Spanish fort that dominates the Gulf of Porto Azzurro.

Begin in May 1605 on the ruins of an older church, designed by the Bolognese Antonio Maria Corbetta; the façade was completed by Carlo Maciachini in 1874-1875. It preserves an organ Serassi of 1833, the relics of the patron saint St Bovo (dead at Voghera in 986) under the high altar, the fresco of the Madonna del Soccorso (1496, attributed to Andrino di Edesia), paintings of Paolo Borroni and, in sacristy, vestments donated by Pope Pius V in 1571; the  "Tesoro del Duomo" gathers gold brocades, furnishings and miniatures.
The Gothic-Aragonese Mother Church.
Founded in 1647, it has a Greek cross plan with three chapels and altars and an octagonal dome with lantern decorated with Baroque stuccoes; the portal in travertine was rebuilt in 1953.
A medieval abbey above the Roman city.

Parish of the hamlet Dagala del Re, in the Diocese of Acireale. According to the census of the churches of the CEI was built in 1631-1632, enlarged in 1710-1715, rebuilt in 1843 and again enlarged in 1861-1872 and 1904-1909, with the completion of the building by 1945; altar and ambo were the subject of interventions in 2008.

Built in sandstone in three phases between the beginning of the twelfth century and 1289, the year of consecration, it was the cathedral of the diocese of Dolia until 1503. Romanesque with Gothic touches: facade and bell tower with arches and mythological figures, a Roman marble with snakes above the entrance, a sarcophagus on columns on the side, capitals with scenes of the New Testament. Inside, a baptismal bathtub of the 5th-6th century, the painting of the Tree of Life and the Retablo of St. Pantaleo of the late fifteenth century in six paintings.

Fortified settlement can be reached by car, bike or on foot; in summer it hosts exhibitions, shows and seasonal dining points. From the viewpoint the look reaches the remains of Castel Pradaglia above the Adige.
The art school majolicas.
Climb alleys and steps to Piazza Alta.
An entirely Berninian church.
The bell tower with the Golden Angel, symbol of the city.
Prehistoric necropolis with 18 tombs.

Ancient challenging mule track that connects Micigliano to the Sella di Leonessa (1,900 m) passing through the Valloni and Elephant mountains (about 2,000 m), with wide views from the summit of Terminillo to the Velino Gorges.
A little Scala on the Po.
The finds of ancient Akrai.

In the ancient village of Pendina, Calvary 'pentacrociato' with five crosses that recall the five plagues of Jesus, linked to the Franciscan tradition; the bronze portal of the master Giuseppe Farina di Monterosso resumes the five crosses as a symbol of the local identity. Pendina had four gates (Royal, Baffo, Portella and Mannacio) and a castle with drawbridge then became the church of San Foca. Guided tour available.
The finds that the Marmolada glacier returns.

The city of ham on the Friuli hills overlooking the Tagliamento: the Guarneriana Library, the oldest public library in Friuli, and the church of Sant'Antonio Abate with the cycle of frescoes by Pellegrino da San Daniele.

Country on a cliff of the Lepini Mountains, more than 400 m on the Pontina Plain, with views from the coast of Neptune to Terracina and the Pontine islands; built after the destruction of Norba in 81 BC, it preserves the archaeological park of the ancient city, the virtual museum Â ÂÂÂÂÂÂÂÂ°G. Essays, the Chocolate Museum and the rock church of Santa Maria above Monte Mirteto.
The only known nuragic aqueduct in a mountain forest.
Paintings, bottled boats, model ships and part of a German torpedo that sank Washington's steamer in World War I.
Popular Rome.
Umbriatourism also calls the church Santa Maria Assunta (XV century): to be verified.
History of war and mountain in the same building.
Romanesque and a fresco attributed to Bonifacio Bembo.

Documented from 1383 and enlarged in 1730-40, with fifteenth-century cloister; on the high altar the Preaching of St. Paul at the Areopagus by Jacopo Dal Ponte called the Bassano and his son Francesco (1574), the most valuable work of art in the city, and on the ceiling frescoes by Giuseppe Graziani.
The woods with numerous hiking trails around the village.

Born in the late 1990s as a sculpture park, it has an internal section for temporary exhibitions on the ground floor of the former 19th-century market, once also prison, and an external section diffused in the streets and countryside, with great environmental works by Mauro Staccioli, Umberto Mariani, Maria Lai, Pietro Coltella, Hidetoshi Nagasawa and others. Managed by the Municipality of Tortoli.
The defences of the castle and the fifteenth-century tower of the Florentine Republic, with a view that on clear days arrives to the sea.

Country of the Nebrodi at about 430 meters, mentioned as "Myirti" in a privilege of King Ruggero of 1134 and from 1643 principality of the Filangeri; in the Cupane Palace the Museum of Costume and Sicilian Fashion, while the churches retain a crucifix attributed to Friar Umile from Petralia and a Madonna of Giuseppe Gagini.

Romanesque church outside the town, the only surviving of a 12th century Benedictine abbey complex, whose name recalls an ancient forest (lucus). Façade in brick with thirteenth-century portal sculpted with vine branches and floral motifs; inside basilica with three naves with frescoes from the 12th century partly faded and, in the apse, remains of a great Christ with saints. The masterpiece is the stucco ambo commissioned in 1159 by the abbot Rainaldo to Nicodemo from Guardiagrele, with David and the bear, the stories of Jonah, St. George and the dragon and the symbols of the Tetramorphus, a rare example of sculpture with traces of polychrome; it also preserves a Madonna with Child of 1490 attributed to Andrea De Lithium.
The wooden Ladin village.
The circuit of Formula 1 and the World Superbike, which can be visited in about an hour and a half; at the entrance the Checco Costa Museum.
The cypresses growing from the marble of the facade.
Built in 1728 near the castle to replace a fifteenth-century church that became too small for the faithful.

The center is spread in three directions from Via Borgonuovo, with Via Varra, Via Castello and the Arch of San Nicola, ancient gate of the village with a newsstand dedicated to San Nicola di Bari; there are sixteenth-century palaces Brosca, Montella and De Cristofaro, with inner courtyard and monumental entrance.

White mulberry among the most important monumental trees of Lombardy: about 600 years estimated, 8 meters high and a trunk of more than 4.5 meters circumference. It grows next to the Jesuit church of Sant'Ignazio, among rural stone buildings in the historic center, and is freely accessible.
A karst cave with a legendary name.

It tells human life in different eras up to the consumer society, with exhibits of prehistory and protohistory and a collection of historical work tools; the guided tour uses multimedia animations and shows in operation numerous devices. Guided tours every Friday at 10 am from April to October; in the other months on request at +39 338 2032429.

Borgo del Subappennino South Dauno near the border with Campania, with the Rione Fossi, the medieval citadel abandoned after the earthquake of 1930, and a center gathered around the Monumental Fountain and the Clock Tower. In the surroundings, the Paduli Wood and the Punta Stone offer centuries-old springs and oaks.
Piazza Erbe is home to the market; on Saturday morning on the Lungorio, next to the Pescherie, the farmer's market is held.
A walk out the door.
Nativity scenes and Tyrolean folk art.
The church symbol of the community, rebuilt after the war.
15 min

In the Ducal Castle, exhibits the excavations conducted from 1988 to 1991 by the Archeoclub of Crecchio with the Superintendence in the Roman-Byzantine Villa of Vassarella, recovered from a cistern used as a landfill that has exceptionally preserved the wood materials, together with ostrogoth and Longobard finds: they tell the Byzantine life in Abruzzo and the Gothic wars between the end VI and the beginning of the VII century, and the trade with the East and Egypt. The Alberto Carlo Fraracci room hosts an Etruscan collection donated in 1995. Seasonal hours according to the MiC card (from 15 June to 15 September every day 10-12 and 16-20), otherwise by reservation.
An intimate experience.

Fraction at the gates of Levanto where in Roman times the settlement of Celua stood; there are the parish church of San Siro, of the twelfth century and then rebuilt in Baroque forms, the tower of the twelfth century and the oratory of Santa Croce.
House of Irish artist Brian O'Doherty, transformed in forty years into a cycle of frescoes that involves the entire building.
Enter the galleries of the miners of the sixteenth century.
The cross you see from the village, seen from close up.
The houses keep the original river pebbles.
No fixed time: openings are communicated month by month or by phone (010 9239921)
The oldest tower in the village, in pebbles with fishbone.

From 1571, after Lepanto, Pompeo Colonna transformed the medieval fortress into a ducal palace; here in 1606 he found Caravaggio refuge, which for Marzio Colonna painted the  "Dinner in Emmaus" and the "Maddalena penitente" (Maddalena penitente). Passed to the Ludovisi in 1622 and to the Rospigliosi in 1670, it preserves grotesque vaults attributed to Orazio Zecca and Domenico Fetti, the Hall of the Battle of Lepanto (frescoes attributed to Giovanni Bianchi called the Bertone), the private chapel of 1630 and the eighteenth-century Alcova with frescoes by Hannibal Rotati. In 1979 Princess Elvina Pallavicini sold it to the Municipality, which has restored it since 2003; she is part of the Latium Historical Houses Network. On the first Sunday of the month there is a guided tour at €7.50, with entrance to the Toy Museum at €1; for other visits you book with the secretariat (info@instituzionepalazzorospigliosi.it, 06 95769401).
Medieval alleys overlooking the lake.
Understand the throat before going down there.

In a sixteenth-century building in the hamlet Corti, it tells the story of the valley and Via Spluga, a link between the Mediterranean and the lands north of the Alps: crafts, winter tourism, rural housing, female work, games and trade. It preserves historical fir staüe, including one from 1576, a section on the Opera Pia S. Antonio founded by St. Louis Guanella at the end of the nineteenth century, a scientific section on the environment with a laboratory on water and energy and the eighteenth-century chapel of St. Anthony. Open every day except Monday 9.30-12.30, Saturday 16-18.
Museum of the Kirchler family with minerals of the Aurina Valley, the High Tauern and all over the world; open every day in July and August.

In the Castle of Santa Severa, founded in 1993 and renovated in 2023: seven rooms with over 450 finds between original and life-size reconstructions, models of ancient boats, nautical instruments and underwater archaeology, on the maritime history of the Mediterranean.
Two sanctuaries between caves and frescoes on the hill.
The district renovated around Piazza Gae Aulenti, with the highest towers in Italy, the time fountains of music and Corso Como a few steps away.
The Etruscan Museum of the city, with canopies, ceramics, funeral sets and terracotta pediment of the Temple of the Fucoli; two sections are dedicated to the Etruscan woman and to the banquet.
The first of the Tuscan villas.
Breathtaking views of the lake and Mount Baldo.
Gothic church of the first fourteenth century in Piazza della Pieve; in the village also the oratory of San Sebastiano and the Madonna del Soccorso linked to the plague.
It is said to bring happiness to those who pass when they play.
Medieval fortress with the Historical-Archaeological Museum and the Medici Arsenals.

The Romanesque façade in white and green marbles and the museum founded in 1859, one of the oldest ecclesiastical museums in Italy, with Christ in Masolino's Pietà and works by Lorenzo Monaco and Filippo Lippi.
Built in 1609; in the eighteenth century he lived there and operated San Crispino da Viterbo and Garibaldi stayed there in 1849 and in 1867.
The fourteenth-century bell tower in the heart of the village.

Promontory wooded Mediterranean maquis at the foot of Mount Licosa, with small beaches of rocks and pebbles over the pine forest and an islet with lighthouse, linked to the myth of the mermaid Leucosia. Cars are reserved for residents: you arrive on foot or by bike from the path of San Marco, almost everything on the floor (about 50 minutes per way), with views of the Gulf of Salerno, or by boat; some stretches of coast are private.
Laves born at the bottom of the sea, today in the hills.

Born in the thirties of the twentieth century on the initiative of Francesco Bardoscia and reopened in 1998 in the former convent of the Dominicans, today Palace of Culture. It exhibits artistic, archaeological, epigraphic and documentary material, medieval finds, a vast collection of drawings, notebooks, prints and photographs by Pietro Cavoti and spaces dedicated to the sculptor Gaetano Martinez and the Galatine artists.
From the village to the large karst meadows of the Lucretili.
The hazelnuts and honey crispy sweet hazelnuts, long gnocchi, sagna a patacca with beans, frascateglio, cod 'guazzetto and artenese bread.
The panoramic churchyard on the lake.

Defensive systems in the lower part of Val Clarea, at the confluence with the Dora Riparia, on the border with Chiomonte: the stream marked the border between Savoia and Delfinato until the Treaty of Utrecht (1713). Cited from 1303, the steps were forced several times: in 1537 by the troops of Francis I, in 1590 by the French of the Lesdiguières; in 1628 Carlo di Castellamonte and Tommaso Stanio planned new barricades and trenches, surpassed on March 6, 1629 by the army of Louis XIII and Richelieu.
Following the Latin poet.

The Rohrerhof, a farm protected in Ronco, at the southern edge of Sarentino, is documented by the end of the thirteenth century in the Urbar of Count Mainardo II of Tyrol; the oldest parts date back to 1325/26, the Gothic hall to about 1530 and the beam of peak to 1703. The municipality bought it and the association, founded in 2004, restored it and set up in museum between 2004 and 2007: smokehouse, room and Gothic rooms, garden farmer, bread ovens and temporary exhibitions on rural life. Traditions such as Sarner Reggele pipe and Sarner Striezl rye are recounted; concerts, evenings of stories and bakery courses are planned in the old oven.
In Borgo Canale, the house where the composer was born: a multimedia set-up reconstructs the artisan district in which he grew up and the sound project "Footprints" tells his life.
The September party with knights and drowning.
The artifacts of Nero's villa.
Verify on museibologna.it (weekly closure to be checked)
