Hiking ring of 30.55 km (about 9 hours) from the square of Montechiaro Piana, next to the high chimney of the furnace: calanchi with brooms and thyme, woods of roverella, chestnut and ash, Punta Marelli (about 470 m) on the Erro Valley, the belvedere of Costa Bella (about 485 m) towards the Maritime Alps and the village of Montechiaro Alto; short variant of about 18 km. Track GPX and downloadable map from the site of the Municipality.

To the northeast of Padua, around Borgoricco, the countryside preserves the network of straight roads that cross at the right angle of the centuriation favoured by Ottaviano Augusto: squares, called centuries, of about 710 meters on the side, divided into lots assigned to the settlers. The municipality describes it as perfectly preserved; along the intersections rise votive capitals.
The Giant Beach.

About ten thousand hectares among nine municipalities, Sinnai included, with the state forest of the Seven Brothers and that of Monte Genis; the seven peaks reach the thousand meters and the highest is the Serpeddi (1067 m). From Campuomu, with the forest station Umberto Noci, a path climbs to Punta Sa Ceraxa through the Arch of the Angel, a natural monument in pink granite. Lecci, corks, arbutus; deer, mouflons, royal eagles and pilgrim hawks. In Campuomu there is also the Sardinian deer museum.
Snow and high-altitude views an hour from Brescia.

Borgo founded in 1383, which takes its name from the narrow gorge between two mountain ranges, the Serre, where the first settlement arose; it is the village of the stuffed chairs, told in the Museum of peasant civilization. In the surroundings the beech forest of Condrò preserves the Margari Stone, the ancient hideout of the brigands.

The town of Trapani, which houses the Cusa quarries, from which the columns were extracted for the temples of Selinunte, abandoned in 409 BC; on the coast the towers of Tre Fontane and Torretta Granitola with the lighthouse of 1862, in the village the Mother Church with the crucifix of Fra' Umile da Petralia.
Cistercian abbey complex; in the great sacristy of the church the museum exhibits important sacred furnishings.
In the complex of Palazzo Ducale, built in the second half of the sixteenth century on a project by Giovanni Battista Bertani, with the organ of Graziadio Antegnati of 1565.

Romanesque Apulian in clear stone, rebuilt in 1068 by Norman bishop William: fourteen granite columns divide the three naves and the floor is covered by the mosaic of 1166 of the monk Pantaleone, with the Tree of Life supported by two elephants, biblical scenes, cavalry and arturian cycles, beasts and the months of the zodiac. Under the apse the crypt with 68 columns and Byzantine paintings; in the chapel of the Martyrs, wanted by Ferdinand I, seven large treasures preserve the remains of the inhabitants killed in 1480.
A Romanesque jewel frescoed in Apennines.
€2.60, reduced €1
Polesine's art gallery.
The 17th-century parish of Avenone.

New parish church started on 13 June 1926 after the earthquakes of 1901 and 1915 to the old church, of which the ruins remain (cited already in 1447); it houses the relics of San Vincenzo martyr, arrived in 1778 from the catacombs of Rome.

Two thick stones: one at the intersection between the provincial road and the Vetus via Tarenti, about two meters high, the other a few hundred meters further on the same road towards Monte Sannace, just over a metre high.
Two churches dug into the rock around the city.

Castle surrounded by an ancient park, built by Giovanni da Varano to guard the north-eastern border of Camerino and transformed into a noble residence by Giovanna Malatesta in 1489; in 1754 the Bandini bought it and the Marquis Alessandro had it enlarged and decorated in the gallery on the first floor by Giovanni Antinori. In 1977 Maria Sofia Giustiniani Bandini donated it with his goods to the Bishopric of Camerino: the museum preserves furnishings, paintings and curiosity of the family, the gallery and the eighteenth-century staircase. Castle and park can be visited; according to the regional portal opens Sunday and holidays 11-13 and 14-18.30.
The Aeneid Gallery and the carriages.
The village of the Longobard necropolis.
On June 24, the feast of St. John the Baptist, the faithful make you bless bouquets of field flowers.

Founded in 1984 on the initiative of Archbishop Antonio Cantisani, it is located in the Bishops' Palace of 1564. The six halls display works from the 14th to the 19th century, including monsters, chalices, candlesticks, vestments, paintings, wooden sculptures and marbles, largely coming from the treasure of the Norman cathedral destroyed by the earthquake of 1783.

Agricultural village between the plain and the Langhe, on the Tanaro, known as the "city of pumpkin" for the fair of the first Sunday of October and home since 1996 of the Baladin brewery; to see the chapel of San Bernardo with frescoes of 1451, the sanctuaries of the Alba Rosa and Madonna della Mirra and the square that recalls the retaliation of 5 July 1944.
The wooden artifacts of one of the most important prehistoric evidences in Europe.

It rises next to the central square of the village, founded in the early eighteenth century with the licentia populandi granted in 1688 by Charles II; the building was born from a warehouse of an ancient farm together with the pre-existing sixteenth-century church of the SS. Crucified. The façade is marked by two large sandstone pilasters, with a tympanum portal and a small rose window; the 17th century square bell tower in carved stone, originally in two orders, was raised with the civic clock. Inside, with a single nave, the ancient main altar with a tabernacle in polychrome marble and, in the niche above, the eighteenth-century wooden statue of the Madonna delle Grazie; altar and modern marble ambos are brothers Giacomo and Lucio Alberghina of Caltagirone.
Vineyards and a medieval church on the hills.

Ancient Bardi feud in the upper Val di Bisenzio, with the Rocca and Casone di San Quirico, seat of the Municipality with the Oratory of San Niccolò; in Montepiano the Romanesque Badia of Santa Maria and the Prato del Sole of Bruno Saetti, in Mercatale the MUMAT textile machinery museum.

Medieval village on the terraced ridges of Monte Calamita, on the island of Elba, with arced alleys called "chiassi" , craft shops and one of the most beautiful views of the island. Around, the Sanctuary of the Madonna delle Grazie, the Fort Focardo, the Romanesque parish church of San Michele, the mines of Calamita with the Museum of the Old Workshop and dozens of beaches, from Lacona to Innamorata.
The religious heart of the city.

It documents the origins of the Albanian community (arbëreshë) of Abruzzo, established here in 1743 by Epirus to escape the religious persecutions of the Turks, and preserves its traditions. Open on request (tel. 338 1655479).
A well-known pilgrimage destination in the area of the Bosco dell'Incoronata.

The Jesuit sanctuary built between 1627 and 1682, with a Latin cross with dome, and next to St. Silvestro, the oldest church in the city, Romanesque of the 11th-XII century, national monument since 1928.
The peasant life of the High Casertano.

The second island of the archipelago, entirely protected, united to La Maddalena by the bridge-diga of the Passo della Moneta (about 600 m, 1958): eastern side of pink granite and maquis, reserve since 1982, and western side with plains and pine forest. Between the beaches Cala Coticcio, called "Tahiti sarda" , Cala dei Due Mari and the Beach of the wreck with the remains of a ship on the shore.

At the foot of the morainic hills between Castiglione delle Stiviere and Castel Goffredo, Medole was marquisato dei Gonzaga di Castiglione from 1602 and on June 24, 1859 he saw the first battle of the battle of Solferino and San Martino; to visit the Gonzaghesque tower with the Civic Collection of Art, the parish with a canvas of Tiziano, the Pieve di Santa Maria and the former convent of the Annunciata.
The "Holy" of the Padua people.

Parish of 1535 at the entrance of the Riu Mulinu valley, so called for a watermill that stood nearby; from 7 to 10 September there is celebrated the feast of Santa Maria, with the rosary recited in Sardinian, the bonfire, the "goccius" sung and processions with knights in costume and banners embroidered.
The church of the alum banker.

Borgo dell'Amiata dominated by the Rocca Aldobrandesca, which houses the David Lazzaretti Study Centre, the Museum of Medieval Landscape, the collection of arms and the MACO; in the surroundings the sanctuary of the Madonna delle Grazie, the Romanesque parish church of Santa Maria ad Lamulas and Monte Labbro with the Jurisdavid Tower and the Faunistic Park.
The peasant life of the Dragon Plain.
The painters of the valley.
Listen to Occitania.
A Romanesque façade signed and dated.
The nineteenth-century residences were built outside the ancient city walls, around the larger space of the square, restored with care.
after the earthquake of 2016 the works are exhibited in the temporary museum     . Floriana Svizzeretto , temporary solution until the reopening of the Cola Filotesio (VisitLazio, 2023)
One of the largest inland views.
The museum in the house where the composer was born, stage of the itinerary of the Puccini places of Lucca.
The fabrics at the Sannio frame.
One of the most important collections in the world dedicated to Etruscan civilization.
The fortress above the village, built to control the roads and defend the waters of the lake.

The Adamello Glacier was war-fighted in 1915-18, with combats at about 3,000 meters in extreme conditions; the museum, in the center of the country, exhibits finds on the glacier by volunteers (arms and cannons, equipment, gavette, tools, uniforms and documents) and is the center of documentation and study of the Great War in Lombardy, with places detached from the forts of Colico. With Adamello Card and FAI card discount of 1 euro on the full ticket. According to Touring, it opens Saturday and Sunday 15-18 and is closed in January, February, March, November and December.

Romanesque church of the first quarter of the thirteenth century, mentioned in the Condaghe of Santa Maria di Bonarcado as a place where the audiences were held to settle the disputes. Originally a single nave with wooden roof and bell tower; in the seventeenth century it had transept and square presbytery, losing the semicircular apse. The three-mirror façade alternates rows of dark basalt and reddish volcanic stone; hanging arches in part with acute sixth.
It has been set up since 2008 on the ground floor of the former town hall and documents the war artifacts of Passo Volaia, Monte Navagiust, Passo Cacciatori, Monte Avanza and Monte Chiadenis.
Church with frescoes from the 14th and 15th centuries.

Dedicated to the Quistellan artist Giuseppe Gorni (1894-1975), architect and artist of international fame who in Nuvolato and nearby municipalities created sculptures, architecture and graphics; it is located in the former elementary schools G. Pascoli is designed and built by Gorni in 1929-1930, and tells about his career and his private life. Visits with the volunteers "Friends of the Gorni Museum."
Renaissance park annexed to the castle, today municipal garden, with the remains of an octagonal fountain and a well fed by the Roman aqueduct.
A perfect Renaissance.

Village 325 meters between sea and mountain, 18 km from Pescara, with views of the Adriatic, Maiella and Gran Sasso: course of noble palaces, alleys and churches, dominated by the collegiate church of San Michele Arcangelo.

In the Palazzo delle Contesse, museum since 1996, exhibits finds that cover over 40,000 years, from the Paleolithic to the Middle Ages, many from the accessories of the Paleovenet necropolis of Mel (VIII-V century BC), including a feline-shaped fibula; the noble salon has a Venetian floor with the phoenix of the Papadopolis. Open on weekends, from Tuesday to Sunday from 15 June to 20 September.
The church of the Candeliers.
A large panoramic terrace overlooking the sea and the mountains, overlooking the small and sober church of the Immaculate Church of the first half of the twentieth century.

On the square, where stood the ancient praetorium, the neoclassical Palazzo Gounela (project by Giacomo Moraglia of 1829, built in 1844-1847), with pediment on four columns and the council hall with frescoed ceiling by Paolo Emilio Morgari; next to Casa Nava, rebuilt in style in 1903 by Vittorio Storchi with arched porch, and Palazzo Beltrami, restored in 1854, seat of the Salone del Millenario. The route of the center ends in via Emilia, the main shopping street.

Fortified rural court, among the most famous residences of the Gonzaga, passed over the centuries to several owners: it has a private oratory and a garden with centuries-old trees and rare botanical specimens.

Borgo on three hills on the valley of Saturday, feud of the De Capua from the 12th century to 1793 and grew in the 19th century with the sulfur mines; the Renaissance Comital Palace houses the Museum of the People Without History, and Giovanni Verga set there the husband of Elena.

The first settlement of Anzio was built on the hill of Santa Teresa in the 8th century BC; here are the first fortifications of the city, called Vallo Volsco: a sandstone wall regularized to the west, stretches of walls in sandstone blocks to the north and deep defensive cuts to the east. The park, managed by the Santa Teresa Committee in agreement with the Municipality, was inaugurated on 9 August 2017.

Founded by the Fossombronesi between the 6th and 7th centuries, the village is described as an open-air museum: almost every house has niches, portals, shelves, frames and decorations carved by stonemasons, active here at least from the 14th century. The works of the stonemasons are also found in the churches of Sant'Antonio and in the parish; every July the square hosts the symposium of sculpture on sandstone "Sculpture in Piazza

State nature reserve in the Pollino National Park, in the municipalities of San Lorenzo Bellizzi, Civita and Cerchiara di Calabria; most of the gorges cross the municipal territory. The river digs a 17 km long canyon from the Lamia Spring to Civita and the Devil's Bridge, also run by rafting.

The main monument of the village dominates the Sinni gorge: of Aragonese aspect, existed already in the Lombard period. In the first half of the sixteenth century there lived the poetess Isabella Morra, daughter of the feudalist, reclused by the brothers Decius, Fabio and Caesar; today it hosts the exhibitions of the Summer of Isabella, which in August animates the village with poetic itineraries, theatrical shows and young people in costume.

Nineteenth-century residence in the district of Vittoria Apuana, with a theatre where evening concerts and spaces for exhibitions and events are held. The rooms tell the story of the landscape and art in Forte dei Marmi, with works by the sculptor Arturo Dazzi (1881-1966) and the masters of the twentieth century related to Versilia, including Carrà, Soffici, Rosai, de Chirico, Campigli and Guttuso, and a drawing by Henry Moore.
A rare fifteenth century Greek cross plant.

Born in 1996 on the initiative of the Archeoclub d'Italia di Baselice and since 2013 in convenient to the Municipality, on the ground floor of Palazzo Lembo exhibits fossils of 20-100 million years ago, especially molluscs and lamellibranches, a section of minerals and rocks and a small part dedicated to peasant civilization; other sections are planned on the first floor after the restoration of the premises.

The entire urban plant was designed in 1935 by Riccardo Morandi, with a rationalist plan, for the workers of the Bombrini Parodi Delfino plant (BPD), which exploded in 1938 causing 60 victims. Today, Colleferro is called "Città dello Spazio" for the Avio plant that produces components of ESA launchers.

Borgo on a hill above the river Platani, identified by tradition with the Sicana Camico, with a necropolis of more than two hundred cave tombs and tholos, the Archaeological Museum in Palazzo Arnone and the natural reserve of the Grotto of Sant'Angelo Muxaro.

On the western side of the hill of Sterparone, the heart of the medieval town of Fiorentino, border center wanted by the Byzantines: here in 1250 Frederick II died, who dictated his will there, as prophesied by the astrologer Michele Scoto (you will die in a place named after a flower). The city was destroyed by papal troops in 1255; excavations since the 1980s have brought to light the imperial domus, of which few traces remain, a building with a cruising vault, the walls of the cathedral and a tower in part preserved. Park established in 2007; guided tours, especially in August with the historical procession in costume, tel. 0882 391114.

In the convention center of the Experimental Cork Station, two floors and six rooms with restored cork processing machinery: band saws, stamping machines, cork dies and a collection of ancient books on cork from the late nineteenth century. Open Monday-Friday 8-14, Tuesday and Wednesday also 16-19.
A rare Gothic in Sardinia, suspended on the edge of the cliff.

Small center of the Serre Calabria, seat of the Sanctuary Basilica of Santa Maria di Monserrato, rebuilt in the 1930s after the earthquake of 1783, and the Surgical Museum Pasquale Castiglione Morelli dedicated to the history of his hospital of the early twentieth century.
The church on the top of the village.
The stars from a sky without lights.
The baroque stuccoes of the Rosary.

Country at the entrance of Val Pellice with the parish baroque of Santa Maria Assunta (1602), the stone climb to the castle above Piazza Santa Maria and, in the hamlet of San Michele, the neoclassical church and the Ecomuseum of the Resistance.

Ancient castle walled today ghost village, built as a village-farm between the sixteenth and eighteenth centuries: remains of the castle, a row of abandoned buildings along the main street and a clock tower with the coats of arms of the owners on the large courtyard, which in summer hosts a festival of popular theatre. The night of St. Lawrence, Good Morning Babylon and Flower of the Taviani brothers and Napoleon of Paolo Virzì.
Built in 1611 with a façade in pink trachyte; inside a 15th century silver monstrance and two wooden statues.
Parish dedicated to St. Nicholas bishop, preserves paintings of Palma il Giovane, Sante Peranda and Francesco Cavagna, a polyptych of the workshop of Marinoni and a wooden choir of Giuseppe Caniana.
The church of the patron, indicated as a stop not to be missed.

The museum of astronomy hosted in the Astronomical Observatory of Collurania.

The walled village, dominated by the fortress, rises on a hill at about 142 m; it is theater at the end of July of the Assedio al Castello, re-enactment of the siege of 1446, and in winter of the Castle of Christmas.
The emperor's country villa.
A hamlet transformed into a gallery.

Fortified village on a ridge at about 650 meters, with elegant mansions, carved portals, fountains, flowered balconies and gardens; among the monuments the Romanesque church of St. Thomas the Apostle, the church of St. Dominic with acute portal, the church of St. Nicholas with entrance to two rows of columns decorated with plant motifs and, little further, the Fountain of St. Leonard with three masks of the eighteenth century.

Medieval village at the foot of Monte Maggiore, mentioned already in 928 and plundered in March 1496 by Aragonese troops: the town with a radiocentric plan rises between arches and steps to the Lombard tower, while in the village you can visit the church of the Annunziata, the church of San Rocco and the small Museum of Sacred Art.
Traditional herbs.

The two-storey house of the first nineteenth century, in basalt, where Gramsci lived from 1898 to 1911 before leaving for the University of Turin; national monument with Law 207/2016. On the ground floor there is the good room with the reproduction of the letter to the mother of 1928 and the prison notebooks available on touch screen, the kitchen with ceiling in cannitzada and well, the courtyard with the oven; on the first floor photos, letters, personal objects, toys built for wife and children and the reconstruction of the prison cell of Turi. Book by phone or e-mail.
The seat of the town hall, so called for the notaries who worked there before 1286, flanked by the Civic Tower rebuilt in the eighteenth century with the bell of the castle's mast.
A village overlooking the Stone of Bismantova.

A Roman plaque and the coat of arms of the village.
A masterpiece by Martini on the promenade.

A small town in the Vercelli plain surrounded by rice fields, just north of the Po: in its territory there are the forest of the Sorti della Partecipanza, the last edge of the ancient plain forests, and the Cistercian abbey of Santa Maria di Lucedio, founded around 1123.

Along Via Regina Margherita, it houses a precious canvas from 1595 with the Madonna and Child crowned by angels between St. Felice and St. Sebastian.

Ruins on a cliff where the upper valley of Bruna opens onto the Grosseto plain, along the ancient metal road: inhabited since the protohistory, castrum in the twelfth century and military and noble complex of the Pannocchieschi in the thirteenth century, abandoned in the fourteenth century. The excavations 1997-2007 have brought to light walls and the remains of a tower; tradition places the death of Pia de' Tolomei, remembered by Dante in the fifth song of Purgatory, and a plaque tells the verses.
The nineteenth century sundial and the sculptures of Gagini.

Not far from Avenone, Spessio is a small group of houses in most of the sixteenth century, with loggias and carved balconies, closed to traffic of cars; there stands the church of Santi Antonio da Padova and Gaetano.
The oldest church of Limone, a small chapel among olive trees, is important for the religious history of the village.
Mount overlooking Stresa and the lake, reachable on foot: from the top you can see Lake Maggiore and Lake Orta and, on clear days, Lake Varese and other minor lakes, with the Alps in the background.

The local speciality is the strawberry grape, celebrated in October with a festival; among the typical products also olive oil, goat meat, vegetable soup "rappagacornuti" and "ciammotte" (lumache).
Palace built since 1738 for the Marquis Nicola Moscati, attributed to Ferdinando Sanfelice, with the famous stairs "with falcon wings" and almost intact stuccoes.

The village is born from the union of seven ancient feuds, Prato, Pergnano, Senaso, Dolaso, Prusa, Berghi and Glolo, each with chapel, saint and own customs; Dolaso has more well-preserved buildings. To see Casa Moscati in Berghi, Casa Martinoni on the Colle dei Frati, Casa Mazoleti in Prusa with a blooming arched and sundial loggia, stone fountains where washing was done and the Cavada, ancient road paved by Prato with the grooves of sleds. The walk "Seven steps to Seven Villas" takes about an hour.

Just outside the village, with the church called "Sant'Umano" the seventeenth-century convent and a guesthouse; in the church a wooden choir in walnut carved by two Franciscan friars of French origin.

House of a medieval Ghibelline family: the frescoes of the entrance hall are the only known profane work of Moncalvo. Visitable only on special days.

Chapel rebuilt in 1491 in Renaissance forms and restored in 1524, with Mannerist façade in terracotta by architect Regorino (1584) and bell tower completed in 1623. Inside, with a Latin cross and three naves, the "Assunta" by Callisto Piazza, the "Sacred Family" by Cesare Magni, long attributed to the Luini, the "Madonna" with the Child" by Daniele Crespi, baroque chapels, organ Serassi and an ostensory of coral, gold and precious stones donated by Cardinal Trivulzio.
The district of the Jewish community present since the fifteenth century: synagogue, museum, unleavened oven, kasher cellar dug into the tuff, butchery and ritual bathroom.

Born in 1970 and since 1998 in the Forno di San Ferdinando, the oldest building in the city, tells Follonica, the main iron centre of the Grand Duchy since 1836, on three floors with interactive installations, wooden models and nineteenth-century castings; the Etruscan section exhibits the finds of Rondelli, with a 6th century BC oven. It is a gateway to the Park of the Metalliferous Hills.

The stone city is on the side of Mount Ingino: Piazza Grande pendant with the Palazzo dei Consoli and the Tavole Eugubine, the Palazzo Ducale dei Montefeltro, the Roman theatre and, at the top of the mountain, the Basilica of Sant'Ubaldo, the destination of the Corsa dei Ceri.

Cave near the Lake Canterno, in front of the Sanctuary of the Madonna della Stella, with stalactites and stalagmites on the vault and more rooms connected by tunnels and narrow corridors; you reach it from the bike path of the lake.

In Monte Granatico of the late nineteenth century next to Santa Giulia: Neolithic finds of the culture of Ozieri, reproductions of the nuragic bronzes of Padria preserved in Cagliari and Sassari, the votive deposit of St. Joseph linked to the Roman city of Gurulis Vetus (I century BC-III century AD) with anatomical terracotta and statues, and a Punic-Roman collection with a thymiaterion with head of goddess. From June to September open Friday, Saturday and Sunday 15:30-18:30; in the rest of the year by reservation.

Inaugurated on August 29, 1981 in the municipal villa, he exhibited works by local painters Pasquale Celommi (born 1851), author of "Il Ciabattino" and his son Raffaello Celommi (born 1881), known for the marines; also present a terracotta by Alfonso Tentrelli and a canvas by Gigino Falconi.

Ionian City with the old town on a limestone island connected to the mainland by a masonry bridge and surrounded by the ancient walls: the Angevin Castle, the Baroque Cathedral of Sant'Agata, the Purity Church, the Greek Fountain and, outside the center, the beaches and the Natural Park of the Island of Sant'Andrea and Punta Pizzo.

A museum-non-museum opened on August 5, 2019 in an old warehouse then textile workshop: 23 stories of love lost in photographic panels and a frame in the center of the hall supporting the photos left by visitors. A few steps from the Museum of Banditism and the MEOC.

Great Etruscan and Roman shrine with travertine pool emerged from the thermal waters of the Bagno Grande: since 2019 more than 24 bronze statues in perfect state, the discovery considered the most important in Italy after the Bronzes of Riace.

On January 23, 1938, the speleologist Franco Anelli looked out over the Grave, the 50-metre-wide and 60-metre-deep access hole, and descended there two days later with Vito Matarrese, who in 1939 discovered the White Grotto, considered one of the most candid in the world for the purity of calcium carbonate. The complex extends for 3,348 meters up to 122 meters of depth, with a temperature of about 16,5 °C; between the caves the Wolf, the Monuments, the Corridor of the Serpent, the Little Paradise and the Lake of Cristallo. Two guided itineraries: partial of about 1 km (50 minutes) and complete of about 3 km (about 100 minutes) to the White Grotto.

St. Peter, probably fourteenth-century plant, stands near the stream Scarzito; Sant'Albertino, on the hill north-west of the center, has a classroom, presbytery and bell tower; the Madonna dei Calcinai, on the road to Pioraco, contains frescoes from the sixteenth century.
The Way of Sweet Life.

A fortress town of the upper Tronto, the only municipality in Europe whose territory falls into two national parks (Monti Sibillini and Gran Sasso and Monti della Laga), dominated by the thirteenth-century Fortress; in the village the church of San Francesco houses an extract of the Holy Shroud and in Spelonga you can preserve the drape of Lepanto. After the earthquake of 2016 historic center, monuments and museums are only partially usable.

Founded in 1981 by the municipality with objects donated by the inhabitants: tools related to the cultivation of wheat, olive and flax, looms, ancient shoes for the harvest and tools of blacksmiths and craftsmen, as well as costumes and furnishings donated by the embassies of the Community countries in memory of the twinning.

Itinerary along the Panaro River with bike paths and paths suitable for families and experienced hikers, and picnic points.

It rises where in 1634 an oratory was built at the Madonna delle Grazie, on a more ancient chapel; venerated by fishermen and sailors of Porto Vado, parish since 1952, restored in 1950-1960. It preserves a bell of 1642, an eighteenth-century marble altar from the demolished church of San Filippo Neri of Savona and the wooden group of the Visitation of Giuseppe Runggaldier (1929). Ancient underground quarry of white limestone of the Climati Mountains, of about 2,500 m2, with tunnels over 280 meters long, times up to 27 meters high and large irregular pillars left by the quarrymen, the 'pirriaturi' . Probably dug from the 15th century and especially after the earthquake of 1693, it provided the stone for buildings of Syracuse, Catania, Messina, Genoa and Malta; in July 1943, during Operation Husky, it was the basis of British troops, who left graffiti. Guided tours by reservation.

From the 13th to the 14th century, partly demolished in 1637, with a square tower in the center; the fief passed to the Del Carretto in 1209.

Romangia town between olive groves and vineyards, overlooking the Gulf of Asinara with about 18 km of beaches between Marina di Sorso and Platamona; in the medieval center the Baronial Palace with the museum Biddas, the fountain of the Billellera and the church of San Pantaleo, in the countryside the sites of Santa Filitica and Serra Niedda.

Car on the ground floor, including a FIAT 501 Torpedo of 1925, and motorbike Guzzi, Benelli and Parilla on the upper floor; the most valuable piece is the Paperina Ragnoli of 1948, unique specimen. Library with books, magazines, photos and racing videos. Open from Monday to Friday 8.30-11.30, by reservation evening and weekend.

Village surrounded by oak and chestnut woods, with small houses with stone facades, doors and windows in natural wood, paved streets in porphyry that go up the hill and the bell tower. The Town Hall occupies an ancient strong house. The spring, with the flowering of the meadows, is indicated as the best time to visit.

For a long time, the largest artificial invader in Europe, built in 1923 barring the Tirso: today's naturalistic attraction of Barigadu, with a great work of engineering; under its waters is the old village of Zuri, which resurfaces during drought periods.

Regional reserve ranging from the Romanesque bridge of Buriano to the central downstream of the Enel dam of the Pen, including the artificial invade and surrounding lands; center visits to Ponte a Buriano and trails towards the reeds and huts for birdwatching, designed for hiking.

On the second floor of the castle, the rooms reconstruct a patrician residence with furniture, furnishings and small collections of objects of affection; among the pieces exhibited the wedding dress of Emilia Caetani of 1830 and a collection of nineteenth-century soldiers of lead. Times indicated by the MiC: Monday-Saturday 9:30-13 and 15-19, Sunday 9:30-19, reservation required.

It rises at about 1,350 m on top of a cliff, at the end of the ridge between Val Grande and Val d'Ala, visible from Cantoira and the heights of Ceres. A pylon dedicated to the saint is considered before 1440; the pastoral visit of 1769 says it arose after an apparition to a pastor and recently expanded, with a frescoed apsidal vault; in 1840 there were added shelters and walls that give the complex the appearance of a fortress. Three paths (from Cantoira to Casa Goffo, from Trambié bridge, from Brachiello to Ceres) end with a stone staircase. Tradition requires the rock of Ceres, church and cantoira festival.

In the open countryside about 2 km from the centre, it was born from the Benedictine monastery of San Leonardo de Carbonaria of the 12th century, mentioned with certainty from 1269 and stop of the Via Angeina towards Puglia; it became a Badia Regia in 1790, was restored in the mid-nineteenth century and received the three-ordered bell tower with pyramid spire in 1871. Outside there is a centuries-old oak inscribed among the monumental trees of Campania; the festival is June 15th.

Cuggiono is the village of Villa Annoni, neoclassical residence of the architect Giuseppe Zanoja with a village park of 23 hectares, the second in Lombardy for extension after that of the Villa Reale of Monza; in the rooms of the villa is the Civic Historical Museum, while in the hamlet of Castelletto the Villa Clerici overlooks the Naviglio Grande.

Elegant Renaissance building that houses the museum of material culture of the people of Abruzzo, with a permanent exhibition on the painter Naïf Annunziata Scipione.

The museum tells the history of the village with finds from the V-IV millennium BC to the 19th century AD. It is located in Palazzo Foglia, built from 1833, which also houses the Fondo Musicale Greggiati, archive of publications, scores and rare period books.

Church dedicated to Santa Maria, San Pasquale and Sant'Isidoro, patron saint of the peasants, probably built between the end of the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries, perhaps on the remains of a more ancient church of Santa Maria: in 1699 it was very ruined, in 1714 it was well provided. Visitable during religious services.

Also known as the Shrine of Thomas, it recalls the apparition of Our Lady in 1432 to a young man, Thomas, to dissuade him from a murder; the fifteenth-century building, partly recovered, was rebuilt in the nineties. Cycle path of about 4.3 km in the forest, gravel and earth, suitable for all ages and also accessible with wheelchairs and strollers. The historic centre combines medieval origins and Baroque architectures and Rococo additions between the sixteenth and eighteenth centuries; the main street is flanked by large medieval porticoes.
