The village, 450 meters above sea level, preserves the 17th century urban system: noble palaces overlooking the main road that connects the residence of the feudalist to the fifteenth century walls, today in ruins.
The famous wall with works inspired by love, including Les Amoureux by Raymond Peynet and Gli innamorati by Ero Pellini, and a mailbox for love letters.

Spa village at 850 meters overlooking the Vallo di Diano, the easternmost municipality of Campania, with the scenic church of Sant'Anna in the square, six-nineteenth-century palaces, the MuMont ethnographic museum and, south of the village, the ancient abbey of Cadossa linked to San Cono.
The shrine was born from a Byzantine icon found in a cave.
Every first Sunday of the month in the historic center. In November the National White Truffle Market Exhibition.

The four villages have traditional country houses with aisles, ramps and stone portals; in Favrio a portal of 1539 is decorated with scissors and pin, symbols of tailors. Ballino, on the pass between Giudicarie and Tennese, has houses lined up along the road and around small stretches.

Country between chestnut groves and vineyards at the entrance of the Valley of Saint-Barthélemy, with the castle of Pilate and the regional astronomical observatory under one of the darkest skies of the Alps.

It exhibits finds from the backdrops of the coast of San Teodoro and donations, from Punic age to modern age: a punic treasure trove, a Greek-Italian amphora linked to the Punic Olbia, Roman amphorae, ceramics and glass from a wreck from the III-IV century AD in Baia Salinedda, a fragment of Roman helmet and a Byzantine tremisse of gold found in the village. It also tells Coclearia, station and port on the Olbia-Cagliari road mentioned in the Itinerary Antonino. It has a naturalistic section with a collection of seashells from all over the world. Prices for the period before closure.
The fourteenth-century churches of a medieval village.
One of the most photographed places in the Apennines.

Born in 1989 with the Waldensian church of San Germano, the museum is dedicated to school and religious education from the nineteenth century to the beginning of the twentieth century and is set up in the Beckwith school of the hamlet of the Plenc: lamps, Bibles, benches, the chair of the master, a wooden blackboard, notebooks, books and photographs donated by the community. The key is to the neighbors.
From the medieval village to the Tolfa dell'alume.

Housed in the premises of the former convent of the Franciscan friars next to the church of San Fortunato, about two kilometers from the park, exhibits materials of daily life, handicraft productions, cippi and funerary are, statues and architectural sculptures and inscriptions on administration and public works of Falerio; there are statues of Augustian age coming from the theatre.
From the 13th century, with medieval exterior and Baroque interior.
The 17th century wooden crucifix.
Panoramic walk under the fortress.
The Aurunci goat cheese.

Opened in the summer of 2003, it collects materials gathered in about twenty years by the restorer Antonio Guerriero on the peasant life of the Senish: agricultural tools, weaving tools, vintage clothes and household objects. It occupies rooms of a noble palace of the fifteenth century in the historical center, next to the Mother Church; other rooms house sacred furnishings, a permanent nativity scene set in Senise and a projection room with vintage photos, and nearby are rebuilt a peasant house and a shoemaker's workshop.
Medieval village among the best preserved of the Bolognese Apennines.
A carved gold ceiling.
The pyrite followed by the well at the plant.

One of the centers of the quadrilateral of the porphyry, grown around the castle of Roccabruna, now town hall; in the surroundings the Gothic church of Santo Stefano between the quarries and the path of Monte Piano on the traces of the medieval silver mines of Calisio.

Behind the building opens a large elliptical galloping hall, bordered by two fountains with obelisks and with a circular temple in the center from which the sovereigns attended the races, especially of the horses of the Persano breed; inside the temple there was a statue of Diana of the Farnese collection, then destroyed. The Foundation presents him as the largest galloping gallery in the world inserted in the perimeter of a royal residence; along the perimeter remain traces of the ditch carrying water to irrigate the lawn. The Persano breed was born in 1744 at the behest of Carlo di Borbone and Ferdinand IV had built for the horses stables and racetrack; in the historical park you can also see the solar clocks, the ancient walls and the Bourbon moat.

Lake to the south of the Lario wet by Lecco, Vercurago, Pescate, Garlate and Olginate, background of the pass "Adio ai monti" of the Promisi Sposi; in the reeds live anatids and folklore and are observed herons ashes and larger whites, garzettes, cormorants, martin fisherman, flares and swans royals. The cycle track of about 18 km, easy and accessible even with strollers, follows the entire perimeter and Garlate runs along the bank before flanking the Via Statale.

Outdoor art gallery along Corso Mazzini, set up in 2006 and commissioned by the Bilotti family: sculptures by Salvador Dalí (San Giorgio and the dragon), Giorgio De Chirico, Giacomo Manzù, Mimmo Rotella, Emilio Greco, Pietro Consagra, Sasha Sosno and a Head of Cariatide by Modigliani.
A Renaissance village intact.
Ancient village at the entrance of the Valtournenche, rich in castles and towers, with historical parks open to the public.
A frescoed medieval wash-house.

From Via Massimo Troisi a paved path to steps descends to the bathing area; on the rocks the "balate" are the ancient deposits in stone of fishermen who in the film were the house of Mario Ruoppolo. To the north is the natural arch of Punta Perciato; to the south is the rocky ridge of the ancient beach of the dialogues between Mario and Neruda, now eroded.
The peasant civilization on the edge of the Baraggia.

Farmhouse of the High Tablekeeper, born around the Mille as a farmhouse of the Benedictine abbey of San Pietro and feud of the de Sangro from 1382 to 1806. The medieval village gathers around the Ducal Castle; about 9 km from the archaeological park of Castel Fiorentino, where in 1250 Frederick II died.
Educational park of about 9 hectares with the dog, the chestnut dryer.
The fountain that tradition binds to Vignola.
A fortified village intact on the Macerata hills.
The main museum of the city, in Palazzo Rocca Costaguta.
The largest view of the park.

The capital of Friuli Venezia Giulia on the gulf, with Piazza Unità d'Italia open on the sea, the Borgo Teresiano around the Grand Canal, the hill of San Giusto with cathedral, castle and remains of ancient Tergeste, and outside the city the Castle of Miramare and the Risera di San Sabba.
Norman cathedral.
Free archaeological section, naturalistic section €2
Church with beautiful frescoes inside, marked by the Touring.

On the plateau of San Giuliano remain the imposing walls in tuff of the fortress, where probably stood the Etruscan and then the medieval town of Marturanum, abandoned at the beginning of the II millennium in favor of the current Barbarano. Next, the Romanesque church with three naves with paintings from the 14th and 15th centuries and a romerium inhabited by hermits until the end of the 19th century; near the Roman bathroom, an indoor swimming pool dug into the tuff.
D'Annunzio underground stage.

San Teodoro, in the south-eastern Gallura, is known for its white sandy beaches, from the Cinta about 5 km long to Cala Brandinchi and Lu Impostu, overlooking the marine protected area Tavolara-Punta Coda Cavallo. Behind it are the lagoon frequented by pink flamingos and the granite massif of Mount Nieddu.
Trekking between Sardinian deer and secular trees.

Ancient building with austere appearance six-seventh-century, just outside the village in the direction of Redondesco: although with the characteristic elements of the villa, it was born as a public palace. The double nature is explained by the history of Gazoldo, the true lordship of the Ippoliti with a special area of autonomy even during the Gonzaga domination and the right to beat its own currency.
The balsamic vinegar told where it was born.

A stretch of landscape and naturalistic interest along the SS 267, which follows the high coast up to about 150 meters above sea level and ends with the Tempa Rossa, a cliff overlooking the sea; the Rio dell'Arena, crossed by a bridge, marks the border with Castellabate.
The last house of the poet John Keats and Percy Bysshe Shelley, next to the Trinity Stairway of the Mountains.

The central square combines the upper and lower parts of the village; the neoclassical Town Hall (1749), the Theatre La Vittoria and the civic tower of the sixteenth century, rebuilt in 1950 after the bombings of the Second World War, which was the bell tower of the disappeared church of St. John, destroyed in war.

The largest fortified citadel in Sicily, over 7 hectares on the peninsula to guard the radium, with defences built in about ten centuries: the castle of Frederick II dominates the enclosure of the Spanish walls, which also contains the ancient Duomo, begun in 1608.
The Coronation Church.
Exhibitions in a 16th century palace.
Founded in 1990 to tell the entire cycle of silk processing, historical tradition of the Como territory.

Parish church with a majestic and elegant neoclassical façade; inside it preserves one of the most refined eighteenth-century pictorial cycles in Veneto, the work of artists from the Tiepolescan school.
16th century church that preserves fragments of ancient frescoes on canvas.

Cave to the north-west of Caldana, active until 1975 and documented by the sixteenth century, perhaps already in Roman times: the stone is a limestone breach called Portasanta due to the resemblance with the ancient marble of Chio used for the holy doors of four Roman basilicas. The excavation flourished in the nineteenth century with Peter Leopold and Leopold II of Lorraine.

Park of 23,000 square meters dedicated to the terracing, villages of the Bronze Age of the Po Valley arose towards the middle of the II millennium BC and disappeared around 1200 BC. Under a cover are observed the excavations with over four centuries of life of the village; the open-air museum reconstructs life-size moat, embankment with palisade, door and two large houses furnished with copies of pottery, tools and weapons. On opening days 9.30-13.30 and 14.30-18.30, guided tours every 45 minutes, recommended booking.
A little Romanesque from Logudoro.

Green area protected by the consortium of municipalities of Busto Arsizio, Legnano and Castellanza, with about 10 hectares equipped between the entrance of Castellanza and that of Legnano: refreshment point, play area, picnic tables and two life paths, including the Pojeco suitable for people with motor and visual difficulties. The park centre is Cascinetta, a Lombard farmhouse renovated between 2004 and 2007. Free and accessible access.
The Romanesque Coros campus.

Founded at the beginning of the 6th century BC as a Greek-Etruscan fluvial port, the city that gave its name to the Adriatic is today the gateway to the Po Delta Park: the National Archaeological Museum with the Tomb of the Biga and the Roman glass, the cathedral with the 9th century crypt and the new diocesan museum, the small center crossed by the White Canal and, in the countryside, the museum of reclamation in the Amolara hydrovora.
Since 1914 it has been guarding the richest collection of the Impressionist painter, born from the donation of his wife Léontine: over 200 works; the rear loggia looks at the sea and Porta Marina.
The bridge over the Piave of 1926, along the path of the rafters towards Borgo Piave.
Built in 1938 and dedicated to the patron saint of the city, it preserves a painting of the Madonna that offers the Child with the hangars of the nearby military airport in the background.
€5, reduced €4 (6-13 years and over 65 €2), cumulative with the park €7
The city's most photographed symbol.

Natural swimming pool in the Gulf of the Crescent, at the extreme south of the island, between cliffs overhanging and deep and clear water, loved for diving and diving; in the basin there are several caves. Parking and refreshment point, just over 8 km from the port.
The places of the family of St. Thomas.
Built in the eighteenth century as a Jesuit college: the staircase with memorial tombstones, the hall of honor, the hall of the junta and the collection of civic art in the corridors.
Beach awarded with the Blue Flag, in front of the Island of Dino.
Menhir in the open country, like five thousand years ago.

Until 1632 it was a cliff with a fishing village, about 400 meters from Stresa: Charles III Borromeo built the palace dedicated to his wife Isabella d'Adda, which forms the "praua" of a ship while the ten-terrace Italian garden forms its "poppa." Inside the ballroom with a high dome, the hall of Napoleon (which stayed there in 1797) in empire style, the gallery of the 16th century Flemish tapestries with the unicorn symbol of the Borromeo and the caves covered with pebbles, tufas and shells; in the garden the Atrium of Diana and the Teatro Massimo.

One of the largest Christmas markets in Italy, in Piazza Walther and in the Christmas park near the station, with wooden houses, South Tyrolean handicrafts products, skating rink in Piazza del Municipio and Krampus around 8 December.

Four small white sand coves separated by rock stripes, at the foot of the capo Ceraso promontory in the hamlet of Murta Maria, the northern limit of the protected marine area of Capo Coda Cavallo, overlooking Tavolara. The floor is gently sloping, suitable for children; accessible to disabled people, connected by bus to the city, with ample parking and rental of equipment.
Walk on the medieval walls and discover the theatre in the Palazzo dei Priori.

Municipality on the Dora Riparia at the gates of Turin, crossed by a branch of the Via Francigena: the fifteenth-century Madonna della Stella with its frescoes, the Romanesque parish church of San Pietro overlooking the river, the remains of the castle linked to the episode of Maria Bricca of 1706 and the ancient factory of Passamanerie Massia.
At the Sarno river, on a more ancient structure: the current building was begun in 1631 and consecrated in 1720, the year of the high altar.
The culture of the Marmilla.
The queen's castle.
A noble palace with guided tour.
The Augustinian hermitage in the territory of Monticiano, a pilgrimage destination.
Visits with tasting by reservation.
A curiosity that children like.

Peschici Bay is one of the largest beaches in the area, suitable for families and, for exposure to wind, surfers; Jalillo is more secluded and shaded in the afternoon; towards Rodi Garganico follow the long beaches of Calenella, Cento Scalini (of the Tufare) and San Menaio, while Suspicious is pebbles between rocky walls. They are among the most awarded Blue Flag beaches in Gargano.
The mine museum, linked to the millennial history of the city's mineral resources.
The stairway and the arabic cloister.
The Jerusalem of Francigena.

The village of the upper Val di Fassa with the hamlets of Alba and Penia, at the foot of Marmolada, Sella and Gran Vernèl: from here you can climb to the Sass Pordoi, the "Terrazza delle Dolomiti" and to the Passo Fedaia; to Penia the Venetian sawmill La Sia, documented from the sixteenth century.
The Hapsburg walk on the river.

Centre of the Sibillini Mountains National Park with an exhibition area in diorami and a fauna area fenced of about 29 hectares on the south side of Mount Cornaccione, between Castelsantangelo and Vallinfante, where deer and roe deer live in semi-freedom and are observed by turrets; the center supports the re-introduction of the deer in the Park. Guided excursions upon reservation (339 6039429).
The city zoo, among the ten things to do in Pistoia.
The arches of the best Roman aqueduct on the island.
Ancient port with Palazzo Marescalchi and the Customs Casemon.
In the Palazzo del Carretto, in the historic centre.
Ancient China in the heart of Emilia.
An aqueduct of Traiano in the woods.
Ortona Sea.
Salento countryside among olive trees and dry architecture.

Cinta of the late Middle Ages with six doors, five still open, in most of the times of Fabrizio Cantelmo (1611-1658): above Porta San Nicola a 17th century fresco shows Santa Margherita that holds the village; then Porta Cencia, Porta San Marco and Porta Santa Margherita. From the church of the Madonna della Libera start the "rue" , narrow and steep streets that descend towards the walls.
A seventeenth-century barn turned into a theatre.

Ancient market square paved with trachytes, with eighteenth-nineteenth-century portico buildings and the Palazzo del Monte di Pietà, the first bank of the city since 1497; in the center also the Town Hall of 1538 with ceiling carved by Marcantonio Vanin (1605) and the Venetian Gothic palace Magnavin-Foratti with pentaphora.
Winter snow and hiking trails in summer.

Outside the village, it is considered the oldest Franciscan monastery of the Marche and according to tradition was founded by Saint Francis; returned to worship in 1989 after a complete restoration. The church has a single nave with two stucco medallions on miraculous events of 1673 and a square cloister with well in the center.
More than 60 works by the poet and screenwriter born here: paintings, sculptures, tapestries, ceramics and printed canvases.

Monastery founded in 1007 on an island between Po and Lirone, donated by Matilde to Pope Gregory VII in 1077 and then linked to Cluny; Luther, Vasari, Tasso and Palladio passed there. The route touches the cloister of the Seculars, the Barberinian staircase, the late Dogotic cloister of San Simeone with the Chapter Hall, the Grand Refectory, where Abbot Gregorio Cortese commissioned a fresco to Correggio and where the Cenacolo di Girolamo Bonsignori (1514) and the sixteenth century cellars returned.

Carsten Höller's panoramic tour on the Timpa della Guardia (1125 m), produced for Artepollino and known as the slowest in the world: 12 colored gondolas for 24 people, 16.75 m in diameter, which run one lap every quarter of an hour tilting towards the ground.
Storks and butterflies in the Lower.
A seaside village from which the typical Calabrian felucas leave for the fishing of the swordfish; from here you can see the Sicilian coast and the Aeolian Islands.

Added to the castle when, around the year 1000, the village became the seat of Robert Guiscard, who enlarged and fortified it. The cone-shaped tower, called "motta" is spread over five floors called rooms: Granals (underground), Prisons, Arms (entrance), Audiences and Prince.
Medieval engineering testimony.
Four centuries of frescoes on the island.
In the Palazzo del Podestà the finds of the Etruscan territory of Accesa, with houses and graves excavated.
The peasant life of Val d'Ultimo.
A place of the Risorgimento.
Views of the plain and the Alps from the isolated mountain of Valle Po.

In the outbuildings of Palazzo Locatelli, with entrance from the inner garden: on the raised floor a thematic section dedicated to the cormonese sculptor Alfonso Canciani (1863-1955); ground floor and first floor host temporary exhibitions of history, art and local culture during the year.

The second mountain hut in South Tyrol by extension, in the geographical center of the province, with marked paths for families, the thematic path of the mountain pine with demonstration distillery, family-run huts and, in winter, panoramic cross-country trails; 360 degree view of the Dolomites.
A Roman villa and a medieval tower on the sea of Scauri.

Municipality at the foot of the Brenta Dolomites, at the entrance of the Val d'Ambiez in the Adamello Brenta Nature Park: the village of San Lorenzo in Banale, born from the union of seven ancient villas, the church of the Santi Sebastiano and Rocco with the frescoes of Baschenis, San Giorgio in Dorsino, the House of the Park and the Nembia lake, WWF reserve.
A stage of memory.
To see before you go up to the Cimone.
The castle is located next to the archaeological area of the Grotto Bella, where statues of the protohistoric and Roman age have been found.

Founded in 1980 in Villa Ippoliti, the sixteenth-century residence of the local feudalists, it is thought as a place of research and study as well as of conservation. The scientific program was born from the studies that have re-evaluated Archimede Bresciani from Gazoldo and Mario Lomini and has brought attention to the Lombard Chiarismo and the contribution of Mantua to that movement. Open from Monday to Saturday in the morning (Thursday until 5 pm); during the temporary exhibitions also Saturday, Sunday and holidays 15-18.
The neo-Gothic sanctuary.
A medieval manor overlooking Parma and Baganza.

It preserves the apse of the first Norman church, dated by tradition to 1105, and the original tower; inside a wooden crucifix of the sixteenth century and the only sundial still working in the Alcantara valley, built in 1882 by the astronomer Temistocle Zona. Next to the 18th century church and the monastery of San Benedetto.
Two centuries of sacred art in the mother church of the village.

The city of palm trees between Sanremo and the Côte d'Azur: the tall city with pentagonal walls, the villas of Charles Garnier, the Bicknell museum, the exotic garden Pallanca and the Argentina promenade.
A village to walk through shops.
The green rocks born from the bottom of the sea.
The last noble seat of Campania.
Outside Porta Santa Maria, Gothic church transformed into a Baroque age with the fresco of the Deposition of Perugino and students (1517) and the civic-diocesan art gallery.

Park with pine trees of the thirties and view to the sea, equipped with hostel, picnic area and barbecue, sports fields, bars and games for children; the huts for the holidays are booked at the municipality.
18th century buildings survived in the village: the old oven, the wash-house and the watermill.
A place of sabauda memory.

Five stages in the village, one for each scene of the screenplay ...The adventures of Pinocchio ... (1972) by Luigi Comencini, with Andrea Balestri, Nino Manfredi, Gina Lollobrigida, Franco Franchi and Ciccio Ingrassia and Vittorio De Sica, shot here; each stage has a panel with texts and images and the house of Geppetto murals and installations.

It occupies some rooms of the lower mezzanine of the seventeenth-century Palazzo Spinola, once used for defensive purposes and as accommodation of the servitude. Since 2003 it has been named after the Partisan commander Gian Battista Lazagna . Carlo , creator of the first Museo della Vallata e dei Partisani (1990). Connected to the Documentation Centre, with a library on the Resistance and interviews, photographs and original documents of the Borbera and Curone valleys. Info: Common, tel. +39 0143 90004.
The bronze portal and the bell tower of the sanctuary.
The Brueghel in Lunigiana.
Country at the entrance of the valleys of Rhêmes and Valsavarenche, with the castle of Sarriod, the rural house Maison Bruil and the bridge over the horrid, where John Paul II spent the summers.
Gaudenzio Ferrari polyptych under a starry sky.

Mountain village with almond trees at the foot of the Terminillo, with doors and towers of Angevin, the Margaritian Fountain in Piazza VII Aprile, the churches of San Francesco and San Pietro and the Sanctuary of San Giuseppe; two thirds of the territory are woods and pastures of high altitude.
Taste the figodindia mustard.
The oldest Benedictine monastery in the city, founded in 978 and rebuilt by Arnolfo di Cambio, in front of the Bargello.
The city on the hill.

Over 800 models in plaster, the result of the secular profession of figurines: the eighteenth-century cats blackened by smoke, sacred subjects, domestic scenes and ancient crafts, and the history of emigration.
The collection of birds in the pine forest.
A refined Tiepolesco pictorial cycle in the center of the village.
Church of the second half of the seventeenth century with ceramic floor of 1758.
House museum of rooms richly furnished with Italian and French furniture, carpets, tapestries and paintings that recreate the atmosphere of the eighteenth century.

Themed route of about 8 km (about 2 hours) among the vineyards of the Lower Atesina dedicated to the life cycle of wine, from the vine to the glass: starts from the center of Cortaccia, where the entrance is marked by a large cluster of pebbles polished by the glacier, and touches Niclara, Magrè and Cortina, with information stations on viticulture, landscape and history, some to recognize the aromas of wine. The traits can also be covered individually.

Country of the Simbruini Mountains, in the Regional Natural Park, between Monte Tarino and Monte Autore and the valley of the Simbrivio; the crenellated tower of the Caetani dominates the square and at 1,300 m, in the rock of the Colle della Tagliata, stands the Sanctuary of the Holy Trinity, a destination of secular pilgrimages.
The panorama all round on the Plain of Lucca.
It opens in the Gulf of Squillace, in front of the medieval village, in a bay awarded with the Green Flag and indicated among the most unspoilt in the province.
Romanesque church of the year 1000 on the Street of the Seven Bridges, with three naves with capitals loaded with biblical, pagan and Etruscan symbols.
The large plateau of the Dolomites.
The church all in ceramic.
The civilization of chestnut.

In 1804 the members Bolognini and Pernici opened at the entrance of the Val Genova, in a loop of Sarca, a  "Fabrica dei cristali" that exploited water, timber and quartz of the Val di Borzago quarry, with glass masters coming from Bohemia; closed in 1888 and Carlo Pernici made holiday homes. Of the kiln building, partly dismantled in World War I, the perimeter walls and a small track with trolleys remain; today it houses a small historical museum and glass processing courses with internationally renowned masters and artists.

Pieve quoted from 1230 and rebuilt in the present forms in 1775 by Don Cerdelli; the Duchess Maria Luigia visited her and gave her nineteenth-century paintings by Parmesan artists, still preserved. Barbiano is inhabited by prehistory, with a Paleolithic settlement excavated on Mount Leoni.
A prehistoric UNESCO village under the waters of Garda.

Court of the end of the seventeenth century of the Montanara possession, belonged to the Marquis Zanetti and then to the Cavalcabo; it was one of the crucial places of the battle of Curtatone and Montanara of 29 May 1848. Sold to the Municipality in 2002 and recovered, since 2004 it is the seat of the Town Hall.

Themed exhibition opened in 2014 at the Navalge Theatre, promoted by Istituto Culturale Ladin, association On the front of memories and municipalities: exhibits the vast Federspiel-Caimi collection with finds of the Ladin de Fascia Museum and private, on about 500 m2 and three floors, in four sections (Galizia 1914, La trenches, Dolomites 1915, War on War) with dioramas, vintage photos, audio, video and reconstructions of trenches, posts and caves; every year a new temporary section. Accessible to people with disabilities.
One of the most precious Romanesque churches in southern Sardinia.
The column on the sea.
The writer's rural villa, preserved with furnishings and objects.

Vibonese Serre Country was founded around the Dominican Convent founded in 1510, destroyed by earthquakes of 1659 and 1783: today the ruins of the ancient complex, the Basilica Sanctuary of San Domenico and, in the spaces of the convent, the Marmi Museum and the Earthquake Museum.

Small agricultural village about one kilometer from Pandino, inserted in 2005 among the most beautiful villages in Italy: yellow houses and red bricks, farmhouses with communicating courtyards, arcades and loggias along the fronts, surrounded by fields; the recovery respected traditional construction techniques. The parish church of the Holy Trinity and San Bassiano, dating back to 1895; just outside, Villa Maggi, dating back to the 17th century, renovated between the 19th and 20th centuries.
Manzù, Quasimodo and the frescoes of Vacca in the town hall.
On Montale's trail.
Walk through pipe portals and hemp memory.
A Renaissance bank remained intact.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione at the entrance of the Po valley, dominated by the Mombracco, the mountain of Leonardo, with the chapel of the Marquises of Saluzzo and the Cistercian Abbey of Staffarda.

In the upper part of the village, in a building built with stones recovered from the rubble of the bombings of 1943, exhibits the findings of the archaic necropolis of Piano Fusaro (VII-VI century BC, 25 burials and a road in use from the third century BC to the Roman age), reconstructions of kitchen, wedding room and classroom, shoemaker's shops, housekeeper, saddlemaker, winemaker, beekeeper, carpenter and blacksmith, tools of shepherdhood and wool related to transhumance, vintage clothes from the seventeenth century to today, sacred art, a large photographic archive and relics of the bombardments. Timetable indicated by italia.it: Tuesday and Saturday 10.30-13 and 15-16.30, from Wednesday to Friday 10.30-13.
The market square at the foot of the walls.
A glacial lake a few kilometers from Tigullio.
Torino on the river.
The colored marbles.
Mandatory online
Village among the olive trees with longitudinal caruggi connected by ramps and ladders under vaults and medieval arches; the civic loggia preserves the stone measurements for oil, wine and wheat.

At 1463 meters it is the highest peak of Supramonte: limestone cliffs with overhanging cliffs, spires and caves, bare peak and holm oaks at half coast. About 650 botanical species, about sixty endemic species; they nest there royal eagle and falcon of the queen and live the muflon. 360 degree panorama to Gennargentu; challenging trails for experienced hikers.
The roofless abbey, one of the first and most notable examples of Romanesque-Gothic architecture in Italy; in summer it hosts the music festival "Summer in Music."
In the Palazzo Comunale Pale, Triptychs and liturgical furnishings; in the center the golden reliquary called Tree of Gold, or Tree of Love, which according to tradition brings luck to lovers.
Regional nature reserve at the border of the Abruzzo National Park, between oak woods and beech: Lake Pio is a natural oasis of water birds, along the Sagittario flanked by poplars.
The frescoes of 1463.
The parish church of San Maurizio, the Blessed Virgin Assumption and the elegant Art Nouveau buildings on the lake.

The Protocenobio di San Sebastiano, a large barn of the Carthusians of Tsulti, considered the best example of 18th century architecture of Alatri; it contains the small church of San Bartolomeo apostolo and is on the Via Francigena del Sud.
The Norman castle that dominates the village.

It rises on the burial site of St. Erasmus, bishop martyr between the third and fourth centuries, and is mentioned by Gregory the Great as early as 590; bishop's seat until the Saracen incursions of the ninth century, then Benedictine monastery since 919, of Montecassino and Olivetani since 1491. Three aisles with Gothic pillars, the main baroque altar in polychrome marble, the Pendlebury organ of 1912 arrived from Yorkshire in 1988; under the floor the excavations of 1970-1976 revealed a Roman necropolis, the tomb of the martyr of the fourth century and a caroling crypt.
Italian garden of the nineteenth century with rare plants and secular trees.
A village of noble residences inside the walls.

Digged in the sandstone on the coast next to the Regional Marine Park      . Costa degli Dei: according to tradition, they obtained it at the end of the seventeenth century Neapolitan shipwrecks, which attributed salvation to a painting of the Madonna found on the beach. From 1880 about the local artist Angelo Barone, then his son Alfonso, expanded it by sculpting statues of sacred scenes and the life of Christ in the tuff. Festival on July 2nd with a procession to the sea; in winter open only Saturday and Sunday.

On the hill there is a park with a path to walk barefoot and a restaurant; on top the parish church of San Floriano, with square pronao and semicircular apse, contains frescoes from the end of the fourteenth-early fifteenth century, partly fragmentary, close to the school of Vitale da Bologna or Tommaso da Modena.
Amarcord Square.

It is located in the Castle of Avondo (sec. XVIII) and collects local Roman finds, the legacy of the historian Don Florindo Piolo, an ethnographic collection, a former vote and a picture gallery. Times to be agreed with the Municipality.
Ghirlandaio and Gozzoli in Narni.
The thirteenth century and then modified, is the oldest fountain of Offida; it is reached from Santa Maria della Rocca.
The sundial and the altarpiece of Salerno.

Borgo 36 km from Rome, with its historic centre of paved alleys and Urbian gate, the Clock Tower, seat of the Civic Museum and the Altomedieval church of San Leone; in the territory the Roman city of Lucus Feroniae, with the sanctuary of the goddess Feronia and a state Antiquarium with free entry.
Promontory joined to the coast by two tomboli, with Porto Santo Stefano and Porto Ercole, Spanish fortresses of the sixteenth century and coves.

Area brought to light after 1956 by the Swedish Institute of Classical Studies with King Gustavo of Sweden, next to the gorge of the river Vesca. A canopy protects the remains of Villanovian houses; then houses with tubs and fireplaces, hypogeal tombs similar to those of Tarquinia, to mound on the model of Cerveteri and rocks with nut and front of the house (VII-VI century BC). The most important tomb is Casale Vignale; the medieval chapel of San Giovenale and part of the castle of Di Vico remain.
The marble veil looks real.
The old walled town is dominated by Piazza Medicea with its imposing fountain, which overlooks many historic buildings.
The countryside inside the city.

Small necropolis with incineration of the iron age, used for about a century between the VIII and VII century BC: in the excavations of the eighties twenty tombs in three parallel rows emerged, the most recent protected by limestone slabs, today partially reconstructed. It is located in the Dominu municipal park, at the foot of the Grizzo hill; the furnishings are at the archaeological museum.

It belonged to the Corbella family (in the cadastral maps of the 1820s it was found by Ludovico Corbella), passed to the Martinelli family, who gave it to the archbishops of Milan: since 1820 it was their summer residence. After the laws of 1866 it was sold at auction to Angelo Sioli; acquired and restored by the municipality, it houses municipal offices, a conference room and an exhibition room.
The church of basil festivals.
Sunset on Stromboli.

Municipal park a few kilometers from the center, on the right of the river Leni, on a hill with the church of the martyr San Sisinnio (XVII century) among the most important community of ancient olive trees in the area, with specimens over 13 meters and trunks of about 5 meters in diameter, linked to the legends of the saint who protected children from witches. On the path of Santa Barbara, with barbecue and tables; total motor accessibility.
The rice fields around the city, beautiful to cycle when flooded between April and May.
the MiC card (Add. 2021) indicates closed every day and sources do not report times: contact the Valdese Foundation
MiC card (updated 2021) indicates closed every day, access to be agreed with the Municipality
The most extraordinary hall of the Buonconsiglio, reached by the walkway of the round: the fourteenth-century cycle of the Months, an absolute masterpiece of late dogotic painting.

Built in the middle of the 13th century and enlarged at the beginning of the 18th century, it has a Romanesque façade in limestone of Monte Cucco; inside frescoes in the style of Matteo da Gualdo. Under the high altar rests the remains of Blessed Thomas, a Camaldolese monk and patron saint of the village.
Seventeen churches and ancient palaces of Baronia.
The ancient village between two streams.
The first Big Bench in the Aosta Valley, inaugurated in 2021, can be reached with an easy walk.
The walls of a Messapian village in the countryside.
In the ancient cellars of the castle, it tells the story of liqueurs, spirits and balsamic vinegar; it includes the seasoning salt of the culatello.

The provincial protected area of about 2,417 hectares shared by Ceriale with seven other municipalities, around the valleys Ibà and Auzza and the peaks of Monte Acuto (748 m), Poggio Grande (812 m) and Poggio Ceresa (710 m). On a calcareous substratum you can see rocky ramparts, pinnacles and the "marmittes" of the giants of the river Iba; living together alpine and Mediterranean plants, including 34 species of protected orchids and the Campanula of Savona endemica, with raptors and a population of deers. Along the ancient streets of transhumance mills, mills and
Capital of Valnerina and home of San Benedetto, patron saint of Europe: Piazza San Benedetto with the Town Hall, Castellina and the cathedral of Santa Maria Argentea.
Where bells have been melting for a thousand years.
The last workshop in the country of potters.
The medieval village with views of the Apennines.

Borgo 60 km from Rome on Mount Celeste, overlooking the high valley of Sacco, with pre-Roman polygonal walls and the tower of the castle of the thirteenth century; from the beginning of the nineteenth century it attracted European painters of the landscape, as the Civic Museum of Art of Villa De Pisa tells with the Roman Vedutes of Joseph Anton Koch, and the forest of the Serpentara that inspired Gustave Doré. It is the land of the Cesanese di Olevano Romano DOC.

The route is divided into seven sections, including a marina with more than 1000 shells, one dedicated to flowers and a diorama of the coral reef; it is part of a garden-botanical garden of about 60,000 m2 on the Ionian Sea. According to the MiC card it is open every day 16-19, in July and August 16-23.

In the House of the Secretary, the nineteenth-century master complex of the Dessì family at the church of the Immaculate, tells with images, documents, videos and interactive laws the life of Emilio Lussu (Brigata Sassari, Party of Sardinian Action, anti-fascism, exile, with a section on "One year on the plateau") and of Joyce Lussu Salvadori, writer and partisan; photo of 1971 by Franco Caruso. In the Cannedu district, the writer's birthplace, in shale, is part of the route. Open from Wednesday to Sunday with seasonal hours.
Small museum in the restored Rock, with objects, documents and photographs on the Resistance in this territory during the Second World War.
The kilns produced bricks and tiles from 1878 to 1985, the slaughterhouse worked until 1968 and the paper mill Perra, of 1911, was at the time the only factory of wrapping paper.
Single ticket with Cisterna and Palazzo Petrignani: €7 full, €5 reduced, €2 from 6 to 18 years

The castle of Luzzana, dating from the commune between the thirteenth and sixteenth centuries, was part of a defensive network that included the nearby Castle of Terzo, called the "key of the Valley." It is the central element of the medieval village; purchased by the municipality in 1989, it was recovered as the site of the museum with the installation of Carlo Pinessi and architects Alberto Trussardi and Luciano Doneda.
A baroque city reborn after the earthquake.
The skiing story.
The round tower of 25 meters.
One of the most scenic castles in Lomellina, with the rare 15th-century recipe.

Medieval village of the Upper Tiber Valley overlooking the Carpinella valley, with walls of the 8th century, the characteristic "vigoli" , the remains of the Longobard fortress and the parish church of Santa Maria; just outside the walls the pine forest of Candeleto with the Silvio Children Ornithological Museum.
Palazzo del Quattrocento, now the town hall, with the windows of Luigi Ontani of 1998.
Majolica architecture.
The Risorgimento in Como.
The mother church of Valfurva.
At the foot of the hill of the Duomo, the current building dates back to 1724; the eighteenth-century bell tower could have been obtained from a castle tower.
The last days of Joachim Murat.
The Pollino butterflies.

The monumental complex of São Paulo, built on the remains of a medieval church, houses the Civic Museum that tells the history of the city from the Roman era to the twentieth century; the early Christian crypt preserves a fresco of St. Francis, indicated as the oldest image of the saint in Veneto.
To the west of the city, well-preserved cube of Byzantine-Norman art with three external apses and three doors: the two side for men, the main for women.
A nuraghe under a palace.

The museum recounts the territory through finds of more eras: traces of frequentation of the Middle Paleolithic (developed phase of the Musterian culture), apulian craters, epichysis and kyathos of the peucet culture (VI-II century BC), objects of the Roman municipality of Genusia including a tabula patronatus of 395 A.D., lay majolica from the rock villages of Casale and Revolt and ceramics of the 11th century. It takes its name from the Benedictine monastery of Santa Parasheve, built with the castle after the Norman conquest at the end of the 11th century.

Mount Ginestro was the seat of the acropolis and the cult of Jupiter Arcano; the belt in polygonal dry work of the VI century B.C. is part of a fortified system of about 4.5 km that encloses also the underlying Palestrina.
Among the places to see in the historic center, next to the Fortress.
One-tower nuraghe, one of the twelve of the territory of Martis, with rows alternated with red trachyte and white limestone.
The house of accounts.
One of the oldest tombs of Giants on the island, with its large perforated stele.

Digged on the north-eastern side of Mount Gravizze to preserve the ice with which the beer was cooled: the production was started in 1844 by Carinthia entrepreneurs with the waters of the river Resia and passed in 1881 to the factory of Francesco Dormisch. Renovated, it can be visited as a complement to the old factory, at the same times as the Mine Exhibition; on weekends reservation at least one day before.

About 3 km from Gavinana, a view of the valley, the river Limestre and the Apennines, with the Astronomical Observatory of the Pistoiese Mountain and the Park of the Stars, a scientific educational garden with great artistic installations on the Solar System; it is also reached with a CAI path.
The road games of the past, recovered and restored.

Ring of about 4 km along Lake Maggiore separated by traffic, passing through the museum and ending in Maccagno Superiore at a rock gym; from the Borgo Superiore the view embraces much of the Verbano, from the Canton Ticino to the Borromeo Gulf.
Church dated 1573, whose sandstone façade overlaps that of the Oratory of the Blessed Sacrament, forming a single building.

Liberty style villa with rationalist innovations, on two floors, built for Primo Carnera, born in Sequals in 1906 and world heavyweight champion since 29 June 1933. It hosts an exhibition on the life and career of the boxer with photos, movies and objects, and his gym, with facade and mosaic floor. It is part of the Lis Aganis Ecomuseo.

The English park was designed in the nineteenth century by Xavier Kurten, architect of the Savoy court; at the end of the century there were built the Orangerie and a glass and iron greenhouse of the Lefevre brothers of Paris. Every spring, between April and May, since 2000 there is held  "Messer Tulipano" with about 100,000 blooms of tulips and daffodils, including a collection of black tulips; in the park there are a coffee, a picnic area and a shop of flowers and local products.

In Borgo Bassano, the oldest area of Soave, outside the walls: church documented from 1098, linked to the apparition of the Virgin to a shepherd in the Ponsara Valley. After the cholera of 1836 (135 died in two months) it was demolished and rebuilt in Doric style on a project by engineer Zanella; on the ceiling the Assunta by Adolfo Mattielli. The façade looks at the lower Val Tramigna.
Walking path along the exterior of the walls, overlooking valleys and mountains; Visit Lazio advises you to walk it at sunset.
Book-shaped benches scattered throughout the country and surroundings feature pieces from Pavese's best-known works.
The trophy of the champion of the Galliate automobile.

Municipality of the lower Val Chisone with the museum of furniture and culture of Valligiana "Abitare in Valle" , the Big Bench of Serremarchetto overlooking the plain of Pinerol, the Fontana dell'Orsa and the mechanical nativity scene of Dubbione.

In the sacristy of the Duomo, wanted by Mgr. Luigi Frascarolo: silverware, wooden furnishings, liturgical fabrics and paintings by the lay companies of the city, including seventeenth-century crosses, monstrers from the seventeenth to the nineteenth century, the reliquary bust of San Massimo in silver lamina and the Book of Baptisms with recordings of 1562-1584. Open on request.

In the former Meroni spinning mill, the large yellow building visible from the Fortress, tells the entire cycle from the breeding of the baco to the processing of silk. Free admission on the second and third Sunday of the month, 14.30-17.

The mining pit is a symbol of the Gavorrano mine, at an altitude of 200 m, from which the majority of the mineral came back; excavated since 1914, it has the current castle in steel trellis of 1963 with two oblique dots, and in 1970 it was deepened up to -140 m above sea level. Next to the buildings of the winch room, the electric cabin and the compressors.

Montecalvo's mother church and sanctuary dedicated to the patron saint, disciple of Giuseppe Calasanzio, founder of the Pie Schools; it is linked to the museum of the memory of the blowjob and is the stop of the hike "Sui passi di San Pompilio."
The pontoon marshes as they were before the reclamation.

In the park next to Villa Sforza Cesarini, co-eval of the walls, it was dedicated to the Juno Sospita cited by Cicero. The excavations began in 1884-1892 with Lord Savile Lumley, who found there the Donary of Licinius Murena, marble group of knights and warriors of the first century BC offered by the consul after the victory over Mithridates and brought to England; the subsequent finds are in the civic museum.
The promenade overlooking the sea on the former railway.
The castle erected from the middle of the 14th century that dominates the village.
Giotto school in Rimini.

Less than 2 km from the village, the river Masino has dug the red trachytic rocks of Badde Traes: at the confluence with the river Pontisella the waterfall makes a jump of 15 meters and ends in a pond between elms and willows. Nearby there are the remains of an active mill until the mid-Twentieth century and a picnic area in the woods. From Martis you go out towards Nulvi and take the dirt road to the right signposted "historic-environmental trail Triulintas mill"; after less than 1 km there is the parking lot, from which the path runs along the stream with two bridges up to the foot of the waterfall.

It is indicated by the regional portal as one of the most famous Baroque monuments of Bergamasca, overlooking Piazza Emancipazione; a overpass connects the churchyard to the first floor of the adjacent museum, which preserves its treasures.
An Austro-Hungarian fortress without war.

In the civic center designed by Aldo Rossi, it tells the Roman centuriation of the territory between Villa del Conte and Camposampiero, bordered by the Muson Vecchio, the territory of Mirano and the Brenta: from the imposition of the agricultural grid to agriculture, breeding, trade and domestic life, to the transformations followed by barbaric invasions. All the finds come from the centuriate area, including those of the recent excavations in Borgoricco with the Superintendence; among the most valuable pieces the bronze strigili and the architectural slabs in terracotta decorated with vegetable bas-relief, considered unique. Guided visits, workshops for schools, temporary exhibitions and activities with the University of Padua. Closed on Mondays; reduced for schools, 7-14 year olds and over 65 years olds.

Fortress of the twelfth century with square tower on a spur of volcanic rock, border fortress of the Heritage of St. Peter, with walls that go down to overhang; according to the municipality the village was fortified by Pope Gregory V in 997, destroyed by the troops of Henry IV in 1083 and rebuilt by the Counts Bovacciani of Chiusi in 1097, and in 1444 it surrendered after months of siege the castle Bernardo d'Utri. From the blackbirds you can see 360 degrees on Lazio, Umbria and Tuscany, from Monte Amiata and Radicofani to the valley of Paglia; today it is a hotel with restaurant and from here starts the Lazio section of Via Francigena.

In the former school of the hamlet Castellengo, which also houses the Park of Baraggia, it is dedicated to the history and rural civilization of the Cossatian area: traditions, nature and memory of work and local life. It is part of the Biellese Museum Network; it opens on established days, with free and free entrance (tel. 015 351128).
€6, reduced €5
Only for groups of 15 people

In the district of San Pellegrino, the feast of September 3, when the porters carry in procession the machine of Santa Rosa, about 30 meters high; the festival is recognized by UNESCO intangible heritage.
Dating back to 1300, about 2 km from the village along a walk in the woods.

The ancient Littoria, before the founding cities of the Agro Pontino (1932): the rationalist squares of Oriolo Frezzotti with the Civic Tower and Palazzo M, the museums of the reclamation as Piana delle Orme, and on the coast the Lido di Latina and the lake of Fogliano in the National Park of the Circeo.
Galtellì as it is in the novel.
A Romanesque abbey on the river Esino.
Stone lions on the Lambro.
The big woods behind the Real Casina.
The Roman Gurulis Vetus told by his ex-vote.

The capital of the Garfagnana dominated by the Ariostesca Rocca, where Ludovico Ariosto was governor extended from 1522 to 1525 and which today houses the Palazzo di Atlante dedicated to the Orlando Furioso; with the Cathedral of Saints Peter and Paul and the Black Christ, and on the hill the Fortress of Mont'Alfonso, reachable with the Path of Ariosto.

The tour of the island by boat touches coves and tips like Cala Felce, Cala del Core, Cala d'Inferno, Punta Capo Bianco (where Fellini shot scenes of the Satyricon), Punta Incenso and the faraglioni of Lucia Rosa and Calzone Muto; the seabed are known for diving and underwater photography, with Punta Papa the wreck of a ship of the Second World War.
A villa on the Riviera opened once a month.
Full Cremonese Mannerism.
Eretti around 1282 by Cardinal Giacomo Savelli, then Pope Honorius IV, and restored in 1769; there is buried San Gaspare Del Bufalo.

Made in the 17th century where there was a pond, measuring 96 by 38 meters and is divided by the Neo-Gothic Town Hall (1788) by Piazza Turati; in the center the marble "listone" is the meeting point of the housewives, the Saturday market and in November the San Carlo Fair. Not far away, near the embankment in Piazza San Martino, the fifteenth-century Torrione, the only rest of the fortifications.
Theatre in 1272 of the assassination of Henry of Cornwall, a crime recalled by Dante in Hell.

A 912-metre-long road that remained almost intact from the fifteenth century, with the two circles of 1367 and 1480: gates, bastions, Ghibelline blackbirds with swallow tails and round walkways. The Torre dello Sperone, pentagonal and 18 meters high, attributed to Francesco di Giorgio Martini, the Torre dello Scorticatore, where the walls reach 15 meters, the Round of enlargement completed in 1490, the Landroni porticoati and Porta San Giovanni; from the terrace near the Bargello the view arrives at the Conero. You can also visit them with a guide.
The history of Italian espresso in hundreds of machines.
Since 2005 the village has been a permanent art gallery with 21 works by internationally renowned artists, in collaboration with the Fondation Gianadda of Martigny, visible all year round.
The tomb of St. Augustine.
Private property, open to the public only on specific occasions (Visit Trentino)
Roman Modena on stone.
Two millennia of Jewish history.
The theatre dedicated to Yves Montand.
The view of the village, from the hills to the Alps.
The collection of anatomical waxes housed in the Citadel of the Museums in the district of Castello.
In Arcello, at 290 m, the primitive fortified fence remains, clearly visible on top of a hill, the tower then become bell tower.
A waterfall in the woods just minutes from the road.
Archaeology with a view of the gulf.
The church of the vote of Galla Placidia.

Norman quadrangular castle (XI-XII century), with definitive appearance in the fourteenth century, which dominates the access to the Civita and the Earth; intact east and west towers, Norman bifora on the tower of via Castello, court with well and numerous wounds. It was the seat of the feudalist and sold at auction by the Savoys in 1868.

The large wool mill designed in 1861 by the Belgian architect Auguste Vivroux: 80 meters long, five floors more basement and attic, 330 windows and 125 cast iron columns; abandoned in 1966-67 and public since 2013, national symbol of industrial archaeology.
Village of houses in dark stone on the basaltic plateau, with the nuraghe Losa, one of the symbols of the Nuragic age.
The city in costume.

The Velino falls with three jumps for about 165 meters, the highest waterfall in Europe, created by the Romans to drain a swampy area; the paths touch the lower and upper Belvedere, the specola of Pius VI and the "balcony of the lovers."

Borgo dell'alta valle Arroscia on the road between the sea and Piedmont, among the most beautiful villages in Italy since 2026: the arcade course, the collegiate, the small Salvini theatre and the museum of masks of the Ubagu.
Dervio offers a lakefront in the green, small beaches and conditions suitable for windsurfing and kitesurfing; you can also go out by sailing boat.

Outdoor amphitheatre of about 4,000 square meters whose setting reconstructs Palestine: Cenacle, Sanhedrin, Gethsemane, Herod's Palace, Pretorio di Pilate and Calvary. Here more than 400 inhabitants stage the Passion, documented since 1816 and interrupted only by world wars; the 29th edition runs from 19 June to 26 September 2027, with up to 3,000 spectators per replica. You can also visit behind the scenes.

Along the highway 16 towards Monopoli, 4 km from Fasano: a small church of the 10th century with three naves with cupolette in axis, indicated as the first example of the genre in the region. Three kilometers further, on the same road, is the crypt of San Procopio, perhaps frescoed in the fourteenth century.
The Roman Ancona on the hill.

The ancient nucleus, probably of high-medieval foundation, has a spiral plant and houses of pink bricks enclosed by medieval walls, with a malaestian well; in the center the work "The sign of fire" by the sculptor Loreno Sguanci, dedicated to the processing of terracotta.

The ancient Praeneste on the slopes of Mount Ginestro: the Sanctuary of Fortuna Primigenia of the II century BC, Palazzo Barberini built on its terraces with the National Archaeological Museum and the Mosaic of the Nile, the buildings of the Forum, the cathedral of Sant'Agapito, the Diocesan Museum and the birthplace of Giovanni Pierluigi from Palestrina.
A walk through meadows and woods to the 16th century church.
The Gothic frescoes.
unmanaged site on private land: the owner's consent is required before crossing the gate

The village has 57 sundials, each with a Latin motto, the work of Gnomonist Mario Tebenghi, including the one on the bell tower; the route in the village goes from the castle to the parish church of Santa Maria della Pace. Bilingual guided tours (Italian and English) with the Montiglio Monferrato Walking Tour, max 25 people.

Circular plan furnace with local stone foundations and raised in brick, discovered in 1957 during the construction of the primary school: the clay hob, of 4,10 meters of diameter, rests on a vaulted corridor, and the praefurnium is partly preserved. It was mainly used to cook bricks and tiles; the Municipality dates to the third century BC, while the archaeological analysis places the last use of it within the first half of the first century A.D. It is considered one of the best preserved in Lombardy.
The visitor center of the forest.
Still visible trait of Roman limestone paved road that connected Nomentum (Mentana) to Eretum; along the route were found numerous tombs of Roman age.

Villette has about forty sundials, many in a courtyard of Vallaro, spread since the early seventies by Eng. Giacomo Brindicci Bonzani, then mayor; the parish church has two, one of the early nineteenth century and one of 1981. They are visible all year round; guided tours are organized on request and a map is available.

Inaugurated for Turin 2006 in the Villa Widemann, it tells the origin of skiing, the birth of the Sestriere station and the history of the Rochon company, an artisan workshop that between 1930 and 1960 produced wooden skis and supplied the 3rd Pinerolo Alpine Regiment, with finds and documents preserved by the last heir Dina Pons. The hall      ... The Factory. Women and work are collected from the former Waldensian Museum on the cotton factory Widemann and the female condition, donated by the Waldensian Consistory in 2009. Visits by appointment (tel. 0121 58601).
The fortress of the village, signalled by Visit Tuscany among the places of the Prato area.
The fort of sugar.
A parish church mentioned in 998.

Oratory of the 11th century used by the Farfensian monks, alternating prayer and work next to their agricultural courtyards: rectangular plan with round apse facing east, frescoes of the 15th century and an Annunciation on the apse.
Mineralogical, paleontological and zolfara museum, with minerals and sulfur extraction technologies.
The summer residence of the popes.

In the hamlet of Campocavallo, 3 km from Osimo: designed by Costantino Costantini and consecrated in 1905; parties of the Addolorata on the third Sunday of September and of the Covo on the first Sunday of August.

Opened in 2002 on the second floor of the building of the Pharmacy Peer, in one of the oldest private residences in the city: in rooms partly covered with historical wood tells about four centuries of history of pharmacy and medicine in Tyrol, starting from the instruments of an ancient family of spiciness in Bressanone.

The village perched 208 metres in the Pollino National Park, with medieval structure built around a Longobard fortress; in the territory the Romito Cave, with the famous paleolithic graffiti of the early Bos, the sanctuary of the Madonna of Constantinople overlooking the Lao and the abandoned village of Avena.
The place where Galileo was born on February 15, 1564, located in the district of Sant'Andrea at numbers 24-26 of the current Via Giusti.

Established in 1982, it tells of the relationship between the territory and work: spinning and weaving, woodworkers and charcoal miners and the silver mine, with historical cartography, tools and reconstructions of life in the mine; it is part of the fifteenth century rural house of the center with domestic environments, artisan tools and agricultural work of the mountain.

Stufles is the oldest neighborhood, with neolithic origins, a time of artisans and poor families and today the artists' neighborhood with small studios. The Aquila Bridge, mentioned since 1233 connects it to the centre: the wooden bridge was destroyed several times by the floods and the iron bridge was built in 1883.

An isolated relief of about 75 metres in the Po Valley, between Lambro and Olona, covered with vineyards and protected as the San Colombano Hill Park. On the slopes are cultivated Croatina, Barbera and Uva Rara, base of San Colombano DOP (frizzante, firm and reserve); the first reference to the cultivation of the hill dates back to 1371, with the reclamation started by Galeazzo Visconti, and in the nineteenth century these wines were compared to those of Valtellina. Itinerary of reference: the Strada del Vino San Colombano e dei Sapori Lodigiani.
Contemporary art in Sicily.
Behind the facade of the Palazzo della Provincia, hanging gardens on several levels and a crypt with 6th century mosaics from San Severo di Classe, under a neo-Gothic tower.

Fraction of a few houses along the Mincio, with water mills grinding wheat and cereals, the turrita belt and the taverns where to stop; the name, fortified settlement, dates back to the Longobards. It is one of the most beautiful villages in Italy; in spring wisteria blooms. Cuisine of Valeggio tortellini and river fish (luccio, trota, eel).
A facade of stone portraits.
The building symbol of the Spa Roncegno della Belle époque.
View of the monuments of the city.
Verona Romanesque art on remains of the Roman age.
Memory of the Great War in a secluded valley.
Like Trapani's salt.
The neighborhood was born in the 1920s like the English garden city, from the Roman baroque to rationalism, set by Caro Diario di Nanni Moretti.
The MiC card reports hours closed every day, but the Superintendence announces events at the museum in October 2026: check opening (tel. 06 91984744)
The fortress became a Dantesque villa.
Visit Tuscany indicates it as temporarily closed to the public
Strong and trails above Gemona.

Site of about three hectares on the western edge of the Giara di Serri, discovered at the beginning of the twentieth century, with Etruscan, Phoenician and Cypriot objects that testify to the exchanges of the Nuragic age; it was frequented also in Punic, Roman and Byzantine age. Four groups of structures: the sacred area with the well-shaped temple, the paved atrium, the two-altar hypetral temple and the huts of the priest and of the chief; the large courtyard of the feasts with porches, seats, common kitchen and market; the enclosure of the double betilus; the courtyard of the supplications and the curia with about 50 seats, perhaps seat of the assembly of the leaders. The nuraghe bronzes and models found in the excavations are at the National Archaeological Museum of Cagliari. On the site the church of Santa Maria della Vittoria, attested in the seventh century and rebuilt by the victorious monks in the XI-XII century, feast on 11 September. Open every day 9-17.
On the trail of young Stradivarius.

Late-Gothic church built by Valentin Winkler between 1503 and 1527, with high steeple bell tower visible from afar; it preserves a high altar of the early sixteenth century inspired by the altar of Creglingen of Riemenschneider, a Gothic pulpit in stone by Leonhard Fabri, the Assumption of Karl Henrici (1783) and frescoes of the fifteenth century re-emerged from the restoration. In the cemetery, tombstones of local nobles and the fifteenth-century chapel of San Michele with three naves with upper ossuary.

The civic heart of the city overlooking the port, with the Palazzo Pretorio (now town hall) and porticos that once housed shops and exchange counters. From here, the medieval centre, built on lands once submerged by the lake, runs through Piazza delle Erbe, Porta Bruciata towards Piazza San Rocco and Piazza Catena, Porta San Marco called "Porta Veneziana," Piazza Cavour and Porta San Michele; in Via Roma you can see the excavations of the Roman thermal baths.

Natural monument recognized by the Lazio Region, includes the municipal park, the nineteenth-century villa of the Clementi family, tree-lined avenues, fountains and the mineral spring of Santo Stefano, whose water, it is said, also helped Michelangelo. During the war the villa was occupied by the Germans and bombed; at the end of the seventies the family donated the part above the SS155 to the municipality. Today lindens, acacias, cypresses, firs and chestnuts on a slope, with ample parking.
Palazzo nobile that today houses the town hall.

A farm of the Roman Republican wine.
The tour along the old town belt offers views of the countryside; near the walls the church of Santa Maria in Castello, with on the altar a Madonna with Bambino del Pomarancio.

With the thirteenth-century Palazzo del Podestà, born from the union of three tower houses and today seat of the Municipality, and the fourteenth-century Loggia dei Priori with the Loggia del Banditore.

The suburban residence of Livia, wife of Augustus, along the Via Flaminia, with gardens, paintings and mosaic floors; here was found the Augustus of Prima Porta, today at the Vatican Museums. Visits suspended since August 2025 for the PNRR yard.
The seaside resort with kilometers of sand, establishments and free beach, shaded by the Tombolo pine forest; connected to the city by a bike path.

Born to document the tradition of the wooden tarsia of the Rolese, bloomed between the eighteenth and twentieth centuries with the round tables called "Rolini" , requested in the seventeenth century throughout the Duchy of Modena and Reggio and then sold abroad. It exhibits ancient carpenter tools, original documents and some furniture; it is also documentation center with library specialized in wood art and restoration and a photographic archive on the inlaid furniture of Rolo. According to the page of the City is visitable by reservation.

Archaeological, historical and artistic museum in the remains of the Franciscan monastery of 1234, with half of a Gothic cloister that houses a Roman sarcophagus and medieval tombs: finds of the Varesotto palafittes, a monoxile piroga from the lake of Monate, materials of Golasecca and Malpensa, epigraphs and Roman finds, the marble pluteo of San Giovanni di Castelseprio, and on the upper floor of the gallery, coat of arms and sculptures. Thematic garden that reproduces the territory, flora and fauna of the Gran Sasso National Park and Monti della Laga, open all year round with free entry.

Opened in 2009 after the restoration of the complex, which also includes a medieval tower and the municipal art gallery. It offers guided tours and educational activities.
The entrance viewpoint and the canvas of Mariano Rossi.

It is the last strip of the Aci Wood, with the Palombe Cave with its columnary basalts, springs such as the Iron Water and raptors as a ghep and buzzard. It is an overhanging coast of lava flows of different eras, up to about 80 meters high, established in 1999 on 225 hectares.
Medieval bridge with ten arches beneath which the Centa flowed, next to the baroque sanctuary erected for the miracle of July 2, 1637 with a triptych of Barbagelata.
A protected granite archipelago.

A 60-hectare park, born from the "cinto de mura" , purchased by Gerolamo Nicolò Contarini in 1407 and grown around the Villa Sigurtà, a late seventeenth-century villa that in the nineteenth century was the headquarters of Francesco Giuseppe and Napoleon. Secular oaks, about one million tulips (March-April), a avenue of 30,000 roses (May-September), eighteen mirrors of water, labyrinth, garden of the medicinals, horizontal sundial, Hermitage, votive cave and farm with animals. Appointed the most beautiful park in Italy in 2013 and Europe in 2015; open from March to November, 9-18.
The Excalibur educational trail is an easy path between beech and larch woods; more challenging is the Monte Caviojo trail, which passes through the military tunnel of Cima Neutra.

Crushed mill in the rock, where oil was once produced, part of the cave system of the carpignan basin; Annibale de Capua built the abbey of Santa Maria della Grotta on the crypt of San Giovanni and a nearby underground mill.
Hanging garden near Piazza del Quirinale overlooking the Markets of Traiano, Sant'Agata dei Goti and the Tower of Milizie.

Remains of the castle of Caterina Cornaro with the Civic Tower and the smallest Reata tower; in the spaces of the castle since 1798 there is the theatre, rebuilt in 1857, today the Duse Theatre with 341 seats.

Built by the accounts Solaro from 1675 on a project by Guarino Guarini and completed around 1780 with the staircase adorned with marbles and sculptures of the Fontana d'Ercole della Venaria; of the Savoy since 1795, summer residence of Carlo Felice. You can visit royal apartments, party hall and Chinese halls. UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Sanctuary of the Holy Valley clinging to the rock in a wood of holm oaks, home to St. Francis since 1217; here in Christmas 1223 he set up the first nativity scene. In the Chapel of the Nativity scene, dug into the rock, a fresco of the fifteenth-century school of Giottesca with the Nativity and the Nativity of Greccio and, on the outer wall, a fresco of the Master of Fossa; you can also visit the dormitory of San Francesco, the church of San Bonaventura (XIII century), the refectory and the cave of Blessed Giovanni da Parma. Open every day from 9 am to 6 pm.

Aristocratic residence between the end of the sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries, entirely in trachite, rare well-preserved example of Sardinian architecture, inhabited until 1978: a single floor with thirteen connecting rooms, courtyard and a portico on the road; red volcanite frames, windows with lozenges and diamond tips, portal with bulls and shells and Christological monogram. It houses the exhibition "Forum Traiani" and "Sardinia Romana" (Roman Sardinia), 18 panels based on 19th century engravings by La Marmora and Spano. According to SardiniaCulture open every day 9:30-17:30 from October to April and 9:30-19:30 from May to September; audioguide in four languages.

The two artificial lakes surround the plateau of Orroli and partially cover the gorges of the Flumendosa: the Mulargia is nestled between reliefs that descend to the shores, on the Flumendosa valleys and sky mirror into the water. Hiking can be done by boat or canoe.
A garden of cedars under the Gonzaghesque rock.
Ötzi's house, the ice-clad man who lived over 5000 years ago and was found in 1991 on the Similaun glacier, preserved with clothes and tools, and the history of the region up to the high Middle Ages.
Romanesque church in the historic centre with the marble bezel of the Blood of Christ, attributed to Donatello and dated to the first half of the fifteenth century.

First mentioned in 976 as "basilica" in the castrum of Agrate, it was rebuilt in Romanesque times and rebuilt several times. It has three aisles and a tripartite façade with a 12th century painted bezel. He's in front of the baptistery.
Church of medieval origin transformed into collegiate in 1630.

Founded in the late Middle Ages and rebuilt after the earthquake of 1456, it has five naves, a rare case in Abruzzo; the golden coffered ceiling of Carlo Sabatini of 1680, stuccos by Giambattista Gianni, and the Baroque wrought iron gate of Santo and Ilario di Rocco (1699-1705) that closes the Captone del Sacramento. Inside the Museum of the Basilica with goldsmiths, statues and sacred furnishings.
One of the oldest springs of the plain, rich in birds.
The castle among the vineyards, today the convention center with Renaissance frescoes, visible from the promenade of the Talvera with the hill of Santa Maddalena and the Catinaccio in the background.

A 17th century shrine on Monte Triona, the sacred place most dear to the Bisacquinese, on a ridge reached by a panoramic road; the floods of 2015 and the fire of 2017 have made the slopes unstable, the object of regional works with networks and paramassi barriers.
The Malaspina and Doria castle.
Terraces built over the centuries with dry walls, cultivated with olive trees, vines and fruit trees; the chestnut grove of Lunch hosts in autumn a feast dedicated to browns.
Snorkeling floors where Jacques Mayol was trained.

Blessing to the sailors.

St. Philipp, who met St. Francis between 1221 and 1225, founded in 1228 the monastery of St. Peter de Molito, submerged in 1940 by the lake together with the old Borgo San Pietro: church and monastery were dismantled and rebuilt stone for higher stone, and the chapel preserves frescoes from the sixteenth century and the reliquary with the heart of the saint. The museum, opened in 1977 and re-assembled in 2000, exhibits capitals, coats of arms and bells from the 12th to the 18th century, the wooden portal of 1511 by Maestro Giacomo di Bernardino, a wooden Madonna of the 14th to the 15th century, the statue of Saint Filippa of the 15th century, tools of pharmacy and leather trunks of the Clarisse, as well as paintings by Giorgio De Chirico, including a self-portrait of 1960. Open every day 8.30-12.30 and 16-18; tel. 0746 558134.

Rebuilt in 1789 on the site of the chapel of the Dominican monastery, whose ruins are visible to the right of the church; the previous, near San Rocco, was destroyed by the earthquake of 1783. Next to it stands the church of the Rosary (XVIII-XIX century). Open during functions.
A terrace on the plain from a thousand year old monastery.

Borgo della val Merdanzo, Orange Flag, with the square Vittorio Emanuele that looks like a theatre, the Castle of the Lizard with the museum of the history of the village, the churches of Sant'Antonio Abate and Santa Maria degli Angeli and the murals of the Sixties.

Area between Garda and the Brenta Dolomites declared Biosphere Reserve in 2015, with alpine meadows, woods and moors; from the valley start trekking towards Monte Corno, Tremalzo, Cima d'Oro, Cima Parì and Val Concei, and the Ledro Trek with two rings (the Low measures 19 km).

Dedicated to the botanist Don Pietro Porta, born in Moerna, who studied the local flora describing new species (some bear his name); he is located in the former turnary cheese factory of the village, in front of his house. Upstairs a multimedia path with objects belonging to Porta and samples of plants collected by him, on the ground floor the original halls of milk processing with kangaroos and sports. Bourbon hunting pavilion in the hamlet of Persano, today inside a vast military area: baroque palace with porch courtyard and four octagonal turrets with spiral staircases, and in the atrium a large staircase of honor with the marble statue of a guard dog attributed to Canova. In the eighteenth-century estate was selected the breed of horses of Persano, from which it is said to derive the palace of Ferrari.

Private cellars and the Cantina Sociale produce Rosso Piceno, Falerio dei Colli Ascolani, Templaria, Gramelot, brandy of marc, anise, mistrà and sparkling wines. The village is also known for the historic Carnival, which closes with the night procession of the Moccoli with lights off, and for the Templaria festival at the end of August.

The fortress surrounded by the moat built by Frederick II in the 13th century on a Norman fortification, then a Renaissance court led by two women; prison and barracks under the Bourbons, is a museum since 2017 with exhibition halls and the collection of ceramics of the "butt."

The square, the neo-Gothic church of San Vittore, the castle, the tower and the park made by Carlo Alberto after 1832, with the Agency created to experiment with new agricultural techniques and today seat of the University of Gastronomic Sciences and the Wine Bank. UNESCO World Heritage Site. The castle is a private residence.

Village 606 m on a hill of the Amiata, at the foot of the Riserva di Poggio all'Olmo, born around the Aldobrandesco castle of Castiglion del Torto, with late medieval tower, Neo-Medieval tower and Renaissance courtyard. The church of St. Nicholas, with three naves, preserves the 17th-century main altar and a canvas of the Madonna with the Sleeping Child; outside the village the seventeenth-century church of the Madonnino. It tells the population of the valley from the prehistory (rests of Elephas antiquus about 120,000 years ago) to the Apennine civilization, to the Lucanian kits and to the ex vows of the Sanctuary of San Marco (III century BC); the Roman section on Grumentum exposes the marble head of Livia Drusilla, a ivory piss from the hole, statues from the thermal baths, epigraphs and coins, until the high-medieval abandonment of the city. The largest natural water of the Euganean Hills, fed by thermal springs, with water at 17-18 degrees even in winter and reeds, willows and cypresses along the banks. Casa del jurista e patriota garibaldino Antonino Greco, on two floors and a basement: on the ground floor the kitchen with the original structure, the rustic beliefs and an ancient furnace, on the upper floor rooms with antique furniture. It preserves rare books, Latin dictionaries of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, the first encyclopedia UET (1863) and a sixteenth-century Petrarch, statues of the nativity scene made of mache, hand-embroidered lines and a cradle painted according to the Venetian techniques of the eighteenth century; the chapel, built around 1850 and consecrated with the bull of Pius IX, houses gold reliquaries, a silver cup and a painting by the Neapolitan Antonio Sarnelli.
Outdoor shrine of ancient Sulky where the ashes of children born dead or dead young were laid in urns: urns, punic votive stele, fences and the Carthaginian belt, with the remains of a Roman cistern.
The great ossuary in the upper part of the city, in Oslavia, with the remains of Italian and Austrian fallen of the First World War.

Trail that starts from Premana: about 2 hours to the alpine pasture, an extra hour to the Lower Lake and another 30 minutes to the Upper Lake, from which you can climb to the Upper Pizzo. In the village you can rent bikes with pedal assistance to reach also the Alpe Campo and the Alpe Premaniga.

Country of the Foreign Judicaries known for the villages on piles built between the late Neolithic and the Bronze Age on the banks of the ancient lake Carera, today protected peat bog: since 2011 they have been on the UNESCO World Heritage List on the serial site "Prehistoric palafittic sites of the Alpine arch." You can visit the archaeological area in the biotope, the Museum of Palafitte in Casa Carli and the Archeo Nature Park; around, Castel Campo, the rural villages, the Camerona cave and the Rio Ruzza waterfall.
A mountain hike to the places of one of the great Italian disasters of the twentieth century, with views of the Presolana.

Founded in 1995 and run by the Nivola Foundation, it is located in the former public wash-house on the hill of Su Cantaru, overlooking the village, with pavilions designed by Peter Chermayeff and Umberto Floris and a park that contains the historical source. The permanent collection contains hundreds of sculptures, paintings and graphics by Costantino Nivola (1911-1988), a figure of modernism of the twentieth century; it also houses temporary exhibitions and artist residences on art, architecture, landscape and public art. The MiC indicates opening 10:30-19:30, closed on Wednesdays.

The center preserves beautiful religious buildings and noble palaces; during 'A Chiena' the course of the stream Tenza is partly diverted and the streets, literally flooded, become a feast with water games and water.
