Three-nave church of the lords of Torre de' Ratti, with the coat of arms of Rati Opizzoni in counterfacade and decorations of the twenties by Clemente Salsa. It preserves the Assumption of the Virgin of Luca Giordano (1690), a Madonna with Child and Saints (1633) attributed to a pupil of the Fiasella, the seventeenth-century altar of San Carlo, a wooden choir of the nineteenth century, the Assumption of Carlomagno Parodi and a crucifix perhaps of the workshop of Maragliano.
Oratory of the thirteenth century, marked by the Touring among the things to see in the city of flowers.

Rare example of Romanesque architecture: the lower part, circular and in irregular stones with pebbles with fishbone, dates back to the tenth century (perhaps around 930); the upper octagon, with blind triphors and hanging arches, is of the XI-XII century and was consecrated between 1122 and 1151 by Bishop Litifredo. Inside a 16th century fresco well preserved and, on the vault, what seems to be the biscione visconteo. Visit to the parish on request.
Longobard graves in open air, next to Roman finds.

Just outside the center, in the plain of the Casale: the monastery was founded by the Benedictines between 542 and 552, about twenty years after Montecassino; the oldest walls of the church preserve Byzantine frescoes with scenes from the Old and New Testaments.
Trevi's art.
A stretch of coast protected as a site of community interest, with the rock of St. Francis and small coves that make it an almost untouched place.

At the foot of the hills of the Bregonze, Chiuppano is the village where fossil teeth and bones of the Anthracotherium were found in 1948-1949, an animal lived about 30 million years ago, today told by the Naturalistic Museum of the Bregonze; in Via Roma stands the parish church of San Michele Arcangelo, built between 1929 and 1942.

Medieval village born between the 10th and 11th centuries on a cliff above the valley of Mingardo, linked to the Sanseverino and abandoned between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. The castle remains guarding the Devil's Gola, the fifteenth-century baronial palace and the churches of Santa Maria degli Angeli and San Nicola; the Cilento Museum of the Emigrant is located there. Walk up from a small parking lot.
The house of Via Morone where Alessandro Manzoni lived from 1814 to 1873, literary living room with the studio and the room preserved.

Built on the ancient Venetian fortress of the village, it has defensive walls, Guelph battlements and cross-windows overlooking the lake; Napoleon I, II and III stayed there and General Mac-Mahon after the battle of Solferino on June 24, 1859. You can visit the Napoleonic halls and the secular garden, from which you go up to the walls; inside the church of San Giuseppe, completed in 1737, with paintings of the seventeenth century.

In the birthplace of Carlo Ceresa, Baroque painter among the most important figures of the painting of Bergamo in the seventeenth century, with over 300 works attributed in Bergamasco. Upstairs, the permanent exhibition of his works, sometimes with temporary exhibitions; from the museum starts the "Percorso ceresiano" (Cesasian route), which connects sixteen paintings of the artist in eight churches of the municipality. Visitable all year round.

Country of the valley of Pescara that takes its name from the  "Turris Passum" (Turris Passum), ford tower in the borders of the abbey of San Clemente in Casauria; today it is known for the Castello Gizzi, seat since 1979 of the House of Dante in Abruzzo, and for the Dante Pinacoteca.

Borgo dei Borghi più Belli d'Italia since 2023, preserves buildings with stone portals and double windows such as Casa Fattarsi, Casa Lorengo and Palazzo Manfroni, as well as the parish church of San Bartolomeo. The name, in the Caldis or Caldesio scrolls, comes from an ancient hot spring today disappeared.
Grotesque sculptures carved into the rock, including sphinxes, warriors in struggle, the hanging house, the Orco and Cerbero, in a path that closes with a small temple.

Borgo della Bassa Valsesia among vineyards and hazelnuts: on Monte Cucco the neoclassical Villa Caccia di Alessandro Antonelli, seat of the Ethnographic Historical Museum of the Lower Valsesia, and in the historic center the Cantina dei Santi, last authentic remnant of the millenary Benedictine abbey of San Silvano, with fifteenth century frescoes.

The center is crossed by the canals San Domenico, Vena and Lombardo, which make Chioggia a small Venice, the city has Roman origins and populated with the inhabitants of the hinterland fleeing from barbarian invasions. Corso del Popolo, elegant and always crowded, was defined by Curzio Malaparte as a great coffee.

The main museum of the city, in the monastery of St. Saviour Santa Giulia: the Cross of Desire of the ninth century, the frescoes of the Chorus of the nuns, the remains of the Roman domus and the basilica of St. Saviour; part of the UNESCO site and seat of large exhibitions.

Closed on Mondays; bookings tel. 0921 551632.

Wanted in 1478 by Count Francesco d'Arco, with the convent of the Reformed Friars completed in 1482 and the church ten years later; portal in bronze and terracotta tiles on the façade of Fra' Silvio Bottes, author also of the statue of San Francesco on the square. In the fifteenth-century cloister, a level below the church, the tombstones of Susanna Collalto and Barbara Martinengo. Church open by day.
Founded by Varano and then dedicated to Saint Clare, linked to the cult of Saint Camilla Battista da Varano.

On the ground floor of the seventeenth-century seminary: silver donated by the bishops of the diocese and paintings of the seventeenth century, including the Madonna del Rosario from the Episcopio and two paintings from the church of San Francesco.

Of the second half of the first century AD, it could accommodate about 6000 spectators; identified in 1814 and brought to light in 1938, it preserves the foundations of the scene and the basements of the porch.

A neo-Gothic castle with three towers built since 1831 by the Marquis Roberto Tapparelli d'Azeglio, Massimo's brother, as a summer residence; Queen Margherita stayed there for many summers. Lounges with frescoes and stuccoes and part of the furniture of the family of Azeglio; around a romantic park of about 50 hectares attributed to Xavier Kurten, with panoramic paths, cave, lake, fountains and monumental greenhouses for citrus. Open on the first and third Sundays of the month from May to October, 14:30-19:00, with guided tours.
The synagogue, a memory of the rich past of the Jewish community of the country, with the Jewish museum complex.

From the Porta Vecchia the Corso dei Lincei crosses the village to the square dedicated to Federico Cesi, on which the palace overlooks; the name of the village comes from the sources of the Amerino and Furapane, which place it between the waters.
To be combined with the visit of the churches.

Medieval village on the Red Hill, in the Lepini Mountains above the valley of the Amaseno, Orange Flag: the Cistercian Abbey of Fossanova, the Roman colony of Privernum and the cathedral with the relic of St. Thomas Aquinas.
It houses wooden sculptures by Pietro Bussolo and the Marinoni.
Villages and peonies.
Entirely carved crypt in the rock, a place of worship of the Basilian monks, with traces of frescoes dating back to around 1100.

The ancient Puteoli, the largest port of the Empire: the Rione Terra on the spur of tuff, the Macellum with the columns marked by bradisism, the Flavian Amphitheatre and, towards the sea, the acropolis of Cuma with the Antro della Sibilla.

Ancient source of Montepagano, probably in use since the 11th century when the village took shape, composed of fountain, watering trough for the cattle in a niche and washroom covered in stone where women washed the clothes.
Five churches in a mile.

The polygonal walls, for which Segni is twinned with Mycenae, go up from the fortifications to the acropolis. The Saracen Gate has a monolithic architrave of over three meters and is the best preserved example of its kind; it was staged on the Grand Tour and designed by Irish painter Edward Dodwell.

The first historical monument that you will encounter climbing from Folla along the Briantea: the Romanesque apse with blind arches dates back to about 1000, sacristy and bell tower are successive and the front body was rebuilt in the second half of the eighteenth century, with facade remained unfinished. Inside the frescoes of the sixteenth century.
An ancient sanctuary in the medieval heart.

The reserve, of about 60 hectares, protects a small wetland considered one of the most important marshes of Tuscany from the floristic point of view. It makes one imagine how the Padule di Fucecchio and that of Bientina appeared before the nineteenth-century Bonifice.
Baroque church of the first decades of the eighteenth century, designed by Carlo Corbellini, with two onion bell towers; it stands in front of the monument to Massimiliano I.
The cathedral with its 40-metre-square-base bell tower, with double-fores and a clock on each side, which dominates the whole city.
Church in a small square with a resigned entrance and a baroque interior decorated with thirteen statues in stucco and gold of the most venerated virgin saints in Sicily.
One of the historic churches of the city.

Protected area from 2006 along the coast between Torre San Leonardo and Torre Canne, between Ostuni and Fasano: sand dunes, wetlands, ancient olive trees and ancient oil mills, with excursions and birdwatching; some paths are also accessible to people with disabilities.

Built between the end I and the beginning II century A.D. in a basin at the foot of the hill of Buon Camino, partly dug into the rock: up to ten thousand spectators, a facade over twenty meters high and an underground corridor of about 95 meters towards a cistern; rediscovered in the nineteenth century by the canon Giovanni Spano.
The national museum dedicated to contemporary arts, born from the idea of 1997.
The medieval town hall.
Roman mosaics on the sea of Sinuessa.

Neoclassical synagogue inaugurated in 1855, with Corinthian columns, stuccoes by Antonio Rusca, grate of golden bronze in the matroneo and the Ark saint. The museum, entitled to the president of the Jewish community of Parma who collected the materials, tells in seven sections the Jewish communities of Parma and Piacenza since 1555: documents, ritual objects, ancient prayer books, wedding contracts (ketubbot), racial laws and the Shoah. Guided tour of about 45 minutes; from March to June and from September to November on Sunday 11-13 and 15-18, during the other months by reservation.
The hills of Soave Classico on foot or by bike.
Five Baroque churches in one walk.

In Palazzo Piella, in the center: ceramics of the Bronze Age (XVII-XII century BC), finds of the Iron Age with an important storeroom of copper loaves used as a means of exchange before the coin, Roman materials with furnishings of a necropolis of the first century BC and a large panel on the centuriation, and a medieval section with ceramics and buckles from the Borgo Franco; there are also preserved remains of houses of the fourteenth century found at the Rocca Magna di Piumazzo.
A Romanesque apse in the hills.

Municipality of Valpolicella known for the red marble called "S." Ambrogio: on the hill of the village of San Giorgio, among vineyards, olive groves and marogne, stands the Longobard-Romanesque parish church with the 8th century ciborium, the cloister, an archaeological area of the Iron Age and the Museum-Antiquarium.
Coast watchmen.
The boss maze.

Hapsburg City of Care on the Passirio: the Medieval Porticos, the Cathedral of St. Nicholas, the Prince's Castle, the Kurhaus liberty and the winter walks, in summer and Tappeiner; out of town the gardens of Trauttmansdorff Castle, where the Empress Sissi stayed.
Former vow of Nicolò Vitelli built between 1483 and 1509 by Elia Bartolomeo Lombardo, example of Renaissance in terracotta and stone.
The temple of the god of the Sardinians in the mountains.

A centuries-old plant of chestnut trees with imposing trees, one of which is called "Castagna del cielo" (Castagna del cielo) and the Municipality is responsible for its recovery, protection and valorization.

The village has a winding road; on the square there are ancient re-trained buildings and in the village you can visit the churches of Sant'Antonio Abate, San Giovanni Battista, San Nicola di Bari, San Michele Arcangelo, Santa Caterina d'Alessandria and Santa Maria di Loreto. The view overlooks the valley and the sea and is suitable for sunset.

In the Monti Ausoni and Lago di Fondi Natural Park, wood with spontaneous orchids and archaeological remains, land of brigands at the time of the unification of Italy, with views of the Ausoni Mountains, the Fondi Lake and the Circeo; it is crossed by the ring CAI 540 Oak of Monaco - Cima del Monte - Acquaviva.
The neoclassical church of the historic center.
Panorama of Ogliastra.

A "taccu" , cylinder of limestone and mesozoic dolomia on a cone of schists, about 24 meters high and 50-70 wide, which reaches almost 1,000; rest of the Jurassic cover of Gennargentu, is a natural monument since 1989 and symbol of the country. It is located about 2 km from the village along the road towards the cantoniera of Cossatzu, among pastures, holm oaks, chestnuts and hazelnuts.
Founded in 1470 and consecrated in 1545, it is the oldest place of worship in the city, built on two previous temples (VIII and X-XI century) whose remains are visible in the underground.
The frescoes of Ferramola on the hill of Nigoline.
In the former convent of San Francesco, the oldest Italian museum dedicated to ceramics, founded in 1898: majolica from origins to contemporary, a rebuilt spices, majolica floors and votive plates.

Ancient small port for the islands of Sulcis, today a town beach of about 250 meters in the northern part of the town, with golden sand, low bottom suitable for children and two cliffs of trachytes that shelter it from the mistral; behind a pine forest with playground, in front of the rock of the Ghinghetta with the red and black banded lighthouse and the island of San Pietro. A path from the beach leads to the Spanish tower.
Romanesque victorious over an ancient crypt.
The Sibyls painted in the land of the Sibyl.
The great Romanesque treasure chest of the Marsica fucense.
The view of the Navy.
A noble palace as it was.
Mountain village of the Serchio Valley, outpost of Lucca, home of the figurines who brought the plaster statues into the world.
The main street of the historic center, with viale della Vittoria and views of the valley and the sea.
The theater square.
The summit of the Circeo overlooking the Pontines.
The Romagna painting in a monastery.
A country church overlooking the valley.
Erected in 115 A.D. and attributed to Apollodoro of Damascus, in large blocks of marble imetius on a stone podium of the Conero.
The vintage radios in a 14th century convent.
In the upper village there is the Baroque church of Sant'Agostino, the parish church of San Nicola di Bari and the neoclassical church of Madonna del Carmine in exposed bricks.
The Great War on Folgaria pastures.
The oldest nucleus of Baranello.

A humid area along the lake formed in 1925 by the barrier Enel sul Liri, with riparian woods with white willow and one of the few stripes of plain forest remaining in the valley of Sacco-Liri. There are 75 species of birds, 32 related to water (vaps, duffet, herons, tarabusin), and is indicated for birdwatching; among the curly mammals, istrice, fox, badger and weasel. It includes the sites of Fregellae in Ceprano and Fabrateria Nova in San Giovanni Incarico, with equipped area and visit centre.

Paleochristian catacomb discovered in 1943, among the rare of Abruzzo: a hypogeum of two galleries dug in the limestone rock, with graffiti linked to Christian worship; the funerary kit given its use between the IV and the beginning of the VII century. It testifies to the first spread of Christianity in the region.
A Norman basilica.
A walk under the porticos of the village.
The art of Nojani painters in a former convent of the center.

Borgo delle Colline Moreniche dell'Alto Mantovano, 170 metres on a hill dominated by the tower of the ancient Gonzaga castle, overlooking the Garda hills; at the foot of the fortress Villa Mirra houses the Museo archeologico dell'Alto Mantovano, and outside the village stands the Romanesque church of Santa Maria.

A basin of 1100 hectares with clayey background closed by the mountains, Site of community importance and geosite: rain and spring water are collected which form the so-called Dragon Lagoon, subject to flooding. The water is swallowed by the Dragon's mouth, a karst hole formed after the earthquake of 1456, capable of absorbing about 900 liters per second and entrance door of a complex underground net; the legend wants the holes to be those left by the three heads of a dragon killed by Prince Jesus. In the summer you walk on the edge of the water; a nature trail leads to the lake. Always accessible.
the castle complex can be visited by reservation

18th century building (House Osèi) renovated as a typical country house, where you can discover the traditions of the past; curated by the experts of the Adamello Brenta Nature Park, it also has a virtual route for children. Open in July and August.

Cited from 1302, it depended on the parish church of Bovegno and became a parish in the fifteenth century; the current building derives from extensions of the early eighteenth century, with stuccoes and frescoes by Pietro Scalvini (1751-1765), a Madonna with Child and Saints by Pier Maria Bagnatore (1583) in the middle of the main altar and a frame carved in 1749 by a woodwork of Levrange.
A church of the fifteenth century by the lake.

The village is closed by walls with rectangular plan reinforced by square and cylindrical towers; inside the Renaissance Palazzo Marcelli, with portal bugnato and loggia with four arches, and the historic Ferrari Theatre.
€5, reduced €4, cumulative with the museum €7

The settlement is documented as  "Montegrossum" from 1207, whose name (Plalum Lactis in medieval sources) recalls pastures and breeding. The old town preserves buildings supported by archivolts typical of an ancient mountain village. The parish church of San Biagio has baroque presbytery and preserves the portal of the oldest church, of the late fifteenth century; next to it there is the Oratory of the Santissima Annunziata, seat of the fraternity; in the village and surroundings there are the chapels of San Bernardo, San Sebastiano, San Lorenzo, Santa Elisabetta and Madonna dei Monti.
A sixteenth century country church with the Assunta di Solaro altarpiece.
A valley mill.

Guido Cagnola expanded his paternal collections, forming one of the most beautiful private collections of paintings: above all gold funds of Tuscan and Venetian painters of the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries and of Lombards between the fourteenth and sixteenth centuries, with works by Ercole de' Roberti, by the Master of the Madonna Cagnola, by Jacopo Bellini, by Vivarini and, for the eighteenth century, by Francesco Guardi. The collection of ceramics, majolica and oriental porcelains, Flemish and French tapestries, antique furniture, plates and bronze sculptures is completed. Visit by reservation (groups of at least 8 people every day); guided tours open to the public on the second and last Sunday of the month at 4:00 p.m.
The Golden Conca from above.
Tower built around the eighteenth century on an outlying rock, with irregular octagonal plan, with still intact walls. It is located about 10 km from the center, at the junction of the Jumenta.
The mastium that guards the Varrone plain.
Baroque carvings by Bernardino Castelli and paintings by Innocent Salvini.
For those who love stars and scientific instruments.
The porch courtyard of a noble residence.
The lunar landscape symbol of Pisticci.
One of the oldest churches in Gaeta.
The ruin that guarded the entrance of the valley.
Great historical complex today exhibition space.
The bell tower in granite.

The Nurse Mountain, 1,600 hectares inhabited by prehistory with domus de janas and parks like Sedda Ortai; 925 meters the bronze statue of the Redeemer of 1901, destination of the procession on the last Sunday of August.
The square as it is on market days.
Fortepiani d'epoca restored and still played.
The most elegant facade of the village.
Beach of about 1500 meters of fine sand, cleaned every day, with separate collection, showers and bathing facilities; Visit Sicily lists it among the beaches Green Flag 2022 suitable for children.

Peschiera rises on one of the three fortified islands that connect Garda to the Mincio; the fortress, enlarged by the Scaligeri at the end of the thirteenth century, owes its pentagonal plan to the walls built by the Republic of Venice, which renewed the fortifications with terrapies and bastions at the five corners of the medieval belt. It was a link between Venice and its most western territories beyond the Mincio, played a role in the Napoleonic countryside and in the wars between the Austrian Empire and the Unity of Italy, and the Venetian defence works have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2017. Walls, gates, canals and water ditches surround a historic centre of cobbled streets.
A village 4,000 years ago on the lake.
The collections dedicated to Maria Luigia d'Hapsburg, Duchess of Parma, and to the ducal court between the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, in the Palazzo di Riserva.

Benedictine Abbey was born around the sixth century on the ancient Pomposia Insula: the church of Santa Maria with frescoes, the bell tower visible from afar and the museum. Here the monk Guido invented the modern musical notation.
The parish church houses a 16th century Crucifix.
The coat of arms of Henry VIII in Vetralla.

In the district of Ceglie del Campo, a castle dominated by a square tower about 35 meters high, probably Norman foundation, set on structures of Roman age of ancient Caelia; modified by the Arcamone between the fifteenth and sixteenth century.
A parish church of the thirteenth century with its museum.

The Costa Smeralda was born in the sixties of the twentieth century as a destination of elite tourism; Porto Cervo is the exclusive center, known for yachts, events and clubs. Nearby is the Poltu Quatu Marina, in a fjordy cove.
The first Norman castle of Sicily.
A rock engraved in prehistory and the view of the Ticino in a short walk.

Gothic castle was built after 1230, when Bishop Gerardo allowed Arnold of Cagnò to build a fortified house outside the village; in 1464 he passed to the Thun, who expanded it, and in 1880 he was sold to the Malanotti, before the restoration of the Province. It contains frescoed ceilings, a stone spiral staircase, the stube of the restored count, the painted room called Olinda's prison, linked to the legend of the daughter of the Count in love with the minstrello, and the chapel of the Nativity of Mary frescoed by Elia Naurizio in 1620. It is part of the Castles of Buonconsiglio, it is open in summer with exhibitions, concerts and guided tours and is a stop of the Trenino dei Castelli.
A majolica floor.
Following Gavino Ledda.

The bridge of the capital, recorded by the Province as medieval, is at the origin of the name of the village, which would come from a bridge of axes near a mill. Next to it stands the mill purchased in 1824 by Paolo Battista Agnesi, from which the brand Pasta Agnesi was born.
The culture of the country of scissors.

The collection of the archimandrita Paolo Lombardo on three levels: introduction to the Byzantine world, rare icons, bronze icons of the Old Russian believers, Greek and Russian vestments and liturgical books from the 17th to the 20th century.

Great neoclassical church with Greek cross designed by Fermo Zuccari and begun in 1840 with the gift of Giovanni Vicenza Ponzone, with dome about 60 meters high on 16 arches and bell tower of 1897-1899. Inside the monuments of Pietro Civeri, the Martyrdom of Santo Stefano by Pietro Verzetti in the apse, painted from the Five to the nineteenth century (also by Giuseppe Diotti) and a copy of the Pala di Casalmaggiore del Parmigianino, whose original is in Dresden.
Convent built in 1502 by the Franciscans on an ancient fortress and rebuilt at the end of the eighteenth century. On 17 January, the blessed breads were distributed there and followed the horse ride.
Offer of €1 per person
The nymph of an emperor's villa.

Originally a hermitic chapel, it was enlarged in the second half of the nineteenth century at the behest of Count Cays, friend of Don Bosco. It rises at the foot of the Musinè, about 30 minutes walk from Cays Square along a paved road with the pylons of the Way of the Cross; every year in January there is a pilgrimage.
A cloistered monastery that you let visit.
Antique, vintage and flea market, with many stalls and small shops.

On the rocky promontory above the stream Galizzi, where the village was born: ruins of a triangular fortress with two towers, perhaps of Swabian age or of the first Angevin period, Caracciolo and Carafa and from the end of the nineteenth century of the Pellican marquises; you enter from a stone bridge with steps.

The medieval village is enclosed by three doors: the Gothic Porta da Capo and the Romanesque Porta da Piedi and Porta della Torre del Capitano. The surrounding districts, green and rich in stories and myths, preserve the fountains of Fraud and Ancino.

The village of Val Fontanabuona is halfway through the Tirello valley, under the Monte Ramaceto (1345 m), known at least from the sixteenth century for the hand weaving of damasks and other silks: the Damask Museum and the De Martini weaving preserve its tradition, around the linear village collected around the parish of Maria Annunciata.
Art exhibitions in the historic town hall.
Historic village on the side of a hill that preserves much of the medieval walls; it is also known for the tower of the parish church transformed into a bell tower.
The fortress swabs on the sea.

Medieval church dedicated to the Madonna della Cintola, restored in Baroque style in the seventeenth century; it was part of an ancient manor today disappeared. Above the altar the frescoed image of the Virgin, venerated for centuries.
The living room of the city with the Venetian lion.

Small center of the Valle della Cupa about five kilometers from Lecce, with the square where the church of Santa Maria delle Grazie faces the Baroque Doge's Palace of 1626, seat of the Town Hall and the Civic Museum; in an alley near the church of San Giovanni Evangelista of 1329 and, in Via Cerundolo, the house-museum of the artist Ezekiel Leandro with the Sanctuary of Patience.
The shrine in the woods.
Language and rite of Albania.
A table of the Master of the Nativity of Castello.
The way of the Infiorata.
The houses of the master potters.
Collection of about 2,000 pieces donated to the local Lions Club, of which over 650 are protected by the Superintendence of Cultural Heritage in Caltanissetta.

Borgo dell'alta Val Lemme dominated by the castle purchased by the Genoese in 1121, known for its medieval bridge with two arches, the Capuchin monastery with its genoese school gallery and the path that goes up to Mount Tobbio.
The Last Romanino Supper.
A sixteenth-century church that is also a cultural space.
A historic crossroads.
Bologna is UNESCO Creative City of Music: here you touch with your hand.
Romanesque long course Garibaldi.
The baroque façade.

The castle was built in the beginning of the 13th century, destroyed in 1428 and then rebuilt, of which traces of the fifteenth-century walls remain; in the historical center the Community Palace, once the entrance of the castle, and the church of Santo Stefano.

The 12th-century Baronial Palace of the Imperial family: it houses the family square, part of the Marseille collection, the Museum of Photography and Messapian collections; the most valuable room is the Sala Flore on the first floor.

Museum of Tyrolean history and rural life, with its religious roots: almost forgotten crafts, war memories, rooms and workshops rebuilt in original style, an exhibition on local fauna and video interviews with witnesses of the time. Open from Palm Sunday at the end of October, only with guided tour in German or Italian (mar-ven 10:10 and 11:10; Saturday, Sunday and holidays 17:00), by reservation; not without barriers.

The Cesanese di Olevano Romano DOC is the pride of the village: at the end of June there is Vinointorno and between August and September the Festa del Cesanese, now in the fiftieth year, with tastings in the cellars along the Strada del vino Cesanese and parade of floats allegorical. At Christmas the panpepato is prepared, the protagonist of a competition.
Fortified building with elegant decorations, built during the lordship of Del Balzo and remodeled several times; under the Gonzaga was an important cultural center.

The karst complex of four large cavities with more than 20 km of development; the Cave Nuova, discovered in 1925 by inhabitants who noticed a slit from which came wet air, has almost 9 km of development and is among the most extensive in the world because formed to the contact between two types of rock. The guided tourist route, illuminated and with walkways, crosses galleries, halls and canyons with stalactites and stalagmites to the Corner of the Crystals and the Hall of the Gran Portone with its natural arch (about 1 hour and 15 minutes, 11 °C constant); on reservation easy speleological excursions of 3 or 5 hours. It is on the regional list of tourist caves.
Trecento frescoes on the Via del Monginevro.
The summit symbol of the Apennines between Piedmont and Liguria.
The Opitergium stones.
A boat in the Spanish Steps.
The peasant life of Ogliastra in an old mill.
Villa of the seventeenth century, recently restored, with original stables, a colonnade and internal gardens.
The high-altitude flora of Gran Sasso.

Layers of an ancient cliff of a tropical sea of about 100 million years ago with remains of molluscs, sea urchins, sponges and corals, one of the rare examples on the Atlantic-Abruzzi carbonate platform; it is a natural monument since 2016 (D.P.R.L. 3 October 2016, n. 193), run by the Municipality. A geological route of about 1.5 km starts from Via Genazzano.

On the ground floor of the historic Palazzo Rossi, in 120 m2, four dioramas reconstruct the environments of the National Parks of Pollino, Sila and Aspromonte and the Regional Reserves of Lake Tarsia and the Foce del Crati. It is one of the four sections of the Natural History Museum of Calabria, created to spread the natural sciences especially among young people.

The oldest village of Baronia, at 1094 meters, from which the look embraces Campania, Puglia, Molise and Basilicata; medieval capital of Baronia di Vico and bishop's seat until the nineteenth century, preserves the Cathedral of the Assumption with the frescoed crypt, the ruins of the castle and the sixteenth-century Port'Alba. The director Ettore Scola was born there.
One of the oldest public museums in Europe.
Next to the Baroque church of Our Lady of Peace or the Bridge, on the left bank of the Dora, exhibits the Treasure of the Cathedral of San Giusto and religious works of art of the valley.
Palace on the port recognizable from the shoe base and the neo-Gothic portal.
To be checked: visits of the mastium and the walkway

Borgata marina just over 3 km from the village, immersed in the pine forest, with a long white beach in the coastal area awarded with the Cinque Vele di Legambiente; there is the Aragonese tower, in the ancient portus Liquidonis of Roman times. Sailing, kite and windsurfing, cycling or horseback riding.

Borgo dell'Ovadese mentioned as "Mons Alpherius" in the 10th century, disputed between Alexandria and Genoa and since 1566 feud of the Doria: the castle of the Doria, the Romanesque church of San Michele with frescoes of the late fifteenth century and the oratories of the village.
One of the oldest churches in the city, with its monumental complex and 15th century bell tower.
A hike into prehistory.
The lake that appears and disappears.
The history of the territory inside the Fortress.

Born in 1978, it is one of the most famous crags in the world, with about 300 routes of every grade up to 8c; the easiest routes are numbered from 1 to 18 and close there is a very simple route for children.
Promontory of cliffs from which, in winter and spring, the waterfalls of the Slighes river are thrown directly into the sea; with the wind they open fan-shaped creating a rainbow effect.
Afro to Lichtenstein.
Venue of the Town Hall in Piazza Italia, with the rooms of the noble floor frescoed by Vincenzo Angelo Orelli.

Fortified village of the plateau of Navelli, with the castle and the restored fourteenth-century tower; in the hamlet of Bominaco the oratory of San Pellegrino, entirely frescoed in the thirteenth century, and the abbey church of Santa Maria Assunta, national monument since 1902.

Where the ancient Roman naval ship was located, a shipyard that supplied timber for boats, today there is a marina surrounded by cliffs and pine trees, with piers where to stroll and dine; the yards of Varazze are specialized in superyacht.
The Asti symbol.
Roman baroque in the heart of the village.
Medieval walk on the Francigena between four churches.
A stage of the Franciscan journey.
Ruins of a late medieval tower, once a fortified residence of the Dell'Arena family, which in the nineteenth century gave refuge to the band of the brigand Giovanni Stella.
impervious site: for the municipality people with reduced mobility can visit only if accompanied
The municipal center of documentation on the lake, among the places indicated by the UNESCO site to know the stilts.

Country of chestnuts on the ridge half coast of the Isarco Valley, with Castel Velturno, Renaissance summer residence of the princes bishops of Brixen, and the Archeoparc of the Tanzgasse with its place of worship of the Copper Age; high up the Velturno mountain hut and the Radlsee lake at 2,250 meters, at the bottom the waterfall of Schrambach 63 meters high.
The lighthouse of the Park of the Remembrance on the hill of the Maddalena, marked as the highest point in the city.
A journey into the bowels of the iron mountain.
An entire mining village 4 km from the dunes of Piscinas.
The crypt dug into the tuff.
The Tuscan villages in miniature.
The ancient center with churches, noble palaces, the Cathedral, the museum of Santa Maria delle Nunche and the Fraternal Fountain in Piazza Celestino V.
Opened in 1986, it collects work tools, household and emigration objects of the twentieth century, wool and linen looms and a small room on mines and miners.

Villa outside the excavation area, so called for a room overlooking the sea with a large fresco on three walls that depicts a mystery rite linked to the Dionysian cult, among the most preserved ancient works.
Airy square in the center of the four historic districts, with the clock tower; the Touring indicates it as an ideal place for an aperitif.
€6, reduced €2 (18-25 years EU); cumulative 7 days with Naquane and MUTRE €12
Medieval defence tower in the upper part of the village, recently restored and used for temporary exhibitions.

Beyond the main embankment lies the Garzaia Nature Reserve; the bike path accompanies along the banks of the Po between poplars and herons flights. Outside the village, barns, ailes and farmsteads mark the countryside.
St. George's column.
The mother church of the parish church, with the 16th century frescoes by Lattanzio Gambara.

The center of the Diano Valley on the Tanagro river, built around a Roman forum along the Annia street, of which remain the Lapis Pollae, the mausoleum of Caio Uziano Rufo and the Roman bridge; in the village the convent of Sant'Antonio and the civic museum of the ancient Pollesi clothes.

Built in 1594 under the patronage of the Marquises of Joyosa on the remains of the little church of Santa Maria di Maratà, then of the Pellicano; it preserves a large canvas of the Annunciation commissioned at the beginning of the nineteenth century by the Marquis Anna Maria Piccolomini Caracciolo.

Museum of art, culture and agriculture curated by an association founded in 2004, which reconstructs the daily peasant and artisan life of the Oltrepò between the Eight and twentieth century: peasant cuisine, tailoring, barberia, school and shoemaker shops, blacksmith and blacksmith.
Art Nouveau building designed by Eugène Ferret, one of the four casinos in Italy; reserved for adults.

Romanesque, wanted by the Norman counts above a Byzantine church that forms the crypt, where according to tradition Jolanda of Brienne and Isabella of England, wives of Frederick II; the chapel of St. Richard was built in 1438 by Francesco II Del Balzo; bell tower of the XII-XIV century and wooden ceiling of the transept.
On the border with Baunei, a fine sandy beach in an oleander forest, reachable by sea or by a challenging trekking; behind the Codula di Luna with millenarian junipers.
Fortress built in 1385 by Nicolò II d'Este on a project by Bartolino da Novara, then ducal residence: prisons, kitchens, Garden of Oranges and frescoed halls, in the path set up by Gae Aulenti.
The Museum of Sacred Art is visited only by appointment
To see inside the historical churches of the village.
Nature and silence in the Park of the Antola.
With the children, on rainy days.
On the Colle della Guardia, reachable from Porta Zaragoza with the longest portico in the world: 3.796 m and 666 arcades, stretch of the UNESCO Porticos.
A bike ride along the Arno.

Small center of the Polesine with the Palladian Villa Badoer, the sixteenth-century Villa Grimani Molin Avezzù and, in the boats of the Badoera, the National Archaeological Museum dedicated to the settlement of the Bronze Age of Frattesina; in the surroundings the Ecomuseum Mulino al Pizzon.
Museum dedicated to the famous folk music group of Castelrotto, open all year round: Monday-Friday 9-12 and 15-18, Saturday 9-12.
Rome's largest district, "trans Tiberim," loved for the atmosphere of Rome once between Piazza di Santa Maria, Piazza Trilussa and Piazza dei Mercanti.

Forest complex of 828 hectares in the National Park of the Tuscan-Emilian Apennines and Site of Community Interest, which preserves wrecked populations of conifers of colder climates; very frequented for excursions, with Mount Cusna as the main destination.

Irpino village at 666 meters gathered around the Castle Ruspoli-Candriano, with its large cylindrical mastio, which houses the Civic Museum "Turella Parva Turris" and the Museum of cinema dedicated to Sergio Leone; outside the village, in the wood of cerri, the Norman tower of Girifalco.
The first sanctuary of Saint Anthony.

River park linked to the Po ecosystem, with a lake born from a former quarry: after the end of the excavations the Bonifiche have reported native species in rivers and wetlands. Birdwatching, sport fishing, life and cycling trails, eco-friendly guided tours.

A city founded in 1933, symbol of Rationalism, overlooking the lake of Paola in the heart of the Circeo National Park: more than 20 km of white beach and dunes, the sixteenth-century tower of Paola and the ruins of the great villa of the Emperor Domitian.

The centre of the Ufita valley, built around the Castello D'Aquino, is a medieval fortress that has become a noble residence that now houses the Antiquarium Filippo Buonopane, and the Mother Church of Santa Maria Maggiore, rebuilt in the eighteenth century with a 36-metre bell tower.

Grey stone houses on narrow and winding alleys, with steps carved into the rock; from Porta Castello, the only surviving of the ancient doors, begins the oldest part, with the steep Via del Macello and Via San Pasquale, between noble houses and stone hands that indicate the direction. Porta Santa Maria (1475), Porta Villotta with Palazzo Onofri (1498) and Porta San Pelino were born with the expansion of the walls after the earthquake of 1456; along the route the "pilucce" , stone kisses where the donkeys were watered.

Small exhibition space at the entrance of the village, on the ground floor of the primary school Sante De Sanctis, with sections on geology and formation of the gorge of the Tane, excavations and finds from the ancient Paleolithic to the late Bronze Age, the Etruscan tomb of Soriano with vases of the Orvieto Group (VI century BC) and the history of the castrum of Parrano, with copies of the Statute of 1559. Church in a 13th century cave, modified in the 15th and 16th centuries, dug into the ridges along the Royal Canal behind the Capharo Piccolo farmhouse, in a complex with two other caves. Rectangular plan with two naves divided by a pillar with three arches in the sixth; thirteenth century frescoes in the apse and on the south wall, including perhaps an Archangel, and inscriptions in Latin and Arabic. Reserve of 997 hectares between Monterotondo, Mentana and Sant'Angelo Romano, between the valley of the Tiber and the Cornicolani Mountains, with hills, pastures, olive groves and oak woods; the karst has created caves, swallowholes, sventators and sinkholes, among which the Well of Merro, sinking deep about 80 meters with a lake on the explored bottom up to about 392 meters. It is reached by train with the FM1 and the Cotral buses.

It dates back to 1200 but has been renovated several times; it is recognized from the high bell tower in square blocks of stone. Inside a canvas of the Madonna della Snow attributed to the school of Raphael and the Madonna of the Rosary of Pietrafesa.

Relief of the Sican area, marked by centuries of sulphur extraction, frequented by the late Bronze Age: there were found matrixes for the fusion of bronze of the 11th century BC, a small sacred building of the 6th century BC with votive indigenous and Greek deposit (bronze belts, a newsstand with Heracles, amphora), a warehouse and a metallurgical area; part of the materials is in the museum of Lercara.

The route is chronological and topographic, a showcase for hut with drawings and reconstructions; among the accessories a dagger and a pin, among the oldest metal objects attested in Italy. Begin in 1897 and open to worship in 1922, it has a single nave with stuccoes and paintings on the life of St. Joseph, wooden and paper sculptures and a wooden organ; it preserves the sixteenth-century stone portal of the demolished Dominican church. A hilly town overlooking the sea, overlooking the gulf of Ancona, the Conero and the Apennines; in the historical center the Teatro Alfieri of 1886-87 and the church of San Pietro Apostolo, on the coast the hamlet of Marina di Montemarciano with about 5 km of pebble beach and the fifteenth century Mandracchio.

Built in 1576 (1580 according to another card of the same portal) for Cardinal Alessandro Sforza, as a summer residence and base for the repression of the brigandage; after the death of the cardinal he fell for a long time. Village of quarrymen about 8 km from the city, born in Roman times among the quarries and famous for the lard aged in marble basins: in front of the church of San Bartolomeo the Monument to the Cavatore by Alberto Sparapani; from here start trails with views of the Apuan and the sea.

The itinerary has three sections (rural work, antifascism and resistance, a family in memory), with agricultural tools, works of art, photographs and the multimedia room Quadrisfera on the twentieth century; on the whole also the Library Archivio Emilio Sereni, a bookshop and an inn.

16-metre-high tower, built between the 13th and 14th centuries on the ruins of the Norman-Svevo castle; it is the symbol of the village, it houses a permanent exhibition on the history of the territory and the civic museum and offers a wide panorama of the Partenio Regional Park, the Sanctuary of Montevergine and the Gulf of Naples.

Fortress on Mount Tenda with origins from the early 10th century, at the time of the invasions of the anguar, restored and expanded by Cansignorio della Scala and passed to Venice in the 15th century. You enter from the drawbridge under the tower with the bas-relief of San Giorgio; three courtyards: the first, Venetian, with the remains of a small church with three apses perhaps of the tenth century, that of the Madonna with a fresco dated 1st June 1321 and the tallest with the Mastio, where in the restorations there were human bones. The Palazzo del Signore preserves the "Caminata" with its large fireplace, a frescoed Crucifixion of the thirteenth century and portraits of Mastino I, Cangrande, Dante, Taddea da Carrara and Cansignorio. Hours: 9-12 and 15-18 from April to 25 October, 9-12 and 14-16 in winter; closed on Mondays and with bad weather.

Elegant 18th-century Palladian residence built by the Bergamo family Locatelli, who lived there since the mid-eighteenth century; the family coat of arms dominates the portal. Beyond the hall there is an Italian garden; the noble floor conserves frescoes from the second half of the nineteenth century by Antonio Picco. Today it is the seat of the municipality, the town wine shop and the Civic Museum of the territory.

The naturalistic section goes from astronomy, with a vaulted room that reproduces the Milky Way, meteorites and interactive exhibits, to mineralogy and geology of Treviso, to invertebrates and vertebrates: the fish room collects about 90% of the freshwater fish fauna of Veneto and an area is dedicated to Montello. There is also an archaeological section with temporary exhibitions.
The medieval crypt with its capitals.

The most frequented bay of the Conero, with free and equipped pebble beach (Blue Flag since 2010), the Romanesque church of Santa Maria di Portonovo of the 11th century cited by Dante, the Tower De Bosis, the Napoleonic fort and two brackish lakes.

Born as an extension of Palazzo Principe, designed by Luigi Canonica and inaugurated in 1843, it hosted opera and prose until 1926; reopened in 1990. Visitable during the shows; groups by reservation free of charge.
The picnic treasures of the Queen of Sirolo.

Opened in 1993, on two floors and six sections from the Paleolithic to the Middle Ages: the civilizations of the Upper Murgia, the origins of bread and a plan dedicated to the European Paleolithic, with the life-size reconstruction of the Man of Altamura presented in 2017.

Inaugurated on September 27, 1891, with the "Force of destiny" by Verdi, on a project by Achille Sfondrini that followed the model of La Scala; frescoed in the restoration of 1935, it became cinema in the fifties and after the restoration ended in 2002 it returned theatre with 639 seats.
A Greek cross church consecrated in 1436, with a wooden statue of the Madonna of the sixteenth century, an organ of the eighteenth century, a painting by Oreste Recchione and a rose window.

The first regional museum dedicated to everyday life in the feudal castles (X-XV century) of the eastern pedemontana of Friuli, is located in the former dairy and collects the finds of the nine castles along the via pedemontana, part of the feudal state of the Patriarchate of Aquileia. Ceramics, glass and metals, sections on hunting, fishing, agriculture and breeding, weapons of the 13th-XIV centuries, the "sword in the rock" and the oldest wooden Madonna of Friuli, the Majesty of Partistagno of the mid-Twentieth century; here are also conserved the more than 13,000 finds of the castle of Soffumbergo. Open on Sundays 10-13 and 14-19; guided tours for groups by reservation also during the week.

The oldest nucleus, on the left of the Black, grew around the castle that the Arroni family built in medieval times, surrounded by walls with circular bastions to defend the road between Rieti and Spoleto; from the 11th to the 12th century it controlled much of the lower Valnerina, until the passage to Spoleto in the thirteenth century. From above you can enjoy the view of the valley.

Altopascio, the city of bread between Lucca and Pistoia, is a historic stop on the Via Francigena, where the Knights of the Tau welcomed and cared for pilgrims in their Hospital for centuries. The center preserves the church of San Jacopo with the bell tower of 1280 and the bell tower "La Smarrita" , Piazza degli Ospitalieri and the Medici Loggia; just outside there is the reserve of Lake Sibolla.

Documented already at the time of the duchy of Gaeta and the maritime republics, with many houses of the twelfth century, it is an intricacy of alleys, stairs, subways and arches that still bears the signs of the bombings of the Second World War. There are panoramic walks of Viale degli Innamorati and via Fontania and the square dedicated to Goliarda Sapienza, with the wall of poetry and benches shaped like a book.

One of the oldest churches in the country, built on the site of a Roman temple dedicated to Cibele (Magna Mater); it has a late Baroque stone portal from 1739 and has been a sanctuary since 2003. Inside the wooden statue of San Ciro by Michele Abruzzi (1863) and, in the sacristy, a fresco of Ecce Homo.

Borgo turrito della Langa del Barolo dominated by the fortress of Falletti, which is privately owned and now under restoration; from the parish churchyard of San Lorenzo the view extends over the vineyards of the Lower Langa Albese to the castle of Serralunga, while the Via del moat turns around the medieval core.
The meeting point of the four neighborhoods.

Built at the end of the 2nd century BC on a large terrace with a temple perhaps of Apollo, renovated under Augustus and then by Septimius Severus with a scenic building of three orders of columns in rare marbles about 26 meters high; cavea of about 85 meters.
The late-Gothic masterpiece.

On the hills north of the village, 450 hectares of the mining district exploited from the Etruscan era until 1976: the galleries of the Temperino Mine, the Lanzi-Temperino tunnel by mining train and the medieval village of Rocca San Silvestro, a village of miners and founders of the Della Gherardesca.
Historical structure of the eighteenth century fed by the water of the stream, recovered and made visitable: during the openings and the didactic activities you can see the gears in operation.
The oldest neighborhood, with narrow streets and steep stone paved; along the main street, among the noble palaces, the Fontana di Maltempo.

In San Magno, about 13 km south-southeast of Corato in the Alta Murgia Park, a necropolis of mound graves dating from the 7th to the 4th century BC: in the center of each tomb a large, mostly rectangular cyst, surrounded by blocks and megalitic slabs that give it a dolmenic appearance. There were found objects in bronze and iron and pottery; the municipality indicates it as one of the most important Dolmenic complexes of the Alta Murgia.

It tells how the Po has crossed over time: images and plastic of the bridge of boats between Boretto and Viadana, whose impalced was destroyed in 1967, collected by the son of the last bridge leader. Open Thursday, Saturday and Sunday 9-12 and 15-18.

Built by the Benedictines at the beginning of the thirteenth century to guard the body of Saint Crispolto, the first bishop and martyr of Umbria; Latin cross plan and nineteenth-century facade of Antonio Stefanucci, pupil of Vanvitelli. Of the Romanesque structure only the cusp bell tower remains.

It incorporates the remains of a tower of the castle of the barons of Cly, lords of Antey until the fourteenth century.

The seaside village of the Riviera dei Fiori, born as Villaregia in the 11th century as a settlement of sailors and fishermen: at the head Don preserves the archaeological area of Costa Balenae with the early Christian basilica, in the center the 18th century parish church of San Maurizio, and is crossed by the cycle path of the coastal park.

Ancient Greek-siculous settlement on the hill overlooking the village, excavated from the twenties of the twentieth century to the beginning of the thirteenth century, with places of worship, housing districts, fortifications and necropolis from prehistory to the third century BC; among the remains the village, the entrance of a cave and an ancient road. The municipality also points it out as a viewpoint with a naturalistic path and panoramic views of the village and the countryside. Managed by the Archaeological Park of the Valley of the Temples, with free entrance.

Borgo Irpino arranged in concentric circles around the castle that Carlo Gesualdo (1566-1613), the madrigalist prince, transformed into a Renaissance court; in the historical center the churches and convents founded by him, including Santa Maria delle Grazie with the pala del Perdono, the Cappellone and the palazzi Pisapia and Mattioli.
Rocky tombs a stone's throw from the village.

The only trilobed plant in Abruzzo.

In the former Augustinian monastery he tells of the human presence in the territory from prehistory to the Middle Ages: prehistoric finds linked to an ancient track prior to Flaminia, Roman materials including a millionaire of 305 A.D. once exhibited in town hall, and a medieval section on castles and the first Christianization. Most of the pieces come from the collection of Giulio Cesare Corsi.

Ring of about 2 km (37 minutes, a hundred meters of difference in altitude) which climbs to the castle of Neuhaus, halfway through, and passes through the former ...Pflegerhaus. From the path you can see the village with the Romanesque church and the ruins of Kehlburg on the hill opposite. In winter it can be frozen.

Medieval village at 822 meters on a spur, about 4 km from the capital for a panoramic road; of the 11th century castle that dominates the valley of the Tiepid remains two towers and a stretch of walls, incorporated into a private property.
On the northern side of Mount Capanne, a place of worship since the 14th century; the present building dates back to 1595 and took its form today in 1799 after various restorations.

The main centre of Trexenta, about 40 km from Cagliari, Senorbì is called "cradle of civilization" for the Carthaginian settlement of Santu Teru and the necropolis of Monte Luna, whose equipments are exhibited in the museum sa Domu Nosta; in the village the Romanesque church of Santa Mariedda and the manor houses of the historic center.

Built between 1284 and 1289, traditionally by Charles II of Anjou, it was a fortress and a residence; in the seventeenth century it became a noble residence with gardens, caves and water games, and in the nineteenth century the Giusso, from which it takes its name, chose the salmon pink colour and frescoed the Hall of Arms and the Hall of Ventagli. Part of the city walls and a terrace overlooking the sea remain.
A village of Apennines with Ligurian colors.

The 23rd chapel, of the Coronation of Mary, at the top of the hill: with more than three hundred statues it is the most complex of the Sacred Mount and an extraordinary viewpoint on hills and Alps; visit by reservation.

One of the most important examples of Romanesque of the Marches, on the site of the Roman city of Pausulae: documented from the 11th century, it was a parish church and not an abbey. Square plan with semicircular apses, two cylindrical towers on the sides of the façade of Ravenna taste and above all two overlapping churches; the Gothic portal in Istria stone of the upper church is an addition. It preserves almost intact the original appearance.
In the contemporary art museum ARCOS, the Egyptian section of the Museum of Sannio with the finds of the temple dedicated to Isis, "Lady of Benevento" .

The municipality coincides with the Val di Rabbi, which is about twelve kilometers long on the side of the Val di Sole, for more than half in the Stelvio National Park: the spas of Rabbi Fonti with the ferruginous water of the Antica Fonte, the Saént Falls, the bridge suspended over the Ragaiolo, water mills and sawmills and wooden and stone farms.

Opened in 1881 and today in the Barchessa of Palazzo Foscolo: Venetian inscriptions, votive bronzes, the three-dimensional reconstruction of Opitergium, monuments of the Roman necropolis and late antique polychrome mosaics of a rich urban house.

Complex of the system of the Sacred Mountains pre-Alpine on the hill of Mount Rigone, with Mount Fenera in the background. The climb between the pines touches 13 newsstands of the Via Crucis painted by Lorenzo Peracino and erected by 1763; on top the church with six chapels on the life of the Virgin, about 150 polychrome terracotta statues and the dome with the Assumption. Built around 1648 for a vow during the plague, with the commitment of the miller Gian Battista Daij called "Paniga" , remembered on the facade. Open for Sunday celebrations.

It collects the testimonies of the lower valley of Coghinas from the Neolithic to the Middle Ages: ceramics of the culture of Ozieri, Bonnanaro finds from Monte San Giovanni, a bronze axe from the nuragic village of San Leonardo, jewels in gold, silver and vitreous paste from the Roman necropolis and Punic, Roman and Renaissance coins. The strong piece are about 80 stone funerary stems, from the end of the first century BC and from the first imperial age, with an anthropomorphic figure enclosed by a palm branch, exposed in the open-air moat together with millstones, large vases and reconstructions of graves. April-September Tuesday-Sunday 10-13 and 16-19; October-March 9.30-12.30 and 15-18.

The nine-pointed star city-fortress founded by Venice in 1593, ideal Renaissance city, national monument since 1960 and UNESCO heritage since 2017 with Venetian defence works; among the most beautiful villages in Italy since 2018.
Cave inhabited in prehistoric times, proposed as a destination for excursions from the village.

The large walls of the Park just a step away from the village.
One of the largest collections of Japanese art in Europe, collected by Edward Chiossone, Genoese engraver called in Japan to draw banknotes.
The symbol of the memory of the submerged country.
temporarily closed for maintenance (the site of the Municipality)
The source on which in 1607 Grand Duke Ferdinand I built a portico, a sign of the European fame of the waters of San Casciano.
The painter's house, a geometric volume with circular courtyard, now an exhibition venue.
The art of sting.

Protected area of about 120 hectares where the heat digs limestone cliffs overhanging: rare ferns and horseback riding, otter, raptors, the giants' pots and the natural bridge of Pietratetta. Panoramic path of about 8 km round trip (4-5 hours, medium difficulty); guided tours on Sundays from the town hall, groups by reservation; also destination for kayaking.

Roman colony founded at the end of the 4th century BC in fair territory, excavated by the Belgian Academy between 1949 and 1979: polygonal walls with four doors, diribitorium, three-nave basilica, macellum, baths with suspensurae and mosaics, shrine of Hercules and elliptical amphitheatre of the 1st century A.D. In 537 it was the winter district of the troops of Belisario; it was abandoned around the sixth century. Open and freely accessible area.

Excellent hiking itinerary, challenging for the rocky conglomerate and steep slopes, which in about an hour of walk leads to the summit called Carrega del Diavolo, an exceptional panoramic point at almost 1,000 meters. Nearby there is the Castagneu, large chestnut wood with a rural house.
Raffaello in a private villa.
The auction by voice.
The Tuscan painting of the nineteenth century.
The museum in the surroundings of the castle, with the Palazzo del Podestà where Michelangelo was born.
A live press museum.
Walking to the Roman port on the Tiber.
private residence of the Cavallari family used in part for events: the source does not indicate regular visits (opens reported only at events, e.g. FAI Days)

Country of the Novarian plain near Sesia, known for the Abbey of the Saints Nazario and Celso, founded in 1040 and fortified in the thirteenth century, with frescoed cloister; in the countryside towards Villata stands the Sanctuary of the Madonna della Fontana.

Parish church built in 1425 and enlarged in the eighteenth century, visited by Saint Charles Borromeo in 1580 and Francesco Morosini in 1594. It preserves a wooden pulpit of 1746, an organ of 1805 and a Madonna with Child carved by the Del Maino brothers.

16.4 km ring with 560 m of altitude difference (difficulty MC+BC) starting from the Lighthouse of Liberty and touching the woods of beech and chestnut trees, the temple of Roccapiatta, the villages overlooking the Chisone valley, Godini (1000 m, highest point), the Didactic Wood, the panoramic Roc Coubalesine and the Cippo dei Martiri del Bric, to close the Museum of Viticulture.
The memory of Chanoux and Chabod.
Castle started in 1380 by Giovanni Spaccalferro and adapted to a Renaissance villa in the fifteenth century; there stayed sovereigns and popes, including Julius II.

Città dell'Agro nocerino-Sarnese at the sources of the Sarno river: the National Archaeological Museum in the eighteenth century Palazzo Capua, the Hellenistic-Roman theatre, the Episcopio Cathedral with the ceiling of the Solimena and the sanctuary of the Madonna di Foce.

Irpino village with its medieval structure lying on the slope, dominated by the Norman castle of the 11th century; under the old town there are caves excavated in the tuff where the Podolic caciocavallo matures, and the village is crossed by the Regio Tratturo Pescasseroli-Candela.
€4, reductions for groups, children, students, schools and over 65
The starting point of the UNESCO train to St. Moritz.

The highest village in Gargano, which grew up around the Archangel Cave: the Sanctuary of San Michele, started in 2011 on the UNESCO site       . The Longobards in Italy , the white district of Junno, the castle and the beech woods of the Umbra Forest.
Shopping in the historic center.

National monument, built according to the tradition in the time of Matilde di Canossa (1080-1090): Romanesque parish church on a spur of rock in the woods, with views of the Parma Apennines and Reggiano up to the Cimone. Inside the floor in sloping stone slabs and the baptismal font with the grifo, the blessing, the lion of St Mark and the angel of St Matthew.
A walking tour that touches the main places of the municipality.
The Marian shrine wanted great by the Colleoni.
The symbol church of the city, free of charge, on Piazza Maggiore.

Borgo della Grecìa Salentina with the oldest Byzantine frescoes of Puglia in the crypt of Santa Cristina, the sixteenth-century sanctuary of the Madonna della Grotta with the nearby underground mill, the Matrice Church in Lecce stone, the large doveyard of the fifteenth century and numerous menhirs.
€10 whole (with audio guide if booked online); reductions for over 65, students and residents

Medieval village on a sandstone ridge, dominated by the Fortified Angevin Castle in the fifteenth century and became known for the murals of the CVTà Street Fest. It is the birthplace of Vincenzo Cuoco and Gabriele Pepe.
The European vanguard of the post-war period in front of the station.
In Palazzo Giacomelli, a path on the symbolism of fire, the sacred, the folk medicine, music and show, the textile tradition and the costume, with the wooden sculpture of the Ciceri collection.
Small frescoed chapel of the historic center, inserted in the itinerary of visit of Spello between Porta Consolare and Santa Maria Maggiore.
Seriously damaged by the 2012 earthquake, currently closed
The symbol of the free Perugino municipality.
The eighteenth-century castle house symbol of the village.
An evening at the theatre.

Ring that starts from the sanctuary and touches a dozen mountain lakes and four hills, crossing briefly into France. From the nearby Strepeis there is also a trek of about 22 km (difficulty E, about 1,450 m of difference in altitude, in two days) that passes from the Passo di Bravaria, from the Lake of Sant'Anna (2,167 m) and from the Passo di Tesina (2,293 m); season recommended from the end of June to July, when snowmen melt.
Built after the decree of 1786 that gave Gaby a parish autonomous from Issime.
Listing in extension: the guide covers 17 of the 29 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
The medieval ruins above the village.
Small cross building of the fifth century, inside entirely covered with mosaics: the blue starry sky of the dome is the most famous point.
Roman road and medieval church outside door.

Country 652 meters high in Valcellina, of late-Roman origins and donated in 762 to the abbey of Sesto al Reghena, seat of the Natural Park of the Friulian Dolomites; it is the door of the Campanile of Val Montanaia and of the Cimoliana Valley, with the visitor center of the Park and the fauna area of Pianpinedo.

Founded in 1991, it has 1,500 m2 of exposure and more than 30,000 fossils and zoological finds; the collection of cetaceans, with about fifty beached specimens, is indicated as the most important in South Italy. In the paleontological section a skeleton of Psittacosaurus, a Brazilian pterosaur of four meters of wingspan and elephants dwarf Palaeoloxodon falconeri found in the territory of Comiso; in the zoological one sharks, moonfish, a clairvoyant of Madagascar, a giant turtle of Aldabra and about 1,600 birds.
The theater square.
The Roman Terni in the historic center.

Municipality of Val Senales, lateral of Val Venosta, linked to the Similaun mummy: Ötzi was found on the Tisa Giogo at 3,210 m and the archaeoParc of Madonna di Senales reconstructs the life of 5,300 years ago. In the valley the Certosa, an active monastery from 1326 to 1782, the Marian sanctuary of Madonna di Senales and the artificial lake of Vernago.
The eighteenth-century portal in the village of Sciglio.
villa under restoration and not accessible: open only on pre-established days with guided tours by reservation (link published by the Municipality on the previous Monday)
Boats and fishermen.
The tower of Del Carretto.
The pioneer machines.

The visitable ruins of the medieval village destroyed by the earthquake of 1693, with the castle and part of the urban fabric, and traces of the previous settlements: Paolo Orsi identified the Hellenized Sicula town of Echetla.
An almost intact Roman furnace.
17th century church in Via Pietà, beyond the Livenza; inside a stone sculpture of the type Vesperbild, characteristic of Central Europe.
Renaissance frescoes saved from the disappeared buildings of the city.
Palazzetto near the church of San Francesco: its sixteenth-century room of the Fireplace, with a fireplace dedicated to lovers, is known as the room of lovers.
The MiC card indicates the villa closed every day: check the opening

Fortress of medieval origin (the sources date back to the 8th century, at the behest of the abbot of Nonantola; first cited in 936), passed to the Estensi in 1336 and infeudated in 1401 to Uguccione Contrari, who transformed it into a residence; from 1507 to the Boncompagni Ludovisi until the mid-Twentieth century, since 1998 it is of the Foundation of Vignola. Square plan with three towers, drawbridge and moat; climb the towers for the view of the village and the countryside. In the Chapel of the Contrari late-Gothic frescoes with the Stories of Christ, by an anonymous Ferrara painter from the fifteenth century. Open Friday, Saturday and Sunday 9:30-13:30 and 15:00-18:30 (last entry one hour before), tickets on site.
The parish church wanted by the Mozzoni, lords of the villa.

Residency of Giulia Farnese "La Bella" (Bella Bella), sister of Pope Paul III, who ruled Carbognano from 1506 for 25 years (his name is engraved on the portal): under her the village, reduced to 25 inhabitants by pestilences, came to about 2.000 and hosted personalities like the Zuccari brothers. In August 2021 part of the vaults of the halls of the noble floor and the ground floor collapsed; the Superintendence is treating restoration and consolidation.
The paintings of the castle brought to the street.
Gothic Church of the fourteenth century, of the Dominicans since 1315, with the rose window; from here starts the procession of Good Friday.

Stone streets, panoramic staircases and historic buildings with the Mother Church and the Town Hall; churches and palaces of the eighteenth century. The patron saint, Santa Margherita, is celebrated on July 20.
One of the best known examples of Romanesque in Tuscany, in sandstone, with the façade with five arches surmounted by three loggias of columns all different; the apse is seen from Piazza Grande.
The heart of the city, between Palazzo dei Priori and Cathedral.
Under the Rock of the Cigno, at about 500 m altitude, with the hall called "the cathedral" , 20 m high, rich of stalactites and stalagmites.
The industrial cathedral.
