The ditch descends from the south-western limestone slope of Mount Nerone to the Giordano Fosso, in a narrow and wooded valley of beech and broad-leaf trees; in the mid-high stretch it forms high waterfalls and narrow holes.
The star fortress.
a collapse in 2018 damaged the outer belt; consolidation work started in 2025 (Italy.it)
A rare Lombard ciborium still in its place.
The painter's rooms.
The facades of the country painted like an open-air gallery.
Access to the North Necropolis only during extraordinary thematic visits.
The trades of the past.

Church of the Basilian abbey founded in the tenth century by San Nilo di Rossano. With three naves with wooden roof and ancient columns, it has frescoes of saints from the 12th to the 13th century and, in the apse, the Presentation of Mary at the Temple; the Baroque dome shows the Creator with holy monks and Saint Nile in prayer. The high altar (1731) is attributed to Domenico Costa, with the painting of the Martyrdom of Saint Adriano probably by Francesco Saverio Ricci and two wooden busts of the seventeenth century. The masterpiece is the floor, partly in opus sectile and partly in mosaic; the main portal has been closed since 1856 and you enter from the sides, under the bell tower or from the Porta dei Monaci with two stone masks.
The memory of the war on the hills.
The museum dedicated to comics and imaginary, perfect for those traveling with children; Lucca hosts Lucca Comics & Games every autumn.
A smoking landscape.
The convent of 1222 heart of the country.
opens only in extraordinary openings scheduled with the Municipality (in 2025 on Saturdays of July and August, 18:30-20:30); visits on request via PEC to the Superintendence
The only catacomb in Umbria.

The village dominates from above Lake Omodeo, suitable for trekking, mountain biking and canoeing and wildlife oasis with rare birds; under the waters lie the remains of a nuragic settlement. At the lake, the pine forest of Istei hosts the festival of s'anzone on Monday.
The rare birds of prey of the Albegna gorges.
Built in the mid-nineteenth century, it has three naves in which the Baroque blends with the neoclassical, with Morani stuccos and high reliefs.

The municipality of the high Garfagnana dominated by the Fortress of the Verrucole dei Gherardinghi, today living museum with costume guides; in the territory the Orecchiella Park with the Visitor Center and its naturalistic museum, the village of Naggio and the Baroque church of San Romano Martire.

Medieval village of the Valle dell'Aniene, on a hill of about 500 meters between the Lucretile Mountains and the Simbruini, about 55 km from Rome; in the Castello Brancaccio, born around the Mille, is located the Museum of Rural Civilization Valle dell'Aniene, among the first demoetnoanthropological museums of Lazio, and in the territory remain polygonal walls, the Roman aqueduct and traces of the Via Valeria.
Stone portals and medieval alleys.
Opens only on special occasions (for example FAI Days): check before going

Born from the collection of Monsignor Antonio Parazzi (1823-1899), it has four sections: archaeological (fossil, bronzes, finds of the Bronze Age and Romans, coins, Egyptian statues and Etruscan-Italic finds), Renaissance (one hundred terracottas of the Padan furnaces and ceramics from the fifteenth to the nineteenth century), art gallery (paintings from the sixteenth to the nineteenth century, torn frescoes, wooden tablets) and ancient fabrics related to the Viadana and saffron. It is located in the MuVi cultural centre.
A collection of shells from all over the world, curious even for children.

A mountain village, the only one in Italy: from the nineteenth century its street vendors brought books all over central-northern Italy, passing from stone to books in 1858. Here in 1952 was born the Bancarella Prize; in August the Festa del Libro fills streets and squares of meetings with authors.
The view from the village towards the coast.
From wheat to bread, in the Low Padana.

A hill country 600 metres of Greek and Byzantine origins, dominated by the ruins of Castello Santapau, mentioned since 1272 and destroyed by the earthquake of 1693; in the necropolis territory from the age of Copper to the Byzantine era and the rock complex of the Cave of Saints with medieval frescoes.
Excursion to a 19th century alpine fortification.
The sunset on the lagoon.

Founded in 1974 with the donation of 500 minerals by Giacomo Perego, since 1983 it is located in the eighteenth-century Palazzo Gualteroni. It preserves about 1,500 minerals and fossils, including the Cassinisia orobica symbol of the museum, over 35,000 insects, 1,000 birds and 1,300 mammals, with reconstructions of alpine environments, showcases on wolf and bear and skull of a knocked bear in Val Gerola in 1887. Open Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday 9-12 and 14:30-17:30.
The great historical theatre of the city.
The tomb of Queen Adelasia.
Roman archaeology and peasant life of Brianza in a single museum.
The oldest monument in the country, born from the plague of the sixteenth century.
A whole Roman city at the foot of Velino.
Elegant church of medieval origin in the hamlet of Faltugnano, recommended to lovers of religious architecture; near the Villas Organi and Ricci.

Born from the commitment of Bishop Biagio D'Agostino for the neglected works of art, it was established on December 8, 1978 as Diocesan Museum and Art Gallery to guard the works of the parishes of the diocese; expanded with restoration workshop and the San Pantaleone room for recent works, exhibits wooden statues and paintings of local tradition.

In the granite building of the old Pretura, in the oldest part of the village, it tells the Gallura banditism between the sixteenth and nineteenth centuries and the Vasa-Mamia feud (1849-1857): four rooms with documents, vintage photographs, weapons and objects, the reconstruction of an office of the 19th century carabinieri and a room dedicated to Sebastiano Tansu, the
An entire village frescoed by the masters of the twentieth century.
Easy ring from the center of the village that crosses six bridges on the streams that give the name to the resort.

Made in 1733 in local travertine by Nicola and Arcangelo Antinolfi of Cava de' Tirreni, in the center of Piazza San Michele, to give water to the population collecting that coming from the village of Sorbo. Four lions at the corners of the basin, in the middle a stele with the coat of arms of Solofra (a radiant sun) and on top four dolphins holding a shell tub.

The center has houses with frescoed facades, wooden balconies, capitals, sundials and municipal ovens \from pan Â Â Â, the Baroque Town Hall and wooden workshops, furniture and musical instrument builders. At Christmas, about the beginning of December at the Epiphany, Tesero and his Nativity scenes carry a hundred handmade nativity scenes in alleys, courtyards, stables and windows, with a life-size nativity scene in the square; in summer the courtyards of Tiezer are reminiscent of crafts, music and cooking in the courtyards.
The gun square between the Rocca, San Martino and the bridge.
More than 200 sculptures created in the international sculpture Symposium on stone, scattered in the center of Fanano and in the hamlets.

Medieval village between a river bend and a rocky spur, with narrow streets, steep staircases and stone houses leaning against the rock; it is part of the Hellenophonous area of Aspromontana, of which it preserves culture and language.
The theatre of the white stone of Comiso.
On the main square, with Palazzo VII Aprile and its clock tower, the Baroque Cathedral whose façade was completed only in 1956.
To get lost in the alleys of the ancient village and overlook the sea from the belvedere.
Ethnographic museum with an unusual exhibition in the center of Ozieri.
The places of poetry.
Telesio and Villa Vecchia.
The mosaic told from the beginning.
The church of the Hunt and Vignola.

Built in the first half of the sixteenth century and linked to the settlement of the Carmelites, then passed to the Franciscans after the suppressions of 1806; the cult of the Madonna del Carmine was tied to the pasta makers of the city. A single nave with a Latin cross, it is accessed by a staircase in piperno; the ceiling is frescoed by V. Severino (1907) with the Virgin of Carmel in glory, the chapel of the Immaculate has a marble altar of 1763 and a wooden statue of 1759, and the chapel

At the Giogo di Tisa, at 3,210 m, a thin stone pyramid marks the point of finding the mummy. You will arrive with a challenging mountaineering excursion of 15.2 km and about 8 hours (1,607 m of altitude difference) from Vernago, for the Tisen farm and the Tisa Valley to the Similaun refuge and then along a rocky ridge partly equipped; along the path the archaeological site of the Schneck with a neolithic stone engraved. The archeoParc organizes guided hiking tours to the glacier every Tuesday.

An ancient olive oil mill transformed into an oil museum, with guided tours and tastings; extra virgin olive oil, Montepulciano d'Abruzzo and saffron are sold there. Opening on request, for groups. Bucchianico is known for the oil produced by several mills.
Church of the fourteenth century with a single nave with ribbed vaulted apse and traces of frescoes from different eras; bound since 1974.
Means, weapons and relics of world wars on the Mainarde front.

Cited in 1289 as dedicated to the Saints Fabiano and Sebastiano, it takes the name of San Bartolomeo in 1360; some constructive characters would date back to the middle of the 10th century. Romanesque remains are the bell tower (probably from the 11th century), the apse, with fragments of frescoes from the 15th century, and the central aisle; at the beginning of the 16th century it was enlarged with the left aisle and the façade was rebuilt using ancient shelves and capitals. Visit on request to the parish house (Via Don Minzoni 5).
times not yet defined, open only at cultural events
A scano beach reachable by ferry.

Medieval village almost 600 meters at the foot of the Colle Rotondo, overlooking the Peligna Valley, with the remains of the Doge's Palace called Fortezza dello Scorpio, the church of the Madonna della Snow built on a Roman temple and the church of the SS. Rosary with the fifteenth century fountain.
Once a summer residence of the Pontifical Greek College, with a beautiful church already mentioned in a papal bull of 1153.
The Eugubino castle at the foot of Monte Cucco.

The Cittadella is one of the oldest neighborhoods, born fortified inside the walls with two gates, including the Milanese gate to the north, and narrow and long blocks on the slope with paved pebbles. On the first floor of the Town Hall the Council Hall preserves the canvas of Andrea Celesti (1693, 262 x 735 cm) commissioned as a thank you for the end of the plague of 1630, with the Doge, the theological virtues and St. John the Baptist.
Park of the nineteenth century villa in the center of the village.
The ridge of Calvana, between horses grazing and hiking itineraries on the hills of Prato.
Gorge under the tower.
The headphones and fabrics of the women of the valley.

Rocca built in the thirteenth century on a small hill by Archbishop Ottone Visconti, perhaps on a previous early medieval settlement, to defend the Contado del Seprio disputed between Torriani and Visconti; the fief was given to a branch of the Visconti, extinct in 1751. Passed to the Bossi, at the end of the eighteenth century it became a noble residence with two terraces with Italian garden and an underground water lily with fake caves, mosaics and shells; in 1960 the restoration was entrusted to the Milanese studio BBPR. It is the stop of the regional route Â"Tour dei castelli viscontei" with Caidate through the valley of the Boya; signposted in the Places of the Heart FAI from 2003 to 2022 and opened by the FAI in 2021 and on the Day FAI of Autumn 2024.

Founded in 1585 by the counts of Arc next to the church of San Lorenzo, with a new church consecrated in 1593; in 1630 some friars died curing the plagues. Suffered by Joseph II in 1787 and then in Napoleonic age, he was damaged in the Great War. Cloister with arches in local stone and well; in the church with a single nave the altarpiece of Paolo Farinati and a fragment of Madonna from the ancient collegiate. Visitable during the day, without barriers.
the MiC card (updated to May 2020) indicates closed every day; check with the Municipality (tel. 0963 313092)
Frescoes and wooden altar of the sixteenth century.
The sea and the summer parties.

Faunistic area entirely fenced of 35 hectares in the Pinedo Plain, between Cimolais and Claut, on the edge of the Park, where there are specimens of the local fauna; with a visitor center dedicated to the senses of nature, the reconstruction of a house of woodcutters and a restored lime furnace. 9-18 hours (last entry into the courtyard at 17); dogs not allowed.
Relax in the shade of the pine trees a few steps from the village.
The vow of a country decimated by the plague.
The stone heads of a lonely artist.
Wanted by Pope Clement VII in the Renaissance to ensure water in case of siege: 54 meters deep, you walk with a double helical staircase of 248 steps.

The villa was built in the eighteenth century by Odoardo Odoardi on the remains of a medieval fortification; the garden was commissioned by Vincenzo Carfratelli Seghetti and built between 1875 and 1890 by the German landscaper Ludwig Winter. On the ridge that dominates the Tronto and the Salaria grow a rare Jubaea spectabilis, palms of the Canary Islands and dates, monumental Washingtonia, red beech and oaks; in the pond, on an island, an eighteenth-century statue in travertine of Venus and Cupid, and there is also the "romitory" typical of the gardens of Winter.
The Giuseppe Meazza stadium, the largest in Italy and "Scala del calcio" in Milan and Inter, with the museum born in 1996, the first set up in a stadium in Italy, between historical links and cups.
Paintings, posters, vestments and books on the life of the monk Cone, patron of the city, and on the devotion brought by the immigrants overseas. Open Monday and Sunday.
The piles of wood become works of art.
In the square the white marble monument in Garibaldi recalls the disarmament of the Bourbon army at Soveria Mannelli on 30 August 1860.
The Sulcis farmhouse as it was.
Hans Clemer's shovels.
A rare sixteenth-century organ.
A devotional climb that ends with the best view on Appiano.
The symbol of the Reggio Musicale.
The MiC has announced a temporary closure for works and new setup: check the reopening
Built in 1843, 96 seats with audiences, two orders of stages and loggia; it is among the smallest theatres in Europe.

The capital of the Cape of Sopra: Piazza d'Italia and the Fountain of Rosello, symbols of the city, the Gothic-Catalan cathedral of San Nicola, the Museo Sanna and the National Art Gallery, Santa Maria di Bethlem dei Candelieri and, out of town, the prenuragic altar of Monte d'Accoddi.
The path between the cultivated countryside that from Torrita leads to Montefollonico, telling the traditions and legends of the holy wine.
The source of Pope John's baptism.
Art and gardens under Castle.
The Gothic on the city's living room.
Bridge over the river Bosso, the most important Roman site of Cagli: the central fornic with the buttresses, in large blocks of stone, dates back to the Republican era.

In the eighteenth-century pontifical customs building commissioned by Clement XIII, a state museum since 1970 heir to the Civic Museum of 1918, on four floors: on the ground floor a Roman copy of Athena Parthenos and the Apollo-Helios, considered a great replica of the Colossus of Rhodes; then the territory from prehistory to the Etruscans (Sanctuary of Punta della Vipera and cult of Menerva), Centumcellae traianea with coastal villas and Terme Taurine, Lviv-Cencelle founded in 854 and finds from archaeological seizures. Tactile plastics, bilingual panels and contents in LIS; open 8:30-19:30, closed on Monday; free on the first Sunday of the month.
Themed trail with a 5.3 km ring (about 1 hour and 30 km) from the Sandhof along the Passirio, among illustrated legends, small mythical creatures called Not suitable for strollers.
The sacred art of Nissena.
Room tomb with barrel vault of the II-I century BC, in local sandstone; the kit is now at the National Archaeological Museum of Perugia.
The ancient village under the castle, made of steep and narrow streets and stairs, where are located the Romanesque churches of San Giorgio, San Bartolomeo and San Leonardo.

Ring of about 2 hours and 476 m of difference in altitude, without difficulty, from Piazza Giosuè Meli (where there is the Monument to the life of Alberto Meli): via Belvedere with Villa Pasinetti, the Cascine Benti and Moioli and the three deodara cedars of 1939 go up to the sanctuary of Sant'Antonio (550 m), documented from 1780, with a bronze of Sant'Antonio abbot and one of Pope John XXIII of Meli and a picnic area with fountain. Higher up the Prati Alti (780 m) with a large roar and the small church of the Madonna del Rosario of 1790, then the Pizzo Casgnola (791 m) with views of the Prealpi Orobie and plain; return to the Pizzo Boscaglia and Costa.
16th century church: on the high altar there is a traditional image of the Madonna with Child.

Medieval village perched, possession of the Aldobrandeschi, then of the Republic of Siena, Medici stronghold on the Amiata and part of the county of Santa Fiora, became free municipality of the Grand Duchy of Tuscany in the eighteenth century. In the central square there is the town hall, the church of Saints Peter and Paul and the small Civic Tower with clock; from the Porta di Maremma you go out towards the church of Our Lady and the Cassero.
A walk through the walls, portals and palaces.

It was created in 1422 by a Romanesque church at the behest of Antonio Colonna, lord of Riofreddo, under the pontificate of Martino V (the date is on a marble plaque on the façade). The only room with a barrel vault is entirely painted with a cycle of Gothic taste: the Crucifixion in the bezel above the entrance, the Annunciation on the wall of the altar and, in the vault, the Triumph of Christ with angels, the four Evangelists and the Doctors of the Church.
From Malga Ciapela the cable car climbs to Punta Rocca, 3265 meters, with panoramic terrace; in winter from here descends La Bellunese, a 12-km track to Malga Ciapela in the Dolomiti Superski.
Rocca and Romanesque portal in one shot.
The village of the Iron Age under the parish church.

The National Park Visitor Centre includes the naturalistic museum and the wildlife area, which houses local animals born in captivity or wounded and then cured and rehabilitated in the center. Timetable indicated by Italia.it: 10-17:30, closed on Tuesday.
A ghost village on the cliff.
The covered commercial gallery built in 1878 by Mayor Bernardo Arnaboldi Gazzaniga and designed by Ercole Balossi, between Strada Nuova and Piazza del Lino.
Castle of the 12th century, today restaurant with hotel; the tower, about 30 meters high, can be visited by reservation.

In Piazza Ottaviano Augusto the Palace of the Apostolic Delegate and the Town Hall, inspired by Vignola at Palazzo Farnese in Caprarola; in the palace are the civic museums. In Piazza Mazzini the monumental Baroque fountain.
In the crypt of the monastery of San Francesco al Corso, home of the Museum of Cavalcaselle Frescoes, the sarcophagus in porphyry of tradition, about ten minutes walk from Piazza Bra.
A walk between murals and organ tradition.
Porticos frescoed and views of the Conero.

The pearl of the Adriatic Sea, birthplace of Domenico Modugno, is a village of white houses on a cliff excavated by about twenty sea caves: you enter the historical center from the Marchesal Arch, you go down to the famous Lama Monachile under the Bourbon bridge and you visit the Pino Pascali Foundation Museum, in the former slaughterhouse.
Arriving at the castle on foot like pilgrims.
Excavation exhibits seen from close up.
The heart of ancient Neapolis.
An artist from Tertenia who arrived in New York.
Walk through the homes of the Milanese nobles.

Town of Val Pusteria founded in the 13th century as a fortified village, with Via Centrale and four doors still preserved, dominated by the castle of the principal bishops that houses the Messner Mountain Museum Ripa; in the hamlet of Teodon the Provincial Museum of customs and customs, the oldest South Tyrolean regional museum.

Massive cylindrical tower dating from the 13th to the 14th century, linked to the fortifications built in Calabria by the Normans of Robert Guiscardo; it was probably a lookout tower for a more important castle and once had blackbirds and ornaments on the summit. A functioning astronomical observatory is now installed at the top. Free visit by reservation via the town control unit (0961 937014).
Heaven for divers.

Designed by Prof. Beniamino Tartaglia with the community of Aquilonia, reconstructs houses, stables and workplaces of the Altarpine world: about 14,000 original objects on 1,500 m2, in over 130 environments divided into 12 sections (masters such as barbershop, blacksmith, shoemaker, sawmill and basketmaker, feeding, traditions, archaeology, protoindustry), plus an outdoor area with vintage agricultural machinery. Guided tours of about 90 minutes, only by reservation (tel. 0827 83826).
Large sandstone cavities dug by man in the woods.
The frescoes of the Crypt of Epifanio, a masterpiece of the Middle Ages.

Cathedral built between VII and VIII century, rebuilt in 1466 and enlarged at the beginning of the twentieth century, with Venetian façade that faithfully reconstructs the fifteenth century; next to the massive bell tower of 1150 and the Byzantine baptistery of 1089, frescoed in the same period.

Castle built in the 8th century, probably on prehistoric structures, as a refuge during the barbarian invasions; rebuilt in the 4th-Fifth century, it was residence of the bishops of Trento and in 1799 passed to the Municipality of Levico. Remain the ruins, reachable by an easy path from the village of Selva.
A medieval church with six petals, unique in its kind.
The millenarian cathedral with the frescoed crypt.
The summit of the Somma, with Vesuvius in front.
A castle with three belts and its medieval nativity scene.
The image symbol of Procida.
€15 with wine tasting, reduced €6 to 18 years
The emperor's bust on the cathedral.
Tourism Marche: after the earthquake of 2016 the area is not accessible
The Venetian square of the city fortress.
The two main churches of the village, San Martino in Foro and the Collegiata dei Santi Lorenzo and Apollinare, which preserve valuable works; in the center also the small Theatre of the Arrischianti.
The palace of the principality.

Established in 2014, it exhibits finds of the ancient Medma, a Locrian foundation: the large necropolis about one kilometer south of the town (about 600 tombs of the VI-III century BC, with burial and incineration), the sanctuaries along an ideal sacred street with the votive crest of contrada Calderazzo discovered by Paolo Orsi, about 33 meters long and filled with terracotta, ceramic and metal offerings, and one of the most important collections of terracotta medmee statuettes, dedicated mainly to Persephone. In closing, finds from the excavations in the city and part of the Gangemi collection.
The work of the zolfatari told by their tools.
A vast collection of archaeological finds, traditional costumes and everyday objects to learn about the history and culture of the region.
Etruscan sutri.
The memory of the Allied landing on the Salento coast.
Baroque canvases and portals in the districts.

Cities of Roman origin crossed by the canals San Domenico, Vena and Lombardo, Chioggia is called the "small Venice": along the Corso del Popolo you will meet the Clock Tower with its museum, the Cathedral of Longhena, the Temple of San Martino and the Pescheria, while towards the sea there are the beaches of Sottomarina and Isola Verde, the Walls of the Serenissima, the woods and the reserve of Bosco Nordio.

Beach between the gardens of Villa Cortine and the Caves of Catullo, whose name comes from "biunda" closed place; in front of the shore a small stone fence where sometimes comes hot water from the thermal baths. Free access, showers, bar and restaurant, pets allowed; sun loungers on reservation the day before.

The palace, begun in 1335 and finished in the early sixteenth century and joined to the town hall, houses the museum with ruins and mosaics of Sentinum and the daily life of the Roman city; on the ground floor the Sala Perottiana with Byzantine and Flemish reliquaries, including the icon of San Demetrio, Byzantine mosaic on late fourteenth century table.
A watermill still working and painting of a lifetime.
The whole Val Gardena, from fossils to carving in Luis Trenker, in a museum.
Guarini's baroque.
Among the main mining facilities in Italy, with the complex of Pozzo Sella: guided tours show wells, tunnels and installations.
The Santacroce polyptych and the view of the Val del Riso.
Pinewood with adventure park.

In an olive grove the remains of the Roman colony of Scolacium, heir of the Greek Skylletion (of which there is nothing left): forum, theatre, amphitheatre, paved roads, aqueducts, mausoleum and a necropolis with sacred area, a basilica and a spa. In summer the park hosts concerts and cultural events.
Understand how caves are born before or after the visit.
€5, reduced €2
The Romanesque Apulian in the old town.
the chapel opens only for the feasts of Our Lady of Loreto and Corpus Domini (VisitLazio)
Pinacoteca and naturalistic collections in the former Dominican convent.
A balcony on the plain of Sibari.
The façade of lava in the heart of the country.
Above Manarola, in an area that produces oil and wine of the Riviera, stop of the Via dei Santuari.
The 18th century press.
The peasant tools kept in a cellar of the Chierese.

Ancient capital of the San Martino Valley, about 20 km from Bergamo, with a historic center of palaces, noble houses and gardens, the eighteenth-century parish church of San Biagio and, in the hamlet of Celana, the church with the altarpiece of the Assumption of Lorenzo Lotto and the Borromaic College with the naturalistic museum of Don Bernardino Gavazzeni.
The oil of Garda at the source.
Cefalù's most beautiful sunset.
Four lakes with an hour's walk.
Thermal waters at the foot of Matese.
Small Romanesque masterpiece with a single nave, the oldest monument in the city (end X-XI century).
Villa on the Cerbaie built on the basis of a castle of the Cadolings of the 11th century, then the Albizi, who erected the current fifteenth-century church; ample view of the Valdarno.

Ancient Rocca Guidonesca, fortress of the thirteenth century on the Laia gorge guarding the road between Rieti and the Tiber valley, long belonged to Savelli; abandoned after the war, it preserves intact the medieval system between ruins of houses and shops. The only restored building, in the eighteenth century, is the church of San Lorenzo, usually closed, where every August 10 comes in procession the people of Rocchette.
Byzantine frescoes in the rock, a short walk from the village.

Former 19th century industrial city, the most important site in the valley: in the eighteenth century there was the largest paper mill in Italy, in the mid-nineteenth century a copper foundry, then the Lanificio Forti, which before the Second World War gave work to more than a thousand workers, with housing and recreational, cultural and welfare facilities for employees.
An armory turned church to make up for it.
The granite village on the sea.

In the countryside, among the most interesting menhirs: at the base there is a small Byzantine newsstand from which you can see the remains of the interior frescoes, with references to St. Paul and Tarantism.
Ten rooms under the square.
The fortress of the Marquises of Saluzzo with the decorated salons of the Solaro accounts.
The Vallaise Road.
A medieval cloistered monastery.

Country at 1,800 meters in the Stelvio National Park, renowned summer and winter station that hosted World Cup Ski World Cup World Championships; starting point for hiking and biking among wooden huts to the glaciers and birthplace of Deborah Compagnoni, to which is dedicated a 3.5 km track exposed to the north.
The door to Mount Rosa.
in restoration according to the source

Borgo Ciociano on a cone hill, with paved streets and stone houses, dominated by the castle Longhi De Paolis where he was imprisoned and died Pope Celestine V in 1296; on the vaults of the castle the hanging gardens at 800 meters, and in the territory the karst lake of Canterno.
The hidden Perugino.

It exhibits the most significant materials of more than forty years of excavation at the Terramara Santa Rosa: ceramics (cetole, cups, dolii, votive objects, fusaiole, frame weights), ornaments and bronze instruments, with a teaching apparatus on the village and on the terramare of the western Emilia; also remains of a Roman villa found in Fodico. Open all year round, on the 2nd floor of the building of the Municipal Library.
17th century church with two facades, one of which overlooks Piazza Cavour.
The medieval nucleus around which the village was born.
A Gothic jewel of frescoes to see with the key of the farm.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 5 of the 6 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
A medieval cloister and the history of the city.
"The center of the center of the world."
Relive the work of the spinning mills in a 19th century factory.
A full day excursion from the station of Pieve San Lorenzo along the path 181, through historic villages, to the panoramic pass overlooking the Pizzo d'Uccello.
The symbol of the center, escaped from two earthquakes.
A castle born in the days of Hannibal.

Village of seventeenth-century terraced houses, some with vegetable garden; until about seventy years ago in place of the square there were the locks, crossed with a mobile bridge. The sixteenth-century Villa Querini Stampalia with frescoes by B. De Pitati and shop, who also worked on young Tintoretto and Bassano.

It was the church of the village of San Leonardo, one of the first French villages in Novara, from which the city took its first name; the pilgrims of the Via Francisca stayed there. A unique nave with semicircular apse, a hut facade and walls in square stones and river pebbles; the interior frescoes, perhaps of Romanesque inspiration, have been recently restored.
The altarpiece with the Prince's portrait.
The mother church with the fifteenth century Crucifix.

Built between the 13th and 15th centuries and completed in 1507, it dominates the village and the Fiastra valley, perhaps on the site of the ancient fortress of Urbs Salvia; it has trapezoidal plan, four towers and a mast with ghibelline merlons and is a national monument.

Ancient coppellate mass, part of the village's life for centuries, then transformed into a fountain. On the surface you can see the cups engraved in prehistoric times and the furrows much more recent left by sharp blades and knives exploiting the stone and running water.

Built between 1700 and 1705 by the Carthusian monks, it passed to private individuals in the nineteenth century; the last owner, Professor Luigi Cantù, left it as a legacy to the City. The municipality indicates it as the most important artistic testimony of the 18th century Casteggiano: restored, it is the center of the cultural life of the city and houses archaeological museum, civic library with multimedia room and events. From the residence you can enjoy a wide view of the Oltrepò hills.
The great golden Madonna visible from afar.
Secular forest and ruins in the garden of the Chigi.
The wine king's castle.
From Dronero start the Occitan Paths that go up to the high valley Maira and the Path on the Maira.

In the Franciscan convent, collection dedicated to the painter and engraver of Oran Mario Delitala (1887-1990): xylographies and some paintings, including portraits, sacred works and scenes of barbaric life.

The most panoramic walk of the village, between vine, lemon, olive, carob and pomegranate: it connects the churches of Sant'Antonio and San Michele up to a sacred newsstand overlooking the precipices of Furore.
The monastery was founded in 1406 and houses the tombs of many Este, including Alfonso I and his wife Lucrezia Borgia.
The Medieval Biella.
A historical theater inside the walls.
The science to touch.

Built in the 10th century under Atenolfo II on a travertine bench in front of the Roman and Longobard center, the residence lived with the town until the destruction of the city by Corrado IV in 1252; from the end of the thirteenth century around the palace a fortified center developed. You can see the pseudosquare tower, transformed into a bell tower in the eighteenth century, the remains of the Comital Palace called Casa di San Tommaso, with two double windows in the façade of the fourteenth-XV century, the defensive walls and the remains of a large cylindrical tower guarding the bridge over the lakes.
The Pordenone of the churches.
The main church of the village.
The Doge's Palace wanted by Ascanio della Corgna in 1560, designed by Vignola or Galeazzo Alessi, the most important building in the village.

Stone theatre built almost entirely by hand by the sculptor-pastor Lorenzo Reina from the 1970s, on a plateau on top of a cliff: the cavea has 108 seats arranged as the 108 stars of the constellation Andromeda and the elliptical stage is made of 365 tiles. At the summer solstice the sun rises aligned with a window of the seabed; it is the heart of the Art Farm, together with sculptures of Reina including the Mask of the Word.

Gravine almost 4 km long, about 40 m deep, with about 600 plant species, many rare and medicinal. It houses a rock village of neolithic origin, inhabited until the twelfth century, with more than 200 houses dug into the limestone: among these the Cave of the Cyclops, with blades of flint and fragments of prehistoric ceramics, and the "Farmacia of the Magic Greguro" , twelve communicating environments where according to legend the magician and his daughter Margheritella preserved medicinal herbs. Guided tours of about 3 hours, from Tuesday to Sunday, with reservation required two days before and minimum 10 participants; variable cost; do not recommend to people with motor disabilities.
The emperor's house suspended on the Gulf.

Designed by Pietro Maggi, built in 1820 and modernized in 1862, it is reached from the portico of the Town Hall: horse-iron plant with 50 stages on three orders, gallery and audience, with stuccoes and golden decorations.
Mills for the mill of cereals, social dairy and a primitive hydroelectric power plant, next to the parish church of San Martino.
To see from the sea the wildest coast of Gargano.
A fortified village among the meadows.
The Renaissance nativity scene in stone.
Just outside the village, you enter it from a portal of the fifteenth century.
A Greek temple inside a church.
Cross a crater along a road dug by the Romans.

Opened on 13 May 2007 in the wooded area of the Parco Pineta di Appiano Gentile e Tradate, chosen for peace and natural darkness, by the collaboration between Parco, Comune and Gruppo Astronomico Tradatese. It includes the main specula, an educational observatory with auxiliary telescopes, the Nature Path with orienteering gym and sensory strip, the EcoPlanetario and the Scientific Teaching Centre, which is also the Park Visitor Centre.
Ruins in the woods.
On foot or by bike on the big handle of the Po.
The cathedral of the work of the triumphin iron.
Since 1985 in the farmhouse Stramiano, former property of the Savoy: a large wetland near the castle where dozens of storks nest and stop in migration.
Solar Observatory: €8, children €4

Panoramic place between Lake Idro and Garda, reachable on foot or by car, with a shelter at about 1,400 m; from the mountain you can practice paragliding and in July, for over forty years, the Alps celebrate a mass at the church on the summit. On the mountain are the military fortifications of 1914 that house the museum of war finds.

Villa built in the early 20th century by Achille Franzosini and sold in 1917 to the film producer Giuseppe Barattolo; since 1989 it is the seat of the Regional Park of the Roman Castles. The 7,500 m2 park has a nature trail with information panels and a pond.

The five historical museums of the University Federico II, mineralogy, zoology, anthropology, physics and paleontology, in the ancient Jesuit College, seat of the University since 1777, and in the complex of Saints Marcellino and Festus.
A prehistoric site among waterfalls in the Apuan Islands.

The Observatory, designed in 1939 and completed in 1965 on the remains of the Roman villa of Matidia, relative of Hadrian, hosts Astrolab, an interactive laboratory of astrophysics from the Solar System at the first moments of the universe, with observation of the Sun on request. Visits for schools and groups of at least 20 people by reservation. It was set from the film about boys from Panisperna Street.

Ring of about 4.6 km (2 hours and 10 minutes, altitude difference about 380 m) from the car park of Via Lacca in Olera: terraces with vines and orchards, woods of hornbeam and roverella, arid meadows and the Canto Basso (900 m) with views of Poscante and the Val Brembana, passing near Monte di Nese. Recommended clockwise.
A balcony over the void and a medieval legend.
The coast by bicycle.

A large public lawn in Montepiano with the large red enameled metal sculpture in the shape of a sun donated by Bruno Saetti, who chose Montepiano as a place of life and work; next to the geometric garden and the House of the Mill, his house-atelier, today home of an art school.
A villa of delight from Romagna outside the circuits.
Moncalieri's Gothic.
€4 full, €2 reduced; free under 18 and the second Sunday of the month

One of the largest monastic complexes in Europe, a university since 1997 restored by Giancarlo De Carlo: Baroque facades by Antonino Amato, neoclassical staircase of honour, two cloisters, Roman domus, ancient kitchens with the Factory Museum and botanical gardens.
One of the hunting residences of the Sforza, with moat and towers.
Sicular necropolis and ancient port with water.
The Archangel Cave.

At the entrance of the village Romanesque bell towers and stone towers; in the center houses of the sixteenth century like the Lichtegg and the Malsegg and the remains of a large round tower that was part of a castle.
The most central and famous beach of Pizzo, along the Lungomare Cristoforo Colombo; there ends the walk of Pizzapundi, from which at sunset you can see the Stromboli.
Gagini sculptures.
In the highest part of the village, from the 15th to the 16th century, rebuilt in neoclassical style with baroque elements; two naves with the floor following the shape of the rock.
The Black Madonna from Castel Mancino.
The crib village overlooking the Majella.

On the ground floor of the convent complex of Sant'Antonio dei Frati Minori, about 800 m2 of works by well-known Italian, European and African artists; next to it are a library of Franciscan and Picena history, the provincial historical archive of the Friars Minor of the Marche and the conference room. Guided tours by reservation.
A unique candle-tree.
The Vasari on the hill.
Where Father Pio stayed.
Of remote origins, it was rebuilt ex novo between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries because considered too modest compared to the other sacred places of the city.

Set up in rooms of the Benedictine Abbey and opened from June 19, 2010, it collects finds of Sannitica and Roman age, from the fourth century BC to the second century AD, coming from the excavations of the ancient city of Telesia; the route follows the Sannita period, the Roman colony and the destruction of the city, in an environment with frescoes of the fourteenth century and underground spaces. Booking not required; the ministerial card does not record active times, referent to Pro Loco.
With 515 meters it is the highest peak of the Vena del Gesso, reachable by trails through white ridges.
The bridge stretches over the stream.

Borgo del Chietino known for the Green Falls, indicated as the highest of the Apennines, protected by the Regional Nature Reserve of 287 hectares entirely in the municipal territory, WWF oasis since 1997; in the Town Hall the Civic Museum Memories of peasant life collects the tools of work in the fields.
The medieval fortress that dominates the village.

Coastal fraction about 36 km from the village, on the Gulf of Angels: about a kilometer of golden sand between Cape Boi and a rocky tip, with a dune, blue sea to emerald green and low seabed near shore that then descends quickly; windy, suitable for windsurfing and kite. A path on the promontory leads to the Spanish tower of Capo Boi (120 m), with views of Villasimius, Capo Carbonara and the island of Cavoli. Parking, dining and rental.

In the Rocca, two sections: the armory with offensive and defensive weapons from the Middle Ages to the seventeenth century and the reconstruction of environments, furnishings and Renaissance costumes with mannequins. Open every day 9-12 and 15-19; 33% discount with the Terra di Tresori Card.
The parish church houses works by Bernardino Lanino and Tanzio da Varallo.

The coast extends for over 3,500 meters with shallow and sandy bottoms suitable for children; the beaches, Blue Flag, have facilities where you can practice beach volleyball, surfing and kitesurfing. The promenade is a long walk that continues towards San Bartolomeo al Mare and Andora; from the port start boat excursions in the Sanctuary of the Cetacei Pelagos to spot whales and dolphins.

Born to recover and preserve the traditions of artisan and peasant Pontelandolfo, grown with the breeding: weaving, embroidery, iron, wood and stone processing. It preserves artifacts from the 17th to the 19th century, especially handmade fabrics from families and institutions, and a photo library.
Baroque jewel that dominates the city, wanted by Vittorio Amedeo II after the siege of 1706; it preserves the tombs of Casa Savoia.

Built in the second half of the sixteenth century at the behest of the Marquis Alfonso Gonzaga, with the contribution of the congregations and the Magnificent Community, is attributed to Bernardino Facciotto or his son Girolamo. Latin cross plan with three naves on monolithic columns and ample dome with lantern. It preserves the fifteenth-century Crucifix Miraculous in wood, altars in polychrome marble and salesmen of the Florentine workshop of Corbarelli, paintings of Brusasorzi and of the Mantua school of the sixteenth century, Baroque paintings of Giuseppe Fali and Giuseppe Bazzani, the eighteenth-century choir of Ceratelli and the self-supporting pulpit of Rizzardo Carboni.
Private villa built by Maffeo Gheza in the early 1930s in Moorish style, with aphorisms in fake Arabic characters on the façade and along the wall of belt; the park hosts rare tree species.
In October, there's the chestnut festival.
How farmers built the landscape of the Langhe.
From the 17th century, with a painting by Peter Brueghel the Younger.

The oldest nucleus is the 'centa doppia', a defensive settlement of houses arranged around a natural rise; the Piazza XXIV Maggio is surrounded by palaces in the Habsburg style and was redesigned in the eighties by the architect Podrecca. Among the historic buildings the sixteenth-century Neuhaus House, the seventeenth-century Tacò Palace in via Dante and the Municipal Theatre of 1908 in via Nazario Sauro.
The rooms painted in trompe-l'oeil.
One of the numerous chapels of the territory.
Lawns and woods above Drena.

Small octagonal temple just outside the village, on the left of the Tiber, near the Colledestro stream, with a unique arch bridge near the facade. It has been mentioned in documents since the 12th century and has the appearance of a restoration of the 16th century.It stands where once there was a pagan temple dedicated to the Tiber.
The Primitivo narrated in his historic cellar.
The full Sienese gold background.

Historical centre of alleys to explore and lakefront with large hotels, villas and gardens overlooking the three islands; the Palazzo dei Congressi hosts international conferences and summer concerts.

Farm village of the Alta Val Trebbia, in the Antola Regional Natural Park, along the ancient \'caminus janueÂ between Piacenza and Genoa: beyond the bridge over the Trebbia there are the Augustinian shrine of Our Lady of Montebruno and the former convent with the cloister and the Museum of peasant culture.
To be combined with the visit of the Cave.
The great sanctuary of Nuragic metallurghi.
A postcard glimpse.

Large green space used for events, concerts and markets; on the south side the complex of the Fortress, adapted for military use by the late Roman Empire, fortified by the Scaligeri (1275-1385) and renovated under Venice (1550-1700), when the square became naval Arsenale. The present appearance dates back to the Austrian period.
Romanesque church founded according to tradition in 1027, with bell tower of 1228 and a Roman sarcophagus in the crypt.
